the flight scenes are incredible. i can't compare it to anything really. they keep you on the edge of your seat and are breathtaking. the movie is funny. the humor is almost indirect, but it works so well. the new characters are really well done. they do a really nice job of honoring the first film. this is probably the first movie i have seen of this new wave of movies to arrive years after their predecessor, to actually serve the older main character well. maverick is a badass, and it's obvious even as an older dude. a lot of times these movies have the older familiar face there just to introduce new characters (star wars is probably the worst offender off the top of my head), this is not the case with top gun: maverick and i love it so much for that.

the bottom line is: if you are on the fence about seeing this movie in the theater, you need to get there and watch it. it's phenomenal. it's emotional. i loved it. it's everything you want from a movie.

there's not many sequels better than the 1st film but i thought this was one of them. it was a great story with top class acting by tom cruise and the rest of the cast. i wasn't expecting it to be that good. great film.

top gun maverick joins the ranks of the empire srikes back, aliens, t2, and the dark knight as a sequel that surpasses the original film. i recommend seeing it on the biggest and loudest your screen cineplex has to offer. i expect it to recieve acadmy award nominations/ wins for cinematography and other techinal categories at the oscars next year.

i just loved this sequel, it feels like i waited for 36 years for this movie to release and grap the box offce. although i am 24 years old.

the cinematics and hats off to the crew and kudos to the tom for performing all the stunts for real.

tom cruise really risks his life on his films. he takes an active role in every movie not only as an actor but also as a producer and writer. modern action movies are a spectacle of cgi, and yet, tom cruise still believes in practical effects, really learning skills for his roles and pushing his body and the rest of the crew for the sake of believability in his movies.

there may be nothing more intimidating than trying to live up to the hype of an all time classic such as the original top gun. the fact that this was developed 36 years after the original block buster cult following classic put even more pressure on this summer release (props to waiting to a post-covid summer). with a new director and cast of virgin "top guns", the pressure was that much more magnified. however, despite everything boated against this film... it delivers with enough g force to take your breath away! the backdrop, drama, conflict, and come-togetherness bring this film at the top notch of its class, i was so expecting to be disappointed and this was the exact opposite. it's almost better then original! the only negative comment is they did not have berlin in the love scene! otherwise... this is perfection. oscar to tom for the love of god and please more miles teller going forward.

it was only 2 years ago that i watched the first top gun movie. i'm usually not interested in classic hollywood movies full of cliches and predictability, but rather movies with complicated stories, complicated personalities, unpredictability and moral dillemas. despite that, i gave it a shot, as i felt the need for something simple and great. it turned out to be exactly what i wanted, and a wonderful experience.

when i learned the sequel was coming out, i was thrilled but also skeptical, due to toxic ideologies destroying so many classics with political correctness.

eventually it came to the cinemas. i am very selective of what to watch in cinema, and upon hearing about good reviews, i decided top gun: maverick was the perfect choice.

the opening hits you right in the face with the energy that was dormant for over 30 years. the original top gun theme song so magnificent it tears you up. and then a burst of masculinity with classic rock music and playing with heavy machinery. the producers knew exactly what to aim at, recreated the soul in a perfect way and from the intro alone you know you're in for a treat.

as the story starts to reveal itself, we learn about what happened in last 30 years with the main characters, and what their lives turned out to be like. they all keep their character and the actors portray them perfectly. we also meet new characters, young and cocky just like the previous generation. there is also a strong, but subtle enough mix of emotions in the movie, from romance, lust and friendly love to anger, sadness and grief.

obviously, the story revolves around the top gun and jet fighter pilots perfecting their skills and learning their limits before going to missions. the scenes are simply incredible, the filiming, the sound, everything is perfect. it really shows how the producers of the movie were eager to make it perfect in every way, and they succeeded.

despite being a hollywood movie with somewhat predictible outcomes, the story surprised me a few times, but what's important is the thrill of wanting to know how everything will turn out, and this movie certainly has it.

the movie is incredible and i give it a solid 9. the reason i'm not giving it a 10 is because although it truly is a wonderful experience, when it ends, that's pretty much it. there's no philosophy about it, the story is simple, clear and all laid out, and there's nothing much to think about when it ends. in a way, that's the beauty of it, though - it's a movie where you don't need to think much, just relax and let the rush and emotions flow through you.

this is what summer blockbusters are supposed to be made of: high-octane action, characters worth rooting for, unexpected wohoo! moments, and nostalgia handled right. top gun: maverick makes optimum use of tom cruise's old-school charm, and his chemistry with jennifer connolly is excellent. miles teller is the trump card, and he undoubtedly shines in the role of rooster. the airborne set-pieces are a tremendous audio-visual triumph. kudos to all involved!

i absolutely fell in love with this movie from the first intro scene with the synthy tones and footage similar to the first film, through to the story development and action, and the high stakes heist style mission and conclusion.

the entire movie is a well thought out and very well delivered action movie with some character development for maverick and some heartwarming stuff as well as he overcomes some unfinished business lingering from the original movie.

there are some nods and throwbacks to the classic movie, and i admired them all. the romance segments were kept short and neat this time around, giving some growth and redemption for our hero without dulling the sharp storytelling.

after watching i was smiling from ear to ear. another shout out to the action here, as it is nothing short of spectacular. there is nothing like it, with the air to air combat being of a level not filmed before in my opinion.

9/10 loved the characters, loved the production, loved the action, loved the heist style story, and loved seeing maverick on his last mission for the navy.

a perfect sequel to an awesome movie!!

seeing tom on big screen that to in jets was really great experience. listening the og bgm really felt nice. loved this movie.

never being a big fan of the 1986 original and consequently feeling very unhopeful about this one, top gun maverick surprised the hell out of me as both a fantastic action film and heartfelt drama. there are so many elements of this film that you truly just have to see to believe- everything works in such a smooth manner it ends up feeling so well crafted that it's honestly hard not to be impressed. tom cruise makes his return to his iconic character maverick and does a fantastic job (as always), alongside miles teller's rooster who was everything i hoped his performance would be. unlike the 1986 original, this film feels a lot more fleshed out. it has a decent plot and story structure and although those are clearly not the most important things to this movie- it takes the time to set up everything in a meaningful manner that allows you to care about the characters at hand rather than just watch planes flying across the screen. the cinematography is electric, and much better than its burnt orange counterpart- and the film in general doesn't at all feel repetitive or bland in its storytelling- in fact it's quite thrilling to watch at times. being on the edge of my seat, watching tom cruise guide youngsters into uncertain undescriptive danger may feel like a bit of a cliche at this point- but it works so well in so many ways that i could not help but enjoy almost every minute of it. in the end, top gun maverick pulls off the impossible- a sequel better than its predecessor- and puts cruise on the map yet again as america's greatest action star.

my rating: 9.2/10.

i heard so much about this movie when this was released in cinema i cannot deny that i thought this might be over hyped but this really is turning me to liking tom cruise. theres 3 movies that make me like this guy and thats mi: fallout, this and tropic thunder. when that opening note of kenny rodgers song started just threw me back to see the first movie.

so much of the first is gun ho america but this movie was something different. this wasnt about how many stars and stripes they could fit in but actually provide an in depth story between mentor and students ultimately leads to a climactic ending. the story is half back in the 80s and half in the new wave of mission impossible where they are trying to ground these with such spectacular action scenes and moments between the characters.

the action is truly where this movie excels! i never thought id be able to see such practical effects and filming since the mad max reboot. that movie changed how so many movies are made that its the revival from just all cgi back to a combination. how the g force actually effects everyone is another amazing thing to see compared to the og. all the way through the film the "enemy" also known as the russians are always being poked throughout the movie.

overall its such an enjoyable movie that i will certainly be watching again. to many movies are plain from tom cruise but every now and again he drops an absolute dime of a movie.

this is the reason why tom cruise is the g. o. a. t. wow! everything about this movie was straight up perfect. the cast was amazing, i like the fact that there was a mix of blacks and white in there and even at the top level, it wasn't all white. kudos to the team for doing that. i loved the pace. this would be such a ride for old fans of top gun. bringing back clips from the old, fusing it into the storyline, bringing in the next generation of top gun pilots was just impeccable. even though you knew the action was delaying, i didn't mind the build up process at all, from the training to the romance to the son, father, father friend drama, it all came together real nice at the end. because of that, you developed a relationship with the main characters and i was just hoping that none of them would die. all in all it was an amazing watch. i almost cried in the end 😂 and that opening scene, wow! mach 10.3???? annnnnnd there were no gay action in this. thank god!

tom cruise returns as maverick after thirty plus years in service in the navy he is being put out to pasture. he gets one last shot at a mission teaching a young group of navy academy recruits. iceman played by val kilmer gives him his shot to teach these kids. he is still dealing with the loss of his friend goose that was played by anthony edwards. miles teller plays his son rooster who still holds a grudge. they try to work together and become a great team. there are so many great action sequences in this film that you marvel at. tom cruise is incredible that he still does all his own stunts. there is some funny dialogue and a great soundtrack that gets you really pumped throughout this film. jennifer connelly plays penny a love interest of maverick's that comes back into his life at a time he needs a boost. i really think this is one of the best films of the year. i hope it does not get forgotten come oscar time next year. lady gaga also does a great song for the film as well. i loved this film, go see it and see the original as well if you have not already.

after failing long awaited sequels/soft reboots a million times, hollywood finally got 1 right!!! and this is that 1! fail a million times, you are bound to get a great try eventually. and it's mostly thanks to tom cruise, he produces most his movies and he clearly has an extra huge passion for what he does, and it shows! love or hate tom cruise, it's extremely respectable what he does. he goes the extra mile by doing all his own stunts, used real jets in this movie to minimize cgi, but most importantly, the story here was on point!

the movie surpasses the original top gun in fundamentally every aspect. i never was a huge fan of the og top gun, of all the big 80s classics, i always found it one of the lower tier ones. the sequel vastly improves upon pacing, character development, emotion, action scenes. i almost cried multiple times during maverick.

you don't really need to see the original to follow and get super invested in this movie, but it does help a little but. the movie is basically a super well-executed build up, with an amazing payoff in the third act. it's been so long since i seen a movie's build-up done this well, and when it finally gets to the big pay-off, not only does it deliver, it knocks it out the park!!! it is one of the most edge-of-my-seat thing i seen in a movie in a very long time.

my only 2 minor complaints is it's a bit formulaic, but that isn't bad at all when everything else is constantly knocking it out the park. my 2nd minor complaint was the love interest was just decent, but not bad at all.

this movie is everything what a big blockbuster should be. a huge action movie spectacle that isn't braindead at all like most big action movies. if you love action movies, you'll most likely love this. if you are in the military, you'll way most likely love this! if you like amazing movies, you'll most likely love this movie! i cannot recommend this movie enough! i hope this movie makes a ton of money, because we need more like it.

top gun maverick it was worth it watching it in theatres the action was great. it had it sad moments and funny moments but overall it was great i loved but i have seen the first one... i really recommend watching it you'll love it my rating was 9.3/10.

loved it. lots of homage to the first movie. simple straightforward no bulls**t storyline. but the aerial jet scenes are outstanding..........no cgi flight scenes, absolutely spoiled....wow!! acting is great. big time impressed with the guy playing gooses' son, we'll be seeing a lot more of him. very well put together movie. cast must have enjoyed making this. massive respect to cruise, he helped deliver a thoroughly enjoyable return to top gun, my inner child and older self was blown away. my head was spinning leaving the cinema, action scenes were that real and intense. definitely will have to watch again. a real treat!

the feel of this film is what makes the film exciting to watch . yes some people would complain about being a bit dragged , or a bit slow but i really don't think so as it's an artistic film .

tom cruise again has done a wonderful job as he does things to a superior & unmatched level .

what took me by surprise was how real this movie felt . the footage of aircraft carrier , their training , emotions , relationships, action .

every element of this film looked real & that's what makes the film phenomenal. it's so rare that you get a sequal that measures up well against a blockbuster of how top gun was .

pros: -seeing cruise play maverick again! you can tell he's missed playing the character -the ariel stunts!!! i've never seen anything like it onscreen!

-the new pilots are actually likeable and challenge maverick indifferent ways.

-the val kilmer cameo!

-jon hamm is always a win!

-the training sequences are legitimately intense!

-the entire last 45 minutes of the film are near perfect!!! including a 'death star' style trench run and an entire mini rescue adventure that i wasn't expecting!

-"you told me not to think"-the entire vibe of the film!!!

cons: -i've never been a fan of miles teller and this film didn't change that!

i loved this movie!!! it feels like an 80's film with modern day sensibilities. i honestly didn't think hollywood still had films like this left to deliver. the commitment to the ariel stunts paid off!!! i was blown away by what i was seeing, it was truly astounding! hollywood needs to go back to practical effects in a big way in order to wow audiences again! use cgi when needed but stop using it for every little thing. there's a shot of the jets getting in formation that you can tell was done for real and it honestly gave me chills!!! cruise is clearly having fun playing one of his most famous characters again, he always commits to the theatrical experience and it 100%pays off here! the whole final act of this film kept me on the edge of my seat unlike anything in the last 5 years! i can't recommend this film enough,definitely needs to be seen on the big screen!!! 9/10.

such a massive improvement for a direct sequel i can think of are terminator 2, winter soldier and now top gun maverick. the movie is my favorite of 2022 for sure and one of the best in the last years.

the cgi and particular the practical effects, the stunts, the direction, the pacing, the acting, the action, the tension, the drama, the cinematography, the production values, the writing and most of all the sound mixing and music are all outstanding. to be fair i can't think of a anything bad about the film. the film is a legacy film and it shows. sometimes if the people responsible for the end product care about it and there isn't any studio intervention, then nostalgia can work with good results both commercially and with the critics and viewers. i liked a lot the bond the team developed through out the movie as well as all the other things i mentioned.

this movie and the northman are the only quality movies released this year for me. if you want to watch movies that were crafted with love and care watch these movies. highly recommend!

everyone knows there are only a handful of sequels that buck the trend and improve in quality over their predecessors. 'top gun: maverick' is one of those rare exceptions, as the film that was 35 years in the making delivers in a major way.

maybe it's the nostalgia factor, maybe it's the fact that many scenes feel like they are updated versions of what were in the original (yes, including the cheesy beach football scene). perhaps it's tom cruise back in his element as the (still) capt. pete "maverick" mitchell alongside familiar faces (val kilmer's iceman) and new faces (miles teller and friends), or the high octane subject matter. it could even be the focused, linear storytelling or the powerful soundtrack - who knew hans zimmer and lady gaga could produce something that sounds like this?

sure, the dialogue could be better, with so many lines written just to get cheap laughs. but somehow, it feels authentic and works well in context. and yes, the last third of the movie gets pretty ridiculous, but it's ridiculously cool at the same time. all of this with the celebration of underdogs and a not-so-subtle undertone of patriotism - how can you go wrong?

whatever it is, 'maverick' is the film we need right now.

top gun-maverick did what a lot of others failed to do... be as good as the original or be as good as a remake as the original and meet ir beat expectations... when i was a kid i remember seeing the original in the theater... i'm that guy that knows every line and would annoy you sitting next to you watching it.... maverick was almost as good as the original... story, cast, mix of action, drama, comedy and of course the jet sequences. just intense the movie flew bye and paid great homage to the original. i teared up and can honestly say i the two people on either side of me cried. walking out of the imax everyone was talking how amazing of a movie it was. if iceman and goose weren't in the original and played amazing by val and anthony this would surpass it... so it's a 1b to a 1a.

tom you did it and you make movies enjoyable and i wish there was a fountain of youth because you give the fans everything they want... i know you turn 60 in a few mths so i'll just keep enjoying your art as long as you can do it! you are an amazing entertainer and do it the right way on screen! thank you!

amazing. top gun: maverick builds on everything that made top gun great and delivers an immersive and riveting experience.

top gun is a classic movie for the ages. filled with amazing fighter sequences, bombastic characters and a burgeoning romance.

top gun: maverick takes all these elements and builds on them in a new and fresh take on the topgun program and the top gun film formula.

there's incredible, load, roaring jets dogfighting on the big screen. there's a love interest for our hero. there's that iconic soundtrack containing tracks like danger zone and yes, there's a "volleyball" scene too.

top gun: maverick is simply a must-see.

as a fan of the original top gun, i was thrilled when it was announced there'd be a sequel. the critics were right: thanks to actual flying (no, tom cruise was not allowed to actually fly multimillion dollar government assets!), a wonderful opening scene, excellent writing, and characters with emotional impact, it's much better than the original. i loved how 'real' everything felt, and the fact that the late goose was still very much present throughout the whole film. the scene between maverick and ice made me cry.

i've giving this a 9 out of 10 because of any and all mistakes, errors etc. even though there's no such thing as perfection, this film comes damn close!

top gun maverick is the best movie this year hands down. while it is not perfect, it truly does a grand stand job in allowing you to visualize and see the action in the air.

i can imagine this is why the movie was so popular this year. anyways, we have an atmos system with an oled and this movie really shines as one of the greatest movies for the setup now next to lotr. the immersiveness and feel of the movie is top notch.

overall it beats all other movies this year. for improvement i think the ending could have been more epic if the us fleet had appeared, but maybe they are saving it for top gun maverick: 2.

i don't give 9/10 ratings lightly. if you just want to see a good movie with convincing acting, solid, sensible plot, great cinematography, and suspenseful action, without all the nonsense we get in a lot of movies today, then you'll enjoy this movie.

the things in seeing people complain about is mind boggling..

was there 80's nostalgia? yes, but you can easily forget about it once the plot progresses. some have issue with the military aspect of the film. top gun is about pilots in the navy. so you not expect them to show the military? if you can't enjoy the movie because you're not a fan of tom cruise, then that's a personal problem.

in the end, top gun maverick is one of the best films this year. it made a billion at the box office for a reason. for every complaint you see about this movie, simply ask yourself, "is that issue really something that will make this movie not enjoyable?" you'll find that it's not. this movie was great for all the things it's supposed to be. i wasn't big on the love interest plot, but you know what? the rest of the movie washed it over for me.

top gun: maverick manages to do something that very few movies accomplish in these recent years, and that is to be better than the original movie.

the movie picks up over a decade later than the previous one, maverick is still the military, still putting his pilot skills to use. but as he's reminded of, he's part of a dying breed because one day there won't be any more need for pilots to actually pilot jet fighters. it's a reflection of our real world and how drones are now being used more and more often to carry out missions. however the movie also reminds people that the human factor is not entirely out of rhe picture. and that's where maverick comes in.

given a last opportunity, given all his missed opportunities, he's tasked with training a new generation of pilots to execute a mission that requires pilots piloting real jet fighters, and even then there's no guarantee of success seeing these new generation of cocky pilots just can't cut it. not at their level of knowledge, that is what maverick does. he teaches them what is actually possible to do with a jet fighter.

the movie chose the perfect cast for the job. they didn't tried to hide tom cruise age, if anything his character age and knowledge are what will make the mission even possible to be executable. maverick knows he's made a lot of mistakes, he knows he has missed on a lot, and tom cruise in a particular scene with val kilmer (iceman of the first movie) they perfectly give to the viewer what is easily one of the most emotional scenes not just in this movie, but other movies as well. both maverick and iceman, didn't had the perfect life, but still a life worth living that gave them the perspective their younger selves didn't had. although short, val kilmer participation was crucial so tom cruise character could reveal to the viewer the immense weight that he carries. not just for his decisions but the decisions of others as well.

miles teller perfectly landed his role as bradley "rooster" bradshaw. son of maverick best friend in the first movie goose. the tension between him and maverick is palpable, and both carry a lot of past they need to fix.

monica barbaro was perfect as phoenix. showing she was as good of a pilot as any of her teammates, but above all she could remain cool and focused where her male teammates would many times let egos fly.

overall the cast was well balanced and each one add something to offer and teach the viewer.

although i don't believe in the perfect movie, this one is dam close to being one. it didn't forget who the recurring characters were, while also showing who they had become and why. the movie is well paced, not being too long or too short, it doesn't impose any political messages or agenda on the viewer and stands above all of that. it's fun, it's emotional, it's serious, all in the right amount at the right time. it closes the circle perfectly that began with the first movie, and shows that sequels still can surpass the original movie. something that in these last 5 years, perhaps more, it seemed impossible. given the number of sequels that failed completely to be sequels to the original movies.

this movie is definitely a must see. preferably see the first top gun and immediately jump to top gun: maverick.

i've been a joseph kosinski defender ever since seeing tron: legacy, and it's nice to have some vindication seeing the acclaim top gun: maverick is getting. (i think most kosinski criticism comes from failed wanna-be's, jealous since they never got a big blockbuster thrown into their laps). this is now the second home run for kosinski when it comes to reviving an 80s product, modernizing it while still retaining respect.

i wasn't even necessarily the biggest fan of the original top gun (tony scott is essentially a lower budget michael bay) but it was still decent. and despite tg:m being one of those dreaded 'legacy sequels' we have too many of these days, it can stand on its own cinematic feet without support from the original. (again, much like tron). tom cruise deserves much of the credit here-much like the character maverick he's pushing the actors to their limits, to the point of using real planes for the aerial sequences, and you will certainly be able to tell as the pilots' heads are twisted around and their faces visibly pummeled with the gravitational effect. add that to a story well told and the movie is an unexpected success, confounding the 'movies are dead' streaming simps and illustrating william goldman's iconic summary of the movie business: 'nobody knows anything'.

side note: it's so nice to watch something that doesn't involve actor's heads transplanted on cgi cartoon bodies. the movie still isn't the most terribly realistic, but then neither was the original in some ways.

side note: again, i think kosinski is really the only hollywood heir to innovative greats like robert zmeckis, james cameron- -even george lucas (at least in terms of unique sound design). if you read about tron legacy or oblivion you can find out how both these films were way ahead of the curve technology-wise, and now tg: m shows a similar skill in practical effects. fingers crossed for his upcoming film spiderhead, though that is on netflix and we all know how standards are there.

*actually, james cameron is returning this year with another long-delayed sequel. time will tell if he's still got the goods.

what a movie, i saw it at 13 and loved the original, i never thought a sequel would be a good as the original but it was perfect, i saw it last week in the cinema and just wow, kudos to tom cruise and all who out this together! what a great movie !!!

i did not expect this movie to be so good even after reading some of the reviews. good sure, but how it this good?

lets start with saying this movie was made for tom cruse. with such a legendary career, this was written for him. he is not just the best pilot in this movie, hes leagues above the best. almost impossibly good considering he at his age would probably fall short on the physical compared to the younger pilots. he just slaps!!!

however, for such a honorary pilot, all his higher ranking commanders all talk to him like hes dirt.

jealousy? no.

its clear he does not want to go up any further then he has. so to make this a perfect movie, i think they could have written his commanders to be a little kinder. they could have scripted it in such a way that they are 'only doing their jobs'. protocol dictates we just have to 'do it this way, sorry tom'.

but all in all, look past that and everything else is just about spot on. a must watch!

even as a standalone film this would be excellent but this really does feel like a return to the glory days for hollywood. tom cruise is just fantastic returning as maverick and he's surrounded by a fantastic cast. gripping, funny, touching and with a hint of typical american cheese (no bad thing!). i absolutely loved it - dare i say, more than the first.

this movie was great. this movie has partly redeemed my faith that hollywood has the potential to make good movies. the fact that it used practical effects just proves that modern movies don't need to rely on cgi to do amazing things. thanks tom, this movie was great.

i never saw the original top gun until recently. it was better than i expected but still a pretty standard 80s hollywood movie.

i didn't expect maverick to be much better. i was very pleasantly surprised. this is better than the original and one of tom cruise's best films. the character development really reaches back to the original film and carries through beautifully through the end of this one. cruise's character is much more flawed here - still an amazingly good pilot but not good at much else. he never moved up the ranks and is still a captain. he never got married or had kids. he does have a nice bike but, hey he's had a job all these years so it's no surprise he could afford a nice bike especially since he doesn't even seem to own a house or much of a wardrobe.

the plot here is really great and the special effects actually work in the service of the plot, not the other way around. of course the events lack credibility and the characters have plot armor but that's minimal criticism for a pretty standard hollywood film. if hollywood made more films like this they would be in a much better place. please pay attention to why this film was so successful, hollywood! make good stories about credible, relatable characters that have flaws like real people. don't shoehorn contemporary political messages/ideas into every story -virtually no-one wants that!

thank you, tom cruise for staying true to the purpose of entertainment and telling a great story here.

if you were coming into this film expecting the same cheesy action flick like the first top gun, you would be sorely mistaken. the overall tone and story of top gun maverick is more melancholic and intense than i anticipated. while there are dog fighting and training sequences that are definitely in the realm for a top gun film, the driving force of the story is the conflict between rooster and maverick as they come to terms with the past.¬¬

but damn, the performances given in this film are just phenomenal. cruise possibly gave his best performance ever as maverick! i know right?! he brings maverick's signature cockiness, but matches it with compassion that wasn't present in the first film. miles teller is a fantastic foil to cruise, as well as being a good casting choice since he looks nearly identical to goose's actor, anthony edwards. rooster is the opposite of maverick in every way and the amount of resentment towards his surrogate father figure is both palpable and understandable.

of course it would not be a top gun film without some jet-on-jet action. this not only elevates the action from the first film but it really keeps you on the edge of your seat, putting you in the cockpit with the other actors. before i proceed further, i would like to mention that many of the actors, cruise included, actually flew these fighter jets themselves. these ingenious stunt sequences lead to what i have to say are some of the most realistic and suspenseful sequences i have ever seen! they also lead to some brilliant cinematography as well; beautiful shots of the bright blue sky to the claustrophobic nature of the cockpit. it was something to behold.

top gun maverick is not just a great sequel to a classic 1980s film, but one of the best sequels to ever be produced, arguably up there with terminator 2: judgment day. phenomenal acting by the entire cast, gives tremendous weight to the atmospheric melancholy. and the action sequences are the best of the best, with gorgeous cinematography to help feel the dire and tense nature of a fighter pilot. top gun may have been entertaining with its cheesy popcorn action, but top gun maverick brings more humanity and intensity than the first to make it possibly one of the best films of the year.

my wife and i watched the original top gun for the first time this week. the hype around maverick and the trailers really intrigued me, but i didn't want to see it until i had seen the first one. i have to say, i wasn't all that impressed with the first top gun. it was a bit cheesy and hard to follow in my opinion. however, top gun: maverick is an awesome movie! it was much easier to follow than the first one and had so many more intense scenes. i was on the edge of my seat! usually sequels don't supersede the first installment in a series, but maverick easily surpasses the first one. it's a must watch!

top gun maverick is exactly what you were expecting.

it has it all, from an amazing cast, beautiful planes, a simple yet enjoyable story and amazing action! oh and did i mention the planes?!

just got back from seeing top gun: maverick in imax. what a phenomenal movie! it's not often a sequel (decades later even) can push the needle so far in the right direction. while the original was great, and very 80's, it lacked much of a plot beyond a machismo machine layered around some nice flybys.

the sequel does a great job of keeping the nostalgia to a minimum and to the beginning of the film to establish the players and bring a new audience up to speed. instead of pushing full steam with a retread of the "hey bros, let's go fly some planes to cool music", you get a deeper character development set with diverse characters, and an actual target mission that serves as payoff for all the hard work of the pilots and their backgrounds.

the action was top notch, with plenty of gripping and exciting thrills. i love fighter pilot movies (which there are sadly few modern ones), several times i found myself tense watching close calls. it has so much fun around every corner without relying too hard on the prior movie. prod and happy to see val kilmer come back and get involved as well.

lots of fun and worth many rewatches.

top gun:maverick is based on a true story of duke cunningham and his accomplishments during the vietnam war in the air force. top gun is the highest earning film of 2022.

it is a high energy funny film that also has friendship and romance so mostly anyone can watch it. it is an action movie but it's more about the deep feelings between pilots.

one thing that makes top gun unique is the camera angles and camera movement, the camera is clear and sometimes it's like you're in your own plane which is really cool.

ps this movie is pg-13 so be careful if you take your kids to watch top gun: maverick.

i have been looking for a kind of film with a different plot, a unique one for a very long time. and in this, i found it. i rarely watch aviation related movies nor fighting jets i just dont have an ample interest in those but this!! this changes everything. the best of the best pilots! i love how the chemistry existed between maverick and penny. the two of em just fits so well and boy jennifer connelly really would never let you down.

aside from that, the character roles here of everyone just fits so well especially mav's. he's recklessness if that is really recklessness is just so good. a living legend.

the soundtrack of this film fits so well also!! the way the songs were played each scene fits just right moreover the lyrics! no wonder the popularity and expectations of this film is so high. and yes, here we are very satisfied with the film.

if ever there is a slight cons here, not sure if this is really a cons or i just really dont know how it works tho. one thing i notice is that the way they executed well the miracles and how they pass the coffin corner which they really have difficulty in the training is just quite smooth when it comes to the actual execution. another is that there are almost no casualty, no deaths although the chances are always there especially when they are being chased by missiles and other jets. i dont know i just really expect that only half of them would survive or none in the mission lol.

i grew up watching this film with my dad and was so thrilled to go see it in theatres on father's day with him, and we were not disappointed! when i say this is one of my favourite movies, my dad and i literally know every word, and i'm pleased that this film had enough of its own story as well as nods to the first to make it an exciting walk down memory lane. the premise was great, acting was great, stunts were amazing, well chosen actors, i could go on. i only give it 9/10 for the romance scene with penny benjamin, just a little awkward and goofily filmed. i did like the idea that they pulled this character out of a quick joke in the original and made a loving reunion and happy ending to the film. it was exciting, dramatic, funny, and a great sequel to a beloved film. well done, good to see you back as maverick again cruise!

i thought making a sequel to top gun wasn't a great idea until i saw this. top gun maverick is easily one of the best movies that i've ever seen.

first of all, this movie doesn't make jokes at the expense of it's predecessor, pays tribute to the original in all ways it can , manages to keep the spirit of the original alive and yet surpass all expectations.

it is well written, good acting by all the supporting actors, great background score, beautiful action sequences, great direction and the movie teaches valuable lessons about life.

this will be one of the few movies i watch for a second time.

what more need be said? a blockbuster that doesn't suck and is original? it can be done!

the positive. let me start by saying that that was an amazing theatrical experience. the action scenes made it epic and they were so realistic. it was like i was there. honestly couldn't tell it was green screen or cgi or whatnot.

to see tom cruise on the big screen is always a pleasure. he's mostly known for doing his own stunts, but we mustn't forget what a great actor he is. that counts for the whole cast, everyone was amazing. even the smaller characters had great acting.

the characters, amazingly written. you want to root for these characters. at the same time, they all have some type of pain. some element in their personality or past that doesn't make any of the characters one-dimensional. makes them interesting. they grow, evolve, change.

the story is good and easy to understand. there is a mission. mav has to train the best pilots to prepare them for the mission. they go on the mission. quite easy, but everything that happens in between is integral to the succes or failure of that mission.

the callbacks, the oneliners, the flashbacks, the action,... i can go on but it all just works.

yes, there are some 'negative' elements but don't worry, it's not a lot. as i said the movie is original, but some cliché's still sneak through. some plotpoints happen to make the story fit and in some degree, the story is quite predictable. but that's the hollywood formula right? it's worked for them over the years and it works for them now.

amazing film and a great experience altogether. go see it!

"maverick" had me hooked from start to finish, mainly because it focuses on what really matters - an entertaining and thrilling story.

the movie has a diverse group of characters. however, it doesn't make the societal inequalities that plague many movies nowadays it's focus. these characters are simply competing to be the best, without any underlying context. and it works. i believe this is the reason the movie became a box office success. i am in no way saying that cinema should not deal with societal issues. the problem with modern movies is that they tell you how wrong the society is, completely missing the point of why we go to watch movies in the first place. there are many examples of works made in the past that managed to both tackle serious problems and have a compelling story.

the movie follows maverick as he navigates the challenges of being a flight instructor. it's been 30 years since the original film, and maverick is still haunted by the death of his partner. this serves as a driving force for his character development which adds depth to the action-packed scenes. what's even more great about "maverick" is how it treats its own protagonist. these days it's less common for sequels to honor their main character instead of making them weak or useless. tom cruise brings his signature charisma and intensity to the role once again. the supporting cast also shine in their respective roles.

the fact that they actually filmed the scenes in the actual planes with the actors onboard is mind-blowing. the movie brings back the joy and excitement of films from a different era. it has an exciting yet simple plot, and introduces us to a cast of memorable characters. i hope we get to see more movies like these in the future.

i just walked out of seeing top gun: maverick, and this movie... is amazing! this might be one of the sequels ever made. the visuals, the story, the characters, everything about this movie is a plus! there are no negatives! it does everything right, while being an amazing, airplane pilot story! tom cruise gives it his all in the movie, and you can see that being expressed! maverick is a compelling character with motivations and character development, and it's a perfection arc. the film does a very well job at pacing its story, and not rushing anything while being hella entertaining!

it does a good job at everything, and balances everything super nicely. i'm still unpacking everything i just saw, and am seeing it again this wednesday, i might edit this review and add more positives, or even some negatives! but, as for my out of the theatre review, this movie is a huge win in my book and i found it to be way superior over the first movie, doing everything right!

second viewing: perfection. tom cruise is perfection. the visuals are perfection. the sound quality is perfection. this movie deserves all the success it's getting. get maverick to a billion at the box office

currently at 9/10- subject to change.

containing everything that the original lacked, missing other elements of what came before, and yet a brilliant revisiting with frequent callbacks and references without getting bogged down.

the biggest success in comparison to the original top gun is that the lead characters have a background. they don't just have a personality, but a reasoning as to why they've been shaped that way. maverick is more mature without losing his edge, and rooster is given an effective backstory that goose never had. the rest of the cast less so, but that isn't important and they just fill the gaps.

being dragged into the 21st century, representation is a clear difference. fortunately it doesn't dwell on it, and a character is founded on their abilities rather than their gender, etc. the new roster all play their bit parts well, it's clear who is to be liked and disliked, and they continue the story. even the new love interest is kept vaguely fresh, hinting at a past without dwelling on it. an inventive way to include val kilmer greatly adds to the context of the film too. cruise cannot be faulted, and teller fits in with great chemistry. plus, stick a moustache on him, he really does look like goose.

the plot is exciting, and even though for a large part it is just training, it actually builds to something, something which is seemingly impossible. keeping that interest right up until the mission is a success because the mission itself is gripping. entirely predictable at every step, but that doesn't really matter, as they're all things the audience want to see. the enemy is still non-descript (bad guys only wear boring helmets), but you could make some fairly easy assumptions.

visually it is superb, cockpit scenes in particular have to be applauded. for many productions it would be all too easy to use cgi, however the lack of green screen adds to an excellent aesthetic.

not much of a soundtrack in comparison to its predecessor, plus fewer quotable lines, but plenty of references back to these to create a nice connection. plus, anyone fearing the lack of beach volleyball would be relieved upon watching the beach touch football.

top gun: maverick won't be as iconic as top gun, but it is certainly the superior film.

bathed in the glow of a setting sun every cast member can show of their perfect - and extremely white - teeth and clench their jaws in perfect harmonious tension.

because can this be done? nobody knows. except tom cruise off course.

plot doesn't make sense but who cares.

it's the perfect summer blockbuster with a nice mix of nostalgia and groundbreaking cinematography.

this shouldn't be a surprise to anyone as tom cruise turns in yet another winner. the man just can't lose, and anyone who's been following tom throughout his career knows that tom almost always delivers. why? because he knows a good story, and he also knows what the audience wants.

and i also want to thank tom cruise for insisting that there be no cgi effects for the flying sequences. i don't even want to imagine how this movie would lhave ooked had they used cgi. too many movies these days rely too heavily on them. it was said that after seeing this film, you would feel as though you'd sat in the cockpit yourself. this is no lie.

maverick is back and up to his old tricks. he still isn't the most beloved pilot in the navy. in fact, he's pretty much the opposite. you still have a hotshot pilot who pushes the envelope, both inside and outside of the cockpit.

on the verge of never flying a plane again, maverick is asked to teach the best-of-the-best, to prepare them for an absolutely harrowing mission that requires the best-of-the-best to even have a hope of completing it. if you thought the flying sequences were spectacular in the first one--and they were!--you ain't seen nothing yet! in this regard, at least, the film was not overhyped!

maverick has new trials to deal with: how to teach a new generation of hotshot pilots and get them to act as a team. the mission requires absolute precision. he also has to deal with the fallout with rooster, goose's son. and believe it or not, there's a lot more it than goose's death. and lastly, maverick has to find a way to prove to the top brass that--while he seems like he's asking for the impossible--what he's demanding is actually possible.

the film is wrought with heart, emotion, and inspiration. nothing is over-the-top, and there are even a few curveballs that you probably won't expect.

we also have a good cast of young pilots, with hangman, phoenix (an inspiration to women everywhere!), payback, bob, and fanboy, and coyote. while the first film had more humor than this one, especially the banter between fellow pilots, this one is just as long on men and women dedicated and masters at their craft.

the music of hans zimmer, harold faltermeyer, and lady gaga (who also helped compose the music as well) is certainly memorable and effective. and anyone who fell in love with the original top gun's opening sequence, will certainly not feel cheated or disappointed with this one!

there are just enough references and momentous nods to the original without becoming overloaded or melodramatic. this top gun is telling its own story, and there aren't too many parallels between the first film and this one.

i'm glad it took 36 years for them to get this sequel to us, as long as they did it right. and boy, did they ever do it right! when it comes to films, there is only one bonafide mega-hollywood superstar left. and everyone knows how that is! and he more than delivers once again.

top gun: maverick is an exciting sequel to an 80's classic combining brilliant cinematography, amazing action, an entertaining plot that isn't hard to follow, and excellent performances from everyone. you don't even have to watch the first top gun to enjoy this, so don't worry about watching the first movie beforehand, i didn't and i still loved it. so to put it shortly: give it a watch. i doubt you'll be disappointed.

with the charm of tom cruise and the character, this movie is really enjoyable. no complicated drama, no complicated strategy and action plotting, everything are just so simple to enjoy. well done.

i leave the theater with a big smile and so happy.

where the sequel is better than the original.

it happened with terminator.

it happened with the dark knight.

it happened with logan

it happened with good,bad,ugly.

it happened with top gun.

9/10 i will not spoil anything.

i will encourage everyone to watch the 1986 first.

this movie is a light in trying times.

i have no words to describe this movie. and i believe most of the reviewers don't either. i hope i am not overstepping when i say this movie is the spiritual and, in some ways, superior successor to its predecessor. the fact that most of the plane scenes and stunts were filmed in real life, the cinematography was reminiscing yet breath-taking, the music beautifully composed and the characters engaging and charming; elevates the movie to the stratosphere.

what top gun brought to the 80s when it came out, this movie brings to an updated era (today) that desperately needed this kind of movie. a movie that even though it's one of those "yet another sequel to revive (or start) a franchise", dares to be great. where sequel movies from franchises like terminator, ghostbusters and matrix, fail to relaunch the franchise; this one passes with flying colors and with great action filmmaking to back it up.

the callbacks and soundtrack pushes the emotional moments of the characters forward while establishing new arcs for them in a brilliant concise way. it's not trying to be a deeply layered movie, it delivers a great emotional core and conflict for the main characters while keeping all the flying scenes enthralling and impactful. even more so than on the first one. perceived today as a "love letter" to the 80s movies, top gun was a simple charming blockbuster movie with a very young tom cruise to drive it entirely as he navigates through the parade of archetypical characters and a cheesy (yet endearing) romance. elements i enjoy quite much but which now perhaps wouldn't work for a modern audience. however, this movie makes it work. it plays with archetypes to establish strong emotional connections, relationships and quips that feel charming and amusing.

in conclusion, the movie overall delivers what everyone liked about the original but through an updated lense, new characters; emotional, visual and musical references to the past while building a strong concluding future; and finally and most importantly, while delivering an enthralling and gripping actions stunts and mission very reminiscing of those "impossible missions" of the latest tom cruise involved mi. i went in with no expectations at all and left with a changed heart. i may have forgotten the first top gun, but i for sure would never forget (and probably would revisit) this one. a bombastic, chilling, real-stunt-made, old school blockbuster movie that delivers great action, music and character work. i'm glad to learn i can still be surprised, glad to learn not all old-franchise-reviving-sequels have to be (only) a cash grab.

i'll preface my review by disclosing that i normally dislike action movies. i find them boring, predictable, and catering to the lowest common denominator. i have no interest in watching back and forth gunfire and/or car chases. this however is not your typical action movie, and i was surprised by how much i liked it. good story, well made, well-filmed, no gratuitous violence nor gratuitous sex. yay!!

i may disagree with mr. tom cruise's personal views, but there's no denying he's a very strong actor, and he definitely comes through here, as does the rest of the cast.

i never saw the original, but maverick did a fine job with filling in the missing pieces.

the story develops nicely and logically, and the build-up is steady and gradual. it will obviously please aeronautics fans, but there is also a healthy - but not overboard - dose of drama, sentimentality, and even romance. so ladies if you think this is one to skip, you might just be surprised like i was! there something for everyone here.

i was also pleased by the ending. i don't like depressing endings, nor ones that leave you hanging, and maverick had neither of these issues. i could actually watch this one again. highly recommended!!

likes:

the opening: if you've seen the first film, you remember the excitement of the opening moment as kenny loggins hit song blasted through the speakers and the planes took off into the distance. it was an awesome setup that introduced so much potential at what was to come. nostalgia reigns king, as the opening moment was more than happy to redo the technique and execute it in a flawless performance that get you ready for the adventure at hand. perfect for fans of the original.

the music: the first film was filled with music of the 80s feel, each making a memorable moment in the film that fans replay in their minds over and over again. well, to the most part, the modern day score accomplishes the mission again as they illicit the emotions you want in your sequences. some classic tracks will fill your ears and take you down memory lane, while other tracks are the tracks modern movies dominate on the theater to really make the moment. blasting orchestral works, those power ballads of love, and other moments await the brave pilots seeing this movie and enjoying the moment. fantastic work with the music mr. kosinski and crew.

the acting: no surprise here, the acting has managed to reach great talents that help enlist the right people to make this sequel come to life and blow us away with quality. teller is just as good as he is in almost all his works, capturing the emotions of the moment while also adding his own brand to the character and making it all feel natural. i love him in this very heavy role, and though there was more i wanted to see, i think he delivered the performance incredibly well. jennifer connelly as the leading lady brought stunning performances for me in both the look and feel of the bartender, and an adequate substitute for the original character. the coyness and sass is all there to go toe to toe with maverick's personality, but still has that softer side that makes her realistic and fun. as for maverick, cruise must have never left the role, because he hits the marks on every aspect and it works so well. he's still got the same jokes, the same attitude, and bold nature we love as he tries things that most people would never dream of. and it's all been modernized to the continuing legacy of the famous pilot to once more accomplish the art of storytelling without breaking the character. he pulls everything of maverick from the 80s and evolves it to the times, and in doing so accomplishes much with his character's revival in this story. the rest of the crew accomplishes their parts well as the pilot jockey bunch and much like the past, establishes a niche family that is very military feel. all in all, it accomplished much with the acting for this reviewer.

the realism: at least to most of the extents, top gun keeps its fingers on the pulse of reality in most aspects of the story. like the first film, there are of course stretches to the realism nature of it, but the physics, the repercussions, and the training all feel like something one would find in a top military program. top gun maverick takes the elements of the original again, beefs them up with the visuals and gives you the combat school experience of the top gun program. it was awesome to be back in the 80s with the updated visuals.

visuals: speaking of that, the technology improvements have worked very well for this movie series and have not gone overboard in their use unlike...well most movies. top gun's sequel utilizes the changing military times and incorporates into the movie, while still relying on, for the most part, live action shots to give the authentic feel. it works well for me, makes the movie feel as lifelike as possible and still keeps things feeling very natural with the inclusion of the tech specs.

the story elements: top gun was not just action oriented, the writers accomplished more than just shooting planes down. to accomplish the legacy writing nearly forty years later was a big set of shoes to fill and fortunately, it worked very well for me and my audience group. maverick's tale has evolved and like the acting, combines the old and new together to make that familiar feeling story. the new age group going against the old, the military squabbles between maverick and the top brass, and plenty of history trying to find its place in the character lives. it's a powerful message of the past sometimes getting in the way of the future, and while a little preachy or cheesy to some, it again feels very much like a continuation of the film we saw years ago. it works for the most part, and keeps the movie's pace strong and consistent to make sure all elements we expected were incorporated to a solid degree.

the action: it's nto the most action packed movie in comparison to other films in the modern day, but it again works to keep to the physics they establish, the characters, and provide the whoo factor you want in a movie. maverick's opening flight gives you an idea of what is to come, and once the training is underway thing ramp up and go back to the familiar plane fighting antics you want. that's the beauty of the new technology and the modern abilities helping to ramp things up and give you the new age visuals. however, the ability to curtail that action into the story, is impressive and almost every scene feels needed, is necessary, and does not stray too far from the flight path in terms of fake abilities and breaking the world.

the top gun feel: the most powerful part for me on this movie, is the respect they had for the series and never leaving that top gun feeling. it's a tough market to respect the foundation and evolve the story, and i know not everyone will like it. however, compared to so many franchises this day, maverick really does achieve the balance for me and managed to take the energy of the original movie, advance it somewhat, and yet not make it something completely different. that to me was a powerful source of enjoyment for this movie and it accomplishes much.

dislikes:

predictable: for viewers like me, who have seen way too many movies, there aren't too many twists and turns to surprise you in this film. i had most of the big moments down and the foreshadowing is not gentle in the means of what they have planned. it is blunted by a little ambiguity and promise, but for the most part, you'll know what is coming.

more time with female lead: the first movie did a great job incorporating the romance aspects of the pilots and the flirting we sometimes saw between the leads. this movie does well, don't get me wrong, but i think there was more and better moments that could have incorporated her into the life versus what we got. these moments felt a little more shoehorned than other moments.

the main mission/timeline: you got to give them props on adding some suspense and consequences to the mix. however, this timeline also is a limiting factor and sort of speeds up and rushes through some things that i think we did not need rushed. i laughed at how convenient things were, or the stretches they made in the story that flies into hollywood magic territory. in putting this, hard timeline, some of the realism got stretched and did not have the natural flow that the first movie did. throw in how much they copied from another famous moment and you'll see the cheese factor come in a little for this movie.

the character usage: impressive in some point, but also weak, the characters of this flight squad are a little disproportionate given the terms of the story. understanding a graduating class vs. the elite being pulled in are two different circumstances in my opinion and that means understanding when to use your characters to better degrees. while the secondary roles are decent, there are some inclusions that held little use and thus made me wonder why we needed 12 instead of a lower number with more focus on them. this is blunted by good use of the other characters, but again why make a big deal in the opening mission montage.

the interruption of the last scene: i can't say much due to spoilers, but there is a moment in the final sequences that feels out of place. though very funny and has some of the most humorous engagement, the last part of the mission feels a little more mission impossible/great escape, than top gun. while in the end they get this tangent to loop back in, it still was the part that was just not fitting in the rest of the montage, even though it has some of that emotional justification. again, a bit nitpicky, but something that gets me given how the rest of the movie flows.

the verdict: top gun maverick is a mission success in my book, in that it handled the big expectations quite well for me. it's top gun with a new paint in some degree, but it takes the elements of the 80s and modernizes it well a few liberties are taking, but the action, dynamics, characters, and story all feel like an extension of top gun with the time that has passed. certainly, the character usage is not the best at times, and the timeline makes for a hurried and conventional skill set, but otherwise this movie did much better than i had anticipated. for something that could have crashed, tom cruise and the squad managed to balance old and new to levels i hoped we would see and made this soar. thus, for this reviewer, i do encourage a theater visit to get back into the legacy, and hope you enjoy it as much as i did. for those who want a score though, here they are:

a sequel to "top gun" has been teased for at least a decade and was even meant to come out in 2019 but got delayed further until 2022. now that the sequel has finally landed, was it worth the wait? i'd say the answer is a resounding yes.

tom cruise returns as pete "maverick" mitchell and assumes the role of flying instructor at his former academy, topgun, where he has to train the next generation of jet pilot recruits for an impossible mission. can maverick train the new recruits to complete the mission successfully and make it safely back home? that remains to be seen.

as a sequel to "top gun", "top gun: maverick" packs an emotional punch along with plenty of tense moments to keep the audience on the edge of their seats where the flying sequences and sound effects alone make the film worth seeing in theaters. the action is great but there are also heartfelt moments involving maverick's relationship to characters and events from the first movie, including the tragic loss of his wingman goose. although not many cast members from the original "top gun" reprise their roles in the sequel, val kilmer returns in a supporting role as iceman and even though his cameo in the sequel is relatively minor, you can still feel iceman and maverick's strong bond from the original movie which further adds to the sequel's emotional core.

overall, "top gun: maverick" is a fantastic sequel that retains the coolness factor of the original as well as delivering an emotional impact which makes it a sequel well worth the long wait.

it's a tom cruise top gun film and it delivers exactly what you expect, and exactly what you want.

reprising his role as maverick, tom cruise is ordered back to the top gun school by admiral 'iceman' (a short cameo from an ailing val kilmer) to train the current generation of super pilots for a near mission impossible. dramatic tension is inevitable with one of the pilots, rooster bradshaw being son of goose, maverick's wing man in the iconic 1986 film of which this is the sequel.

the plot is completely derivative and predictable, the characters two dimensional. but you know that before the film begins. don't whinge about it.

the flight photography is constantly stupendous and never confusing; the story rips along, very well paced by director joseph kosinski. there's a few meta jokes pertaining to the first film, again as you'd expect, and the soundtrack is superb.

the film's main flaw, such as it is, is its casting imbalance. tom cruise dominates throughout; with one notable exception toward the end, none of the supporting cast ever really get a chance to shine. i guess this is near inevitable, however, when you're one of the greatest film stars of all time and also the film's producer. no different to hamlet though.

this is a beltingly good action movie which will disappoint very few who enjoy this genre of film. and who doesn't?

excellent sequel. many references to the original top gun, to the point it felt excessive, but the story was unique enough for an entertaining watch.

the plot is coherent, as long as you accept what you're told by the filmmakers without questioning it too much. fortunately you're not spoonfed every basic detail, but the constant narration during the flight scenes seemed unrealistic. the last act felt like an entire bonus.

the movie focuses on maverick, but all the actors were excellent.

excellent visuals and audio, even if the computer graphics were overstylized. the music was mostly a nod to the original score.

after a few years of less than remarkable movie releases, watching top gun: maverick feels like you finally get to eat cake and ice cream on your cheat day after decades of chewing on bland chicken and broccoli. this movie spoils the audience in more ways than one: the abundance of fantastic cinematography, perfect use of tension, and stellar actor performances; which all culminate in a satisfying tie up to the story of maverick.

i remember watching the original top gun and having a few moments where my attention would go elsewhere and my eyes wandered from the screen. this did not happen once during this movie. even while following a somewhat predictable plot structure, top gun: maverick never fails to capture your immersion from the first minute. additionally, a few lines of dialogue in the movie felt cheesy just from reading the subtitles, but the actors involved really sold these lines to make it all but imperceptible.

writers for this movie understood our protagonist and what makes him click with the audience, and were able to incorporate this into the story masterfully. unfortunately this cannot be said for the vast majority of tv shows and movies regurgitated by mainstream media today.

while the tony scott original is hard to beat in terms of character development and story this sequel triumphs in it's cinematic spectacle and action.

i was legit stunned for most of the movie and i don't usually rate movies this high. the story was really good (aside from just a couple of scenes that weren't really needed in my opinion, like the bar scenes and the scene where bradley and maverick meet up in the forest after they both get shot down), the cinematography and action were flawless and filled with risky sequences, the performances were done well, and the real actual fighter jet flying that all of the main crew had to do was impressive to say the least! this movie is much more memorable and higher quality than the first movie yet the movie had some good 80s feeling to it as well! i wish i saw this in theaters, tom cruise blows the audience away yet again!

come on, mav. don't think. just do.

now that's a dangerous advice, but it's an advice that produced an amazing thriller. i'm not exaggerating when i say that maverick is probably the best action thriller of this year.

after the opening scene, i knew that i'm gonna get some amazing cinematography. the shots at the beginning are definitely going to be on my wallpaper lists. i loved how the beautiful blue color made it look like tom cruise was traveling in space. it was magnificent.

in the first movie, the training arc was annoying for me because of the choppy editing and confusing technicality. maverick improved on this significantly. i had so much fun watching tom cruise trashing on the graduates. the editing was clear and actually helped making the training thrilling and enjoyable.

another reason was maverick had that the first didn't have: a clear direction. maverick set up a destination that was high-stake that made me invested in the training of the characters. the border between life and death was clear.

the third arc was where the intensity was at the highest. a large part was due to the great set up from the training arc. i was so invested to a point that i became emotional. oh man it was so goddamn amazing and thrilling.

now with a host of new characters, it's obvious that some will be focused more than the others. i think the movie did a decent job balancing all the characters, although i would like to see the other less important characters shine more.

one way was to have the training arc longer. at one point i looked at the time on my phone and was surprised that 1.5 hours had already passed. i felt such good vibes from these characters that the movie went by fast. at that point i wanted to watch another 1.5 hours of this movie.

the romance improved from the first. it was a lot sweeter, but i still had the same problem of not having as much significance as i wanted.

there were important moments that happened to the old characters that returned from the first. this didn't hold as much weight as i wanted to mostly because of the first movie's fault for not setting up the characters that well.

overall, i had a blast and will for sure watch it again. this time it will be in imax. can't wait to be blown away again. 9/10.

this movie takes a simple idea of mentorship to the max. this film deserves all the praise for being an excellent movie and an incredible sequel. in the art of filmmaking, execution is critical in keeping the audience hooked, and maverick successfully did it from start to finish. there are three things the movie successfully executed, its visuals, characters, and nostalgia.

first, the visuals; maverick made sure to make this one of the coolest movies ever. they ensured all their jet scenes were top-of-the-line, from actual footage of real-life jets to excellent compositing of digital planes. the movie makes you believe you are watching a real-life mission. this movie is stunning, even the shots without the aircraft. the scenes on the beach can signify good times, like when the pilots play football, or uncertainty and sadness when maverick tells penny he's going on a mission. props to the director for keeping the visuals consistent throughout the film's entire runtime.

second, the characters; this movie makes sure to highlight essential characters but give secondary characters their distinct characterization, signifying their justification for being part of the movie. i'll mention one example, the pilots. the first film only characterizes the important pilots, while the rest are just not doing anything. but maverick makes all the pilots important by first showing them their nicknames and the goal of picking the best of the best. although the pool scene shows the main pilots that the film will highlight, the rest of the pilots aren't just useless bags of nobody. they play a role in the story, and although minor, they mark themselves as actual characters in the story.

last but not least is nostalgia; this entire film is built upon one factor of the previous movie. that maverick's old partner, goose, died; in this movie, he's dealing with the conflict he has with goose's only son, rooster. this idea is the core conflict of the film. there may be an evil army, but the movie is more about the conflict of a family that isn't by blood. the movie also builds up legacy characters. in the first movie, we see maverick as the cockiest pilot, but in this movie, we see him still cocky, but time has made him wiser and more meticulous. even iceman was essential for maverick's arc and the arc of the audience that people may come and go, but what's important is what they left behind.

and in that sense, maverick has left behind a symbol where sequels of old franchises can work if it is built upon execution. my only issue with this movie is the lack of expounding of the pilots finally being as a team and hangman's arc. this movie may not be perfect as a solo film, but it's an excellent sequel. where audiences old and new can connect and embrace movies that can bring out the youth of everyone by being awesome and profound at the same time. it shows hollywood can make good blockbusters if the right people are placed.

just to make this perfectly clear for everybody: the plot is not about aviation. it's about teamwork in a competetive environment, heavily focussed on mind-over-matter. the planes are there for the drama and for the action, not for realism of any kind. this is not a documentary and it doesn't care about realism - which is a good thing, because the movie wouldn't be thrilling at all if that were the case.

the mission is suicidal, the training illegal and the behaviour of maverick would've caused him to be in prison or shot down by the military for not listening to anybody and violating basically all laws of aviation and the navy. nothing is correct concerning military regulations, piloting rules, aviation physics, weapon systems, you name it. and it doesn't matter at all.

fans will like the movie for the same reasons as the first one: planes are beautiful and exciting and we all believe in maverick, a hotshot who breaks the rules (and laws of physics) to get the job done where nobody else can.

that being said, even if you like your movies to be realstic, watch it anyways. the aviation scenes alone are worth the visit.
