in an age filled with movies relying overly on computer generated imagery, it is refreshing to see a film that primarily utilizes practical effects to achieve even the most difficult of sequences, and the approach has clearly paid off. with top gun: maverick, tom cruise and joseph kasinski delivers a thoroughly engaging, riveting and emotionally impactful sequel to a classic blockbuster, while simultaneously managing to improve upon the original in every possible way.

there is perhaps no other actor other than tom cruise who has managed to consistently maintain the same level of global stardom and public relevance for over four decades. nearly 35 years later, cruise returns to his iconic role of pete "maverick" mitchell, the role that solidified his global stardom. cruise once again showcases his acting talents and his unparalleled dedication to the craft as he along with other cast members, perform complex and difficult flight/aerial combat sequences that is all done practically by the actors themselves, with little to no usage of cgi. the rigorous flight training undergone by cruise and the other cast members totally paid off, as all the aerial sequences, particularly the entire third act, forms the strongest aspect of the film. the dogfight sequences are quite possibly the best ever put to film and are constantly engaging and thrilling and keeps you at the edge of your seats throughout, due to realistic and accurate portrayal of them.

another strong aspect of the movie was its emotional weight. the film has numerous callbacks and homages to the original film that manages to tug at your heartstrings particularly for long-time fans of the original film, as they manage to evoke a sense of nostalgia in them. however none of these come across as cheap nostalgia-bait or fan service, which has become common in many new hollywood blockbusters. instead, these are perfectly incorporated with the story and are even necessary for the development of maverick's character. the impact of goose's death in the first film is present throughout this film and the effect the event had on maverick was perfectly portrayed. maverick trying to be a surrogate father to goose's son, played by miles teller and his subsequent relationship with him, forms the emotional center and the true heart of the movie. val kilmer's return as tom "iceman" kazansky was a truly delightful inclusion and resulted in one of the most emotionally powerful moments in the film.

the cinematography by claudio miranda was another noteworthy aspect as the film is filled with gorgeous visuals. the sequences are made even more powerful by the exceptional music composed by harold faltermeyer and hans zimmer. may it be a heart to heart exchange between two characters or an intense dogfight sequence, the music always manages to perfectly fit and elevate the impact of the sequences.

with exceptionally crafted aerial combat sequences, beautiful cinematography, emotional weight, nostalgic callbacks and a spectacular central performance by tom cruise, top gun: maverick succeeds at being one of the best legacy sequels ever made along with the likes of mad max: fury road and blade runner 2049, while simultaneously paying respect to the original film and further solidifying cruise's unrivalled starpower.

"top gun: maverick" is the sequel to the 1986 action drama film "top gun". directed by joseph kosinski ("tron: legacy", "oblivion", "only the brave") and starring tom cruise, val kilmer, and miles teller, it exceeds the original film in every way possible by delivering a follow-up worthy of being considered one of the best sequels ever made.

thirty-six years after the events of the first film, pilot pete "maverick" mitchell (tom cruise) still remains in the rank of captain due to him intentionally avoiding promotion, which would result in him being grounded. under the orders of his friend and former rival tom "iceman" kazansky (val kilmer), maverick is given the job of training a group of newly graduated members of the "top gun" program to undertake a dangerous mission. upon meeting the young pilots for the first time, maverick notices that one of them is bradley "rooster" bradshaw (miles teller), the son of his deceased best friend "goose" (anthony edwards). in spite of the initial tension he has between rooster and the rest of the pilots, maverick eventually earns their respect in the air as a skilled tactician capable of leading them through enemy lines.

if you are ever required to name movies that define high-octane 80s action to a tee, i'm sure "top gun" would be fairly high on many people's lists. this is because it was able to appeal to virtually all audiences, with some great fighter jet stunts for the guys and a love story for the girls. though the film was far from perfect, it managed to blend all of these tropes together so harmoniously that it rightfully cemented its status as a part of pop culture. i think roger ebert summed it up best by saying that "...the good parts are so good and the bad parts are so relentless". this belated sequel, which was 36 years in the making, is so entertaining that to merely call it better than the original would be a huge understatement.

what i think separates this film from other sequels that capitalise on nostalgia was its ability to stand on its own without too much reliance on the original. in the first film, the plot was simple enough to follow that you could basically ignore most of the dialogue and watch everything unfold through its groundbreaking action sequences. later, things would be counteracted with some cringe-inducing 80s clichés like the soundtrack blaring loud synth rock over a love scene between two characters. here, the film keeps its 80s roots to a minimum by presenting a more modern look at how much naval technology has advanced over the past three decades.

one scene in particular shows maverick flying his old fighter jet, complete with all the archaic bells and whistles, alongside the high tech present-day jets piloted by the younger crowd. despite being a technical dinosaur by today's standards, maverick is able to manoeuvre his jet through the air with relative ease, showing these young folk that he is still a force to be reckoned with. in most sequels that feature an older version of the original protagonist, we tend to see them in a more vulnerable state, where they would believe they're in danger of being bested by the current youth. here, on the other hand, maverick is still just as confident and level-headed as he was in the first film, which is a refreshing change from that old formula. it's almost feels as though he's been in suspended animation over the past few decades and has now been thawed out for our own enjoyment.

taking over from the late tony scott, joseph kosinski steps into the director's chair to deliver a workmanlike, streamlined film that will make any doubters realise that this is a sequel we never knew we needed. as previously mentioned, the film doesn't play too much into the audience's assumed nostalgia for the original but it has just enough of it to remind us of its overall significance. like "tron: legacy", another belated sequel directed by kosinski, there are enough flashback scenes and minor easter eggs to spark the memories of fans of the original while simultaneously informing newcomers of any back story they need to know. with that said, it isn't entirely necessary to have seen the original to understand the full scope of the sequel's story, except for one major thing.

in order to fully grasp the importance of maverick taking rooster under his wing (pun very much intended), you need to be familiar with maverick's close friendship with goose in the first film. since rooster is goose's son, the audience needs to know why maverick is so insistent on ensuring his safety. the use of selected flashbacks to remind viewers of how close the two were would have been very helpful here, not just for the uninitiated but older fans as well. unfortunately, the film only briefly glances over this, so some of the emotional impact will be lost on anyone who hasn't seen the original. aside from that, everything else in the film is conveyed very effectively, especially with how maverick is able to have remained such a skilled pilot after so many years.

i'm sure many will agree that one of the best things about the original film was its brilliantly shot dogfights. even today, they still stand out as some of the best choreographed, best edited aircraft combat scenes in cinematic history. but if you thought it would be impossible to outdo such exhilarating moments all these years later, you'd be dead wrong. this film takes what made each of those scenes so memorable in the first place and triples their entertainment value. the third act alone is one of the most exciting, nail-biting climaxes i've seen in recent memory. planes pass through beside one another and flip upside-down with such jaw-dropping precision that you'd swear it was done through cgi. but no, according to some research, there's not a single bit of cgi used during these flight scenes. instead, it is all real manoeuvrability pulled off by highly skilled pilots coupled with an equally skilled cinematographer. and best of all, there isn't any use of shaky cam to ruin the whole experience. reportedly, these creative decisions were made at tom cruise's insistence so we have him to thank for that.

even after more than three decades, tom cruise is more than capable of delivering another exciting performance here that, like everything else in this film, is better than the original. his take on an older maverick is quite satisfying to watch, showing that despite the whole world changing around him, he has remained true to himself throughout even the worst of times. it amazes me that this man is almost in his 60s but can still hold his own both physically and mentally alongside much younger cast members. regardless of what you may think of his personal life, you've got to hand it to someone this committed to giving the audience exactly what they want.

i also liked miles teller as rooster, the young and ambitious son of maverick's late best friend goose. when he was first introduced, i half expected him to be arrogant and unlikeable given the hostility some of his fellow pilots initially show towards maverick, but for the most part he tries to remain respectful. as the movie progresses, you really get the sense that maverick and rooster are forming a surrogate father/son bond, which makes their interactions so much more interesting. without giving away spoilers, the film's final act makes great use of their teamwork, especially when things seem at their lowest point.

in this growing age of nostalgia-based sequels, it is a pleasant surprise to see one that not only eclipses the original in mere entertainment value but also redeems it of some of its faults. many years from now, people will look back on "top gun: maverick" as a textbook example on how to do a sequel right, from the action scenes to the character motivations. companies like disney should take note because there's a difference between expanding upon an old story and milking a dormant franchise until it's completely dry. i can't help but wonder if there will be more belated 80s film sequels to look forward to in the future, because this one has truly taken my breath away. regardless, i'd say things are looking pretty good.

i rate it a solid 9/10.

to be honest, i only thought this was an 8 at best. i knocked off 1 for the star wars plot and one for the layers of cheese in the movie.

i'll admit that i had my reservations about them making a sequel to top gun, but top gun: maverick delivers the same thrills the original did, along with improved & highly impressive aerial action sequences. the story is fairly standard, yet that's part of what makes it great, as it feels like a throwback to the summer popcorn flicks of the 80s. i don't think top gun: maverick is as iconic as the first movie, but i do think it's the best possible wingman for top gun.

with it's enduring popularity and influence in pop culture, i always wondered why they never churned out a sequel to top gun. after reading a little bit about the behind the scenes of this movie, some of it had to do with tom cruise's dissatisfaction of how the original top gun was shot. i walked into the theatre hoping for some eye-popping and thrilling stunt sequences and maverick certainly delivered on that front. the action was breathtaking to see on the theatre screen, leave it to cruise and his team to bring some juice to the acrobatics to help re-invigorate the franchise for modern audiences. i can't speak to the technical specifications or how much of the movie is accurate to real life but nothing felt outlandish enough to shatter the illusion of the movie. the dogfighting and aerial manoeuvring will have you dipping and dodging in your seat and top gun: maverick and even if you're not familiar with the previous film, it will keep you engaged while you get to know the characters.

transitioning to the character, we join pete "maverick" mitchell at the tail end of his career. he's satisfied with his current assignment (he's working as a test pilot) but he's still haunted by the events of the first movie. over the course of the movie, he has to confront both his past demons and his career arc when he's ordered to start training pilots at top gun again. val kilmer also returns as tom "iceman" kozansky, who has been acting as maverick's shield, keeping him in the navy after all of his shenanigans. while tg: maverick is very romantic when calling back to the original, the returning characters all were treated with care and their arcs feel organic from where the first one finishes. i also really enjoyed most of the new characters; phoenix, bob, hangman, payback, coyote and fanboy all are distinct and fun characters to watch develop. rooster's conflict with maverick is earned considering what's transpired between them. the only character i had a problem with was cyclone who is just very one dimensional as the disapproving chief that's always on maverick's case.

tom cruise is a complete enigma off the screen but you can count on him to bring his 'a' game whenever he's starring in a big action movie (other than the mummy..... but let's not talk about that). he's great as maverick again, he nails both the "wild card" nature of him flying but also the emotionally conflicted man off the tarmac. i was pleasantly surprised by both jennifer connelly and her character of penny. penny looked like a throwaway love interest for pete in the trailer but connelly is so smooth and at ease in penny's shoes and she is every bit as good as cruise (although in a smaller role). miles teller is up to the task as rooster, i haven't always been his biggest fan but he gives an intense performance with a couple of moments where he's allowed to be charasmatic. it was nice to see val kilmer again as iceman, they do their best to fit him in with his limitations (he is almost unable to speak now) but his character's relationship punctuates maverick's need to grow so well that i couldn't imagine the movie without him. jon hamm is fine in the movie, his character was problematic but that's not the fault of his performance. bashir salahuddin, monica barbaro and lewis pullman were the standouts for me in the new supporting players but the entire cast performed capably and nobody stuck out as being off key with their acting.

if there's any fault to find in top gun: maverick, it's that the movie is so jam packed with nostalgia and love for the original film. if you're a top gun superfan, this will be a positive as most of the call backs are done in an almost sweet way. but if you're part of the uninitiated, it could be a little grating. the sentimental/cheesy slant of the first one has carried over as well and one of the friends i saw this with was rolling her eyes consistently. i think the movie walks a fine line without being too corny but perhaps not everyone will feel that way. my last nitpick is that tg: maverick can't seem to decide when it wants to wrap up, i thought the movie was steering towards wrapping up at least a couple of times but it just kept going.

i was so pleased when i saw the box office numbers later in the same week for top gun: maverick. it's a throwback that borders on too sentimental but with the awesome action set pieces, solid acting and good enough story about letting go of your past and learning to live with your demons, it's going to make my list of my favourite theatre experiences this year. if you haven't seen it already and are interested in a more old-school action blockbuster, this isn't your standard entry in the genre, it's exceptional and well worth your time.

the hype has been around for this ever since it came out. the only film from 2022 to stay in the imdb top 250 at the end of the year.

great film.

despite a pretty good trailer, i really didn't have high hopes for this. i wasn't a massive fan of the first one, even though it's a classic and has a huge fanbase. the story, writing, and acting felt cheesy and very hollywood. i had a good feeling about this one when the music starts playing over the opening and the "danger zone" song comes on during the aircraft carrier scenes. the actor names appearing in sync with the music was a nice touch. the writing is a lot more mature - no cheesy lines, dance routines, or childish acts on the part of any of the characters - making you a lot more invested in the movie. the history of maverick, rooster's son, and connelly's character was introduced slowly and nicely, and the reasoning behind each character's motives are rational and well-done. the humour was light and appropriate, done at the right moments. flight sequences were amazing - real, engaging, and accented the story instead of making the whole movie just about random plane scenes. the build-up to the end mission was well-done, and you really felt the stakes (i honestly didn't know what would happen). nice aircraft all around. i'm not a pilot or plane fanatic, but there were some nice jets, both old and new. the conflict between the new era of ai and old-school fighter pilots was an interesting touch to the story, and also helps ground the movie, since those issues are very much at the forefront of future air warfare today. overall, an extremely well-done movie, great music, mature storytelling, and surprisingly, one of those sequels that's definitely better than the first.

had to write my review immediately. what a film , the kind of film you always hope you're going to see at the cinema but very rarely do .

now that's what you call a perfect movie. the casting, music, dialogues, action scenes, storyline, acting, direction each and every component just fits perfectly in this art called top gun maverick. soul touching creation for all the tom cruise and top gun fans out there. the experience is further enhanced if you watch this in theatre. spine chilling and refreshing. beautifully crafted piece worth watching, especially in theatres for sure.

everything every man wants to be. the hero gets the girl does not come close to describe this cinematic masterpiece. if you can't be the hero navel aviator top gun maverick lets you live vicariously through maverick, rooster, ice, honda, cyclon, warlock, phoenix, fanboy, and of course every man's crush penny. tom's attention to detail, the cinematography, even the mission was authentic and never done before. bravo mr. cruise of should i say maverick for a sequel well worth the wait. most men would never get be a hero naval aviator but we all got to live it with this excellent film. great soundtrack as well. best action movie in a decade.

i like the original top gun, but there was still room for improvement. top gun: maverick keeps everything good about the original and fixes pretty much all of its problems. it's still cool, occasionally homoerotic and full of stunning flying, but now with a clearer goal and action scenes that can actually be followed.

it takes the original's emotional core (maverick's friendship with goose and his relationship with iceman) and develops it in extemely moving and satisfying ways, not only making for a great watch, but also making me appreciate the original a lot more.

the original top gun was a true classic. it oozed cool, had great camerawork and characters, and featured real f-14s. top gun: maverick is that movie, but better in every way.

the camerawork is easily some of the best in modern cinema, nearly all of the effects are practical (there's little to no cgi), and the f-18s are badass. cruise made the cast go through a 3-month boot camp so that they could actually be in the f-18s for the scenes. it's that dedication to creating the most real, visceral experience of piloting a fighter jet that makes this movie shine. the plot is more than serviceable and the payoff at the end is awesome. this movie has raised the bar on practical effects, and shown that cgi is not the only answer these days. then there's the more lowkey stuff...

the volatile relationship between maverick and rooster evolves organically throughout the film in a way that keeps you emotionally invested.

there are numerous callbacks to the original film, most of which are wonderfully executed.

all in all, this is a great summer blockbuster and one of the coolest movies you'll have seen in a while. tom cruise has done it again!

it's very possible this movie is better than the original. tom cruise is one of the last few true superstars in hollywood. his energy, passion and charisma shine in this film. i don't believe another actor can bring all of those things to the degree that he can.

it's refreshing to see a movie without the typical woke garbage that hollywood normally produces. maybe they can learn and make more movies like this.

looking forward to watching this again!

top gun: maverick. thoughts...

more than an ode to (military) aviation, it is an ode to cinema. to classic nineties & noughties movies that us millennials & younger gen-xs grew up on.

makes sense, because it was made by that generation's action god jerry bruckheimer.

(on the topic of bruckheimer: the use of the who's "won't get fooled again" in the first dogfight training scene was an exquisite tribute to another one of his wildly popular shows csi: miami.)

being crafted using classic nineties/noughties action formulae, top gun had its fair.

share of cringe. but what makes it stand out as an exceptional piece is that cruise & bruckheimer used the crème de la crème of world cinema.

look at the filmography of the film's producers and you'll see what i mean...

editing: kingsman production design: zero dark thirty art direction: grand budapest hotel casting (immense cast): saving private ryan

and the primary feature of the film...

cinematography: benjamin button & life of pi.

it's writing let it down. dialogue was weak and kitsch, with a painfully thin plot. but that's expected for bruckheimer (never my favourite movie producer).

if decent effort had been invested into the screenplay, this could have been a masterpiece. instead, it was outstanding.

a cinematic marvel. right up there with some of the best cinematography to grace the big screen (think revenant, tree of life, avatar, blade runner, 2001, psycho etc.)

it's unfortunate that such a marvel couldn't be served a better script.

but what do bruckheimer & cruise care?

they don't. it's done its job. it is one of the most successful films of all time, and deservedly so.

but for those who appreciate a little more than just eyegasmic experiences and seek provocative inspiration, it let itself down. and for that reason, there is not a chance.

it will be nominated for a best picture oscar.

cinematography? highly likely. along with all of the other disciplines i listed above. heck, even cruise might get a nomination for his intense military training for the film.

when it comes to acting, the overall cast was, as mentioned, immense. besides john hamm (or perhaps his character?) letting the whole team down, the acting was extremely solid, with jennifer connelly absolutely stealing the show.

this was a movie that i would gladly see again in the cinema.

in a world overrun by miniature screens, top gun: maverick reminds us that the big screen remains an important part of our cultural heritage.

as maverick returns to top gun, now as an instructor rather than an active fighter pilot, he must equip a group of the country's best pilots for an important, yet practically suicidal, task. he is forced to confront past traumas and make decisions bigger than himself. all the while proving to everyone yet again that "it's not the plane, it's the pilot."

"top gun: maverick" did something i have never seen. kosinski and the entire cast took an iconic 1980's film and molded it into an equally iconic film for the next generation to enjoy. so many have tried: rambo, terminator, ghostbusters, jurassic park, and even star wars (just to name a few) but they have each failed miserably and their only legacy is mediocrity. everyone of these films has featured their same cast yet outdated, their same plot yet watered down, and their same idea yet clearly forced into a film that never should of been produced.

however, "top gun: maverick" did not fail. it exceeded; it entertained. it successfully brought the original "top gun" into the 21st century. it has you pumping your fists and cheering for the characters because you grow to love them so dang much. it honors the original film while also making a name for itself. it features original characters while also bringing relevant, fresh personalities onto the scene. it has an original, captivating plot that leaves the audience crying, laughing, and applauding. it is thrill-seeking, fast, epic, and intense, but also underneath, it is soft, sentimental, tear-jerking, and authentic.

watch it! soak in the high flying jets, the leather jackets, and the rad sunglasses. "top gun: maverick" is what cinema is all about.

i honestly didn't care about going to see this movie but i had forgotten how much i loved the original. i absolutely loved that they played so much of the music that was in the original. it took me right back to 1986. i only wish i had watched the first one again before going to see maverick just to refresh my memory. i loved it none the less. i just sat and enjoyed it without trying to pick it apart. just go see it. if you were young when the original came out, you'll see what i mean about the nostalgia. get it whenever you can. it'll keep you young at heart.

there a few movies that i award with the designation "experience". this amazing film definitely deserves it. i recommend seeing it in the cinemas. i had the privilege of seeing it in a dolby cinema, which heightened the experience.

i moderately liked the first movie. the trailers and use of real planes excited me. and i was blown away. i knew from the nostalgic and nerve-wracking opening sequence that this was going to be an enjoyable ride.

the practical, realistic visuals are breathtaking, as they are the product of technical wizardry. the flight sequences are some of the best action sequences i have ever seen. they were genuinely exciting. the high-stakes third act is memorable. there are also numerous shots that are aesthetic.

cruise is great and his commitment, as always is unparalleled. he is, as milles teller said, a "movie-making machine". truly a unique personality. trough his movies, he underlines humanities sense of perseverance.

on the story and character level, furthermore, the movie also does a perfectly solid job, as it is engaging. from sadness to laughter, it generates a lot of emotions, a signal of its quality. the dynamics are authentic and delightful. val kilmer presence was noteworthy.

finally, the inherent apolitical nature of the film is greatly appreciated. the fact that they did not choose to replace the taiwanese flag to appease to chinese audience put a considerable smile on my face.

in conclusion an exciting, joyous and tremendously well-done film that qualitatively and quantitively surpasses its predecessor.

a true movie.

i loved it.

i only went to see this film as last minute plans with 2 friends, i'd never seen the original top gun and had to have the story explained to me during the car journey to the cinema.

i walked in the theatre with low expectations but can safely say it's one of the best films i've seen in a long time and i'm very picky, particular and critical of movies.

it was corny and cheesy but in the right ways - great action sequences where you're genuinely on the edge of your seat, great storyline, acting was brilliant and character developments i actually felt invested in. even a few comic relief parts were corny but it suited the vibe of the film (i'm looking at you disney star wars). you didn't necessarily need to have seen the original because top gun maverick sets the movie up in a way that explains what happened previously but could have easily been a stand alone film because it goes in its own direction.

9/10, loved it!

we all know that sequels, almost without exception, tend to fall short of the original.

especially if the original was a huge blockbuster. movies like ghostbusters ii, the matrix reloaded, die hard 2, all flopped because they tried to ride the coattails of their predecessors, but lacked vision of their own.

top gun: maverick, however, is on the same par as terminator 2: judgment day. it so far outshines the original so as to eclipse it. this is the movie people will remember years from now, the one they'll keep coming back to.

so, what's so good about the new top gun? the aerial scenes are incredible. so much so it's hard to believe they were not done in cgi. but, as it stands, the actors flew those fighter jets themselves. for realskies.

the plot is clear, straightforward, and engaging. unlike so many other movies where the storyline is confused and/or muddled by subplots and twists and turns, top gun 2 keeps it simple, in the best possible way.

the cast is great. whether it's someone like glen powell (call sign: hangman) who portrays the "smug" fighter pilot who knows they're the best of the best, bob (call sign: bob), whose "boringness" brings a healthy dose of comic relief, miles teller (call sign: rooster), who plays the role with much heart, or even jon hamm (call sign: cyclone), who sells the "prick" of an officer who can't stand tom cruise's face.

the scenes taking place on the ground as opposed to in the air are a bit of a hit-and-miss. some are more interesting than others.

however, as a whole, this movie is packed with action, heart, unexpected turns, and tear-jerking moments, and is damn well worth a watch.

i went to the cinema with a complete open mind, given how dreadful 'some' sequels are, but, top gun: maverick was an absolute joy to behold.

a fantastic story throughout, with constant reminders of the original: top gun. a lot of twist and turns, and maverick (tom cruise) showing, that the sky is literally, the limit!

if you're apprehensive whether to go and watch this, in fear it wont live up to the original top gun, don't! it's an absolute blast! plus, you're only delaying the inevitable.

it was great to see iceman (val kilmer) again, even if it was limited and the role of rooster, (miles teller) was excellent; it brought a real connection from the original movie.

top gun maverick was not a sequel that needed to be made; there were no loose ends left by the original, nothing really that needed to be resolved.

then the word came that a sequel was in the works. unfortunately it was delayed with the death of original top gun director, tony scott who was set to lead again.

while, i was excited at the prospect of a top gun sequel, i maintained a "wait and see" attitude as it had been so long since the first movie and sequels have a hard act to follow.

once it was established who would be taking the director's chair, they set out to ask the navy's permission for support of this movie, assembled the cast and crew, then put their efforts into it. it paid off as they brought us another great presentation!

again, sequels to hit movies are no easy feats. tom cruise and company delivered as we were entertained with an above average continuation, plus (again) exciting flight scenes thanks to the department of defense and u. s. navy.

again, this was not a sequel that needed to be done, but paramount and the top gun maverick cast and crew did their due diligence to to deliver a spectacular sequel to a hit movie!

i was one year out of high school when top gun came out. i loved tom cruise. i had said goodbye a year previously to my (tom cruise lookalike) boyfriend as he went to the air force academy to become a fighter pilot. so my new boyfriend forbid me from seeing top gun in the theater out if jealousy. because i was an idiot, i honored that wish. i have always regretted that. i saw top gun eventually on vhs then dvd many times. so when top gun maverick was being made i was stoked. hey covid hit and i waited.... and waited. anyways, i was so afraid this sequel couldn't possibly live up to my expectations... wow was i wrong! this is a superior movie in every way. the writing, the cinematography, everything is perfect. the flight scenes are so exciting and immersive.... you must see this in imax! the music, the callbacks to the original, all flawless. i came out of the theater pumped! even my husband, who isn't impressed by anything, loved it. tom cruise really delivers and the young cast is also good. run to see this... it's so much fun!
usually the sequels are not that easy to follow. but this one did. one might argue that it is better than the 1st. i'm not a tom cruise fan. but boy, he delivered. it is really that good.

after some 30 years since his last mission, maverick appears as a pilot that has only achieved mediocrity. the time comes for him to prove himself when a nato threat calls for a fleet of elite pilots to extinguish the target. you're in for a heartfelt journey filled with elegant supersonic jet maneuvers, navy salutes, and nostalgic callbacks to the initial top gun.

this film struck the immaculate balance of action and storytelling. there was hardly a dull moment in the movie, and even though i felt that there should've been more to maverick's arc than flying, i think we see enough of his life on the ground to know the real him. i especially loved his interactions with the other pilots--one pilot in particular. the juxtaposition undeniably made the aftermath of the first film feel real, raw, and relatable to anyone who has experienced loss.

it's an energetic adventure that will take you to the skies.

the characters were awesome. bringing back some of them from the first movie was a great choice by the director. tom cruise still got it. overall: great action, great characters, amazing cinematic experience.

watch it. it is worth it.

i was very excited about this sequel, especially after all the hype and as i haven't been to the cinema for over 2.5 years.

picking up over 35 years after the original top gun, this film follows pete "maverick" mitchell (tom cruise), who is now a test pilot recalled to the top gun academy, this time to be an instructor of a bunch of hot-head graduates. the training takes the new best of the best for a near-impossible strike mission, reminiscent of the star wars plot, a virtual suicide mission that only the best pilots in the world would ever contemplate. all of them are taken to their breaking points.

one of the graduates is played by miles teller (who portrays the son of 'goose,' maverick's old flying partner). there's an obvious and justifiable atmosphere.

almost all the airborne sequences were achieved with practical effects, no (or very little) cgi and it really shows.

not a complicated plot but, like the original, it didn't need to be. this film retains the spirit of the original and is everything you would hope for and kept me engaged from start to finish.

after a long period of development, production finally started in 2018. after filming was completed the following year, the release was postponed several times for post production and covid-19 it finally saw release in 2022...and was worth the wait.

after a fun prologue, the film has a fairly straight forward plot-maverick training a younger generation to pull off a mission- but the writers do fit in a good character arc for maverick (dealing with his aging and his relationship with goose's son) and similar to mcquarrie's work with mission impossible work, the mission has it's own complications, especially in the extended climax. while a little cheesy at times it succeeds in being very entertaining and surprisingly very funny at times.

cruise put a lot of energy into promoting the film and is clearly having fun reprising the role. the character is very enjoyable and pushing him into a mentor role he's clearly not comfortable with leads to some great character moments. miles teller is great as goose's son who's journey-while predictable at times-is convincing and well performed. the rest of cruise's team are a likable bunch and get an extended scene together acting as an introduction but in a film running only slightly over two hours, it's perhaps inevitable some of these parts are a bit thin. jennifer connelly is very charming as maverick's old flame penny (a character mentioned but not scene in the original) though it does feel like the role was a re-cast. val kilmer gets a short cameo as iceman which, in acknowledging his real life health issues-is very touching and the emotional high point of the film.

as to be expected in a belated sequel to a beloved film, there are plenty of call backs (especially a very similar opening/credits sequence set to 'danger zone' again), with some 80's nostalgia. there is lots of good use of action with some stunning plane sequences. joseph kosinski previously collaborated with cruise on the visually stunning 'oblivion' and the film looks fantastic, especially with the use of desert in the training and snow at the climax.

there are flaws-the opening sets up a 'humans vs drones' idea which-other than to establish maverick and 'top gun' itself as out of there time doesn't get much further exploration and it can be a bit predictable at times but is fun enough to ride out the cliche's.

ending with an enjoyable lady gaga song [if not quite as memorable as 'take my breath away', this is a really fun time. it would have been easy to cobble together a rushed sequel/rehash back in the day but this, while respectful of the original, is a great film.

as for tom cruise, he seems to be at the receiving end of some very bitter, cruel and vile comments at times, especially due to his private life. yet he has an acting career nearly spanning five decades. all he has done for me is entertain with some brilliant and at times incredible films, especially with the last few mission impossible films where he has taken stunt work to a whole new level to give the cinema audience the best experience.

although he's approaching 60, i hope he has a few more films left in him like top gun: maverick which is without a doubt my film of the year so far and one of the best sequels ever made.

top gun: maverick brings back everything we loved about the original while ramping up the excitement and spectacle in ways that make it a must-see cinematic experience. from the moment the film starts, it grabs your attention with stunning visuals, intense action, and a story that keeps you engaged without trying to push any hidden agenda. this is what movies are all about-a pure, entertaining thrill ride that reminds us why we love going to the theater.

visually, the film is nothing short of spectacular. the aerial dogfights are some of the best ever put on screen, with the practical effects and real-life flight sequences taking the action to a whole new level. you can feel every twist, turn, and maneuver as the jets cut through the sky at breakneck speeds. the cinematography captures the sheer power and precision of fighter pilots in a way that puts you right in the cockpit with them. it's a visual feast that will leave you breathless.

tom cruise returns as pete "maverick" mitchell, and he hasn't lost an ounce of his charisma or edge. he fully embodies the seasoned pilot who still has a rebellious streak, now facing the challenges of training a new generation of elite pilots. his performance is a perfect blend of nostalgia and growth, as maverick grapples with his past while trying to guide the future. the chemistry between cruise and the younger cast, particularly miles teller, who plays rooster (the son of goose from the original), brings an emotional depth to the film that complements the action.

what's refreshing about top gun: maverick is its straightforward, no-nonsense approach to storytelling. it doesn't get bogged down by unnecessary subplots or try to force any underlying message. it's a movie that knows exactly what it is-an action-packed blockbuster that's here to entertain. the stakes are clear, the characters are relatable, and the plot moves at a perfect pace. there's a sense of urgency throughout the film, but it's balanced with moments of humor and heart that keep you invested in the characters and their journeys.

the supporting cast is fantastic, with standout performances from jennifer connelly, jon hamm, and glen powell. each actor brings something unique to the table, and the dynamic between the veteran pilots and the rookies adds an interesting layer to the story. miles teller, in particular, shines as rooster, capturing both the swagger of a top pilot and the emotional weight of his family legacy. his arc with maverick is one of the film's emotional highlights, and their evolving relationship brings a satisfying depth to the narrative.

the film is also a love letter to the original top gun, paying homage to key moments and characters while updating the story for a new generation. the soundtrack, which brings back the iconic theme music and kenny loggins' "danger zone," perfectly complements the pulse-pounding action and nostalgic callbacks. yet, top gun: maverick stands on its own merit, delivering an experience that feels fresh and exhilarating, even for those who may not be familiar with the 1986 classic.

in a world where many blockbusters come with heavy-handed messages or convoluted plots, top gun: maverick is a breath of fresh air. it's an unapologetic celebration of speed, skill, and bravery, wrapped in a well-executed story that delivers exactly what it promises-nonstop entertainment. this is the kind of movie that reminds us of the magic of cinema, where the combination of storytelling, acting, and visual effects creates something larger than life.

overall, top gun: maverick is a spectacular achievement that's sure to satisfy both longtime fans of the original and newcomers alike. it's a high-flying, adrenaline-pumping experience that you'll want to see on the biggest screen possible. whether you're here for the action, the nostalgia, or the incredible visuals, top gun: maverick delivers on every front, making it one of the best action movies in recent years and a worthy sequel to a beloved classic.

sequel to top gun (1986), top gun2 was in making ever since 2012. initially, tony scott, who also made the original, decided to start. however, after his death, the project was shelved, eventually taken up by joseph kosinski who took over in 2018 and after 2 years of delay, top gun 2 saw the light of the day.

pete "maverick" mitchell is a high reputed captain, could've been a senator like his mate iceman who recruits him to lead this mission. the movie is very clear with what it is, and not trying to hard to overdo things. the characters are interesting, and tom cruise is phenomenal. the dogfights, the bgm adds to the already thrilling movie experience. a must watch.

we have been given remakes. reboots. crappy, shoddy movies that don't understand what their betters were.

and now, we have a sequel to top gun. a sequel, not a remake, not a reimagining, a pure sequel. as a sequel? glorious. a master work of how to make a proper sequel. this is what we wanted, what we needed.

as a movie? a bit cheesy, and predictable. all the tropes are there, there's no plot twist. but the end result? it works. it works *very well*. and those flying scenes are about as good as they get - no cgi, it's all real. props to cinematography and stunts, that's one hell of a job.

so realistically this movie is maybe a 7.5 out of 10. but spiritually it's flawless. i average that to 9 out of 10. sounds reasonable to me, at least.

finally, one last word for tom cruise. scientology or not, this gentleman has been providing us with top notch entertainment for close to 40 years. you won't get an oscar any time soon, tom... but in our minds, you are one of the greats. frack academy recognition, you have our admiration, love, and respect. kudos.

cinematography/special effects- 10/10

because this film took place more than 30 years after the original, the technological advancement is noticeable. so the quality, and special effects are much better than that of the first's. it may come as a surprise to know all the jets used in the film are actual jet fighters. so the fighting sequences are much more entertaining this time around. not to mention that the soundtrack is an absolute banger!

characters- 9/10

nearly every character, old and new has a ton of characterization and the perfect amount of screen time to make them fun to be around. shockingly, some of them had some emotional resonance as well. i love the fact that penny and maverick weren't chasing after each other like some couple. instead, their relationship felt a lot more real and natural. speaking of which, maverick is way more interesting and likable than he was in the first film. he isn't your generic cocky main protagonist this time around. he is compassionate about his students and his passion just shoots straight through. maverick makes for such a great teacher. the only problem with the characters is that hangman could have been given a better motivation but it is not that big of a sting though

writing- 9/10

the writing was spectacular. it is good from start to finish and tells the story in a shockingly mature way. it makes you think this is a modernized 80's film and that just adds up to its freshness

enjoyability- 10/10

yes, there may have been no deep moments or any funny characters but instead, this film has awesome flying sequences and interesting dialogue. i am hearing comments about how they only were on the edge of the seat and i can totally relate! it was that much of a good time

overall: 9.8/10

honestly, this film was very close to being perfect. it boggles my mind. like why did you guys put time and effort into making a top gun sequel. that was just an aggressively ok film but this film feels like it happens in another universe because the difference in the quality is that big. i can honestly say that i'm ok with a 3rd installment

i will now award top gun: maverick the badge of awesomeness and the badge of a perfect sequel.

top gun: maverick has to rank up there with some of the best sequels ever made! i was so pleasantly surprised by this beautiful and action packed film that i had to watch it a second time. first off, tom cruise is back and better than ever as maverick. we are thrown right into the action from the opening minutes of the film and the foot is never taken off the gas pedal. the younger cast takes over as the new generation of pilots and this seems to work really nicely with the older cruise/connelly love story. putting the audience in the cockpit with our heroes as they actually fly the planes was next level as an audience member, and i really couldn't think of a better way to top the original!

waited for this movie for 36 years and was not disappointed in any part of it other than the soundtrack.

the story for tg:m was always going to be fairly simple and formulaic - the original was as well. i wasn't expecting citizen kane or godfather or godfather part ii, and this movie certainly wasn't any of those, but it wasn't that kind of movie! this was the continuation of a fun and entertaining story from three+ decades ago, and well worth the investment in time and money to see it in a large screen setting. the callbacks to tg were nicely done, and it in no way diminishes tg:m to have not included meg ryan (carole bradshaw) or kelly mcgillis (charlotte "charlie" blackwood). the choice of jennifer connelly to be penny benjamin was a masterstroke, and val kilmer's cameo as iceman was exquisitely well done. the characters played by ed harris, charles parnell, and jon hamm were good and, frankly, realistic. the young pilots and backseaters were fine. all of this made for an enjoyable film.

downside - the soundtrack sucked, even before one compares it to the tg soundtrack. in that context, the soundtrack really sucked. they'd have been better off using the entire soundtrack from the first movie again for this one. the other minor downside is this: in the scene where pete mitchell is tossed out of the bar, i am utterly convinced the younger pilots would know exactly who pete "maverick" mitchell was and would've acted a little differently. tossing him out that way would be analogous to joe dimaggio or mickey mantle being tossed out of a new york city bar in the 60s 0r 70s. wouldn't have happened.

other than those two nitpicks,it's an excellent use of 2:10 of your time. what are movies supposed to be other than entertaining? top gun: maverick is entertaining from start to finish.

the film is undeniably a masterpiece. beforehand i'd never seen any work from director joseph kosinski, although, after watching this it's fair to say i'm eager to see more work from him. the way he took a huge task like making a sequel out of one of the most classic 80's films out there and managed to make it as good, if not, even better than the first one is admirable and impressive. he made it feel like an 80's film, but at the same time had a modern-day feel about it too. the cast was certainly stellar and the performances from each and every one of the actors/actresses were phenomenal. tom cruise never fails to impress me and miles teller's portrayal of the son of maverick's late best friend goose was done to perfection. although with performances such as war dogs and whiplash, it was expected. the cinematography and visual effects were stunning and you felt, not only, like you were in the 80s but like you were in a fighter jet! the pacing of the film was also terrific as well as the score.

however, where it fails to meet the demands of the original film is where the soundtrack is concerned. although it was nostalgic to hear the classical theme at the start and the end, as well as hearing a brief cameo of "danger zone", i can't help but miss tracks such as "take my breath away" during the romance scenes. this brings me to my second flaw. the romance aspect of the first film was spot on so the sequel shouldn't have been expected to live up to its predecessor. therefore, i believe more of an attempt to develop the character of peggy, would've been interesting to see. although, it more than made up for it with the action scenes that were certainly more developed and exciting than the first one. and even if romance wasn't as developed in this film, the emotion was certainly still there and i believe it was more emotional than the first one.

to conclude, the first one has greater aspects than this film in terms of the romantic development of characters and a more memorable and catchy soundtrack. however, it cannot be expected to be completely greater than the first film as it is a classic after all. therefore to manage to make an action-packed, emotional, adrenaline-pumping sequel, was incredibly commendable and this is why it betters its predecessor and is a better-made film overall. i loved every minute of it and believe it cannot warrant anything below a 9/10.

i will right up front in saying, i never saw the first movie. to be perfectly honest, i was in my twenties at the time, and i was not a huge fan of cruise.

but i digress. fast forward to 2022, and on a hunch, i decided - after watching a composite trailer/interview with cruise and the film-makers, that the movie seemed compelling enough to watch.

honestly, i have to say, i think not having seen the original added an edge of complexity mixed with being the only one in the theater who didn't know the back story. consequently, i was on a steep learning curve about the background characters.

overall conclusions:

(1) top gun - maverick is clearly an epic enough story, in and of itself, to a point where you needn't have seen the original movie to appreciate and "get" the storyline and whole drive of the sequel.

(2) if you're going to try replicating real-life, jet fighter combat ...heck! any combat, top gun maverick has well and truly set the new benchmark by which all other future movies of this ilk will struggle to match.

(3) if i had to hazard a guess (seeing as i'm in the absolute minority of one - having not seen the first movie), this sequel not only crushes the original for storyline and atmosphere, but also has clearly got to be light years ahead of and improving upon air combat replication and special effects.

(4) the believability factor for tg maverick is huge, and really cannot be understated. it's quite frankly breathtaking and genuinely awe inspiring what the director, cinematographers and live action production crew have accomplished in this instant movie classic.

lastly, the nod for story telling and screenplay adaptation is masterfully constructed - as it doesn't follow the expected and dross cliches of similar action movies based on a military theme (and its predecessor is in that number). the significance in saying that, lies in the believability and original nature of the main character interactions throughout.

all told, any movie worth watching once, must surely be worth watching again (and even again). top gun maverick is that great a yarn.

first of all, let me say this is my 1st ever review on imdb... absolutely one of the best theatrical experience's i've ever had! perhaps my best ever! perfectly casted. beautifully written. and the cinematography was, well, literally breathtaking. the original top gun (1986) was classic. top gun: maverick for me was, freaking legendary. to answer your question, "did maverick live up to the hype?" umm...an understatement.

i was really apprehensive about this movie. i mean how do you too what was an entertaining movie back in '86? the story was straightforward and honest about what it was.

after watching this movie, the first thing i liked about was pacing. the movie was very careful linking the first movie and the references contained therein. the second thing are storylines were intertwined very well without becoming convoluted and just ridiculous. i thought the cinematography was very good and allowing the audience feel like they were in the cockpit with tom and the view was outstanding. another thing i especially enjoyed was the main plot of the movie. you could consider the movie formulaic but it worked here. the esthetics of the movie were spot on and easy on the eyes now the content of the movie was a tearjerker and pulled at my heart strings. the movie was a continuation of the first one but was darker on a lot of levels. first mitchell was an old man. he obviously still maintained his rebellious streak that cost him his job at top gun thus directly affected his relationship with charlie from the first movie. he knew he was coming to end of the road and faced the realization time catches everyone including capt pete mitchell. the movie was deliberate in providing clues of mitchell's old age. the calendar with his appointment in telemetry a day before flying his experimental plane.

another good thing was mitchell's conflict with getting away with stuff because iceman had his back. iceman was promoted and looked after mitchell like an older brother who understood him and his need for speed. another point to add another layer of depth to mitchell's character was the realization that he was no teacher. he decided at one point in the movie to give a graduate level training and those "top of their classes" weren't as good.

i looked at the movie as though it was me. not because of the stunts pete has pulled at work but i, just as maverick did, know things are changing and they will pass us by. the thing we can do is to pass on what we know and guide those younger than us. i really loved the movie but on another level it was a reminder that our movie "heroes" get old and we get old. it forces us to realize our own morality.

the short and sweet of top gun, maverick: it's entertaining. the cinematography is outstanding, the story is relatively good, and the acting is also good but not oscar worthy. it's a fun movie and for fans like me of the 1986 original movie, the story lines match up great.

it's worth a second trip to the theater to be entertained once again.

i've never been a fan of the movie "the best shooter". the picture somehow passed by and was remembered for a good story at one time with several significant moments and a completely passing plot. however, the announced sequel to the film and the ardent interest in tom cruise's new work attracted my attention. the picture became even more interesting when it began to bypass large-scale blockbusters at the box office one after another. that's when i decided to watch this movie to personally verify the quality of the proposed sequel. and i really liked the picture.

the film boasts an impressive budget of $ 140 million and an excellent box office, which is close to $ 1.5 billion. such figures are not amenable to every mastodon, of which there are a lot only among movie comics. what impressed the viewer so much with the second "maverick"? i won't say for everyone, but for me it became a high-quality large-scale action movie, where drama and full-scale shooting are successfully intertwined. when viewing the latter, they are somehow noticed by themselves. verified shots, dynamics in flight scenes, unusual angles - all this really attracts and does not look somehow hackneyed in our modern era of blockbusters, where such scenes have become the norm for a long time. it is in this film that action scenes are especially memorable.

i consider the close connection of this project with the first film to be important. an excellent and even somewhat cunning move on the part of the creators. the writers and director skillfully play on the emotions of the audience, who are repeatedly sent to the events of the first part, which happened more than 35 years ago. they do it both cheekily and cleverly. i, as a spectator, understand this, when here and there they tell and show what is connected with the first picture, but at the same time the success and sincerity of the previous film respond with a kind of longing for the past, when the main character was young, and my generation, along with the film, was just born. now we are older, and maverick cruz managed to raise his friend's child, protecting him as best he could. decades have passed, but the hero is still with us. don't know. it's a strange feeling, but it's like you've lived your whole life, and for maverick and cruz, these 35 years have passed, he's back with us, his story continues, and you grow up with him. the more interesting for me was the appearance of val kilmer in this project. the actor has been fighting laryngeal cancer since 2015. in the film, this moment is played out interestingly.

some scripted moments look controversial. for example, i was little convinced by the storyline just with the son of a goose, a rooster (in the original, the call sign rooster). the conflict between maverick and bradley, that's the guy's name, looks somewhat far-fetched and even implausible, given that maverick did what he did, and the young guy himself could not influence it.

the line with the heroine jennifer connelly was also weak. the actress played perfectly, demonstrating maverick's long-standing love interest, but it seemed to me the whole movie that the girl was introduced here simply because the actress kelly mcgillis refused the original role of charlie from the first film (i don't know the true reason for her non-participation, just an assumption). it would be wiser to develop this line, especially considering that the creators made so many important references to the first picture. in general, the heroine connelly penny fit well into the picture, her story with cruz was revealed, but there was clearly a certain alienness of this narrative.

the film itself looks dynamic and with interest, despite the high duration of the film. director joseph kosinski did a great job, managing to present aerial combat scenes to the audience with unusual visual solutions, convey the same recognizable camaraderie that the first film was imbued with and competently depersonalizing the main antagonists of the picture. there is dry information about the "enemy base" that needs to be eliminated. what kind of enemy it is, why it was recorded there, is not discussed. and for good reason. the audience should be focused on the story of the pilots, their flight and the approaching attack. competently, without any political agenda, this will suit everyone.

the film is not replete with technical data so that it is clear which plane and what is better. however, through dialogues, it is easy to understand who has the advantage, why it is impossible to fight with some planes against others, and which of the air vehicles are more maneuverable than the others. there is no confusion and by the beginning of the final act you clearly understand what the advantages of the team are, and what awaits them in case of an error.

the picture is remembered by several twists, but i was more impressed by the visual component and the music. the creators were able to transfer that spirit of the mid-1980s into modernity and at the same time do it, successfully combining it with the current rhythm of the narrative of the paintings. the scenes of flights and aerial shootouts are very impressive, and cruz once again proves that he doesn't care when he is masterfully flying real planes even in his 60s.

"maverick" came out as a worthy sequel with a new and interesting story, excellent visual and audio sequences. the picture is designed to remind of the past, to show modernity, to reveal the old problems that still oppress the heroes, and also to give a couple of fascinating hours to the audience.

in an age of hollywood defined by big budget franchises, live action remakes and adaptations, it's easy to be critical of much of what has been put out. originality is often shied away from because of the fact that it doesn't bring in the cash, so all that's left are massive franchises like the mcu and harry potter, or nostalgia heavy but ultimately flat reboots and sequels such as jurassic world and ghostbusters afterlife. so where does another seemingly nostalgia baiting sequel such as top gun: maverick fit in all this? for me, maverick joins spider-man: no way home as an example of how to make the perfect sequel in this day and age: maverick never once feels like it's overly relying on top gun to make it worth the viewers time. this film employs flashbacks and subtle alludes to the first film with nuance and precision, so as to not flood the viewer with memories and distract from it's story. speaking of which, the story more than stands on its own as a strong, feel-good action packed movie, with strong ensemble acting from all fronts, clever dialogue (mostly), electric flight sequences, and a brilliant performance from tom cruise. maverick is a joyride of a film that manages pushes your sensory limits without completely overloading you, especially if you watch it in the theatre (which i strongly recommend). a pleasant surprise was miles teller, who sort of dropped off my radar after his star turn in whiplash. he's cocky, cool, rash, and emotional, reminding me exactly of tom cruise in the first film. the writing is, at some points, formulaic but what's interesting is now matter how cliche it can feel, the viewer is reminded why the cliches became so widely used in the first place. from a technical standpoint, maverick is an out and out masterpiece. the sound design is flawless, the camerawork is electrifying, and the editing is smoother than tom cruise's iconic slide in risky business. if any film should sweep the technical oscars this year, i can confidently say it should be maverick.

maverick feels like a glimpse of what a modern classic can be, and it's a shame that a film like this is so rare these days. maverick is a near-perfect combination of brain and heart, and it's technical wizardry is icing on the cake. is this suddenly the best movie of all time? no, not by a long shot. is this even the best movie of the 2020's so far? even that is debatable. but it's a giant leap in the right direction, and if this is an indication of what hollywood has to offer, than i'm in for the ride. i strongly recommend seeing top gun: maverick, even if you haven't seen the first movie because it's still as enjoyable and in every respect a better movie. my verdict is a 9 out of 10, and i hope you enjoy it as much as i did.

top gun: maverick is a sequel to top gun (1986) - and it suits the movie to be updated. this applies both storywise, it applies to the camera work and the whole context. but top gun: maverick is also a movie that clearly knows your origins and uses it in the best possible way. it is in many ways a film where action and character work go hand in hand, even though a lot of star wars inspiration has been taken for one of the crucial moments in the film. there is a theory that maverick dies at the beginning of the film and that everything afterwards is his death dream. this explains the individual parts of the film that are a bit skinny. so in light of that theory, this film has to be said to be one of the best films of the year so far.

growing up with top gun, the music and the aura, this movie throws you back into this spirit. this film does its best to recreate the jingoistic feel of that 1980s classic, albeit without everyone sweating bullets or the berlin song "take my breath away".

pete "maverick" mitchell (tom cruise) is ordered back to top gun upon the request of his former teammate and wingman, and now commander of the u. s. pacific fleet, tom "icemen" kazansky (a starkly diminished val kilmer). maverick's task is to train the best fighter pilots of the us navy for an urgent mission to destroy a nuclear power facility of an enemy nation. among those young pilots is bradley "rooster" bradshaw (a bullheaded miles teller), the son of pete's best friend and co-pilot nick "goose" bradshaw in the original. their relationship is more than complicated and one of the underlying plots following us throughout this action-loaded movie, with incredible highspeed stunts with f-18 fighter jets.

the crowd of young pilots has a similar dynamic to the team of top gun, with the rivalry between "hangman" (glen powell) and "rooster". also, the modern age is reflected in the navy, with the female fighter pilot natasha "phoenix" trace (monica barbaro) who is a bad-ass top gun cadet. overall, this movie is great to watch on the big screen, loaded with stunts and action! a must-see of 2022 for everyone who likes a little thrill and action. the perfect movie for the memorial day weekend.

top gun: maverick manages to create a sequel, 36 years after the original that, despite its occasional shameless use of nostalgia, creates a distinct, excellently paced, suspenseful movie that not only does the 1986 film justice, but surpasses it in many regards.

i have to admit that i found this film somewhat better than the original. that is probably because it actually had more of a plot than the first film, which was basically about a bunch of hot shots going to a training school for elites, and then having a bit of a battle at the end. okay, one could argue about the first film being about how a hot shot is humbled (or like tarantino, claiming that it is a film about a man coming to terms with his homosexuality), but in the end, as far as i could tell, it was just an advertisement for the us navy.

okay, one could easily argue that about this film as well, and in part you are right. however, i did feel like that it had more of a plot, and there was much more to the battle at the end than it was in the original. in fact, i was somewhat surprised that once the mission was completed, there was more to the film than i expected.

there are two elements to this film though, one being that it is about an older fighter pilot struggling to maintain his relevancy, but also about a man who is struggling to deal with the ghosts of his past. in fact, one thing that is pointed out at the beginning is that maverick has pretty much stagnated in his career. despite the fact that he is a highly decorated officer, he still basically flies planes. however, his response to that is quite good, namely that he likes to fly planes.

it sort of makes sense though because there is so much talk in the modern world that success if measured by how far up the ladder you climb, but the reality is that there are actually quite a lot of people that don't want to climb the ladder. i have worked with a number of people who are really, really good at what they do, however they have no interest in moving up the ladder, or as other say 'progressing their careers'. this is the impression that i get from maverick, that he is happy where he is, and that is flying planes.

apparently cruise was insistant that he did not want any blue screens in this film, which basically meant that all of the shots in the planes were actually filmed in the planes, the same being with all the stunts and maneuvers that were performed (though i'm not entirely sure whether cruise can actually fly a jet, though he does know how to fly). another thing that stood out is that in part the film still followed the track of the original film, which included a scene where everybody is playing ball on the beach. though the interesting thing is that at the bar scene at the beginning, instead of being amongst the young people, he is sitting alone at the bar watching on. in a way, these two films seem to bookend maverick's life, with nothing in between, despite the fact that we are given an idea of what went on between the two films. however, one thing is clear that while he has aged physically, he hasn't really matured all that much.

as i mentioned though, compared to the original, i felt that there was a lot more meat to this film than the first one, which was just about a bunch of flyboys going to a training camp, and then fighting some migs at the end. this one, there was more urgency, and more of a plot, and more depth to maverick's character than the original. mind you, it was also quite interesting that they used the opening credits for the first film for this one as well.

"top gun: maverick" is the long-awaited 2022 sequel to the iconic 1986 blockbuster "top gun," which turned its then-24-year-old star tom cruise into an international megastar and pop culture icon. in the 36 years since "top gun," much has changed - technology, the military, even the very nature of aerial combat itself.

and that is what this film is pretty much about: how the art of aerial dogfighting and highly trained fighter pilots are becoming obsolete as technology (read: drones) has all but eliminated the need for actual flesh & blood human beings.

this is the dilemma facing capt. pete "maverick" mitchell (cruise) as he is reluctantly called back to topgun by his former rival adm. tom "iceman" kazansky (val kilmer) to help train twelve elite naval aviators for what would otherwise be a suicide mission to bomb a secret military facility in a foreign - possibly russia, or russian-occupied - country. the problem is that despite these pilots being the best of the best in the modern united states navy, for most of them, their only real combat experience is through high-altitude bombing runs, not actual dogfighting. this is why maverick is called back to train them, due to his experiences 36 years earlier in the first movie.

but training these new pilots for this mission won't be easy, since amongst them, is bradley "rooster" bradshaw (miles teller), the son of his late rio and best friend nick "goose" bradshaw (anthony edwards, from the original "top gun"). bradley resents maverick for stalling his flight career for four years while he was still at the naval academy and he also blames him for the death of his father in 1986. (the tensions between these two is what ultimately makes up the emotional core of the film.)

joseph kosinski is the young hot-shot behind the camera of this belated jerry bruckheimer-produced sequel. kosinski is no tony scott (who directed the original "top gun" and committed suicide in 2012, and the film is dedicated to his memory), but he handles the story and the characters very well. if anyone was to fill tony scott's shoes, it was him.

admittedly, while the story is not as interesting as the story in the first movie, the characters definitely help to bring the script to life flawlessly. tom cruise is at the top of his game, as always, and he uses his age - cruise just turned 60 today - to great advantage in showing us that while he is way past the prime of his youth (and he knows it) and many of his peers have succeeded him in the u. s. naval ranks, he still has many tricks up his sleeve and many things to pass on to a new generation of fighter pilots. and he also finds the time to rekindle his affair with an old flame, the hard deck bar owner penny benjamin (lovely jennifer connelly), who lights up every scene she appears in.

the other pilots are also quite colorful, though some obviously get more screen time than the others. of course you have the arrogant and pig-headed "hangman" (glen powell, filling in for "iceman"); ace female pilot "phoenix" (monica barbero), who is arguably the best and most level-headed of the bunch; her nerdy rio "bob" (lewis pullman); and then of course, there's miles teller's "rooster," who bears an uncanny resemblance to his father and even does his own live rendition of jerry lee lewis's "great balls of fire."

one of my greatest concerns going into "top gun: maverick" was the authenticity of the film's flying sequences. the original 1986 "top gun" utilized actual active-duty navy pilots for the aerial dogfighting scenes, in addition to scale models for some of the more dangerous stunts. here, it's even more authentic: the actors are actually in the cockpits of real flying f/a-18 hornets (the actors reportedly had to sign waivers attesting that they did not in fact have a fear of flying), which succeeds in re-creating the dizzying, vertiginous flying scenes that were made so famous in the 1986 original.

"top gun: maverick" is a long-delayed sequel that was well worth the wait. the return of a now-60-year-old tom cruise, vertiginous flying sequences, a new generation of young naval aviators, and the delightful callbacks to the original "top gun" all made it worthwhile.

i took my dad to see this as an early father's day gift and wow! we were absolutely blown away. for context, my dad is not a frequent moviegoer like myself, but as a fan of the original, he was highly anticipating this movie, which did not disappoint. personally, i thought the first film was a fine action movie, but as a younger viewer, i lacked the emotional attachment and nostalgia that the previous generation has for it. to the few people that read this, i will absolutely have that nostalgia for this movie and plan on showing this to my children in the future. maybe we'll even see top gun 3 in 2058!

in my humble opinion, this movie actually improved many aspects of the original (such as the storyline, action, humor and romance/love interest element), which is why i argue that this movie surpassed its predecessor in quality. while viewing this movie, if you find yourself wondering if you feel the same way, the climax (a visually stunning culmination of the two hours that just flew by) will definitely convince you. the phrase "on the edge of my seat" is flaunted about quite often, but this was one of the few movies to literally keep me on the edge of my seat. easily one of the best 3rd act action sequences i've seen in recent years coupled with a nice rapport between tom cruise and miles teller (who channels his "whiplash" acting here). the latter portrays rooster, the son of goose from the first top gun. kudos to the makeup department for creating an impressive goose look-alike.

speaking of legacy characters, it's well-known that val kilmer appears in the movie (for crying out loud, his name is in the opening credits!) without spoiling anything, i felt that both the character and actor were done justice by the story. it was so satisfying to see him return (albeit briefly) to the role that arguably propelled his career. last but far from least is the titular maverick. tom cruise was in top form here, even at nearly 60 years old, delivering a great performance, this time as instructor of top gun (not a student) and a distant yet caring father figure to rooster. the class which pete taught contained a variety of welcome additions to the cast. i also quite enjoyed the aspect of pete's romance with old flame, penny benjamin (the admiral's daughter referenced in the first movie).

despite my fear of a 35 year-old sequel, top gun: maverick met and exceeded my expectations. everyone, do yourself a favor and check this one out. even though i loved the batman, i have declared a new winner for best movie of 2022. there's a reason this movie got a five-minute standing ovation at the premiere and has a near perfect score on rotten tomatoes, where i will soon release a copy of this review.
