ok, there are many elements that go into a movie. a great movie can be weak in certain areas if it is exceptional in others. what we, the viewer, look for in a movie is highly personal and subjective. objectively top gun maverick has the most amazing jet fighter action scenes ever filmed. the combination of incredible cinematography, tight editing and bombastic sound effects make these jet fighter action scenes absolutely visceral and riveting. the scene where maverick successfully completes the near impossible training run in his f18e was among the best 10 minutes of cinema i have ever seen. i was totally gripped in my cinema seat. for this scene alone i give the movie 10 stars. whilst i am sure some cgi was used in places (particularly the fictional mach 10 spy plane in the opening scene), a large majority of what you see is real footage, either in cockpit, from aeriel vantage points, or land vantage points. tom cruise is great, again. the rest of the cast is very strong. the story is entirely predictable, but with a clear direction and purpose, and serves to move the movie from one incredible action scene to the next but with meaning. the characters are a little 2d, but have sensible arcs and growth that increase emotional investment. the original movie had great action scenes with iconically cheesy dialogue and beautiful cinematography and great direction. top gun maverick has less cheesy and less memorable dialogue but still very humerous in places, beautiful cinematography throughout, incredible action scenes and tight direction. both movies blend a lot of fantasy with reality, but they are movies, not documentaries, so that's fine by me. anyway, if you are remotely interested in the idea of a navy jet fighter action movie, watch this movie on imax. it will blow you away. watching this movie was one of the most memorable and enthralling cinema experiences i have ever had. i can't even tell you what the run time was, it seemed like 5 minutes as the movie just flew by (pun intended).

i genuinely cannot enough good things about this film. it had everything that anyone could've asked for in a sequel. i actually watched the 1986 top gun the morning that i went and saw the sequel. i had no idea what to expect after the original.

i watched the original with absolutely zero knowledge of the film or even tom cruise. somehow, i had never seen a film where tom cruise was the main protagonist. i had also never heard of anthony edwards before in my life. i had probably heard maverick & goose at some point before i watched the film, but i didn't really do anything with that. i kind of thought the original was going to be bored when it started, but it hooked me within minutes and of course the tragic dogfight scene and everything after had me sobbing on my couch for a good 45 minutes.

i had a few hours in between finishing the og version and going to see the sequel. i genuinely did not know how they would top (lol no pun intended) the original, but they did. they absolutely blew it out of the water. every time there was a goose callback in the film, i couldn't help but tear up. i absolutely lost it when rooster made his entrance. miles teller has always been a star, and i'm glad people are appreciating him for the great actor that he has always been! the dynamic between mav & rooster took my heart on a two hour rollercoaster, but i would genuinely do anything to get more screen time with those two. every interaction they had made me have an emotional reaction (sometimes heart-wrenching, other times heartwarming). tom and miles have such an incredible dynamic on screen, and i need another film with their characters. miles did such an incredible job carrying on goose's legacy and i swore that in the scenes after rooster came back to save mav after he had just saved him and they were in the f-14... that was goose in the back. like, it looked just like him. i am just so blown away by their performances. then when they hugged at the end? "thank you for saving my life." "it's what my dad would've done." i was in tears. i couldn't do it. then right before lady gaga's masterpiece of a closing track "hold my hand" showed us the credits and rooster hit the picture of goose??? no. i could not see anything but tears after that. i have to have more!

digressing from the main characters, i think what makes a film good is when you can follow the main protagonists and navigate their stories/conflicts and then be satisfied at the end with the conclusion of said stories/conflicts. what makes a film great is when the supporting characters carry just as much weight as the main characters. this supporting cast was nothing but captivating. i loved every second that every one of the supporting characters were on screen. phoenix/bob were such a great duo, and i knew they would become two of my favorites right from the get go. payback/fanboy were also two very great characters! i enjoyed their interactions with each other but also with the rest of the characters! and then of course... hangman. i had never seen glen powell before and i've watched most of the things he has acted in, but i knew he would have some kind of redemption arc the second he showed up on screen and spoke. i loved the mav/ice & rooster/hangman parallel. then when he pulled that little hat trick out near the end? my heart genuinely was about to stop. i could sit here and ramble on for paragraphs about each character, but i'll stop here.

this film was nothing short of a masterpiece. i didn't have to wait 36 years for it, but the 7 hours between me finishing the original and then me seeing the sequel seemed like an eternity. it is hands down my favorite film i have ever seen. i don't say that lightly. it had me on the edge of my seat with my heart racing pretty much the entire time. if i wasn't in painful anticipation of what was happening next, i was moved to tears. all around, this film has everything that a summer blockbuster should. i'm sure everyone has probably seen a video of the beach scene by now. the soundtrack was also absolutely amazing, so after you watch the film... go pay the soundtrack a few listens. i cannot recommend this film enough. go see it once... and then twice... and then maybe even 10.3 more times.

that gong!!! as a retired sailor in the american navy, i have to say this film is an 11 out 10. the intrinsic value of this work of art is the way it was filmed. all of the work put it into it, is a testament to its essence. tom used the phrase "a love letter to aviation", as i watched this film, one word constantly came to mind--love. and i don't mean a romantic type of love, but a love that my brothers and sisters demonstrate on a daily basis, first off, for each other and for their country, no matter what its present condition. although i never flew, i was part of the flight deck ground support on various flat tops. this film is a tribute to all of us; and i did feel that--love. i could be wrong, but based on lincoln bobble head and hangman's "give 'em hell", i'm sure this was shot on two different carriers--abraham lincoln and the harry s. truman (i had not researched this information prior). this film unified u. s. back in 1986 and i hope it unifies u. s., again today. this film has it all.

it was a surprise to see the poster of the sequel to one of my favourite childhood films, in a recently renovated cinema house in my hometown of peshawar, a city that is an hour away from pakistan's border with afghanistan, its a city which for the longest part of the last decade post 9/11 had only seen blood,chaos and suicide bombings. so to see maverick's poster outside the cinema which was once shut down for a long time when it was almost war in my city, it was a breath of fresh air to buy a ticket to see top gun mav. the film is overall really beautifully filmed, the casting, the screenplay, the direction are top notch, the youngsters fit in their roles really well, however i must say i did not digest john hamm in his role as cyclone for some reason, i felt he was wearing a uniform but was a disconnect from the charecter, he acted more like his charecter from mad men tv show. jennifer connely has really good acting skills, i think her role could have been of more substance and that could have also added a lot to the film apart from its high fidelity air combat sequences, connely's role could have had more meaning to it. the biggest turn down for me was how maverick easily slips into enemy air base ,easily finds a tom cat f14 parked, ready like a piece of cake ready to be eaten , maverick and goose's son run towards it and within seconds easily taxi it and fly off the enemy base, this made the film look like an indian film. over all, i loved the film, its continuity from the prequel and how well the cast (except for hamm) have played their charecters. two of the minor turn offs apart from john hamm for me have to be the absence of a new soundtrack song which i wish were there and as good as berlin's song in the prequel, and the second turn off has to be maverick still being a captain. with this review, i rest my opinion about the film, lots of love from peshawar,pakistan.

when i heard they were going to make a sequel to top gun i was excited by the prospect, but we no longer have the original director tony scott. who we have instead is joseph kosinski, and i'd argue he's even better.

as the name suggests, this film focuses upon maverick. if you're a fan of the original you won't be disappointed to see what he's been flying since, or that he's still flying.

and it's those flying scenes that are stunning. far better than the originals, better not just because technology has moved on, but because the actors are in aircraft being flown. real aircraft, being filmed under the stresses of flight.

kosinski's previous successes are tron: legacy, oblivion and only the brave. if you've seen those three films you already know he's probably the best director working today. yes, he's that good.

top gun: maverick works because the director, kosinski, somehow manages to make you feel that you're part of the film, that you're right there with the people in the film. the pace is perfect, the action precise, and yes you'll be on the edge of your seat!

kosinski should be getting an oscar for top gun: maverick.

the film will have been out only a month tomorrow (as i write this), and it already has almost twenty four hundred reviews here on imdb as it ranks in the top fifty of viewer all-time movie ratings. i saw the original "top gun" from 1986 only a couple years ago, but i'm glad i didn't hesitate to see this one just yesterday. the flight scenes are an adrenaline rush if there ever was one in moving pictures, and i defy anyone to state that it's impossible to not be in the cockpit when pete 'mavarich' mitchell leads his f-18 fighter crew on the raid against an iranian enrichment plant. if anything, i thought that was an intended tweak against the terrorist nation that the film makers sought to marginalize with the story line. i can't imagine the mullahs are very happy about the outcome of that little put-down against their regime. in real life, the successful raid against the enemy target here may not seem very realistic, but who cares when you hear the roar of those jets and experience the in-flight maneuvers of accomplished pilots performing those daredevil theatrics. the emotional ending with 'hangman' (glen powell) making the save for mitchell and wingman 'rooster' bradshaw (miles teller) is about as pulse pounding as it gets when it comes to movie finales, so if you haven't seen the picture yet, let this be your recommendation to get to your nearest theater to experience the excitement.

as an aside and on a humorous note, the last streaming movie i saw just yesterday had a line of dialog that was a precursor to the scene in this film when tom cruise's character bailed out of the experimental aircraft at the beginning of the story and found himself asking where he was in a small town diner. arnold schwarzenegger got the same answer to the same question when he parachuted into a junkyard in the 1996 film "eraser". in both cases, the young kid responding to the question said - 'on earth'!

after giving this some thought, i can honestly say this was one of the best blockbuster action movies i've ever seen in a movie theater. not since independence day and terminator 2 have i walked out of a movie theater this satisfied (this is limited to action blockbusters before you roll your eyes). every second of this movie was fun, enjoyable and/or exhilarating with the perfect mix of nostalgia. while it stayed true to the original, it surpassed it on just about every level. huge credit to the director and editors that kept the pacing perfect and the remarkable score/sound team. i haven't heard a movie sound this great...maybe ever. it felt like i had a subwoofer in my seat which made the flight scenes even more immersive.

finally a mega budget production that seemed to care solely about putting the best possible film on screen rather than playing it safe and catering to as many demographic groups as possible. oh and by the way, this movie has an outstanding cast that happened to be very diverse.

over the past two days, i had extremely high expectations for two premiers: maverick exceeded those already high expectations beyond my wildest imagination. the other, obi-wan, made me nearly lose hope in the future of the star wars franchise.

top gun (1986) is a classic slice of feel-good cheese but it's also very dated; and i was always skeptical of this sequel before release. maverick however, is totally awesome and is a hell of a lot better than it has any right to be.

at nearly 60, tom cruise still knows a thing or two about making an exciting, purely old-school summer blockbuster and maverick delivers and more. if ever there was a reason to see a film in imax this is it: the stunts, aerial combat scenes and cinematography are undoubtedly impressive, more so i think than christopher nolan's dunkirk.

everything is bigger and louder for sure but maverick still retains the heart, emotion, thrills and feel-good spirit of the original whilst being superior to that film in every way possible. all of the characters are likeable, too, and there's also a touching cameo with val kilmer's iceman.

top gun: maverick is perhaps the best tom cruise film i have ever seen. tom cruise is clearly the top-billed actor in this movie, but it wasn't just cruise's performance that helped this movie "soar." miles teller (rooster) of whiplash fame gives an excellent performance as goose's son. teller makes you feel the emotion that he's putting into his character. while also being the son of an iconic original character, you can't not root for him. glen powell (hangman) is a good antagonist (not villain) character for this movie. monica barbaro (phoneix) showed that she is a future star as well as her wso lewis pullman (bob) played "bob," a funny goofball character. the performance by these young actors and actresses is some of the best parts of this movie, but you cannot forget the veteran actors. the veterans include franchise veterans val kilmer (iceman) and ed harris (hammer). kilmer, whose battle with throat cancer led him to lose his ability to speak, had his voice digitally remade for one line in this movie, and it was worth it. kilmer was the reason i got into biographical films with his portrayal of jim morrison from the doors in the doors (1991) and doc holliday in 1993's tombstone. ed harris, who has been in so many great films that it might take me a paragraph to write about, is in very little of this movie though he gives off the same "hard-a*s" vibe from the original film. two veteran actors new to the cast include jon hamm (cyclone) of mad men fame and jennifer connelly who i've liked since she was in labyrinth. which coincidently was released when the original top gun came out in 1986.

when i write a full review, i always try and explain my favorite and least favorite parts of the film's plot. i would hate for someone to click on this review and have the movie spoiled before they see it, so i'm writing a review without giving away any plot details.

so my opinion on the first top gun movie is that it's not the greatest thing ever, but also not the worst. it's entertaining and fun, but really has no meat to the bone or anything. for top gun maverick i have two words to describe this movie: emotion & heart, two things that the first film lacked, but they are utilized to their fullest potential in the sequel. i already have massive respect for tom cruise as an actor, but with this movie, my respect for him has gone past 1000 because this is clearly one of his greatest works. not only does he perform all these flying stunts for real, but this is definitely one of his most emotional performances of his career. miles teller is also great in the film playing goose's son rooster and you feel more the impact of goose's death in this film than you actually do in the first movie and because of that you really feel the emotion and the dynamic between maverick and rooster. i also love the choice to have jennifer connelly play a past lover in this movie. you feel the chemistry and you sense the history between her and maverick which is a romance storyline i can get on board with unlike charlie and maverick in the first which felt forced and unnatural. we are also introduced to new characters played by glenn powell, monica barbaro, jay ellis and many more and they managed to give these new characters enough personality to them to feel a sense of camaraderie. every character instantly felt like family and they made us care in just a matter of 2 hours which is very impressive. the collaboration score harold faltermeyer, lorne balfe, hans zimmer and lady gaga is absolutely astounding. they just take the original top gun theme and amp it up to make it sound fresh and modern.

in a world that is fatigued with marvel superheroes and funny (most times unfunny) and unoriginal content, top gun comes to bring a breath of fresh air with a new, compelling and realistic story that has nothing to do with superheroes or a franchise*, and still packs the action and high stakes of a hollywood blockbuster thriller! it is so refreshing, there's no man-to-man combat or hand guns, just the jet's missiles and bullets, but it's not an uncomfortable "army" film. this is a film of heart more than army. the army is but a small part, and the only thing you get to see are the jets and battleships, making this film focused solely on the characters, and the mission and training with the jet planes. the story is so simple and straightforward, but at the same time brings unexpected twists, and the stakes get higher as you move along. there is real peril, and it is very realistic, and yet, it takes you out of the boringness of the daily life and takes you on an epic mission and flight. plus, you don't need to do any research; the film explains itself. no need to watch previous films, or need to know about the army, or jets; everything is explained in the film so you can enjoy it to the fullest. a wonderful experience.

the characters are not empty slates, they are compelling, with their own realistic backgrounds and growth throughout the film, which makes you care and connect with the characters. real relationships, real connection, and real growth. straightforward goals, but incredibly difficult to achieve, which makes you journey through the story along with each of the characters, especially the protagonist pete "maverick" mitchell. there are romantic moments, but not uncomfortable or cringy, they seem really good for the film, and the broken friendships from the beginning come to a satisfying conclusion. the connections between the characters make the stakes for the mission higher than ever and you actually fear that any of the characters will die.

this film has one of the most impressive plots and action sequences i have ever seen! the mystery and difficulty of the mission is impressive as we travel with the trainees to master their given mission which is attempted in the climax. the training sequence was fun, fulfilling, with a few laughs along the way, along with scares and sequences that will get your heart pumping faster than ever and keep you at the edge of your seat as accidents happen. you truly feel the stakes and the pressure of the mission as the pilots leave for their mission, and attempt the mission. and oh my gosh!

the jet scenes. just the jet plane scenes are a wonder to watch! you truly feel like you are in a jet plane taking on the g forces, and attempting crazy maneuvers. but the sequences are so well shot and cinematographically made, it is so enjoyable and fulfilling to watch. many unexpected twists and challenges with the jet planes, but it is an absolute joy to watch. the stunts that were pulled with the jets is something like i've never seen before.

the heart of the film is something absolutely gorgeous. there's a backstory and a wrong that needs to be undone to restore the relationship in the film, and it comes to a beautiful conclusion at the end of the film. and the way teachers and students, fathers and sons dare to give their lives to save the other is something truly astounding. something so beautiful and satisfying to watch.

and the musical score, was fantastic! it elevated the emotion and epic-ness of the film! the cinematography was gorgeous across the entire film. you really feel people poured their hearts and work into this film. this film tried, and it did it.

this film gets a 10 out of 10 from me. it is an absolute masterpiece in a time where masterpieces are so rare in the cinema world. this is an amazing story and spectacle you have to watch, if possible on a big screen with good speakers. this film did not disappoint, it met with the expectations left with the trailer, and what you expect of a good film. seriously, jurassic world: dominion is going to be around for some time, watch this film before it leaves the theater forever! big screens is where you can truly experience the spectacle of the jet sequences and the mission and battle at the end to the fullest.

seriously, you don't have to be a jet fan, or army fan, or fan of anything to enjoy this film. you will love it!

top gun has been one of my top 10 movies since roughly 1988, and i've wanted a sequel for so long. so when it was announced that it was being filmed, my excitement levels were on overdrive. however, i genuinely never thought the sequel would outdo the original. how wrong i was! it was 100% worth the wait, even when covid got in the way of its original release date. my husband and i had goosebumps as the opening song began, and from start to finish my emotions were all over the place. goose's son, bradley (rooster), couldn't have been portrayed better than by miles teller. the similarities between them, are what makes the character of rooster so believable. having him playing the piano and singing 'great balls of fire', was both heartbreaking, and a well thought out way to completely cement their connection. especially when maverick has the flashback to the last time they were all together, and bradley (rooster) was sitting on top of the piano, singing with his dad. i also loved that they both 'spoke to goose', to help them get through any intense moments, and that they ended up flying together, with rooster doing what his dad did. their on screen relationship was electric - one cares unequivocally for one, the other is intensely angry at him, and when maverick says he won't tell rooster that it was his mum's dying request, and he'd rather rooster be angry at him and not his mum, is such a beautiful and sad moment. he loves him like a father would, and you get to see how rooster's feelings towards maverick changes, and how maverick finally sees rooster as an equal, and not the boy he once knew. the acting by all cast members is of an extremely high calibre, the story itself is extremely well written, and the mission has your heart racing with you sitting on the edge of your seat. it was definitely better than the one in the original. also, seeing val kilmer as ice man, really was the perfect touch. it's a film for everyone - a story of strength, power struggles, great flying scenes, heartache, saving lives, love, pride, faith (not religious), trust, and tom cruise still manages a flyby. the gratuitous beach football scene, is one not to be missed - if half naked, muscular/well defined men bonding, is your cup of tea. i certainly wasn't complaining... it's a movie to watch more than once, and the all the feels will still be there. 10/10 from me, my husband, and our children.

in my mid forties now and not many movies excite me anymore. but this, this is way, way more than i had hoped for. i haven't felt this excited watching an action movie in a long time. this is how action movies should be made and many thanks (again) to tom for bringing it to us. sincerely hope future generations of actors and moviemakers learn from this one.

lastly, i do have one bone to pick. maverick's ending dialogue to rooster should have been "you did well. i'm proud of you", which is what we as fans want to say to tom and everyone else involved in making top gun maverick one of the best sequels ever.

do you know how you can easily tell if a movie is awesome?

you know movie is truly great when you want to watch it over and over again every year whether by yourself or with your friends and family.

top gun maverick (tgm) is the kind of movie that you will want to watch over and over and over again every year either by yourself or with your friends and family.

the formula for a great novel/story/tv/movie is the same. you must have a great setting, character development, plot, climax, resolution. we learned all this back when we were kids in school.

now the plot can be simple and straightforward, but it can still be good. it needs to be clear and not confusing as hell.

tgm has all these elements. it's directed by joseph kosinski, whom i think is one of the smartest directors. no wonder tgm is such a awesome movie.

in terms of story, tgm has more story than tg. basically tgm has more of everything- more action, more story, just more.

which movie is better? it's difficult to beat nostalgia. tg was 30 years ago when many of us were just kids. and that's what tg was about - kids.

now tgm is about being adults.

it's a tough call, but i would say that tgm is better than tg in every way, except for the nostalgia factor.

after 36 years, tom cruise reprises his role as pete "maverick" mitchell where his iconic character continues to push the envelope as a test pilot and then becomes an instructor to a new generation of fighter pilots. everything about top gun: maverick is sublime from the script to the breathtaking cinematography and aerial sequences with no cgi or green screen that would keep fans on the edge of their seats. i believe tom cruise, joseph kosinski, christopher mcquarrie, jennifer connelly and the entire cast have done a brilliant job and it is worth the wait. top gun: maverick belongs on the big screen and it'll take your breath away.

there is an unspoken rule that sequels are almost always worse than the original, and, as you might expect, maverick breaks that rule with style.

this movie is a throw back to a time when most of the people involved in making a movie were in the business of entertainment and storytelling. it's fun, it's gripping, it's awesome. practical effects return to show how much better they can be than soulless cgi. legacy characters are respected and developed rather than being torn down. the audience is entertained rather than preached to or lectured.

movies like this have become an endangered species, and until bankruptcy starves out the media industry's current ideological infection, they are not likely to come along often. so, if you haven't already, treat yourself to this masterpiece, spend a couple of hours being reminded of what good storytelling can bring to the table, and enjoy that rarest of treats: a sequel that actually builds on and surpasses what made you love the original.

tom cruise rarley fails to impress whenever he's working in an action blockbuster and he always gives it his all. i was excited when i heard that this movie was being made, since it has been ages since i've seen a movie about jet fighters and dogfights since, well the origional.

i was also worried that this movie would not be able to live up to the charm of the original top gun. being over 35 years since that movie, i felt that this sequel would have been diluted or even had flopped because of the sheer amount of time it took for it to get made. but i can assure you that if your fearful that this will not live up to the 1986 film, put them to bed, because this is exceedingly better in every aspect that it is awe inspiring. of course the technicality would be superior since this is not the 80s anymore and filmmakers have so much more at their disposal now, but the thing about this movie is staggeringly practical!

what really helps this movie is that tom cruise is now a real life fully licensed fighter pilot, meaning that all the shots of him in the cockpit are real, not chroma keyed. i'm not sure if this was true for the rest of the actors, i think they were passengers behind the camera. it has incredible directing with shots that are wide, fluid and clear. no shaky cam or jarring and ammeter editing. it's always clear and easy to understand what is going on during the flight scenes which is amazing. this would have been so easy to screw up, but the dedication by joseph kosinski and his team was truly noteworthy.

miles teller was definitely a standout actor in this movie too, i've enjoyed all the roles he has been in and he certainly doesn't disappoint here. the story is great too, it doesn't feel forced or shoehorned in even a bit, and is such an incredible balance of delivering the right amount of fanservice and nostalgia aswell as giving something new and fresh with the updated technology.

top gun: maverick soars back onto the big screen with a bang, delivering an adrenaline-fueled sequel that captures the essence of the '80s classic. as a fan of the original film, i was skeptical about whether this follow-up could live up to the iconic status of its predecessor. however, i'm thrilled to report that top gun 2 not only lives up to expectations but surpasses them, offering a thrilling spectacle of aerial action, heartfelt drama, and nostalgic charm.

tom cruise reprises his role as the charismatic pete "maverick" mitchell, reminding us once again why he's the master of on-screen charisma. cruise effortlessly slips back into the cockpit, radiating maverick's passion for speed and his unwavering dedication to his craft. it's a testament to his acting prowess that he can still captivate audiences after all these years, infusing the character with a mix of humor, vulnerability, and undeniable charm.

joining cruise in this high-flying adventure is miles teller, who portrays goose's son, a talented pilot known as rooster. teller brings a fresh energy to the film, embodying the same cockiness and determination that made his father such a memorable character. the dynamic between maverick and rooster adds an emotional layer to the story, as the torch is passed from one generation to the next.

director joseph kosinski and cinematographer claudio miranda deserve accolades for their masterful work in capturing the essence of the original film's visual style. from the iconic flight deck sequences to the breathtaking aerial maneuvers, every frame feels authentic and exhilarating. the decision to use practical effects and real aircrafts further immerses the audience in the heart-pounding action, creating a genuine sense of awe and excitement.

while top gun: maverick pays homage to its predecessor, it also charts its own course, introducing new characters and storylines that blend seamlessly with the established universe. the film strikes a careful balance between nostalgia and innovation, offering fans plenty of callbacks and easter eggs while still delivering a fresh and engaging narrative.

jennifer connelly delivers a standout performance as maverick's love interest, infusing the film with a touch of romance and vulnerability. her chemistry with cruise is palpable, and their rekindled connection adds an emotional anchor amidst the adrenaline-fueled sequences.

the film is not without its flaws. the plot may feel familiar at times, echoing the original film's structure and themes. additionally, the stakes don't always feel as immediate or urgent as in the first installment, which might be attributed to the younger generation of pilots lacking the same gravitas as their predecessors. nevertheless, these minor shortcomings do little to dampen the overall enjoyment of the film.

top gun: maverick may not be a thought-provoking war film, but it never claims to be. it's an unabashed popcorn action movie that celebrates the thrill of flying and the camaraderie among pilots. the movie's focus on real stunts and practical effects, coupled with tom cruise's unwavering dedication to the role, creates an exhilarating cinematic experience that will leave audiences on the edge of their seats.

in conclusion, top gun: maverick is a triumphant sequel that pays homage to its roots while forging its own path. it's a rollercoaster ride of nostalgia, heart-pounding action, and charismatic performances. so buckle up, embrace the need for speed, and get ready to take flight with maverick once again. this film is a must-watch for fans of the original and anyone seeking an adrenaline rush at the movies. i give it a solid 9/10, as it proves that even after decades, top gun still knows how to deliver blockbuster entertainment.

the opening text mentions how in 1969, the u. s. navy established a school for fighter pilots. it is officially referred to as fighter weapons school, but the recruits call it "top gun". we see several recruits and navy men on the ships where the pilots take off or make their returns.

captain pete "maverick" mitchell (tom cruise) rides his motorcycle to a base where he is set for a scramjet flight demonstration, but he is told that rear admiral chester "hammer" cain (ed harris) is on his way to shut the program down to redirect funds elsewhere. not feeling deterred, maverick takes the jet just as cain arrives, and he flies it into the sky, taking it past its original mach 9 projection and hitting mach 10, to the delight of the crew. however, maverick tries to take it faster and ends up wrecking the jet, but he manages to eject in time.

cain chews maverick out for his actions, but while he wants to have maverick grounded, cain instead informs him that he has been called back to nas north island by his former rival/colleague, admiral tom "iceman" kazansky (val kilmer). maverick heads to the base to meet vice admiral beau "cyclone" simpson (jon hamm) and rear admiral solomon "warlock" bates (charles parnell). cyclone makes it clear that he doesn't see in maverick whatever ice sees in him, but he informs maverick of the task at hand. a rogue nation is operation a uranium facility, and maverick must teach a new group of recruits to find a way to make it to the base and bomb it.

maverick goes to a bar where he reunites with penny benjamin (jennifer connelly), an ex-girlfriend that he left a while ago, which pissed off her admiral father. she bears no ill will toward maverick, but she ends up making him pay a round for everyone at the bar. at the same bar, the new class of pilots are there to drink. among them is hotshot jake "hangman" seresin (glen powell), who sees himself as the most likely to lead the new class. there is also natasha "phoenix" trace (monica barbaro), robert "bob" floyd (lewis pullman), reuben "payback" fitch (jay ellis), and mickey "fanboy" garcia (danny ramirez). entering moments later is bradley "rooster" bradshaw (miles teller), son of maverick's late best friend goose. after maverick's card declines, penny has hangman and payback playfully throw maverick out. outside, maverick watches rooster playing the piano and is reminded of goose, but maverick still feels guilt over goose's death.

maverick later meets with the pilots to introduce himself and go over the mission. since the facility is located deep at the bottom of a canyon, maverick's plan to take it out involves having two jets destroy the entrance to the facility before hitting the base itself. some of the pilots aren't onboard, like hangman. rooster resents maverick because he pulled rooster's application and set his career back by four years. maverick then goes on with the dogfight exercises with the pilots, showing off his skills to mess with the younger crew. the pilots that fail their exercises are forced to do push-ups. later on, hangman discovers rooster's connection to maverick.

maverick goes back to the bar to pay penny back what he owes her. he then spends the afternoon on her boat with her, and there is clearly still a spark between them.

in the next round of exercises, maverick explains to the pilots about how they may lose oxygen and consciousness if they fly too high, reminded them of how high and low they will need to go when they carry out their mission. during the exercise, rooster is shown to utilize a more cautious approach in his flying. hangman brings up maverick's friendship with goose, which provokes rooster into nearly attacking hangman, but the other pilots split them up.

ice requests maverick go visit him. he is suffering from throat cancer and can mainly communicate through a computer. maverick expresses his concern over working with rooster, fearing that something will happen to him like with goose. ice tells him he must work closely with rooster, and he manages to speak to maverick and tell him that the young pilots need him more than he realizes.

cyclone steps out onto the runway to find that nobody is there. he finds that maverick brought the pilots over to the beach to play volleyball as a bonding exercise, which appears to work since they are all having fun. maverick later goes out with penny and tells her that he pulled rooster's application because his mother asked maverick to look after him before she passed away.

the pilots then undergo a training exercise to strike the target at a certain altitude and in a certain amount of time. everyone fails to complete the task as needed, with phoenix needing to eject before her jet crashes. maverick chastises rooster for how he handles his exercise, leading to them arguing over maverick hindering rooster's flying career. they are interrupted when warlock comes in to inform them that ice has died. a funeral is held for him days later, with maverick, penny, and the other pilots in attendance.

cyclone decides to take over instructional duties from maverick. when he proposes an alternative plan, the other pilots seem to question him. outside, the radars detect maverick flying his jet to complete the exercise, where he is able to fire at the target on the ground with seconds to spare, impressing all the pilots, including hangman.

the mission is carried out, with maverick picking rooster as his wingman, and being joined by hangman, phoenix, fanboy, payback, and bob. they fly toward the facility, with their nearby aircraft carrier firing tomahawk missiles at the base to destroy the runway, causing enemy jets to scramble back toward the target. they manage to launch a missile and destroy the facility, but the enemy sends more pilots after them. the pilots start to fly back, but maverick's jet is shot at, causing him to crash.

rooster turns around and goes to save maverick. a chopper begins firing at maverick while he is on foot, but rooster shoots it down, just before his own jet is shot down, but he manages to eject himself in time. maverick and rooster reunite and devise a plan to get out of there. they spot an f-14 tomcat and take control of it. they start to fly away and are pursued by enemy jets, leading to a dogfight. although maverick manages to take two of them out with bullets and flares, they run out of weaponry just as a third jet comes their way. rooster is also unable to eject himself, so the two accept that they are about to die until hangman comes through and destroys the last jet.

maverick and rooster make it back to the carrier, where their crew congratulates them. rooster and hangman have a newfound respect for one another, while rooster looks at maverick the same way his father looked at him.

rooster helps maverick work on a p-51 mustang in maverick's hangar. penny shows up, and maverick takes her for a flight in his plane. rooster sets down a photo of himself and maverick right next to an older photo of maverick and goose.

it's not often that i'll call a movie 'perfect' but top gun maverick is a perfect movie. even more impressive, it joins a club of very rare movies whose sequels are actually better than their classic originals.

as far as returning cast, val kilmer does so much with so little and leaves an indelible mark on the movie; likely his last.

charles parnell's warlock and bashir salahuddin's hondo were great additions to the continuing story and played wonderfully alongside tom cruise, adding levity and sincerity with precision.

jennifer connolly is simply stunning and endearing as maverick's love interest. how she manages to look better with each passing year... one of life's greatest mysteries *wink wink*

the young top gun class is as vibrant as they are diverse and echo the original class mightily. their similarities are not hackneyed however, as said similarities allow us to see them through maverick's lens as instructor, which informs his evolution and self-awareness. watching the original movie recently certainly helps with this.

miles teller shows again why he's one of the best actors of his generation. his range is on full display here and there are moments where he remarkably captures the essence of anthony edwards' goose.

this movie has everything... drama, love, nostalgia, action, comedy, wit, tear-jerking... i mean, everything!

the subtlety with which the nostalgia is dealt with is the masterstroke. many directors/writers try to pack too much in, especially with massive gaps between installments... some get so caught up in wanting to recapture the spirit of the original that they end up doing an accidental remake; not this movie... as i said, it's perfect.

run, don't walk, to the theaters to catch this on the big screen! it's definitely worth it!

our rose-colored glasses make us yearn for simpler times. but were they really simpler? a drug epidemic, political turmoil, russian aggression...are we talking about the 80's or today? although the cinematic enemy goes nameless, this film feels like it is retelling a true story. delayed by the covid-19 pandemic, its release seems to align with current affairs in a way that couldn't be more intentional, if not for the pure happenstance that pushed back the release.

this film does not miss a beat. literally from the word "go" you are thrust into a whimsical world of nostalgia competing for screen time against a modern day instant classic. this piece is a well calibrated dance that does not leave you feeling duped. it has all the hallmarks of past action films that we miss, such as cheesy humor, cocky characters, and the music that makes it all so beautifully palatable.

from the title screen you're introduced to the aging pete "maverick" mitchell who looks phenomenal for his age. wearing his archetypal outfit to include the white t shirt, denim jeans and that iconic bomber jacket. he unveils the classic kawasaki bike and makes his way into work. it looks as if nothing has changed in 36 years!

maverick is now a test pilot for the us navy. he wastes no time at all getting into trouble as he deliberately disobeys orders to remain grounded on a upcoming test flight. this series of events sees him reprimanded by his chain of command. as it all looks dim for captain mitchell, an unlikely set of orders saves him from ucmj uncertainty. he gets word that in lieu of traditional punishment, he has instead been reassigned by orders from a specter of his past: iceman, who is now an admiral.

upon arrival to the top gun facilities pete is greeted by a whirlwind of emotions. he walks into his own shadow; of the past he shared with his classmates, including his deceased friend goose. maverick now faces the prospect of teaching among many other pilots, goose's son, rooster. old wounds, old flames, and old memories come together and pit pete against his own wishes. with only a matter of weeks maverick has to cultivate a team of top performing top gun grads into a well oiled strike force in order to eliminate a growing nuclear threat.

the film is a corny 80s classic that so many of us love mixed with a well-shot modern masterpiece. it is full throttle fan service for the older crowd with callbacks and nods to the previous film, but it is also a great introduction for a new generation to cling to. you are given the same maverick/iceman type of rivalry, along with a feast of other young alphas who undertook the role with no doubt in mind what was being asked of them.

sequels have a reputation for not living up to their predecessors. sometimes they're hyped up too much for the sake of ticket sales. from a fan of the original film, take it from me. this film might be better than the original. it closes chapters that you never felt were left open. it has a few good laughs, and honestly it almost made me cry. for every predictable thing that comes to be, there's another one that is unexpected. this film is an instant classic and should be viewed while it is still showing in theaters. i highly recommend watching it in imax or a dolby certified theater. it will be great on dvd/blue ray, but you'll never understand it the way it was meant to be unless you watch it in a theater!

top gun: maverick delivers on the promise of its title, soaring into the stratosphere of action cinema with breathtaking aerial sequences and a surprisingly heartfelt story. tom cruise, as ever, is a force of nature, effortlessly embodying the rebellious spirit of maverick while showcasing his unparalleled commitment to real-life stunt work. the film masterfully blends nostalgia with fresh thrills, paying homage to the original while forging its own path.

**what works:**

* **stunning visuals:** the aerial combat sequences are nothing short of spectacular, pushing the boundaries of what's possible in filmmaking. the sheer intensity and realism will leave you breathless.

* **emotional depth:** beneath the high-octane action lies a surprisingly poignant story about legacy, redemption, and the bonds of brotherhood. maverick's journey is both thrilling and emotionally resonant.

* **strong supporting cast:** the supporting cast is excellent, with miles teller particularly shining as rooster, the son of maverick's deceased best friend.

overall: top gun: maverick is a must-see for fans of the original and action enthusiasts alike. it's a thrilling, visually stunning, and surprisingly emotional experience that will leave you wanting more. **10/10**

this was the most exhilarating theatrical experience i'd ever had the pleasure of being a part of. top gun: maverick outdoes top gun in every conceivable way, and is the single best legacy sequel of all time, bar none.

the premise revolves around an aging maverick, who is called yet again to instruct new recruits at top gun.

joseph kosinski does a masterful job of directing this movie. he puts in just enough elements of the original to retain adequate nostalgia, but not too much so as to overpower the potence of the sequel. a lot of legacy sequels like ghostbusters: afterlife and the matrix resurrections make the deplorable mistake of adding way too much callbacks and references to the previous movies; so much so that the sequel itself feels more like a lazy rehash than a worthy continuation and/or conclusion. the movie corrects many of the original's problems, with a more grounded premise and graver performances. fighter weapons school finally feels like an actual military academy rather than a mere high school for adrenaline junkies.

tom cruise is quite literally the greatest movie star of all time. he's starred in classics since he was in his 20s and is still pumping out his best stuff, as proven by this movie alone. i love how his character of pete mitchell has expectedly grown more nuanced and complex over the last 30+ years. he appears tortured by events from the first movie, and his dynamic with bradley bradshaw (cast and played excellently by miles teller) is undoubtedly the film's most riveting aspect.

jennifer connelly has an astonishing amount of chemistry with cruise, and i don't think people give their on-screen relationship enough credit. once again, the childish romance from the original was greatly improved upon, with a moderately approached but genuinely heartfelt new relationship. i love the way val kilmer reprised his role as iceman, and the few short scenes he was in did the actor justice and gave his character a truly beautiful role to play.

the filmmakers somehow succeeded in making the new recruits to top gun interesting characters by themselves, instead of just cloning the original movie's cast. monica barbaro, lewis pullman and jay ellis all give distinguished performances, and so does glen powell (even though he's technically this sequel's version of a young iceman). other pedigreed actors like jon hamm and ed harris, and lesser known ones like charles parnell all play their characters in memorable fashion.

maverick is also absolutely hilarious, and i can probably remember about 15 times when the audience around me burst into hysterical laughter (including myself, no doubt). the dialogue is unexpectedly smart, the jokes feel anything but forced, and the scenes of humour are so well set-up that they never feel manufactured or out of place.

but of course, what really sets this movie apart from and above other legacy sequels is its brilliant writing. the screenplay packs so much emotional punch and payoff that it's virtually impossible to unpack all of it even in a single spoiler review. the callbacks and moments of nostalgia are never in there for the sake of it, and strictly serve the plot. every single narrative decision made for this film was perfect, with a believable and realistic story that is unexpectedly mature and thus way more engaging.

with all that out of the way, it wouldn't be a proper top gun review if you didn't talk about the action. and jesus christ does this film have some of the most astoundingly intense and mind-bogglingly entertaining action sequences in film history. seriously, the final act alone is on par with any of the recent mission: impossible movies (also starrimg cruise), and even mad max: fury road.

maverick veritably dethrones the original movie's all time greatest aerial fight scenes with even better ones. the cinematography, visual effects, editing and soul-shattering sound design during the training and dogfight sequences is so incredible it can barely be put into words. some segments of this film were so edge-of-your-seat thrilling that i'm surprised no one (especially me) got a heart attack or at the very least, passed out.

the end product is so well presented, it's rather difficult to pinpoint where the cgi ends and tom cruise's stuntwork begins (although, knowing him, i'm willing to bet he played his part in some of the stunning aircraft-mounted shots).

on top of that, the production of the non-action scenes was done well too, just like in the original. i certainly enjoyed the restrained use of the first films music and score, incorporating some pretty good original songs like "i ain't worried" by onerepublic and lady gaga's spectacular "hold my hand".

top gun: maverick exceeded all expectations by a light year and a half. it is the type of legacy sequel every classic blockbuster deserves, and the monumental sendoff all legacy sequels aspire to become.

and if it isn't also one of the century's best action movies, then i have no idea what is.

edit: so apparently none of the flight sequences used green screen, and the actors went through flight training to film all those insane shots practically. can i love this movie any more?!

top gun: maverick, directed by joseph kosinski, delivers a soaring return to the skies, eclipsing the legacy of its predecessor with thrilling aerial action and a poignant exploration of legacy, honour, and redemption. set more than three decades after the original top gun, the film follows pete "maverick" mitchell (tom cruise) as he trains a new generation of elite pilots for a perilous mission. with its breathtaking visuals, remarkable practical effects, and a performance that captures the essence of maverick, top gun: maverick is a captivating and emotionally resonant experience that elevates the franchise to new heights.

tom cruise delivers a standout performance, embodying maverick's fearless, rebellious spirit while adding layers of depth that showcase his character's growth over the years. cruise expertly balances the physicality and vulnerability of maverick, portraying him as a man grappling with his past and navigating the complexities of mentorship. the emotional core of the film is further strengthened by the chemistry between cruise and miles teller, who plays bradley "rooster" bradshaw, the son of maverick's late friend goose. their dynamic adds a powerful layer of emotional depth, underpinned by themes of friendship, forgiveness, and loyalty.

kosinski's direction heightens the impact of top gun: maverick with awe-inspiring visuals and meticulously crafted aerial sequences that immerse the audience in the heart-pounding action. the use of practical effects and real-life flight footage creates a sense of realism and intensity that is rarely seen in action films, allowing viewers to feel as though they are experiencing the high-speed manoeuvres and dogfights firsthand. the cinematography, which captures both the vast expanse of the skies and the intimate intensity of close combat, further enhances the film's visceral appeal. the score, featuring contributions from harold faltermeyer and hans zimmer, provides an epic, nostalgic backdrop that complements the film's adrenaline-fueled pace.

beyond its spectacular action, top gun: maverick honours its origins while expanding on the original's themes of camaraderie and courage. the film's focus on maverick's personal journey-balancing his role as a mentor with his need to reconcile with his past-imbues the narrative with emotional depth, allowing it to resonate beyond the spectacle. by blending nostalgia with fresh perspectives, top gun: maverick stands as a powerful, self-contained story that speaks to audiences across generations.

in conclusion, top gun: maverick is an exhilarating, emotionally rich sequel that combines spectacular action with a heartfelt narrative, capturing the essence of what made the original iconic. with its dynamic performances, breathtaking visuals, and poignant storytelling, it stands as one of the year's most exhilarating cinematic experiences.

after more than three decades, top gun: maverick not only delivers a worthy sequel to the 1986 classic but surpasses it in nearly every way. with breathtaking aerial sequences, emotional depth, and a powerful performance from tom cruise, this film is an unforgettable cinematic experience that balances nostalgia with fresh storytelling.

the story follows pete "maverick" mitchell, who, despite his legendary status, is still pushing the limits as a navy test pilot. when he's called back to train an elite group of top gun graduates for a dangerous mission, he must confront his past-especially his complicated relationship with rooster (miles teller), the son of his late best friend, goose. this emotional core drives the film, making it much more than just an action-packed thrill ride.

one of top gun: maverick's greatest strengths is its ability to blend heart-pounding action with genuine emotion. the practical aerial stunts are nothing short of breathtaking, with cruise and the cast undergoing real-life flight training to ensure authenticity. every dogfight and high-speed maneuver feels intense, putting the audience right in the cockpit. the minimal use of cgi enhances the realism, making it one of the most visually spectacular films in recent years.

beyond the action, the film delivers a heartfelt narrative about legacy, loss, and redemption. maverick's interactions with rooster are filled with tension and emotion, creating a compelling father-son dynamic that gives the film depth. the inclusion of val kilmer as iceman adds another emotional layer, making for one of the film's most touching moments.

the supporting cast, including glen powell as the cocky but skilled hangman, adds new energy to the film. jennifer connelly's penny provides a grounded romantic subplot without overshadowing the main story. the balance between old and new characters is handled brilliantly, respecting the legacy of the original while paving the way for the future.

the film's soundtrack, featuring an epic score by hans zimmer and lady gaga's emotional song hold my hand, enhances every moment, making the experience even more powerful.

final verdict: top gun: maverick is more than just a sequel-it's a cinematic event. with stunning visuals, an emotionally charged story, and a career-defining performance from tom cruise, it's a film that makes you feel proud, nostalgic, and exhilarated all at once. a perfect 10/10 blockbuster that demands to be seen on the biggest screen possible!

"top gun: maverick" is the long-awaited sequel to the 1986 film "top gun," which starred tom cruise as pete "maverick" mitchell, a young naval aviator who is sent to top gun, the navy's elite fighter weapons school.

the sequel, set 34 years after the original film, stars tom cruise once again as maverick, now a flight instructor at top gun. the film also stars miles teller, glen powell, and jennifer connelly.

the movie takes place decades after the original film, and follows maverick as he faces the challenges of modern air combat, including the use of unmanned drones.

maverick is also mentoring a new generation of pilots, including teller's character, bradley bradshaw, the son of his late wingman nick "goose" bradshaw, who died in the first film.

the film's visuals are stunning, with breathtaking aerial footage and state-of-the-art special effects. the dogfight scenes are particularly impressive, with a level of realism that immerses the viewer in the action. the sound design is also impressive, with the roar of fighter jets filling the theater.

the movie has a good pacing and keeps the audience engaged throughout. it also has a decent storyline which is a combination of nostalgic feeling and new perspectives. the interactions between the characters are well-written, adding depth to the film.

tom cruise delivers another strong performance as maverick, showing the character's growth and maturity over the years. he is surrounded by a talented supporting cast, with miles teller in particular delivering a standout performance as bradshaw.

overall, "top gun: maverick" is a thrilling and visually stunning film that is sure to delight fans of the original. it's an action-packed film that will keep you on the edge of your seat with its high-speed dogfight scenes and state-of-the-art special effects.

it also has a good balance of nostalgia and new elements that keeps the audience engaged. despite some of the cliche and predictability, it's still a well-made and entertaining movie.

what make this top gun better than the original is the human element of it. the ice man (val kilmer) scene is sad and emotional. i teared up watching it. and the relationship with rooster (goose's son) is a big part of the story. lastly, i find his relationship with penny is loving and genuine. it is funny to see maverick doesn't know how to sail as a navy man. it makes maverick a human. plus the fact penny has a teenage daughter give us a view what maverick life will be like after retirement.

did top gun: maverick meet my expectations? yes it did and i'm so glad i got to experience it at the cinema, it has to be one of the best cinema experiences i've ever had. the big reason being tom cruise who served as producer along with returning as pete "maverick" mitchell. at the insistence of tom cruise, there are minimal green screen and cgi aerial shots in the film, and even the close up cockpit shots are taken during real in-flight sequences. this meant that much of the cast had to undergo extensive g-force training sessions, to withstand the physical demands of the g-force pressures during flights. that's the main reason why the experience was so epic, the jet sequences were top notch and sounded perfect. overall, top gun: maverick is superior to its predecessor in every way. with the aerial flight sequences and emotional weight being better by miles. i also need to praise the cinematography, it was visually a stunning looking movie.

after more than thirty years of service as one of the navy's top aviators, pete mitchell is where he belongs, pushing the envelope as a courageous test pilot and dodging the advancement in rank that would ground him.

the cast includes many well known and recognizable actors, names like: miles teller, jennifer connelly, jon hamm, glen powell, lewis pullman, ed harris and val kilmer.

top gun: maverick was directed by joseph kosinski and written by ehren kruger, eric warren singer, and christopher mcquarrie, from a story by peter craig and justin marks. i found the writing to be such an improvement than the previous film, with it feeling more mature and just succeeding better with its themes. the direction was also quite great. the sound design, musical score and soundtrack was brilliant, the two latter ones being what made the first top gun iconic. with songs like danger zone returning, the addition of slow ride and won't get fooled again is used perfectly. the editing is another highlight.

though the film is similar to other action movies, maybe too similar to the first top gun. i still feel like it was an unforgettable experience and extremely entertaining, and at the end of the viewing, my high expectations were met. tom cruise was the reason this film worked for me, making the first film to have actors flying and doing all the aerial sequences. just wow. tom cruise personally designed a 3-month aviation training course for the new actors to become ready to handle riding in an f-18. it made the film stand out like no other film. another thing that stood out was how it was shot entirely on imax-certified sony venice 6k full frame cameras, specially developed for the film in order to shoot the cockpit sequences. top gun: maverick will most likely go down in history as a box office hit and also a brilliant action film.

highly recommended this movie, imo you couldn't have done better the actors where great, the details in the movie where pretty much spot on. like the subtle skunk works signage on the prototype aircraft. scattering of laughs thrown in made it also great. loved seeing some of the legacies for the old top gun. great work tom...!

nothing i would change about this movie. absolutely amazing. movie of the year!!! i understand why tom cruise decided to run it back and give it his all. the actors that were chosen for the characters were spot on, storyline was entertaining, and miles teller has grown into a phenomenal actor and had nearly a role that was just perfect for him. i'm not getting my hopes up but i would love to see the top gun franchise expand and make more movies. maybe maverick can pass the torch down to rooster and top gun can continue. people have no idea the amount of work put into this film. so much greatness in one movie. may be one of my top 5 movies of all time.

nominations for best picture, director, and best actor (tom). it might pull off those last three, but it lacks the wokeness that hollywood seems to love and cater to. this is a new classic that has surpassed the original 1986 film. it keeps the feeling and look that tony scott gave us, and matured it like a fine wine. screenplay and direction made this work, a rarity for a sequel. the dialogue is tight, as well as the camera focus on the actors. the aerial shots and dog fights are incredibly well done - whatever cgi was utilized blended seemlessly into the background with the live action. the love story between penny (jennifer connelly) and maverick was mature and believable, nothing gratuitous about it. there's enough homage paid to the original to remind us again why we loved the 1986 film, without depending on it too heavily to justify the current version. i will say that the first 2/3rds of the film were perfectly crafted, in the best film category, but the last 1/3rd at times stretched credibility to where i said "no way" at least twice. pretty dramatic shift in the action. but overall an amazing storyline well worth the wait. it's a roller-coaster ride of entertainment that almost everyone will enjoy. go see it.

when i first saw the trailer for top gun: maverick over 2 years ago i was really excited and was hoping it would at least meet my expectations. of course it was delayed like a lot of films because of covid but the hype machine has been in full overdrive for the last couple of months. well for me and seems for most people the wait was worth it. i just saw it today and it met and in some ways exceeded my pretty high expectations!!! the story is simple just like the original but as with it coming so many years after their needed to be more drama and true in to some of the conflicts in the first film. of course maverick if still a captain in the navy but still loves flying and breaking the rules. it's really not a spoiler but maverick is called back to top gun to train some new hot shot pilots for a very dangerous real world mission. he is actually called back by his old nemesis/friend "iceman" played of course by val kilmer. and also something that was already know is that val kilmer would be back for this film. his presence is really effective in this film. in fact he is part of what is the best scene in either of the top gun films. the main part of the story is that one of the pilots that called to top gun is bradley "rooster" bradshaw. the son of goose, maverick's rear and best friend who died in the first film. rooster is played by miles teller. he has conflict with maverick about things in that past that held his career back. maverick tried to protect him and he lost opportunities in the navy and rooster resents him. it isnt hight sophisticated drama but this film dies pay more attention to the emotional parts of the story more the the first film.

of course the aerial action in the film is spectacular. there was obviously slot more budget for this film so the flight scenes are longer and more complex visually. like the first film most of the action was done with real jets but this one does have some cgi involved but the they work. i will say that even though they are like the first film they arent a fast cut and frenetic. tony scott didn't have the budget for longer scenes so he replied more on fast editing and the soundtrack to create the sense of speed and danger. this time director joseph kosinski does much of the same but the scenes are longer and more elaborate.

the truth is that the success of the film hinges on it's star tom cruise. and he delivers. his performance is very good. even though he i almost 60 the guy looks as young as the actually younger cast members in the film. he is just a movie star. he is one of the last true hollywood movie stars he might be a kind of crazy character in real life but he is just one of those actors with the star power to carry a film. he does here

even though the film relies on our nostalgia for the first film it isn't all just a carbon copy. . there are call backs to the first film but because the new aspects of this sequel mostly work i really enjoyed the winks to the original.

"top gun: maverick" is the sequel to "top gun" that i always wanted, but until now, never had - it's truly perfect. i can't believe they were able to pull this off; not only did they make a film that lives up to the original, but i would also argue that there are many elements that surpass the first film. i love the original movie from 1986, but this in my opinion is a much stronger film! it's thrilling, intense, and surprisingly emotional, the film has a lot of heart. the opening scene alone, which parallels the original's opening in such an awesome way, was pretty much a religious experience for me, and i'm sure it would be for any fans of the original. right off the bat i had a huge smile on my face, and that smile continued throughout the entire movie! it's exactly what i wanted it to be, and yet so much more. a truly epic, supersonic, exhilarating blockbuster!

one of the things i really loved here was the story! it was the perfect continuation of the first film, and i loved how it truly dealt with the emotional fallout of events from that film. it felt like this was truly bringing maverick's story to an end, especially in the guilt he has for the death of goose. i love how goose was used in this film, and how that internal conflict inside of maverick led to such an interesting dynamic between himself and goose's son, rooster, who is now one of maverick's students. without saying too much, i loved how their relationship evolved throughout the film, how it both left them confronting their feelings about the loss of goose and how this inevitably brought them together. i wasn't as much into the relationship between penny and maverick, as this felt like it just sort of happened to check a box, but it was entertaining nonetheless. the film also deviated a lot more than i thought it would from the original story, i liked that it really showed us something new instead of just rehashing the original. don't get me wrong, it has some great nostalgic moments, but these are done sparingly and just enough to get a reaction out of the audience without detracting from the current story. in some cases, the use of a nostalgic element actually seemed to enhance emotional moments for the characters, and i loved that. i was also pretty excited to see there was an actual mission the story was building up to this time, and let me just say the 3rd act does not disappoint! i was on the edge of my seat the whole time, and i loved how intense it was and how much it kept me on the edge of my seat, yet showed me everything i really wanted to see in this movie! (also is it just me or was there a moment that felt like a top gun version of a star wars scene?)

and oh my god... the aerial sequences here are unbelievable! i've never seen anything quite like it, and i don't think we ever will again. not only is the sheer talent of the pilots of the jets on display here, but i'm amazed that the filmmakers were able to get the footage they did. shots where the cameras are mounted to the plane, or even inside the cockpit are just jaw dropping and really enhance the intensity of scenes. this truly is a spectacular visual experience (it looks stunning in imax) and i'm so happy they committed to doing everything for real. trust me, you can tell the actors are in the jets as you see their genuine reactions and the ways their faces react to the gs. tom cruise somehow handles it like a pro, he's truly a madman but i love his commitment to the theatrical experience. it's like tom cruise just became maverick in this movie, he looks like he's having a blast in all the dogfights and aerial sequences. he also looks like he hasn't aged a day, and fits right in with his younger co-stars in the beach football scene. i also loved the emotion he displayed in this, it's what truly makes me think this is one of his career best performances! miles teller was also perfectly cast as goose's son, he really looks the part, but also played off of tom cruise so well (just like his on-screen dad) and really sold the emotions his character is feeling. and while on the topic of actors, val kilmer has one stunning scene as iceman that truly was so perfect and heartfelt that i was nearly in tears, i loved that scene more than anything.

tony scott would be proud of this film. i thought joseph kosinski did a spectacular job taking over as director for this sequel, and really crafted such a great film. it's a little more mature and emotional than the first, which i loved, but also way more intense and visceral. it's such a unique cinematic experience, one that deserves the biggest screen with the loudest sound! i loved the visuals, especially in the jaw dropping aerial sequences, and the sound design packed a punch, on top of using some of the great music from the first one! "danger zone" is here, and it's as good as ever! this movie was insanely good, it's everything i wanted it to be and more! i adore the first film, but this managed to surpass it in every way. it's wildly entertaining, exhilarating and heartfelt! i truly loved it and highly recommend seeing this, it's a must see if only for the stunning cinematography and once in a lifetime visuals on display. it exceeded all my expectations, "top gun: maverick" really is a blast; it took my breath away! it's one of those rare flicks that reminds you how incredible a movie-going experience can be!

*if you don't like the original (but how could you not, it's amazing), this is much better.

**if you love the original... this is still much, much better!

top gun maverick: pete mitchell returns as a aviator he has been tasked with a rather impossible mission and train elite graduates across the country to successfully execute it.

with legacy and tom cruise as the criterion, the movie already had a huge cult following irrespective of how it turns out. managing and exceeding expectations was already a huge ask. but this movie does it better, it exceeds the expectations by a huge margin and brings out many surprises along the way. tom cruise is a legend, i think he can do no wrong, may it be the stunts, his involvement in the characters, charisma, whatever you give him he aces it and the director realized this factor and used it to the movies' advantage. everything in the movie is centered around maverick and its surely a one-man show coupled with few brilliant performances for other actors who merely seemed like support characters. maverick steals the show and carries the movie throughout no flaws what-so-ever.

the premise is rather simple and easy to understand and if you've seen top gun recently (just before the movie like me) you will follow the love letters to the older version and relish it. an enemy base which needs to be destroyed because of the illegal activities involving nuclear reactors and if left alone might pose serious threat to global arena. sounds more like a mission impossible montage, but since its a movie about flights, the trick is to get down via a narrow entry point, destroy target, exit with huge incline and survive to make it home. maverick was called in to train the best of the best because why not? he is the maverick. strapped for time, and a impending doom, maverick does what he does best. showboating his skills and inspiring the fleet of aviators.

the premise and story until then is more than sufficient to hit a home run, however the director had few moments, like training goose's son, reconnecting with his first love, the move on from goose's death, the bond of ice-maverick. all of these made such beautiful connections that you would want to see how it all turns out. this was a very difficult ordeal as it is and with so many backstories, the director gave a very clear and proper screen time to justify their involvement in the movie, truly inspirational directorial brilliance.

other thing you will relish in this movie are the flight scenes. it is obvious that there will be many; but in every scene you feel that the maneuvers, dog fights are actually happening. it was shot so well and not just the actors did a great job, but the special effects coordinator deserves a huge round of applauds as well. there were scenes when the plane banks right you lean and when the pilots feel the jet flush you will feel your breath stops for a moment before gasping for air. it was a real treat to eyes and a very convincing play by the director that makes you believe you are travelling along with the actors, a very very difficult feat to achieve, very well done

just got out of the cinema, and figured i'd jot this down before i forget. like the rest of you, i've been hearing about top gun 2 & had been looking forward to it for ages, and finally, it's here. i didn't care to watch any of the trailers, since watching trailers these days is equivalent to watching the entire movie. so, i was going to the cinema with no expectations whatsoever.

watching movies like the northman & top gun maverick kinda gives me hope for the future of cinema. or maybe, it's the last of a dying breed of films. but like maverick says, "..maybe.. but not today".
