top gun is a different film, they mix many aspects to do the film, using old aspects, new productions, old actors, new actors, and this made a very different film.

top gun successful film made in the 80's and in 2022 they decided to do top gun 2 using the old actors like tom cruise as maverick, jennifer connelly as penny benjamin, and val kilmer as iceman, they used the general history too, but with modern technology, some new important actors like miles teller as bradley 'rooster' bradshaw and a different plot.

in this story the principal, maverick, was called for his old friend iceman of top gun, the school for the best pilots of airplanes, to make a work.

maverick had to command a team to do a very difficult mission and the commanders made a plan and in this plan the team would complete the mission but this plan had little chance of continuing alive. maverick didn't like this and he decided to do a new plan and in his plan they have more chances to be alive, but the mission is very, very difficult.

the commanders didn't like maverick's idea, but iceman, the leader of leaders, approved the idea of his friend.

maverick didn't have much time to train his team and he had a conflict with rooster because rooster's dad was the duo of maverick in the past, but he died as a pilot with maverick.

this is a very emotional film because maverick has many conflicts with the team, his old girlfriend penny, the commanders and the time.

this film has a very good production, and compared with top gun 1, top gun 2 has so many battles and effects, and it makes a better film, because when the plane explodes the effects make us feel like the plane really exploded. and analyzing the plot, this film has a more interesting plot and with more surprises, principally in the final, when maverick is alone at the island full of enemies and rooster go back to help him and they escape from the island, the audience think that the conflict are resolved, but in the way back home they had another problem, and this surprize the audience a lot.

concluding, this is a new film based on an old film, but with a better production and a better plot. additionally, this is a film with many surprises, so you can't say the finale of history if you don't watch it. thats a nice film for everyone who likes action movies.

thirty-six years in the making, 'top gun: maverick' has finally arrived after being extensively delayed from its original july 2020 release date. does this long awaited and highly anticipated sequel soar as high as its predecessor?

1. first of all, i rarely ever give films a 10/10 rating, especially action flicks, but this one totally exceeded expectations. in recent years, superheroes and sci-fi fantasy blockbusters have ruled the box-office but the this year the crown goes to tom cruise. not saying this film will break the bank but rather deliver something special that will surely resonate with fans of the original and those witnessing the glory of fighter pilots taking flight for the first time.

2. tom cruise proves himself a legend above all actors of his generation and present day. he surely has immortalized himself as one of the greats that can never be touched in this lifetime. cruise carries this film with the same charisma and enthusiasm as he did 36yrs ago. regardless of the controversy or what people might think of him, his will to perfect his films and the respect he has for art of filmmaking is yet to be rivaled by another actor.

3. it is no secret or spoiler that val kilmer appears in this film reprising his role as tom 'iceman' kazansky, and despite his disability to speak, it never hinders the emotion he conveys when he's on screen. the new young pilots (who i thought i'd dislike) proved me wrong to the point where i actually felt for them and the dangers they found themselves in while flying. majority of the weight falls on miles teller (rooster) as he has the most screen time with tom cruise, and though their relationship may seem rocky at first, its the thing that truly is the heart of the film.

i can go on forever as to how fantastic this film is but there just isn't enough words. i was overwhelmed with joy from start to finish and found myself weeping tears of joy by the last 15mins of this film. 'top gun: maverick' is the definition of why we fall in love with cinema. this movie is special in its own right and has an indescribable uniqueness to it that ultimately warms your heart and makes you want to take flight again and again.

what a story, what a thriller ride without any cheesy cgi, it felt real, it felt authentic, and story stayed true to its predecessor. tom cruise hasn't aged a day, just as young and fit as the first one and yet again has outdone himself. excellent character builds, great lines, kept you hooked from first second till the last. if sequels good sequels will take 36 years in the making, then it's worth the wait as long as it's made right like this instead of cash grabs. well done team top gun!

top gun: maverick is one of the greatest love stories ever and perhaps the greatest sequel ever made (other than the terminator 2). i haven't had such positively strong feelings about a movie in a long, long time. in my opinion, it is easily the movie of 2022. perfect blend of classic and modern.

top gun: maverick is a love story about pete mitchell, call sign ''maverick'' (tom cruise), a distinguished pilot/naval aviator who uses his tough life situation to his advantage in order to re-ignite the past love with a stunning owner/bartender of a local military personnel favored bar penny benjamin (jennifer connelly). penny benjamin was only referenced as a character in the original top gun, so bringing her on the big screen in the sequel was a great decision as is shown in the movie how much potential her character had.

due to the facts that maverick and penny have a shaky history and that penny is now a single mom, meaning her priorities have greatly changed, maverick realizes right away that he's going to have to really dig deep in order to achieve his goal, which is of course, to win penny's heart again, this time once and for all. thus he puts an epic, extatic and romantic plan in motion in order to achieve his goal.

with the help of his old friend/wingman tom kazansky, call sign ''iceman'' (val kilmer), maverick gets reinstated back as the instructor in the famous top gun school in order to be close to penny's bar and therefore close to penny. he cleverly drops by to her bar and acts like he didn't know she owned it in order to keep things casual which doesn't go perfectly. penny forces maverick's hand with the bar rules and puts maverick in a situation where he's forced to pay for everyone's drinks at the bar. unfortunately for maverick, his card gets declined which reveals to penny that he doesn't really offer the financial security she, as a hard working single mom, deserves. however, penny immediately shows why she got a hold of maverick's heart by showing she doesn't mind and thus reveals, although very subtly, that maverick still managed to lay a very much needed foundation for the achievement of his ultimate goal.

upon arriving at top gun school, maverick enters the second stage of his plan. he uses bradley bradshaw, call sign rooster (miles teller) - his former deceased wingman's son (who is also one of the top graduates at top gun school), to practice being a father figure and with it convince penny that he's fit and able to be a good father figure, which is crucial as penny has a daughter. throughout the movie, maverick goes all out and over the top to achieve this crucial part of the plan - he gets really into it to the point where he even saves rooster's life at the end of the movie even though he didn't have to since penny was not there to see it. by the end of the movie, maverick and rooster bond like father and son, thus showing maverick's second stage of his plan is complete.

and while completing the second stage of his plan, he also completes the third and final stage of his plan - the mission he was sent to do for the navy which he manages to do in a spectacular fashion, therefore solidifying himself as the man penny has been waiting for.

the message of the movie is beautiful and clear cut - it's never too late for love or, if you want, all you need is love. unequivocal 10/10.

top gun: maverick accomplishes exactly what it sets out to do, taking the audience on a 120-minute emotional thrill ride and surpassing the original film in almost every facet.

whilst there are clear elements of nostalgia, they do not detract from the story, in which cruise's expertly-acted fighter-pilot ace "maverick" must confront and overcome past trauma in order to perform his duty and mend his broken relationships.

though the script was not particularly notable, powerful lines were delivered and the actors seemed to sink into their roles, conveying a lot of meaning through non-verbal communication. it also helped that many of the supporting characters went through their own minor arcs. all this aided by a stellar soundtrack well suited to an epic blockbuster. in addition, i do not mind the presence of an acceptable level of old-school hollywood cheese/cliche in the plot and script; we are reminded that this is a movie made for the purposes of entertainment, and boy does it pay off in spades.

what can i say about that action that hasn't already been said? go and watch this film. the final act is an absolute goldmine of all-time wide-eyed cinematic awe, and that's not to undersell the earlier action scenes.

full of heart and surely satisfying fans of the original whilst also forging a new path for the franchise, top gun: maverick was an immensely enjoyable and satisfying experience. i will be re-watching it multiple times into the future.

in 1986, "top gun" changed american blockbuster cinema forever. besides being a powerful military recruitment tool, the film captivated audiences with tom cruise's charismatic performance as maverick, captivating aerial dogfighting scenes, and a now-iconic soundtrack. while that film is unquestionably a cultural touchstone of its era, i never have loved it the way that some people did. that said, as a fan of tom cruise's action films, i was most certainly looking forward to seeing the sequel. to my shock, the film is utterly outstanding and far better than it had any right to be--blowing the first film out of the water.

the plot is relatively simple. maverick is back as a flight instructor, and has to instruct a new class of fighter pilot recruits (among them the son of goose from the first film) to take out an enemy nation's uranium enrichment facility. that may seem like a relatively simple or generic story, but the film's technical craftsmanship and emotional core are utterly superb and riveting throughout its entire runtime. the flight scenes are just impeccably shot, with top-notch cinematography, sound design, and editing. you truly feel like you're in the cockpit, and the results are utterly riveting, visceral, and thrilling. the sharp editing ensures that you can always keep track of who is who and what is what during these scenes, while simultaneously maintaining a strong sense of spatial awareness outside the aircraft(s.) it's been a long time--maybe even not since "mission: impossible--fallout"--that i've seen action scenes filmed this well and wholly committed to technical filmmaking rather than cgi effects. every single sound feels like it was carefully crafted to most accurately and authentically recreating the fighter pilot experience as possible.

any reviewer impressed by this film could go on and on about how technically stunning it is, but what else sets this film apart from other modern blockbusters is a strong devotion to powerful, emotionally impactful plot and character development-driven storytelling as well. unlike many blockbuster franchises, this film manages to tell a thoroughly compelling and authentic story in the here and now rather than spend far too much of its runtime setting up a million sequels and spin-offs. tom cruise still remains as charismatic as ever as maverick, but he's more thoughtful and wise this time. the new recruits are all very strong in their performances, especially miles teller; the emotional and dramatic tensions between him and maverick over goose's death feel realistic and believably raw. jennifer connelly is also great as penny, a bar owner and maverick's love interest. val kilmer's return as iceman is also emotional and compassionate, helping solidify the impact of the film's stakes on the viewer. the screenplay is much sharper, tighter, smarter, and wittier than the first film, and never lets go of ensuring powerful interpersonal relationships between characters are felt to create a gripping and high-quality narrative. unlike many other blockbusters that feel they could have been trimmed by 30 minutes or so, the film is practically immaculately paced--with no scenes that feel too long or too short to keep the audience thoroughly interested and entertained through its entire runtime of a little over 2 hours.

"top gun: maverick" proves that you can have a summer blockbuster that manages to excel in the highest levels of technical and aesthetic prowess and never lose sight of a genuinely powerful, relevant, and thoughtful story--all while simultaneously keeping the audience entertained and thrilled from beginning to end. that's why i was so blown away by it, leaving the theater with a huge smile on my face. i hope others feel the same way too. 10/10

note: i saw the film in dolby cinema. without question, this was an outstanding dolby experience. the sound design utilized the dolby atmos system and bass incredibly well, and the rumble was utilized in tandem with increasing fighter jet engine noises. the picture quality, lighting, and color contrasts were excellent as well, and noticeably better than they would likely be on a standard screen.

remember the last time you were in a movie theater, and realized that your jaw dropped for awhile? or when a scene is so thrilling that you find yourself on the edge of your seat, holding your breath? well, i lost count of how many times i felt like this watching top gun maverick. a sequel that is superior in every possible way to the original film.

top gun, from 1986, is a great action movie, no wonder it became a classic, but we have to admit that it has its flaws, a little relevant plot, which is basically two guys arguing about who has the biggest dick. top gun maverick is arguably more polished, layered, tense, and emotional. we start the film with several established relationships between maverick and other characters, such as his friendship with iceman, and his relationship with penny (connelly), which doesn't need to be didactic for us to realize all its nuances and complexities. the mix between the old and the new is very present here, including references to the original flick, without ever seeming out of place, or mere fan service. i don't know if i need to talk about the action scenes, but they're absolutely mind-blowing. the sound effects and soundtrack will leave anyone with goosebumps. the cgi doesn't draw attention to itself, and a lot of the visual effects are practical, which brings a wonderful physicality to the action.

the supporting cast is very efficient, with hangman being an updated, and even more douche, version of iceman, but without the same personality and presence as val kilmer's character. miles teller also doesn't shine much, but he does a good job. tom cruise is the absolute standout, no exceptions.

perhaps something that top gun maverick lacks is the courage to let go of some characters. despite having moments of life or death, literally, where we feel like anything can happen, there is no real risk, which ends up taking some of the weight off the mission.

a film that really deserves the title of blockbuster, which goes beyond the a mere action movie, and delivers us an exciting, mind-blowing and chills-filled adventure.

top gun pilots, top rate movies timing couldn't be more appropriate for me to watch this 2022 sequel today - exactly one week after i watched the original release top gun (1986). and let me tell you something. you need the background knowledge of the 1986 episode for a compete and thorough understanding of the sequel. rarely is a sequel as good as its original release due to tapering viewers' sentiment which in many cases is an unfortunate reality. yet this movie has broken the curse.

there you go. top gun: maverick (2022). what a group of top guns! and what a series of top rate movies! to an old school 70er like myself, the 2022 session is a long anticipated and much needed extension of the 1986 nostalgia. to me it's almost a remake of the 1986 top gun in many ways. the opening credit is exactly the same which provides a very good flashback of the old series. interpersonal relationship in this sequel dreadfully and eerily mimics those in the 1986 release. the intimate relationship between maverick and the woman, the rivalry between the two best trainee pilots rooster and hangman, are nothing short of a remake and reflection of how various characters interacted in the 1986 top gun.

what surprises me is that the 1986 top gun only earned itself an acceptable 6.9, a far cry from 8.6 for its 2022 sequel. my take is that the maverick session has more combat scenes than its predecessor, which makes it easier to attract young viewers. still it strikes the right balance between its more drama genre and the fighting scenes. after all it is meant to depict the career and personal lives of naval pilots. hence fighting must take a secondary place.

scenes and themes are multilayered and sophisticated. there are a good mix of tense yet upbeat, uplifting while emotional scenes. argument breaks out between fellow trainees. disagreement ensues between commander and officer. flashback reverts back to deceased father and his successive pilot son. mind twists between protecting deceased mate's son and fulfilling his career aspirations. all are naturally, logically, coherently, organically and consistently woven together and permeate into each other. it is indeed a great deal of information to process.

i love this movie this was my 5 time to watch this movie in one of the more memorable lines in the original top gun, maverick gets chewed out by a superior who tells him, "son, your ego's writing checks your body can't cash." sometimes i wonder if tom cruise took that putdown as a personal challenge. no movie star seems to work harder or push himself further than cruise these days. ridiculously entertaining top gun: maverick. cruise was in his early 20s when he first played pete "maverick" mitchell, the cocky young navy pilot with the aviator sunglasses, the kawasaki motorcycle and the need for speed. in the sequel, he's as arrogant and insubordinate as ever: now a navy test pilot in his late 50s, maverick still knows how to tick off his superiors, as we see in an exciting opening sequence where he pushes a new plane beyond its limits. partly as punishment, he's ordered to return to topgun, the elite pilot-training school, and train its best and brightest for an impossibly dangerous new mission. and so the three screenwriters of top gun: maverick - including cruise's regular mission: impossible writer-director, christopher mcquarrie - have taken the threads of the original and spun them into an intergenerational male weepie, a dad movie of truly epic proportions. they're tapping into nostalgia for the original, while aiming for new levels of emotional grandeur. to that end, the soundtrack features a lady gaga song, "hold my hand." it's nowhere near as iconic a chart topper as the original movie's "take my breath away," but tugs at your heartstrings nonetheless. the action sequences are much more thrilling and immersive than in the original. you feel like you're really in the cockpit with these pilots, and that's because you are: the actors underwent intense flight training and flew actual planes during shooting. in that respect, top gun: maverick feels like a throwback to a lost era of practical moviemaking, before computer-generated visual effects took over hollywood. you start to understand why cruise, the creative force behind the movie, was so driven to make it: in telling a story where older and younger pilots butt heads, and state-of-the-art f-18s duke it out with rusty old f-14s, he's trying to show us that there's room for the old and the new to coexist. he's also advancing a case for the enduring appeal of the movies and their power to transport us with viscerally gripping action and big, sweeping emotions.

the original top gun from 1986 is iconic, an entertaining, thrilling testosterone-filled 80s summer action saga with rocking music and a plethora of memorable moments (mav's serenade to charlie, goose's finger, iceman's teeth bite, the volleyball scene, the fly-bys) and adrenaline-filled aerial combat sequences. but top gun is very much a "style over substance" film. this sequel reverses that by building on the rather thin characterization and relationships established in top gun and heavily being influenced by mega-star's tom cruise's expert acting ability that he's perfected over the last 3 decades. at the time of top gun in '86, cruise became a movie star, but he wasn't taken seriously as an actor. within 3 years, he received critical praise for rain man and got his first oscar nomination for born on the fourth of july. within the next decade, he would score 2 more oscar nods for jerry maguire (for which he should have won) and magnolia while jumpstarting the mission impossible series in '96 with in my opinion still the best film of the franchise. within 5 years after magnolia, cruise delivered his best performance ever in the masterpiece collateral, for which he should have won the best actor oscar. getting overlooked so often probably made cruise opt to focus mostly on action movies the rest of his career. it's ironic that cruise has been making mi sequels nonstop for the last 25 years when this film top gun maverick may be better than all of them. regardless of being passed over for the elusive oscar prize, cruise is one of the best actors in hollywood. dare i say it, but the insane popularity of this film might just score him his long overdue 4th oscar nomination. longshot, but here's hoping.

the exceptional sequel opens up with pete "maverick" mitchell (impeccably reprised by cruise) at his current assignment station somewhere in the midwest where he is the test pilot for an advanced stealth jet with the ability to push mach 10. as a result of pushing it too far, the program is shut down, but mav gets immediate re-assignment as a training instructor back at the top gun program in san diego. the mission commander (excellently played by jon hamm doing his classic don draper delivery) tasks mav to train the "best of the best" pilots for a dangerous mission in enemy territory where they must destroy a secret energy cache and they must hit the target to implode the base (pretty much a star wars death star attack). the movie boasts a cast of young stars in the making playing the mission pilots. the de facto main character among the young guns is rooster (stalwartly played by miles teller). rooster is goose's son and teller looks very much like anthony edwards, who was a scene-stealer in the original film. but in this one, the mood is more somber as rooster is angry with and at constant odds with mav, but not necessarily for the reason that people think. of course there's a love story in this as mav re-connects with the infamous penny (effervescent jennifer connelly), the "admiral's daughter" that got an early mention in the '86 film. but the absolute best part of the movie was the emotion-filled scene between mav and iceman himself (val kilmer making a memorable appearance). cruise and kilmer really acted superbly in that scene. this is where i feel that this sequel may possibly top the classic original, because the heart in this movie feels more palpable and real due to the history and gravitas that cruise brings to his role this time. in '86, both mav and cruise were cocky stars-in-the-making. in 2022, they are smarter, wiser, world-weary veterans who have mastered their respective crafts. also, there's all the aerial stuff! lol pretty impressive that the actors actually trained to fly jets so these sequences look as authentic as possible. but where top gun maverick succeeds that so many modern movies fail is that it focuses on the heart of the story underneath, so all of the action is just icing on the cake.

top gun: maverick is a masterclass in cinematic adrenaline, with aerial sequences that set a new standard for realism and intensity. from the moment the engines roar to life, the film plunges you into the cockpit and doesn't let go.

the camera work is nothing short of revolutionary. every shot is meticulously crafted to place the audience directly into the heart-pounding action. real fighter jets and in-cockpit cameras make the sequences feel astonishingly authentic, capturing every sharp turn, stomach-dropping dive, and afterburner-fueled climb with breathtaking precision.

tom cruise, reprising his role as pete "maverick" mitchell, not only commands the screen with his charisma but also showcases his commitment to realism. the practical stunts and live-action maneuvers elevate the film to a level of immersion that cgi-heavy action flicks can't touch.

the aerial combat scenes are pure spectacle. the choreography of the dogfights is thrilling, with tight formations, split-second decisions, and jaw-dropping maneuvers that leave your heart racing. the sound design complements the visuals perfectly, with roaring engines and sonic booms pulling you deeper into the experience.

top gun: maverick isn't just a movie; it's a visceral experience that demands to be seen on the biggest screen possible. it's a triumphant blend of groundbreaking filmmaking and pulse-pounding action that soars far beyond expectations.

when i first read about the possibility of a top gun sequel, i had little-to-no confidence in the film's ability to even come close to the original. 1986 was quite a long time ago. tom cruise is like 60 years old, and the legendary f14 is now retired and replaced by the f18 and f35. this movie can't compare to the original, right?

wrong.

top gun : maverick does the seemingly impossible. it doesn't just match the original. it surpasses it. tom cruise is just as "maverick" as he is in the original. but he also does a great job of showing us a more down-to-earth, mature maverick. he's still a smart*ss to many superior officers. but he also looks after his team and trainees like a great commander should. i know some people prefer the whole kelly mcgillis relationship from the original. but i personally think jennifer connelly as penny makes you forget the 1986 one-night-stand type situation even happened. the maverick-penny relationship is way more personal, and that makes it so much better. plus it's jennifer connelly, so you can't really go wrong. miles teller's "rooster" starts off kinda whiny, but he turns it around, and does a great job with it. glen powell's "hangman" is essentially "iceman" from the original. he's good. he knows he's good. and you know it, too. he can be a jerk, so you don't want to like him. but you do. not gonna elaborate on the rest of the squad, but they all do a great job, especially phoenix and bob. jon hamm is the 100% by-the-book air boss of top gun. and he is without a doubt exactly how the real boss would be.

the flight and cockpit scenes are absolutely fantastic, thanks to cruise's insistence on using real footage instead of cgi. the musical score takes the legendary theme and adds even more to it. the soundtrack is loaded with scene-fitting music throughout. and of course they throw in kenny loggins. you can't have top gun without kenny loggins.

all-in-all, the film is fantastic. is it the best movie ever made? of course not. is it great fun, exciting, and even depressing at times? absolutely.

the film is an absolute blast from start to finish.

and maverick is of course no one else than tom cruise. top gun: maverick is really a great movie and worthy successor of the original top gun from 1986.

in top gun: maverick tom cruise returns as pete mitchel. what has changed during the past 35 years? nothing much, pete mitchell is still reckless, "do not think, but do" and goes beyond the limits of what a fighter jet is designed for. the only real difference is pete mitchell is a captain now.

in top gun: maverick captain pete mitchell returns to top gun with the impossible task to train america's best fighter pilots for an assignment which is even more impossible. where the young team of fighter pilots convinced they are the best of the best, captain pete mitchell proves them there is still much to learn. and all that in a timeframe less than three weeks.

the built-up of the movie is very much similar to the original movie. the flight scenes on the other hand are just great, spectacular to watch and you almost get the feeling you are sitting next to tom cruise in one of his jets. but also for this movie, you have to use your imagination.

the original top gun was like a 2 hour music video. it was visually stunning scenes set to iconic music tracks and it was like nothing we have seen before.

top gun maverick took all of those good qualities that made the original special but added heart and character to it.

while in the original movie, maverick did everything out of ego and put his own comrades at risk because of his ego. in this movie maverick does what he does to protect his comrades not put them in danger.

top gun maverick is much more family friendly than the first moves with the sex scenes dialed down, more diversity. and a greater respect for women than just frat-boy objectification.

and then what was done so well in the original movie with the actual plane footage was even taken to a much higher level in this movie with cameras out inside the cockpit and real footage of the actors pulling gs and really feeling the stress of those high speed maneuvers. you can see the physical tool the pilots endure in that kind of flying that you just don't get a perspective for in the original.

all in all it is a recreation of the original for modern times, with a heavy dose of nostalgia, beach sport scene and all.

the only negatives i see: everything that is good about this film harks back to the 80s including tom cruise. but the younger cast, with the exception of "rooster", is very forgettable. iceman, slider, and the others were much more memorable. there are also a couple dull scenes involving discussions between officers that somewhat slows down the movie and could have been done without.

to sum up, the highlight of this film are the nostalgia, the soundtrack, and above all the flight scenes. i rarely say this but this film is one of the few that deserves to be watched in the higher-end rooms (dolby surround, etc).

i am a part of the younger generation, but i had seen the first top gun a few years prior to writing this review, and i must say, my dad was incredibly excited after seeing the first trailer for this film in 2019. i was skeptical however, i have seen my fair share of soft reboots/crappy sequels, and i didn't expect much from it. the delays for this film just convinced me more that it would be a flop, boy was i wrong.

i didn't expect anything from this film, i was hoping for it to at least be a decent directed movie with an ok plot, but i got more then i could ever imagine, the plot was a solid 10/10, one of the best written stories i've seen on the big screen, i am still in shock after a week from seeing the movie, and i am so excited for my next opportunity to watch it again.

the characters of the film were great, and the returning cast were a complete fan service, tom cruise still hasn't lost his charm as maverick and they even managed to get val kilmer to act in a few short scenes. but i think the best characters of the film were by far the new additions, and i am talking specifically about 'rooster', played by miles teller, this character bought some of the most emotional stakes i've seen in any film, mainly through him being the son of mavericks deceased wingman from the original 'goose'. the other pilots present throughout are also great, and feel like genuine people, bringing some strong comedic relief.

the cinematography for the film is some of the most realistic and incredible practicality i've ever seen, those where real jets 99% of the time! i was amazed by how real the movie felt, being a huge step up from the original, which if i'm correct only used flight simulation for most of the climactic scenes.

i can't say to much else without spoiling, so i will leave it at this, this movie is one of the greatest if not the greatest sequel of all time to a classic film, everything about it will leave you either on the edge of your seat, or staring in amazement at the big screen, if i could experience this movie again for the first time, i would do so 100%, please see this movie, whether it's at home or before the film leaves cinemas, i can guarantee the movie will end up high in your ranks as it has mine, i give this movie a 10/10 and i would make that an 11 if i could!

just got out of seeing 'top gun: maverick'. granted, i'm of a certain age that 'top gun' (1986) had a dramatic impact on my 10 year old psyche. yes, i know it's rooted in u. s. military propaganda, but so were 90% of american action films of the 80's (cold war anyone?). as for the sequel, it puts its predecessor and all other american action films to shame.

exhilarating, perfectly cast, and executed to perfection; 'top gun: maverick' is the greatest action film in existence from my perspective and has almost single-handedly won over this tom cruise skeptic. definitely see it in a theater as it deserves to be experienced in one. 10/10.

the original top gun wasn't a movie i enjoyed very much. i have never been fascinated by planes and jets, so watching a movie that existed simply as a way of showing off how cool jets were wasn't enough to do it for me. and that was top gun's biggest flaw. the story existed only to tie in the cool jet moments together and served no greater purpose. however, in its sequel almost 30 years later, all its flaws have been rectified.

top gun maverick is so much more approachable a film than the original top gun simply because there was a story with actual stakes despite the jets and the aviation jargon, that feels universally relatable. we feel the clock ticking and we feel the pressure mounting. and while the jets are still integral to the movie, they no longer feel like an excuse to make a top gun movie, but merely tools through which a great story is told. and that's what makes top gun maverick a more enjoyable movie experience.

this movie also benefits from being a sequel in that it carries a lot of history and built up conflict that we can immediately recognize, that over the course of the movie are resolved on screen, and resolved well. i had a lot of fun watching this movie, and i think its approachable enough that anyone could go into this move and have a great time!

movie review (no spoilers)

welp. my 18 year old son eli & i went to see top gun - maverick this evening. we were hotly anticipating it. heck, i even watched the original top gun over the weekend in preparation. to say that i have been anxiously awaiting this, or, that i have been anticipating this to be "the movie" of 2022 is an understatement.

so, the question is: "how was it?"

hmmm. how should i put it?

well, to start with, i won't tell you whether or not i cried. no, you'd just laugh at me anyway, like eli does when i cry in movies. no, i won't tell you whether i cried (or how many times). instead, i'll tell you that eli cried. twice.

how about the action? i'll refer you to the king-schreifels article published earlier today in the ringer. i'm serious - if you're planning on seeing this movie, that article is a must-read background piece to help you understand what you've watching. the tldr is that tom cruise insisted that this movie have no cgi and no green screen shots of the fighter jets. this is the real thing, and it is adrenaline pounding, tension building, fingernails-clutching-the-seat-handles, get your heart pumping movie.

how does it compare to other movies? did eli & i enjoy this? how can i best describe it? let me say this: i'm filing a formal complaint against imdb and considering even filing a lawsuit. you see, when i went to rate this movie, imdb disallowed me from giving it the proper rating that it deserves. oh sure, imdb would allow me to give it a measly "10 stars" but that does not do this movie justice. it needs not 10, not 11, but 12 stars to do it justice.

on that note, i've made a decision. i'm cancelling netflix, paramount +, hbo max, and amazon prime. we have no more need of them. i'll also be purging my vudu library of all movies except for top gun, and soon, of course, top gun - maverick. i *might* consider keeping other tom cruise movies, simply out of respect for the master.

from now, every time i'm tempted to watch hot garbage like braveheart, gladiator, or the dark knight, i'll be watching top gun - maverick instead. no doubt you're asking yourselves "what about the godfather or the shawshank redemption??" pshaw. there is no longer any need for watching those poorly made pieces of trash. the shining or avengers: endgame? no! disgusting! no!!! nothing else is worthy when you have an opportunity to watch top gun - maverick.

thank you, josiah, my 22 year old son, for suggesting that i purchase an amc a+ pass. it will allow me to see top gun - maverick for free multiple times this summer.

now the only remaining question is, will your mother still love me if i go to see it every single day all summer?

oh, and, finally, i suggest watching it in imax. it was shot with made-special-for-this-movie imax cameras.

normally, sequels to decade old film classics aren't really that good. however, top gun: maverick, which is sequel to the 1986 film top gun, is a rare example of when the sequel tops the original. i thought the film would be good only, however it was actually better than i had expected it to be.

tom cruise reprising his role as pete maverick from the original, is excellent in this film and this is got to be one of his best performances in recent years. miles teller as bradley, the son of the deceased goose, is a great addition to this film and his relationship with pete is interesting to see. jennifer connelly as penny(pete's new love interest) is also delightful to watch though it's confusing why they never mentioned anything about kelly mcgillis's character from the original. val kilmer is also wonderful as iceman and the emotional weight is felt when he passes away. glen powell, monica barbaro and others as well are also great additions to the film and give out splendid performances.

the action sequences such as the pilots flying out the jets and then performing the final task are suspenseful. the scenes had splendid cinematography and had some of the crazy angle shots ever in a film. the sound(specifically that of the jets) too is done beautifully and it truly deserved the academy award for best sound. songs such as hold my hand by lady gaga as well as i ain't worried by onerepublic are wonderfully fit into the film. even the screenplay by christopher mcquarrie, ehren kruger and eric warren singer is done splendidly.

overall, top gun maverick is a rare example of when a sequel is superior to the original. it's one of the best movies of tom cruise as well as the best movie of the summer of 2022.

i was born in 1984 so i can't say top gun was "my time" but it's definitely my mom's and my uncle's time (her younger brother and only sibling). growing up i have noticed that my uncle owned a huge poster of top gun with tom cruise and kelly mcgillis together. it was pasted on his wall above his headboard. i have no idea who they were that time until betamax player came, then vhs player, vcd/dvd player. my uncle buys a copy of top gun each and every time a new vcr system for home entertainment comes out in the market. that's how much he loves top gun- that i understood! it was really cool to watch it with the whole fam!

and now that i've seen the sequel after decades! it didn't disappoint me, my husband and my mom. it even exceeded our expectations! this movie is truly spectacular! loved the story, there was enough flash backs to understand what is happening now. the special effects! no cgi! actors where all inside the cockpit of a flying f18. even the scene with the old f14 was rad too! this is the highest level of effort and dedication! made me really happy. how i wished my uncle's still here with us. he would have cried, he surely would have love this movie.

so thank you paramount and to all the producers of of top gun maverick. you're all awesome! you all gave my uncle's favourite movie a beautiful ending that it deserves and you brought back one of my amazing childhood memories.

actually, this movie is so good, the 1986 original should be called a prequel. the writers ingeniously wove penny benjamin, the unseen admiral's daughter mentioned in passing in the original, into the current story in addition to goose's son, call sign rooster. in fact, in the final sequence, rooster is sitting behind maverick in an f-14 just like his dad in the original. and it was moving to see maverick reconnect with his old nemesis iceman thirty-six years later. the film also paid homage to the famous volleyball sequence in the original, but unlike the original, this script was filled with humor. maybe best of all was the breathtaking aerial photography and sound design. this film deserves to be called a blockbuster if any film ever did.

finally, a movie done right! great cgi great characters and it makes you feel nostalgic in a modern movie. i had so many chills throughout the movie even in the kinda "predictable" parts. well done tom cruise.

top gun: maverick is a long-awaited sequel to the 1986 classic top gun, which left a lasting impact on pop culture with its iconic soundtrack, memorable characters, and thrilling aerial combat scenes. as a fan of the original film, i was excited to see how top gun: maverick would live up to its predecessor.

the movie follows the story of pete "maverick" mitchell, now a veteran pilot who is tasked with training a new group of top gun graduates. as he navigates his new role as a mentor, maverick must also confront his past and overcome personal challenges.

the film does a great job of capturing the nostalgia of the original while also introducing new and exciting elements. the aerial combat scenes are just as thrilling as before, with impressive visuals and realistic flight sequences. the addition of new aircraft and technology also adds to the excitement.

tom cruise delivers a strong performance as maverick, showing both his confident and vulnerable sides. the supporting cast, including jennifer connelly, miles teller, and ed harris, all bring depth to their respective characters and add to the overall story.

one of the strengths of the film is its ability to balance action with emotion. the story explores themes of loss, redemption, and loyalty, making the characters more relatable and giving the film more depth than just a simple action flick.

overall, top gun: maverick is a worthy successor to the original film, delivering on the nostalgia and excitement that fans have been waiting for while also introducing new elements to keep things fresh. it's a must-see for fans of the original and anyone who loves thrilling action movies with heart.

top gun: maverick (also called top gun 2: maverick) is a 2022 american action drama film directed by joseph kosinski, a sequel to the 1986 film top gun. it premiered on may 27, 2022 in the united states.

it grossed $1.493 billion worldwide, becoming the second highest-grossing film of 2022, the second film released since the covid-19 pandemic to gross $1 billion, and the highest-grossing film of tom cruise's career.

i just came back from the lido cinema here in singapore, the same cinema that, in 1986, me and my classmates sat there, wide-eyed and amazed by top gun. now, in 2022, with my family tow, we sat in the lido again, seeing these these iconic words flash across the screen, that unstoppable rush of nostalgia gushes out with palpable force from the very first frame of top gun maverick, and what a fantastic movie it has been! gosh i have waited 36 years for this movie, and man, the wait has been worth it. this is one of the few rare sequels where it's better, no, make that way way better than the original. the people behind the movie, jerry bruckheimer, joseph kosinski, tom cruise et al have made this a labour of their love. every scene, every shot and every interaction is masterfully woven with intricate care and detailed planning. the action sequences are top of their class, surpassing that of the original by a country mile. with the passing of time comes emotional maturity, and dear me, the emotional segments, especially that brief reunion scene between maverick and ice man reaches deep into your memory and pulls out those bygone feelings which has been buried deep in your heart for so many years. for the first time in many years, i feel like 17 again.

topgun maverick. from dangerzone, to the fighter flip, to the iconic runway ride, everything about maverick is what topgun was, only upgraded and more enhanced. the dog fights, the plane details, the explosions, everything is amplified and shows how far the technology has come. loved every minute of it. noted sci-fi fans will identify that the main mission is a tribute to starwars deathstar attack but still immaculately pulled of. kept waiting for might wings, hot summer nights and take my breath away but guess topgun ost will remain my all time favorite. already thinking of watching again as this movie really makes you feel good and is want going to cinema is all about.

i've been waiting for this sequel for such a long time. i consider top gun as a never fading classic, a true masterpiece that will go through the challenge of time. so maverick has huge shoes to fill and the shoes got filled alright!

first, this movie breathes nostalgia especially regarding the brotherly relationship maverick had with goose. after all those years, maverick hasn't still completely moved on from the tragic death of his best friend. it still haunts him to the high point especially now that goose's son, rooster, is following his dad steps and became one of the top pilots in the navy. the story between maverick and rooster is so rocky it breaks your heart as rooster believes maverick is preventing him from achieving his true potential while all maverick wants is to protect him and be the father rooster lost too early.

then you have the come-back of iceman who has moved up to the ranks and became the commander of the us pacific fleet as a full fledged admiral. he has become maverick best friend and has been using his position to protect him and keep him in the navy as he believes that the navy needs maverick. watching val kilmer and tom cruise interacting with each other so sweetly and still joking around about who is the best pilot can't stop bring you a smile. it also breaks your heart when iceman finally passes away as you cry along with tom cruise as he buries his wingman.

finally there is the f-14. the cherry of the top as we see maverick and rooster in one last epic dogfight taking on 2 su-57 in this mighty aircraft. that scene alone is a blast, keeps you out of breath every second as it's so intense and breathtaking. the f-14 is still as gracious as it can be and that plane still can fly.

of course the f-18 is also as majestic. what a beautiful plane that is. i'm glad they picked that plane instead of the f-35 which is not as gracious on camera. i believe it would have taken a lot of magic off the movie if it was the f-35 on screen instead of the f-18.

finally i have to give one last special mention to lady gaga for her amazing song. i love it so much and it gives such a powerful ending to the movie with the p-51 flying around in the sunset. such a raw talent she is.

i laughed, i cried and for a little over 2 hours tom cruise transformed into a credible, grown up version of his maverick persona and was somehow even more endearing than the maverick everyone swooned over in 1986.

for me, this is the first movie in an incredibly long time that truly felt worthy of a trip to the cinema because flying fighter jets just doesn't hit the same in your living room.

further, this might be one of the best screenplay examples of an individual character arc in motion picture history and it took a span of 35 years and two films to accomplish.

two thumbs up.

at the beginning, let's admit that tom cruise is the gringo who can always deliver strong action movies like top gun. from directing (joseph kosinski) to writing (ehren kruger, christopher mcquarrie, eric warren singer) to soundtrack (hans zimmer, harold faltermeyer) to acting (tom cruise, jon hamm, miles teller, glen powell, charles parnell). the movie tells the story of capt. pete mitchell (maverick) who returns to top gun school again after 36 years to teach an elite group of fighters how to accomplish a mission. the story is actually good as the movie doesn't need you to watch the first movie. it's so emotional, you'll smile, sit on the edge of your seat, you'll feel the danger that they fall in. the soundtrack is as good as it can be. the cinematography is stunning and the whole movie should be seen in imax to enjoy every detail in. the acting is superior from everyone from tom cruise to every role in the movie especially that cruise made the crew fly real real jets and they had extensive g-force training sessions to withstand the physical demands of the g-force pressures during flights. at the end, the movie deserves the wait, the hype, and to be watched on the biggest screen available. my rating is 10/10.

after 36 years, we are finally able to watch the sequel to the 1986 top gun. i was a little baffled when they announced they were making a top gun sequel as i wasn't fond of this idea of making sequels to really old movies for the sake of banking on nostalgia. the first film was pretty great and i just didn't feel like the sequel could be as good as the first one. so is top gun: maverick a cash grab or a worthy sequel?

firstly, the flying scenes are breathtaking! all of these sequences make you feel like you're in the cockpit and air with them. this is because they did it practically by actually having the actors be in these jets for real. the director fitted cameras into these cockpits and attached them to the side of these jets. this allows for some downright amazing shots and makes the scenes feel more believable. the action scenes are just intense and exhilarating with it having me on the edge of my seat. this is especially noticeable in the final act which is one of the best i've seen in recent memory. additionally, the music score by harold faltermeyer, lady gaga, hans zimmer, & lorne balfe is very good. i love how they incorporated those 80s tracks into the film while giving more modern and fitting music as well. furthermore, their music score during the intense action scenes are well done and helps to make the scenes tenser.

tom cruise is still great as maverick even after almost 30 years. he still embodies the character perfectly and does feel like a natural evolution of his character from the first film. i genuinely believe that this is what maverick would be like in 30 years. miles teller is also great as rooster, goose's son, and he has great synergy with tom cruise in their scenes together. jennifer connelly plays the new love interest for maverick, penny, and she is also great in her role thanks to her great chemistry with tom. glen powell plays the rival to miles and he is very good at being this overly cocky, hateable guy. likewise, jon hamm plays the commander that is antagonistic to maverick and he also does a good job at being hateable as well. val kilmer is one of the few actors from the original to return and i was interested to see how they would handle his throat cancer situation in real life. thankfully, this film handles it respectfully and probably results in one of the most emotional scenes in the film. the rest of the supporting cast, including those who play the recruits, all do a good job as well.

moreover, the story itself is also surprisingly enjoyable. the first top gun was a cheesy action flick but this one is a very down to earth, character-driven story. maverick is a lot wiser now thanks to the character arc he got from the first film when he was a student. however, now he has to be the teacher and this is a great antithesis to the story in the first film. the conflict he has now is having to train these recruits to do a suicide mission. he is struggling with the idea of sending other people to their death. it gets worse when one of these recruits is the son of his once best friend. the conflict between maverick and rooster is the emotional core of this film. this family dynamic is the most engaging aspect of this film and where the heart of the story lies. seeing maverick still trying to cope with the death of goose and having to deal with the fact that his son could also now die is just captivating stuff.

nevertheless, i do have some minor nitpicks with the film. i do find the dynamic of the recruits never does quite match the dynamic of the recruits from the first film. i never felt as strong of an attachment to the recruits and this is probably due to the film focusing on the teacher maverick. there is also a romantic subplot with maverick and penny that just feels very superfluous. it never felt like the romance part was even connected to anything in the main plot. heck, you could take this romance subplot and penny out of the film and the main story is still the same. it just felt like the romance plot just took away screen time from the interesting stuff. i am also a little annoyed that there is no dialogue or line to explain why maverick isn't with charlie from the first film anymore. especially, considering how relevant that character was in the first film.

overall, top gun: maverick is better than the first movie in almost every aspect. it has more amazing action sequences and a more interesting character-driven story. in a world where cgi seems to always be the go-to solution, we then get a rare movie like this where the majority is practical and it is all the better for it. this is not only a worthy sequel but also an amazing accomplishment in movies.

36 years is a long time wait but top gun: maverick delivers for both new and returning audiences in a sequel that is superior to the original 1986 box office hit. as executive producer for the film, cruise's insistence on authenticity and excellence are on display throughout the film. audience response has been nothing short of phenomenal, earning over $1.4 billion at the box office to date.

as the film opens, viewers discover that pete mitchell (aka maverick) has aged but he's still the maverick. ignoring orders from his ceo, maverick skips an intermediate stealth fighter test and switches directly to the project final objective target (mach 10) to save the project and succeeds but at the cost of the aircraft which explodes. fully expecting dismissal by commanding radm in charge of the project, maverick is informed he has been reassigned to fightertown usa (top gun training school) instead.

a secret mission is necessary to eliminate a uranium refining complex being developed against international sanctions in an underground location within a mountain that's due to start receiving nuclear materials within 3 weeks by a rogue nation. the mission will involve a low-level approach under enemy radar thru a winding narrow corridor heavily defended by sams on both sides followed by an extreme ingress and egress with massive g-forces while targeting a minuscule drop zone requiring a precise strike not once but twice to have any prospect of success. an impossible mission. sounds like a job for ethan hunt but maverick will have to do. what! typical military intelligence. the pilot best suited for this mission is tasked with training other top gun grads to complete the objective. to succeed maverick will have to resort to unorthodox training techniques to develop personnel who function as a team and think outside the book. his role is complicated by the inclusion of the son (rooster) of his deceased best friend (goose) on the training roster.

top gun: maverick succeeds in every level possible. it utilizes all the best elements of the original while updating the story relatable to today's audiences. cruise has committed every resource to this personal project. guess who really owns that wwii vintage mustang in maverick's hangar? did the cruise missiles come from that same source? probably not. the visuals are excellent throughout (example: darkstar test flight). never have computer screen simulations been so exhilarating. the musical score which includes themes from the original film augmented by classic and current songs should satisfy viewers young and old. and the movie also injects humor into the film regularly to offset the more serious themes.

cruise fully committed himself to his signature role as maverick eliminating the cockiness of the youthful character for a more measured performance but retaining his rep as a 'maverick'' at critical moments within the structure of the story. not only does maverick have to contend with his own morality, obstinate superiors, and the eventual end of his flight career but he also wrestles with his guilt over goose's death, along with potential casualties among his trainees if he fails as an instructor (especially rooster, because it involves a promise). flying jets is easy. making life and death decisions for your charges is gut-wrenching. will maverick ever be able to form long-term relationships with the opposite sex or just die alone?

cruise's performance is backed by the entire cast including ed harris (cain to maverick's able), jon hamm (cyclone), charles parnell (warlock) and bashir salahuddin (hondo) with newcomers monica barbaro (phoenix), glen powell (hangman) and miles teller (rooster) shining among the mission's top gun candidates. jennifer connelly as maverick's old flame, penny, is believable in a romance targeted for mature audiences which rates almost a pg rating. as the only returning member from the 1986 hit, val kilmer's gives a touching performance (to anyone who's aware of kilmer's real-life medical plight) as maverick's confident and 'guardian angel' iceman (adm. kazansky).

the mission impossible overtones are as obvious as is the nature of mavericks day job which is really a risky business. wait! doesn't penny's porsche bear a striking resemblance to the same vehicle from cruise's 1st hit in 1983? maybe. and doesn't the climatic mission run strongly mimic the attack on the death star in star wars: anh? the fighters must maneuver thru a narrow corridor lined with weaponry to deliver a surgically precise strike on a minute target not once but twice. was that obi wan imploring rooster to trust his instincts or maybe jedi master maverick on the headphones? 'use the (naval air) force, rooster'. whatever! the film exceeded all expectations, so i give top gun: maverick 11 stars out of 10 stars.

on a casting note: was ryan gosling ever contacted about a certain pivotal role? just curious.

after 36 years, tom cruise returns in one of his most iconic rolls in an effort to satiate our need for speed. straight to the point. it's hard enough to get a hit film, putting together a sequel that equals let alone surpasses the original is harder still. cruise and company (jerry bruckheimer produces again but also credits former partner don simpson who died in 1996) have done precisely that in "top gun: maverick".

in short:

want nostalgia?

got it!

well timed humor?

check!

amazing practical visual effects?

double check! the submersive cockpit camera is over the top. tossing aside the green screen pays major dividends.

"top gun: maverick" is a perfect blending of the original, from music, characters, and various call back/parallels and the next generation of naval aviators. from beginning to end this film is a heart pumping thrill ride that keeps you on the edge of your seat combined with a high-stakes storyline filled with surprisingly emotional depth, heart, and relevance.

incredible direction, stellar pacing, fantastic acting, extraordinary cinematography and sound, "tgm" is a 2-hour 11-minute triumph. "top gun: maverick" has enough heart and soul for two films and satisfies in every possible aspect.

so, dust off your ray ban aviators, hit the highway to the danger zone and check out "top gun: maverick" on the big screen the way it's intended. you won't be disappointed.

who knew a sequel made 36 years later would not only surpass its predecessor but soar far above what anyone could have imagined. tom cruise has once again delivered a masterclass in the art of making a blockbuster with top gun: maverick defining what makes a true cinematic experience. he felt the need-and though some may say it comes a few decades late-the need for speed never dies within all of us and this movie proves that right from its invigorating opening sequence.

cruise teams up with frequent collaborators, director joseph kosinski and producer christopher mcquarrie, which told us we're in for a mission: impossible-level event film. yet, all expectations were blown out of the atmosphere at hypersonic speed. the talent and dedication to the craft is visible from every actor's performance, every shot, every angle, and every heart-pounding flight sequence. this film is meant to be seen, heard, and felt on the largest screen with the most powerful sound system. it's sound mix is oscar worthy, along with its inventive cinematography techniques that put the audience directly in the cockpit with maverick.

i have to admit i wasn't around back when top gun hit theaters and pop culture. but even i could feel the nostalgia through the soundtrack, callbacks, and tributes-and the many white-haired fellow moviegoers who all had an edge-of-your-seat thrilling time watching this rare movie. they really don't make them like they used to anymore.

the visual effects here are minimal, of course, due to the very real practical effects as we see the daring young actors get taken up in the fighter jets with the adrenaline king, tom cruise. as he continues to age, he seems to be worrying less about his own safety and more about living in the moment and pushing past current filmmaking limits as much as he can. this makes for an obviously exhilarating filmmaking process which translates to nothing but pure entertainment at its highest level.

top gun: maverick cannot be hyped up enough because it's not just a nostalgic node to an iconic 80s movie. it's a breathtaking experience from start to finish that might be the last of its kind, just like it's main character. still, it has made its mark-and hit its target-as a memorable summer blockbuster. it makes anyone want to come back to the theaters again and again, taking the highway to the danger zone.

how can you make a movie truly beautiful? how do you redeem a lost franchise? how do you make a film you treasure from your childhood so much better than it ever was before? when i walked out of the theater from watching top gun maverick. this movie does all of that and so much more. i first wanna touch on the cinematography and atmosphere that it presents. from lighting cues, to the way the sun shines on different angles from different times of day, to a militaristic setting, you can tell that the creators had while creating these elaborate, and breathtaking sequences, they thought every scene's atmosphere out with intricate care and detail, this is probably my favorite atmosphere provided by any movie i've ever seen. the first top gun was iconic and very popular, but somewhat poorly rated by critics. top gun maverick took everything we loved and treasured and applied it to a clever script, better atmosphere, and had more memorable characters overall. the note that the first top gun ended on, it left a lot of conflicts and moral issues left unresolved. somehow this movie swoops in and fixes every fault that the first movie has. it presents a redemptive process between its two main characters maverick and rooster, goose's son from the first movie. through the mechanics provided, it not only redeems the emotional chunk missing from top gun, but also the internal conflicts residing within the two main characters. the other characters provided give just enough needed to present interesting surprises, and revisits that were present in the original. the stunt work is similar to the original by giving better set pieces and more fighter stunts and better jets. top gun shows why we love movies, everything is catered to the fans and gives us great surprises throughout, but never seems in your face; it's all very subtle. there are a few minor elements that are somewhat off putting about this film, such as faulty script writing or nonsensical romance. however, this is nothing that outright ruins the experience. top gun maverick is a very personal movie to me. i feel like this is everything i want out of any movie, and for that reason i have to recommend it to all audiences of age.

the danger zone for sequels is merely rehashing what worked before and hoping the audience didn't notice the lack of quality or care in the midst of six-packs, beach games, and high-flying jets--something "top gun: maverick" wisely avoids.

when you're in the company of hollywood's tireless maverick in tom cruise, premium entertainment is promised. nostalgia and emotional resonance in old yet viable characters is the icing on the cake in joseph kosinski's sequel. it's been over 30 years since cruise's pete mitchell aggressively took to the skies to steal the hearts of 80s romantics and beat the bad guys in the end, but little rust can be seen on the new film. he's still pushing the limits of the marriage between the aircraft and the sky in the opening scene, flying a brand-new updated jet through the clouds fast enough to doodle a circle in pursuit of a mac10 finish.

the g-force created by the jets in this film is real, and you can feel it. while the cast and crew do a wonderful job of bringing back the fire of the late tony scott's original, it's the aerial action sequences and dogfight combat scenes that will take your breath away here, pushing the film to another level. before the pandemic caused further, multiple delays, they were the initial reason that the film's star and studio wanted to delay the release date after fans got the first trailer over three years ago. the wait was well worth it, because these scenes push the envelope for what hollywood can do in the sky.

think of cruise's pilot as that incendiary (for a good reason) element that won't accept less than top-tier entertainment. when maverick finishes the flight by going so fast over a closed down gas station that the roof lifts temporarily into the air, you'll feel the good vibrations too just like ed harris' old curmudgeon rear admiral does, even if his "hammer" doesn't approve of the younger captain's methods.

every character has unique call names, like glen powell's hangman (a combo of young maverick and iceman) and miles teller's rooster. it's teller's affecting portrayal of the son of goose, anthony edwards' best friend to cruise's pilot in the first film, that acts as the launch pad of the plot. his dad's history hasn't been known and absorbed by the characters in the film, but by the audience as well. when maverick is called back in to train young top guns, the tempestuous relationship with teller's ben bradshaw burns at the core of the mission. how do you teach someone whose father you couldn't save?

the relationship between the drama from the original carries over well here, thanks to a deft script from ehren kruger, eric warren singer, and christopher mcquarrie. the writers lean into the assorted treats and thrills of the source material while giving it all a nice upgrade. the arrival of jennifer connelly as the flame that got away from maverick is a classy, old-school cinema romance, and jon hamm makes for a steely admiral. the st. louis actor mixes his mean don draper persona with the decorated, by-the-book thread of his beau "cyclone" simpson here. it all just works well together.

little works better or will become more emotional than val kilmer's return scene as maverick's former rival and current friend, tom "iceman" kazansky. without going into detail to spoil the impact, it's a very well-acted and well-written scene that pushes on the relationship of the characters as well as shining a poetic light on kilmer's recent battle with cancer. soulful is the word, and it's a scene you won't soon forget.

"top gun: maverick" is a movie i won't soon forget. with all the tragedy happening throughout the world, a little cruise goes a long way. he's the glue that holds all of this together-making you believe in everything his daredevil pilot can do by doing as many of the stunts himself as possible. he's the real-life maverick, pushing the envelope until it sticks together, forming a cohesive sequel that makes you feel the rugged yet exhilarating power of scott's original. as people call into question his ruthlessness on set and his unusual offscreen persona, the legendary actor proves he's still got the need for speed--as do we.

cruise and company were all set to get this film going ten years ago before the director's untimely death, and i think this is something ridley's brother would absolutely adore. from the lady gaga theme song-she's easier on the eyes and ears than kenny loggins-to the piano sing-along scene to the thrilling finale that will keep you guessing, "top gun: maverick" checks all the boxes of a worthy sequel. eventually, it flies even higher than the original.

one more piece of advice: see it in a theater. a big, loud, and crowded one. see it with the fans. that's the way these summer blockbuster blasts were designed to work.

finally, i have just discovered this cinematographic phenomenon, which continues to race ahead of all others at the top of the world box-office of the year, while waiting to be dethroned by "avatar: the way of water".

i don't understand the stellar early reactions, the overhyped critical acclaim selling it as one of the best films in cinematic history, or those who look down on it, claiming it's just another military video recruitment campaign disguised as a film. because, in my humble opinion, it is neither.

"top gun: maverick" (2022) is an excellent movie, which is well written, technically flawless and performed with conviction while paying a fine tribute to tony scott's 1986 film, and i don't struggle to justify my rating of 10 out 10.

the best scene is undoubtedly the "iceman scene", which is so moving because reality is larger than fiction and val kilmer partly plays himself. those who have suffered from ent cancer know this, and would not even want their worst enemy to experience such a journey through hell.

what about the role of the us military? well, i am the first to condemn war crimes, but above all i have the greatest respect for armed forces who defend their populations and the free world. and of course, the utmost contempt for any invading force. here, i did not sense any heavy or silly propaganda, as i might have initially feared after reading some biased reviews.

hollywood is smarter than any other institution, because "top gun: maverick" had to toe the line when it came to casting its villains. congratulations and thank you to the executives, crew and cast of the film for making a smart film devoid of political propaganda, which can be enjoyed anywhere in time. if only the majority of political animals and disinformation, misinformation and propaganda media could have this level of decency and intelligence.

by the way, i know some "liberals" who are unable to analyze the various shades of demonstration of human violence in hollywood films, while supporting the jingoistic propaganda of some of their most powerful elected officials and furthermore showing that they've lost their moral compass when it comes to clearly call out barbaric acts of terrorism. last but nor least, let's also not forget that president eisenhower (r) warned against the military-industrial complex, while truman (d) justified the use of nuclear weapons.

the biggest weak point in my opinion is that charlotte "charlie" blackwood, the astrophysicist and civilian instructor from top gun, played by kelly mcgillis, who was maverick's primary love interest in the original film, isn't mentioned at all. "what became of her?" remains an open question when the end credits begin to scroll.

in conclusion, the ethics behind the use of force and the legality and morality of the mission in "top gun: maverick" have been analyzed and voted on by the united nations security council. it's a larger-than-life motion picture, and nothing else, which endears made-for-the-big-screen movies and delights aviation enthusiasts, while wishing characters with that kind of emotional and intellectual intelligence would deal with such important issues in the real world, which is unfortunately not always the case nowadays.

top gun: maverick is an adrenaline-fueled thrill ride that delivers on its promise to bring back the excitement of the 1986 classic. the plot of the film follows maverick as he returns to the top gun academy as an instructor, where he meets a group of young pilots who are training for a dangerous mission involving a new stealth jet program. among them is lieutenant bradley "rooster" bradshaw (miles teller), the son of maverick's late friend and wingman nick "goose" bradshaw. maverick also rekindles his romance with penny benjamin (jennifer connelly), a single mother and bar owner who happens to be the daughter of his former commander.

"the movie features spectacular aerial sequences that will leave you breathless, with top-notch special effects that bring the action to life. the film delivers on its promise of exhilarating aerial action scenes, featuring stunning cinematography by claudio miranda and impressive practical effects that showcase cruise's dedication to performing his own stunts. the film also pays homage to the original with references to iconic moments and characters, such as val kilmer's return as admiral tom "iceman" kazansky, maverick's former rival turned friend."

that's why tom cruise once again proves that he is one of the most iconic action stars of all time, bringing a level of intensity and nuance to his performance that will leave you on the edge of your seat. the supporting cast is equally impressive, with standout performances from jennifer connelly and miles teller."

the film's score, composed by harold faltermeyer, is a nostalgic throwback to the original that is sure to get your heart racing. the editing is sharp, maintaining a steady pace that keeps the action flowing and never feels stale.

overall, top gun: maverick is a triumph of filmmaking that will thrill audiences of all ages. it's a fitting tribute to the original and a testament to the enduring power of the franchise. whether you're a fan of the original or new to the world of top gun, this movie is a must-see. i highly recommend it!

top gun: maverick is all blockbuster. after decades of the top gun series being idle and rumors that a sequel will come one day. it arrived in top gun maverick. which not only earned it's right to share the name of the original, but it does everything original did, but better.

better planes, better action set pieces, more fleshed out characters, and beautiful scenery and tension to go with the dogfighting. this is as good as it gets for a movie based on military dogfighting led by maverick, who still buzzes the tower even when the pattern is full decades later. must watch for action/war/military movie fans.

'top gun: maverick' isn't an oscar winning movie. it isn't some some deep and meaningful societal drama. it isn't a superhero movie filled with mindless effects, bland characters and social messaging... thank goodness!

'top gun: maverick' is what has been missing from the cinema in recent years... a movie with great characters who you want to root for. action and adventure, a dash of romance, a classic hero, and a patriotic story of good vs evil. no agendas, no lecturing, just good old-fashioned heroic fun with heart.

it hits all the marks, from the nostalgia nods (without drowning in them), through to being a sequel that adds to the original without detracting from it. the character of maverick finally grows up, but without feeling like he's been a useless man-child in the interim. there are touching moments, most notably with val kilmer, and an appropriate level of romance to round out maverick's character arc. the side characters are all enjoyable clichés of the best kind, ergo the type that are established quickly and well, and that you like and enjoy.

one factor that makes this all even more enjoyable is that maverick is _still_ the best-of-the-best (with iceman possibly equal...). he's not portrayed as the tired 'ace' who has to move aside for the newer, younger, superior hero. no, he's just the best. and that provides the film with a huge, grinning sense of satisfaction.

the plot itself is nothing original, but it didn't need to be. it's a mix of inspiration from the original film, with a dash of star wars and even a little iron eagle thrown into the mix. the heart of it is maverick finally finding a home, and dealing with the fallout from losing his best friend (goose) in the original, and the repercussions it had on goose's son.

from a visual standpoint, the film is appropriately stylish and the hefty dose of real aircraft footage, mixed with the effects sequences, helps to sell the film far more successfully than if it had been done with digital effects alone.

if i had one complaint, it would be that the music just isn't up to the original. hans zimmer does the job, and it works, but outside of harold faltermeyer's original main theme, only the 'darkstar' music is particularly note-worthy. meanwhile, the integrated songs don't capture the new era the way the original did, but how could they? however, the soundtrack is a minimal complaint.

ultimately, 'top gun: maverick' succeeds by being all that it needed to be, without trying to shoehorn in anything else. it tells a new story but honours its origins and leaves the viewer thoroughly satisfied.
