i've read in many places that this sequel has surpassed the original, but i don't really agree. when top gun came out, it was something extraordinary, it remained a classic. this sequel is obvious that is somehow better, since cinema evolved since then, but times have changed and i don't see maverick becoming a classic like top gun. there wasn't the same hype as with top gun. maybe because we have higher standards today. it's hard to compare them, but it is indeed a good sequel.

it doesn't happen very often that the sequel to a beloved and iconic film is better. i'd say that top gun: maverick is arguably better than its predecessor for many reasons.

firstly i'd add that my opinion of the 1986 original isn't the same as most people. i didn't grow up with the film it was made 9 years before i was born, i didn't actually see it until i was in my twenties. i liked "top gun" although i had my issues with certain story elements. basically i don't have the attachment to the characters or film that someone who was alive when it came out and loved it !

for "top gun: maverick" i was hoping for more up to date action and aircraft used, more modern story and less of the cheesy romantic elements. that for me, bogged down the original! for the most part i'd say yes that this film lived up to the hopes and expectations i wanted from it, however i do still have issues with it!

tom cruise and joseph kosinski have teamed up yet again and delivered an incredible rollercoaster of a film. cruise has dominated the blockbuster genre his entire career, arguably starting with "top gun". at last the technology has caught up to the story that is being told. the original had its hands tied with what action it could shoot for its time.........this film blows not just that film but majority of action films out of the water! heart-pounding, realistic, slick and jaw dropping from start to finish. every action scene must have taken months and months of planning for to be executed in this precisely! hats off the cruise and kosinski for breaking barriers technologically to shoot parts of this film.

the story is more modern and up date! hints at what the future holds, that manned aircraft will be a thing of the past soon. (there is a video i saw that explained how the film and lockheed-martin teamed up to create that futuristic aircraft at the start of the film, super cool 100% check that out). gone are the f-14 tomcats of the original film, with the f-18 (pretty sure its the super hornet) taking centre stage! (although itself being replaced by the f-35 these days). facing off against the new su-57, which was awesome to see! the mission is simple but effective and give us the chance to get behind a new, young team to take on this task....that seems almost "mission impossible"...haha get it ....its sad i find that amusing!

the cast for the most part are great, really bounce off each other and gel really well. every single character gets a little moment to shine, however some more than others. one of the biggest highlights for me was the cameo of val kilmer as iceman. it as handled incredibly well considering the health issues kilmer has suffered in his life. once again showing us a new technology to get around an issue, giving kilmer his voice back......gave me goosebumps!

cruise, directing, action, majority of the story and most of the characters worked for me!

i have a few negatives, firstly miles teller! i dislike this guy more and more every time i see him on screen. now finding out that he isn't the most likeable person to work with in the world either isn't a surprise. his performance for me doesn't work, feels forced and wooden at times.....secondly jennifer connelly. i love jennifer as an actress, always brilliant in everything she does and she is good in her role in this film. however for me, the character or relationship with maverick is not needed and doesn't really achieve anything for the story! i think it was just put into the film to nod back to the original film that had a love story thread! it easily could have been taken out of this film and not been missed!

lastly the ending! maybe i'm a sour person haha but i was really hoping for a sad ending. i think the story was hinting at it throughout but never payed it off. maverick dying to me would have done the character justice in the circumstances of this film. handing the torch over to a new generation of pilots! it would have been bold and worked well.........sadly they went for the easy option ! although even i'll admit that seeing the f-14 tomcat at the end was a cool !

75% out of 100 ! i would watch this over the original if i was given the chance, not saying the original is bad but this has more going for it in a modern context!

i struggled with rating this. i was between a 7 for story and an 8 for experiencing a movie going feeling i haven't had in years. i'm so happy i saw this at the theatre. it does not have as much charm and fun as the original. but, we are all in need of a popcorn big screen event and this delivers. you can tell there was a lot of effort put into the flight scenes which is why you should see it on the big screen. tom cruise is the movie star of the last half century. they somehow made a war movie that stays away from any politics. the casting is great. the audience i saw it with on early access tuesday made it fun. if you want an escape from the grueling topics of today, i highly recommend going to your local theater. i'd watch this by myself, on a date, or with the family. go see it just don't set your expectations too high.

top gun: maverick is certainly excellently shot and cinematically impressive, and no doubt one of the current leading examples of spectacular military aviation in modern film. however, the plot itself is the equivalent of a himbo-fest with (generally) shallow characters glossed in a sheen of eighties rock cuts. the ace lineup of the "top gun" (top 1%) of fighter jet pilot graduates are expectantly wry, hubristic, and engrossingly overconfident. the film seemingly attempts to bridge the jingoistic 1986 with 2022; creating warm-blooded eighties sensibilities crossed with cutting-edge 21st century accoutrements.

it's a popcorn flick through and through - and maverick (tom cruise) puts it best; "don't think, just act" (or better put; don't think, just watch)! let this polished top gun sequel-homage exercise its brazen bravado, and you might have a blast. don't let it fly over your head!

7.4/10.

top gun: maverick is not a great movie, but it is entertaining. it is a sequel to the 1986 film top gun and stars tom cruise as maverick, a hotshot fighter pilot who is struggling to come to terms with his past. he is ordered to train a new class of top gun pilots to run an impossible mission while dealing with the ghosts of his past.

there is nothing truly original about top gun: maverick. it is a standard hollywood action movie with predictable plot twists. what is outstanding is the aerial footage and the dogfight scenes. they are amazing! real pilots performed the stunts, and it shows.

like most tom cruise movies, the movie is all about tom cruise. he is the star, the producer, and the driving force behind the movie. and he delivers a solid performance. he may be getting older, but he can still play a convincing action hero.

if you are looking for a deep and meaningful movie experience, you will be disappointed. but if you want to see some awesome flying and some good old-fashioned action, then you will enjoy top gun: maverick. make sure you see it on a big screen!

i just got home after watching the movie in the theater on screenx, and while it certainly has its moments and delivers more than a few thrills, i think it was missing something, or rather, it left something on the table, the potential for a truly great movie. in my opinion, top gun: maverick was good, a bit above average, a solid 7.5, maybe even pushing an 8.0 out of 10, but that's mainly because of the visuals and action sequences, and i just think it could have been better in many areas, including the action sequences. i cannot understand how this has an 8.6 rating here, probably too many people lost in the spectacle and not thinking enough.

i don't know, maybe it's just me, but i think it needed a bit more of everything, a deeper core, that means more heart/soul. i know there was definitely something there, i'm not saying otherwise, but it could have gone just a bit deeper to make us feel a bit more. to me, the emotions never culminated, they never went all the way, the movie never took us all the way, and because of that, it just felt hollow or something, unsatisfying, at least for me.

and the same goes for the plot, it could have been just a bit more complex to give us a slightly fuller movie instead of the rather linear one-dimensional story we got. yeah, we got the character conflicts, some motivated by the backstory from the original movie, and of course, that colors the story and gives it context, but ultimately, this movie really goes pretty straight from a to b. there may have been a few pauses along the way, but no real detours, and it's the detours and meandering, when done well, not aimlessly wandering to find dead ends, that make a story more complex.

lastly, in regard to missed opportunity, and i don't understand why this most fundamental thing is absent from so many action movies, and that's the action climax, in this case, a true all-out battle. i wanted epic dogfight scenes, star wars with fighter jets if you will, but while we got a few nice set pieces, they could have taken it to the limit and pushed it over the top, mainly by using more planes, but they didn't. i don't know, maybe there are regulations on what can be done that prohibit such scenes, there probably are, but i wanted "controlled chaos," well, more controlled chaos; more, more, more. i mean, i feel the need, the need, for speed, taking me on the highway to the danger zone; i didn't quite get it.

but i suppose my biggest issue was, and yes, i know it's a movie, but i didn't really find it very believable. i get that it's tom cruise as maverick, and he's a legend, in the movie and in real life, but what he does in this movie strains credulity just a bit too much for me. i'm not saying you can't do it when you're old, but i think it's hard to do the impossible when you're old and out of practice, no matter how naturally talented someone is.

as said in the title - since a rather young age, i have been drooling and nerding about fighter jets.

the first time i have seen the original top gun, i haven't been aware of what is realistic and what not. yet even with this knowledge the original stays one of my favorite action movies - truly there are no particular great aviation movies out there..

but did top gun maverick improved on the original? yes and also no...

first of all - yes - the movie is just objectively better made. the flight scenes are absolutely stunning - and there are even mostly realistic planes flying (all of the main "protagonists'" planes are real types - not talking about the mig-28 from the original movie). except maybe the darkstar.

the problem is: there are also really massive issues.

one is lazy writing. so kudos for maverick to mention, that the f-35 would be the ideal airplane for the "main story mission". but lazy is, to take it out because of "gps jamming"... really? it could be so easy to say, that the f-35c didn't achieved combat readiness before the mission... or something along these lines...?!

but overall - the f/a-18 has nothing what the f-35 cannot do - maybe just, the experience of the superhornet sets it apart of the lightning ii.

then there is the issue that nobody really wants to say, that it is iran. but iran is the only country which still has f-14 tomcats. what they don't have yet though are su-57.

and the whole "felon" characteristics is simply nonsensical. the su-57 doesn't really exist - as serial model (only about 15 demonstrators where produced - of those 15 - 2 pre-serial models - at least one of those has been destroyed. it is absolutely fiction, to expect that the su-57 could be used for anti-air defense - especially not of iran.

also the sam defense could not be worse. you don't need to have every few km the same anti-air defense battery (one or two s-400 which look totally different are more than enough - plus maybe some short range systems).

also - the whole missile "thing" makes no sense. first: using "flares" against ground to air missiles which are normally seeking with radar makes no sense. second: if a missile is close - there is no way you can avoid it with fancy maneuvers. and where is the enemy awacs? if it is such a high value asset, there should be a form of awacs... oh - and then: there would be definitely detection - even if the planes would fly very low.

this makes me sad - because defending against air defense systems or against other aircrafts are far more like playing chess than than a "dogfight". with good writing and good cinematography it would have been possible to really catch the tension and the techniques a fighter pilot would use. but because of "action movie" - fantasy totally took over.

so all action scenes were breathtaking - but like a harry potter attack. "movie magic".

aside of the technical details: the "personnel" things were also not realistic. and focusing on dogfighting in the first "days" of training, while the mission mostly needed for ultra-low level flight? wtf...

i do think, with a bit more input of real fighter jet pilots and ex-military conductors, the movie could have been far better.

instead of the "magic" su-57, they could have used su-30. this is a fighter jet iran apparently really procured.

the whole mission could have been far more realistic. no need for this "villain lair" in the middle of a volcanic crate.

and to be honest: why should the pentagon ask the navy to do the job? if the target is so high value, a usaf b-2 spirit could enter the airspace without the enemy having a chance of detection - and it would have far more payload.

and even further - if the navy anyway attacked the runway near the high value target - why not using loads of cruise missile to destroy the target?

some realistic s-300 or s-400 could have been used. and yes - the f-35c would have been also sexy - instead of the workhorse f/a-18 (let's face it - both the super hornet and the lightning ii are workhorses and not as sexy as the tomcat in its time. but the f-35 is at least very modern and at the edge of technology - similar to the tomcat, when the original movie came out).

so no - the movie doesn't make any sense of a defense standpoint. this is sad, because the strategies and techniques are extremely interesting.

so... did i enjoyed top gun maverick? yes for sure. like an avenger movie. if you turn off your brain, it is perfectly fine entertainment - with a slight dash of propaganda.

what just makes me sad is: that it could have been just far better. but hollywood is hollywood i guess - and we are living anyway no more in a subjective reality?

captain pete 'maverick' mitchell (tom cruise) defies his superior's orders during a test flight, and breaks the sound barrier flying at super sonic speeds. despite his recklessness, those same superiors decide he's the best man to train a group of best-of-the-best fighter pilots who've graduated from the legendary 'top gun' academy, in a mission to take out a uranium plant in an iranian oilfield . along the way, mitchell reunites with faces from his past, including ailing former rival admiral tom 'iceman' kazinsky (val kilmer) and former love penny (jennifer connolly), while clashing with lt. bradshaw (miles teller), upon whom he honours the memory of a fallen comrade.

even before the time of covid and the current cost of living crisis, before cinema chains had to recoup their losses in a big way, the industry never broke out of the recessionary mindset and were only willing to take a chance on 'sure things.' and so sequels to long dormant franchises remained the order of the day. all the same, the producers of top gun: maverick were still taking a massive gamble, getting behind a sequel to a thirty six year old film that has more miles on its clock than most of the modern cinema demographic. however ingrained it may remain in the pop culture sphere, if a guy my age approaching forty has never actually seen the original, a younger generation would be even less likely to have had it cross their radar. nevertheless, the film has still broken box office records, emerging as the highest grossing film of the year so far, owing in no small part to a massive publicity campaign on tv and in the media. and you can't argue with success.

it certainly hits every mark on authenticity, with lead star cruise reportedly insisting (and paying for) all of the younger cast members to train with real life us fighter pilots to ensure a degree of accuracy on screen, which pays off. it recreates a sense of 80's style as well, that original director tony scott magnified from all of his films (this is meant as a tribute to him), especially the sense of glorified machismo from that time. the big problem, especially for a film stretching over the two hour mark, is that it's largely been designed to cater to fans of the original, from the soundtrack (minus, oddly, berlin's take my breath away) to the nods to the original, which, not having seen it, were lost on me.

it's all technically very impressive, and well made, but it required me to connect with a sense of nostalgia that i didn't have, and what remained really wasn't strong enough to carry it for me. ***

"top gun: maverick" (released 5/27/2022 (covid delayed 2 years), pg-13, 2hrs, star: tom cruise, director: joe kasinski) was almost a scene-for-scene remake/update of the original, simply changing character names and actors for most, though keeping the same characterizations in place. this is mine and many, many others' chief complaint, but maybe after a 37-year (!) wait, they could claim it's really for the generation that never experienced top gun (1986) though that's not really an excuse given the vcr rental years, the dvd rental years, and the streaming years. however, the final 45-mins of the new mission raised this from a 5 rating to 7 or even 8. it was a great departure from the original and really broke new ground with amped up air combat. yes, there was a lot of implausible crappola after maverick bailed out but it moved fast enough that you were kind of forced to accept it, part of the magic of movies. the final save scene was really reminiscent of 2012's "battleship" so that kind of paved the way for this. but this kind of "yea us military!" seems out of place in today's world, though it's $1.5b box office will make it hard to dissuade producers of that.

top gun: maverick is a fantastic piece of film that entertains and immerses you into into the top gun world. i think that the storyline carries over well and tom cruise returning as the flight captain was a great choice.

i'm also pretty interested in the fact that the actors were really in the planes for the scenes. that adds a whole different level of production and i can't even imagine the planning that went into something like this.

overall very enjoyable.

on paper top gun maverick is the sort of film i despise. it is a hollywood blockbuster film sequel of a beloved (though overrated) 80s pop corn film classic, yet i found myself won over. the original film itself does not justify a sequel so that justification needed to be earned by the film and it to earned it. on the surface it has all the makings of a rubbish film. characters with little depth and a greater emphasis on action and spectacle. yet those qualities are what make top gun 2 work. people have described films such as 2001 a space odyssey and apocalypse now as experiential films as they have a greater emphasis on the cinematic experience which is used to further enhance specific idea. i think this can be applied to some extent to top gun maverick, though naturally any comparison beyond this would be practically blasphemous. top guns main appeal comes from the cinematic experience. it is an immersive film by design and this is where it it succeeds at. one of the problems with the the first film was its emphasis on character but given the characterisation was rather blunt and surface level, it resulted in a rather cheesy and corny film which at many points are rather laughable in execution with the flying being in the background. the flying scenes have always been the highlight and top gun masterfully makes use of it. its by no means perfects as the character beats are fairly cliché and predictable and it does annoyingly repeat a lot of elements from the original. overall it is an exciting and thoroughly entertaining film and a suggested watch if you want a nice piece of escapism.

top gun: maverick (2022) follows maverick as he finds himself training a group of graduates for a specialised mission. this is a very fun and heartwarming film! i feel i would've liked it more if i had nostalgia for the first top gun, but this is definitely a solid film!

the visual effects and stunts look very good, but i expected a little more from the cinematography. the action sequences are so much fun to watch, especially in the third act, this really adds the tension built up. the colour palettes are subtle, and there's some good camerawork and use of slow motion, but it doesn't feel imaginative.

the soundtrack used is very 80s and really adds a lot of life to the film, and the sound design is fairly decent. however, the score feels a little basic and forgettable.

there are some great performances in this film, and in my opinion, miles teller really outshines tom cruise. the actors have a lot of chemistry and contrast well with each other, and i ended up really caring for their characters! the dialogue is pretty good too, and there's some very funny lines.

the film sets up the story well, however it is quite hard to fully get into and isn't immediately engaging. the plot does feel a little messy at times and i got a bit confused, but this really picks up in the final act which is incredibly tense and gripping!

a few months ago i watched the original 1986 first "top gun" and it is still today a solid movie, with amazing aircraft fights scenes and memorable characters such as "goose". however, it had several flaws, such as the love story between pete and charlie that took way too much screen time, the ridiculous dialogues lines and the general cheesy american patriotism that was so beloved by the audience during the 80's. this sequel fixed all these issues and it is a way better movie. the action sequences are amazing and kept me on the verge, as the good guys are very often in difficult situations that are difficult to solve. interactions and conflicts between different characters are believable. i loved how the relationship between maverick and bradshaw evolves along the way. the director played just the right dose of nostalgia with some sequences that were obviously quoting the original production.

i feel that this movie achieved a lot: these were two intense hours and the payback for the audience is huge. you get to see a movie with a simple and yet entertaining story. the photography is phenomenal and there are some scenes that are truly breathtaking, especially if you watch them on a big screen. cast members delivered some good performances, even though i was not very impressed by any of the actors, including tom cruise. he looked and sounded pretty average, i was expecting more under this department, especially from a star of this caliber. the music is always on point and there is a nice mix between rock classics, orchestral music composed by hans zimmer and some modern pop songs. i was pretty skeptical about this film, because usually sequels made several years after the original entry often disappoint me. here instead, i was pleasantly surprised.

have you ever been to chilis, applebees, or pizza hut and it was better than you thought it was going to be? you get dragged to these places because someone (not you) decided that it was the least risky place to meet another couple. the food comes, and you're dreading it...and then..blammo! the food tastes great.

that is what this movie is. i have to say that a 30+ year gap between the original and the sequel did not promise much to me. i think of the shows that i stopped watching because they were on hiatus during the pandemic and i just couldn't get back into them--i'm looking at you killing eve. so 30+ years? i didn't have high expectations. suffice to say...they were all exceeded.

this sequel catches up to captian pete mitchell (cruise) who, in the intervening three decades, has accumulated a closet full of accommodations, achievements and feats that were distinguished...distinguished...distinguished (inside joke for those who've seen it). now, "the enemy" (an enemy nation is never mentioned by name) has built a site to weaponize uranium that is in the bottom of this canyon rimmed with sams and only low-altitude fighter jets can fly in under the radar and blow it to smithereens.

the brass want cruise to train the latest crop of top gun graduates to do the mission. so he is given twelve fighter jockeys to mold into a team--this attack has to be done by four aircraft. and the predictable, contrived, and all-too-familiar devices come into play. cruise meets his team the night before he is introduced to them. in a bar. where everyone is singing. they embarrass themselves. even tossing him out of the bar onto the beach. the next morning...the 2nd in command announces him to the class from a podium in front of the twelve aviators. cruise walks up right through the middle of them just like kelly mcgillis did in the original. the pained expressions of the fighter jocks take place next. there is competition, humiliation, insubordination, passion, a beach scene where they are playing two way football at the same time!!! the brass isn't happy with maverick, the fighter jocks aren't happy with maverick...the new penny (played by jennifer connelley) isn't happy with maverick...

so the mission comes up. the "graduation-cut-short" scene in this film is that the uranium enrichment plant is coming on-line early and the crews have to accelerate their training. the 12 jocks all try to fly a simulated run to knock out the enrichment site but can't get it done. mav pushes them hard but they are not able to do it....tempers flare and mav has it out with one of the fighter jocks. and because of this--mav is grounded by the brass. huh? here is where the movie loses what little credibility it had to start with. apparently the pilot who is distinguished...distinguished...distinguished enough but only got one grade promotion in the last 30 years didn't do anything egregious enough to get grounded. but somehow in this movie, he stepped over the line (where no lives were lost) and got grounded when "the enemy" is about to enrich uranium and destroy the world? nope.

so, what does mav do? he, of course, steals a plane and shows that the mission can be done. so what does the brass do? of course, they name him mission lead...the guy they grounded 3 scenes earlier.

the logical fallacies in the move are too numerous to count. for example, the reason four planes have to fly this mission is because they are in pairs. one of the planes points a laser onto a target while the other plane fires the missile. the next pair do the same thing but actually blow up the facility. somehow, high level bombers couldn't do this? the opening scene in the movie saw maverick's program being shut down so unmanned drones could be funded. perhaps they could have done this mission? the pathway they fly down to the uranium enrichment site are lined with sams (dozens of them) but "the enemy" didn't think to put sams right at the site itself? there are dozens more.

back to the movie. the rest is predictable so i won't go too much into it. to the shock of no-one, i'm sure, the mission is a success. what happens after the success of the mission though is straight out of monty python. its almost comedic.

the saving grace of this movie are the fighter scenes. they truly are spectacular. i'm sure there was plenty of cgi but, unlike a lot of films, you can't really tell the cgi part. connelley and cruise sizzle on the screen. i hope those two make another film together...there is some real chemistry between them.

so i give this movie a 7 out of 10. much like chilis, applebees, and pizza hut....sometimes they hit the mark just right. but, in the back of your mind, you know that there is better food down the street.

i only watched the original "top gun" for the first time in the last couple of weeks, and if i'm honest, i didn't really care for it. i saw this follow up more out of a lack of something better to do, rather than any real desire - but i was pleasantly surprised about how much i enjoyed it.

after years as a test pilot, pete mitchell (tom cruise) returns to the 'top gun' aviation school to teach a group of the navy's best pilots. rather than just general improvement though, mitchell is tasked with getting them ready for a specific mission, to destroy an underground nuclear bunker belonging to a hostile force. the decision of which pilots to send on this dangerous mission is made more difficult when bradley bradshaw (miles teller) the son of his late co-pilot goose (anthony edwards), is one of the class.

whilst i wouldn't go as far as to say that this is one of my favourite films, i don't think it's even the best film i've seen this week, i would say that maverick redresses my two problems with the original film. there's an actual story to this one, rather than just a bunch of unconnected scenes. the film builds to an actual mission, which we get to see, rather than just a completely random encounter. the paying off of the relationship between maverick and bradley is alright and the interactions with jennifer connelly's character and the returning val kilmer are nicely done.

the dogfighting scenes are much improved too. real footage of the actors in planes is integrated with the exterior shots but everything is a lot more dynamic and easier to follow than with the previous film. the film in general really looks wonderful but those scenes in the air are really first rate.

it's not much more than a better version of the original but it's certainly an entertaining time.

it's actually a really good follow up to top gun, ticks all the boxes. action romance drama however the scene between tom and jennifer was not needed it didn't add anything and was only an annoyance. the film was a good action film by with tom cruise as actor it just didn't need a love story to be added in the idea could have been planted and then just left in the back ground not needing any more focus on the relationship between maverick and rooster that is more important for this film, a love arc is far from needed i hoped for so much more with this but should have guessed with tom cruise as a part.

i probably have a very different view of this film than others. the beginning was absolutely brilliant and the music drew me in immediately. the pace was quite fast so it didn't always take too long for some action to occur or it just went by quickly because i was having fun. as far as the action goes, it's much better compared to the 80's one, which is quite logical considering the evolution of cinematography with better cameras and better effects. so hats off to the action scenes. very nice show. what was also better in my opinion was the story. more interesting and, i would say, more suspenseful. it was all so cool and i enjoyed it so much, but there was one thing i missed terribly much and that was the song take my breath away. i understand that they didn't want to repeat themselves and give it a new twist, but when the song danger zone was played, which put a smile on my face, the aforementioned take my breath away would have made me even happier. all this time i was waiting and hoping in vain that at least for a moment it would be heard, but nothing. for me, it was an incredible shame. it very much brought the film down for me. to sum it up. top gun: maverick will be better than the original 1986 one for many people. it was good. a lot of people will be excited and i definitely recommend it to fans of the first one. just giving my opinion here. a lot of people will probably remember top gun for the fighter jet action scenes, which are plentiful and really great and sometimes very suspenseful. it's because they're i'd say better that this film has gotten so much positive feedback. but i had a different take on the original top gun and that was the 80s atmosphere, which was brought out beautifully by the song take my breath away. this movie is not from the 80s anymore. that's a fact. but if they've done danger zone, i'd ask for take my breath away. i'm repeating myself enough. this thing bothered me, unfortunately. don't get me wrong. this movie is hilarious and like i said you probably won't regret going to see it. i just wanted to say that for me, unfortunately, the absence of the aforementioned song made it lose the charm i loved so much about top gun. other than that, a good film for me and i recommend it.

i was worried about this movie because the first one was terrible in my opinion. this blew me away, fantastic camera work, captivating story, great acting, and cool planes. my complaints would be that the love story is out of place and random at times. they tried to restore nostalgia in a few places that could have been left out. finally, the idea of maverick being bullied by everyone seems out of place considering how accomplished he is. other than that, i thought this was an amazing movie and was even better in theaters.

given the mixed, to be generous, results of reviving long dormant movie titles how good could this film really be? pretty darn good it turns out.

of all the films to bring into the modern era top gun is on paper one of the hardest to mesh with current sensibilities. the america is bad ass spirit and corny dialogue that ruled the roost in 1986 just shouldn't work in 2022 but the filmmakers inject just enough 21st century flavour to deliver a blockbuster experience for everyone.

the films success is down to two things, the moviestar charisma of tom cruise and the practical effects. people flying around in planes shouldn't be so thrilling but after years of someone standing in front of a green screen pretending to blast tennis balls on sticks there is no doubt the air of authenticity takes the action scenes to another level.

the main challange the filmmakers face is finding suitable real world bad guys and a modern day mission requiring expert fighter pilots. the movie goes to laughable lengths to obsure who the enemy is but it is probably the right call. we settle for some small unamed rougue state backed by one of the also unamed big boys. the actual mission is, if course, ridiculously precise in what it requires but provides the perfect conditions for dramatic tension.

cheesy but plenty of fun, maverick is better than it has any right to be.

is this a top gun or tom cruise career film?

this film brings a nostalgic and amazing old feeling as it looks that we are watching a movie in the 80s or 90s. but why in 2022 americans still look arrogant, coky and the best thing the world have to offer?

i'm sure this movie was very very expensive to make and tom cruise is on it and he is probably the best action actor career still in active but is this movie so great that the entire world was crasy about it? "oscar winner" and all... top gun was a movie about friendship, overcoming the impossible, confidence, competition, beeing american (40 years ago) with one of the best soundtracks of all time.

and now? is it a take 2, 40 years later with a complete disproportional notion of the american ideals and mentality of the 21th century. with tom cruise and a extence budget. it could be a cinema movie but it entertains very little, it could be fantasy but is not either fantasy or reality. general idea is a movie to watch one time in your lifetime and forget.

this was an entertaining, theater film worth seeing "for old time's sake" despite its cringe-worthy acting, script and plot. outstanding action scenes, well filmed there. the sailing scene was fun. tom cruise wasn't doing anything new but he's good and i like him. like eating an in n out burger. you don't expect fusion or intrigue, but it's still good every time.

shots of text message convos are poor cinematography. panning over the photo of mav and iceman about six times is wasted space. cliche shots abound. character expressions and personalities are canned and might as well be cgi. "dad and 'son' wrenching together" shot made me cringe-how cheesy can you get? there are countless scenes like this. are we in the zombie apocalypse that so few others seemed to notice this? i watched this again with my wife recently and she, not a movie aficionado, cringed outwardly, without my prompting.

looping back around to the positives: no political agendas! tom cruise, way to go, you've brought all of america together around a movie by not clobbering viewers with divisive agendas. that alone brought this film from 5 to 7 stars. hollywood take note. a distinctly subpar, cliche movie got ridiculously high ratings, and one of the primary reasons was that it united people instead of dividing them.

but let's be clear. the original was groundbreaking. i'm in my thirties and i'm saying that. top gun: maverick was like a nice daydream.

have people really become so starved of traditional blockbusters that they think top gun: maverick is something special? this genre was everywhere in the 80s and 90s.

it follows very closely in the footsteps of the original. in fact a couple of scenes are shot-by-shot tributes. but it rarely stretches itself.

the only scene that adds a new angle is at the very end, where dogfighting results in us airmen on the ground behind enemy lines, who have to find an unconventional way of escaping. this final mission is the best part of the film overall.

but generally speaking it doesn't have the charm or energy of the 1986 original. top gun focused on young pilots who were building their lives, finding their friendships, and facing up to rivalries. maverick gives us an older captain pete mitchell who doesn't really have anything to prove. and the younger cast don't really have enough screen time. adding a female pilot to the mix, while more contemporary, drains all the crude machismo out of the situation. but that crude machismo was part of the charm.

by far the worst part of top gun: maverick is the introduction of jennifer connelly as the love interest. thankfully she is age-appropriate for cruise, but her character is so obviously a substitute for kelly mcgillis' charlie that it becomes embarrassing. she seems to be living in the same beachfront house, and even drives a classic silver porsche (a 911 this time instead of a 356). it just isn't a convincing romance and could have easily been left out of the whole film.

best moments are the flying scenes, with their slick combination of real footage and cgi. again, these are clearly inspired by the formula created in top gun, but with an extra layer of slickness and complexity that makes them feel modern yet still suspend-your-disbelief realistic (take note, superhero movies).

there is a brief yet touching appearance from val kilmer (who has been battling cancer in recent years), and glen powell and miles teller both put in decent performances. but overall the cast just isn't as engaging as in top gun.

top gun: maverick delivers what we should expect from a big budget production with a talented cast. but it doesn't deliver anything beyond that. it's good. but not that good.

but the cast was good. miles was great and glenn powell reminded me of val kilmer. monica barbarob was also good. and tom cruise was great as always. the sequel was missing the great soundtrack the original had. it was also missing that special friendship that maverick and goose had. i liked that val kilmer was there from the original. top gun original will always be a classic. it's been more than 30 years old and people still love the soundtrack, cast and quotes from the original. this second one will only be remembered as tom cruise movie. he is the only memorable guy in it. even though i love tom. i think they should have kept him as the teacher and made the students the focus point. he could have worked through his issues with goose's son and actually had a conversation with him. they also should have said what happen to his love interest from part 1. they could have divorced. instead they never mentioned her.

'top gun: maverick' manages to achieve the impossible when it comes to modern summer movies, and that's finding the perfect balance of crowd-pleasing entertainment and a quality movie.

i originally had no interest or excitement for this movie and wasn't planning on seeing it in the cinema, until i saw the glorying reviews it received that convinced me to check it out, and i'm glad i did.

this was the most satisfying movie experience of the year.

all the flying sequences...well, it took my breath away. but surprisingly the story had a lot of heart to it, and some emotional scenes that i didn't expect to strike a chord with me. it keeps you on your toes and it's entertaining throughout. it's got heart, humour, and most of all a sense of freedom.

tom cruise is fantastic in this by the way. he's a great action star but the movie reminds us of his dramatic chops.

i also like the fact that this movie openly acknowledges that he is getting old. unlike the 2017 movie 'the mummy', where one of russell crowe's lines refers to cruise's character as a "young man", despite cruise being two years older than him. i mean, he looks so good for his age, but there's one scene in this movie where he's shirtless on a beach and he's got that body of someone approaching 60.

the chemistry between jennifer connelly and cruise was electrifying and believable.

also, how the movie handled val kilmer's character and how they wrote kilmer's real health condition into the movie was beautifully handled.

you don't need to see the first movie to understand what's going on in this one. it's a sequel that doesn't rely too much on nostalgia. the sequel is a massive improvement over the original, while at the same time it respects the 1986 film and director tony scott.

overall rating: 'top gun: maverick' is one of the biggest surprises of the year. with this being tom cruise's highest-grossing film of all time, i can see why, as there's something re-watchable about it.

lots of mindless action, and a vague and implausible storyline here... but it was a fun watch. but so many "ouch" moments...

rebellious ne'er do well steals a billion dollar plane, sets a new speed record, and then crashes it with no repercussions? ouch. impossible mission, yet maverick chooses to bench the best pilot in favor of the sentimental, but illogical choice? ouch. stealing a relic usa plane from an enemy base, yet it's all gassed up and operational, sitting there waiting, with all munitions loaded up? ouch. hideously outgunned yet thrives in a david vs. two goliaths battle? ouch. and so many more...

to me, the biggest "ouch" were all the shameless throwbacks to the original film. literally every scene was an unnecessary homage to the original. just too much. they could easily have made an exciting top gun sequel without all the sappy throwbacks. totally detracted from the film... and every maverick-rooster exchange was cringeworthy.

so, an okay action film, absurdly hyped, spoiled by too much absurdity and faux sentimentality... but still a decent (if not grotesquely predictable) watch. ouch.

anyone who carries a lot of nostalgia for the first "top gun" will probably slobber all over themselves and this sequel. those who don't, me included, may think this is either a decently entertaining popcorn flick or a dumb piece of cinematic fast food. or maybe it can be both those things at the same time.

and let's call this what it really is. it's not a sequel -- it's a reboot. it nearly recreates the original movie scene by scene (we even have to have a character with a mustache!) when it's not ripping off the "star wars" death star trench run wholesale.

tom cruise never ages, and that seems creepy to me. it's refreshing for once to see jennifer connelly in a sexy role, and boy does she try hard to be sexy. she practically licks tom cruise's face every time they have a scene together. you can tell this movie really wishes that nothing since around the year 2000 had happened and that the world still wants nothing but movies about macho white guys saving people. but it also understands that it has to at least pretend to be progressive, so hey look, there's a woman pilot! there's a black guy! how far we've come!

grade: b+

perhaps people really just needed something familiar. this was not a great movie. the writing was standard for an action film, but considerably less funny than most. the action was excellent, but bracketed with an ill-conceived love story between cruise and connelly with no discernable chemistry. to read the early reviews you would think this was saving private ryan, but in fact it was a lesser version of the original. the sentimental inclusion of val kilmer was a nice touch, but felt exploitative at times. some of the scenes were hard to suspend disbelief, like a bar full of gen z pilots listening and singing along exclusively with 1970's and 1950's rock ballads. i guess i was just expecting too much based upon the prior ratings, but this is not on my top 10 movies of 2022, and not on my top 20 tom cruise movies.

i didn't like the original movie that much as i thought the story was boring and nothing really exciting happend, but this sequel was definitely better. i was intrigued right from the beginning and i liked the role of tom cruise's character of being a fighter pilot teacher. i liked the action scenes which were shot well and the fight scenes and explosions looked realistic. i thought the ending was kind of cliche, but it was entertaining nonetheless. i'm a bit surprised that the movie grossed over 1.4 billion dollars as it feels like the only movies that gross over 1 billion dollars are marvel and other superhero movies, so this is a refreshing thing to see.

good movie. actor playing rooster looks a lot like goose. tom cruise is the greatest in the business. but one thing bothered me. the enemy planes were presented as spectacular, enemy pilots were bad ass to the core, yet they didn't manage to take one down? this is the part of american movie making world hates and this is why i give this movie 7. on the movie making perspective - amazing. camera work is truly brilliant and i liked the romantic moment with old porsche and gaga's song. it was 80's vibe we all wanted. acting actually wasn't that great except mr. cruise's. he really is one of the best if not the best in the business.

this movie is made to attract a large audience. without trying to spoil, i would love to highlight some topics.

* lots of memories for those who watched top gun. they tried to reuse settings, styles and events. gen xers who watched top gun in their youth will have a 80ties flashback.

* no named enemy. it is clear that they fight someone, but this enemy is very unspecific. that way, you are inclusive.

* diversity. we have a female pilot and every skin color is present (we might argue that we are missing a bit asian american presence, but this is common in all modern movies, focus seems to be to include african americans). the only thing missing was a gay person, but sexuality was not a topic in this movie (besides the one of maverick) * maverick, the one and only, he is the hero. he and just he. it is difficult to write about it without spoiling something, but sometimes it feels it has been written also for tom cruise.

* still, the movie provides what every one wants. suspense, emotions, conflicts to be resolved, friendship, sexual attraction, sentimentality.

all in all, i see top gun: maverick as a very good movie, just i do not see it as an elite movie. i assume this high rating is there because they do not piss off any group.

top gun: maverick is a movie that opens with excitement and spark which is dazzling enough to make you buckle up your seat for what's coming. right from the opening shot to everything that follows in the first act, radiates an amount of energy that hits the spot well and doesn't quite miss. the actors in the film starting from tom cruise to miles teller, val kilmer and everyone else works as perfect catalysts that balance the ongoing plot and the story that keeps moving forward at a perfect pace. talking about the story, it takes off and lands later on a smooth runway with no extra new flavor to add to the dish. the other departments have also done a good job with notable mentions of sound and cinematography whereas the editing could have gotten one more polish. director joseph kosinski has created a platter of dishes that fills you up just enough so that it doesn't get bloated. all in all top gun: maverick stands high as a movie that enters the room does its part, and leaves on a good note.

a sequel to top gun (1986): captain pete mitchell aka maverick (tom cruise) is a top-notch military pilot in his fifties and is assigned to train ten exceptional recruits to destroy a uranium enrichment plant.

this film might be confusing to those unfamiliar with the prequel but for the rest of us, it fits as fine entertainment.

the main character is fascinating in that he is confident of his exceptional talents while being self-aware enough to know that using his talents to climb a career path with a series of promotions is just not his thing. in this way, he is a tribute many who are like him who march to the beat of a different drummer rather than cave in to mainstream standards.

the grand finale seems standard but it is enhanced by a solid plot twist. overall, "top gun: maverick" is big-budget hollywood at its best with many thrills. - dbamateurcritic.

usually when an imdb rating has the true peak around 10 or even theoretically higher, i'm sure it must be an outstanding movie. with this one the fan base seems to have drifted the result heavily.

too often the cringe in this movie threw me out. i gave it a 7, mainly for the nice action scenes. some well spent effort went into these. although unrealistically unnecessarily dangerous maneuvers, when it's just training, like only choreographed show pilots can do. but i get it, they're the best of the best, this is too easy for them...

but otherwise the story is flat, unrealistic and extremely cliché driven: an old fart showing the younglings he's still the best, by far, easily on the first try.

for thirty years simply nobody has come close to his physique and skill, so he must do the job himself. he doesn't give a lot about rules, but the executives can't do much about it, since he's the maverick.

no mention worthy other characters or character development, apart from the maverick. probably by design, since he's just too special for the rest.

on the side he impresses his ex so hard in a couple of days that she forgets she's an adult. the charms of a returning rebel and overachiever is apparently irresistible to any woman. but this time of course it's gonna be the perfect relationship.

then the usual old plot about not leaving a single soldier behind, even if it's plain stupid and a calculated risk in a secret mission anyway. but of course it works out, since nobody tries to hunt them down in the woods. the incompetent enemy being in full chaos, they manage to escape in a stolen rusty old plane. but only because somebody is always there to rescue the protagonist, literally the very last millisecond.

finally returning to the carrier, the whole ship celebrates like winning a championship, despite the fact that probably almost none of them should know what just happened.

verdict: just watch the awesome flight action scenes and skip through the rest.

positives:

1) tom cruise is a phenomenal performer. the stunt work is of course breathtaking, but he is also a brilliant actor that is able to portray all of the complex emotions and feelings that maverick goes through, particularly with regards to aging and to the loss of goose 2) the imax plane sequences are what the movie sells itself on and they are sensational. the film gets as close as it can to putting you in the cockpit with the pilots, while also never making you lose your sense of geography in terms of where all of the planes are in relation to each other 3) i thought the film paid homage to the first film in a really great way. the musical cues are obviously great, but its mainly the relationships that have the most impact. maverick is still reeling from the loss of goose, which plays brilliantly into his relationship with rooster, and the film also expands on his relationship with iceman in a really compelling way. also, having maverick and rooster fly in an old f14 plane from the first film at the end was a really nice touch and led to some good moments

negatives:

1) jennifer connelly's character should've been cut completely. this would shorten the runtime by around 20 minutes, making it a much more relentless experience, while also cutting out all of the moments where i was bored. her character has no impact on the main story and, while i understand this is a minor point, it really bothered me that she's shown to be running this extremely busy bar on her own when that would be impossible and would take about 10 staff to run in real life 2) the film is just so american and therefore, to a non-american life myself, it became overly cringey at several moments for me. some of the dialogue was very cringeworthy and the scene where they all play topless football on the beach while that god awful one republic song played was almost vomit inducing. it's also incredibly obvious what is going to happen throughout, especially that maverick is going to become team leader, so i think a bit of subtlety and nuance would've been welcome 3) while there were some nice moments in the last 15 minutes that wouldn't have happened if they changed the ending, i personally think the film would've been better if maverick sacrificed his life for rooster like the film teases he might have. this would've been a fitting end for maverick's character, going out as a hero in battle, whilst also avoiding the ending we got, which grew quite repetitive.

if you forget teh last quarter of the movie, it's really good, for today hollywood standards. it's proven (again) that cruise can't make a bad movie.

soundtrack ( gaga) is nowhere close to the original.

honestly this could be closer to a 6.5 but for what it is, it is a comfortable 7.

i was never a big fan of top gun. i know it was all the rage in the days of my youth, but i never loved it all that much. that's not to say i disliked it, but i never for a minute thought the world needed a sequel almost 40 years later. turns out most of the world disagreed and has welcomed this movie with open arms, so i finally decided i needed to see what all the fuss was about. turns out, while i may not have been all that crazy about the original top gun, this film is passionately in love with it. some requels like to drop little nods throughout the runtime to the original film, but this one just drops in clips of it. characters from the original are treated like mythical gods worthy of worship and praise. it's really the weakest aspect of top gun: maverick that it is so tied into that film it doesn't fully take off and tell its own story. it was so bad that i started to chuckle how every single time iceman was mentioned or appeared on screen they would cut to a photo of him and maverick shaking hands at the end of the original film. i fully expected an inappropriately placed cut to that same image in a later scene related to iceman which would have felt horribly inappropriate (luckily, they didn't go there.) things eased up a little in the latter half of the film, but the entire first act is just a nonstop reminder that the writers and directors really loved that movie from 1986 and you should too. i have to guess that for lovers of the original this must be truly delightful, even if some of it was lost on me.

all that being said, when top gun: maverick dares to attempt telling a new story it is a fun romp. it reminds me of the kind of fast-paced action films we got back in the 80s and for that i applaud the film-makers. even though the plot is ridiculously predictable, and the characters feel like carbon-copies of people we've seen before, i was still invested in their mission. i liked the fact that they didn't even broach the subject of what country they were attacking, instead they left it completely ambiguous (and didn't even show us the faces of the enemy) so we don't have to go down a rabbithole of explaining how the us could get away with this kind of military attack on another country. i liked the training sequences, and how maverick shows the kids up, while also showing them what can be done. i wanted more of that, because the transition to the final mission felt rushed. this is where many of the memory-montages could have been jettisoned (along with the pointless love story) and left room to flesh out all the training the kids go through. i also had some sliver of hope that the film-makers would recognize all the homoerotic undertones of these films, and just embrace it by making the main guys actual homosexuals, but i suppose that would be a hard sell when the alt-right review-bombs movies for any minor thing they find morally objectionable. anyways, i grudgingly admit that top gun: maverick made for a fun day at the movies (i even liked it better than the original,) but i think it could have really soared if it was a stand-alone film.

here is my take and why i think its an "okay" film, just not a great one. there really isn't a whole lot of meat and potatoes to this story. it's largely a copy pasta in large chunks from the older film but with newer, younger faces. maverick is charged with training a squadron of top gun fighter pilots to destroy an enemy uranium enrichment plant that is about to come online and operational. but it seems the producers want to maximize the profits for this film and not offend anyone in the real world. so this enemy doesn't have a name or a geographical location. the enemy has 5th generation fighter jets and some james bond evil villian sized sam batteries around the mountain's summit. it is a snow covered terrain so that rules out many enemies in warmer climates.

then there is the lone aircraft carrier delivering these jet fighters to the enemies doorstep. well, by now most people know that wouldn't be the case. carriers are heavily guarded and their presence would trigger the attention of any adversary. no way could four f18 sneak in under radar to blow up this plant unless we accept the enemy isn't aware of a huge freakin carrier of their shores. so there is nothing resembling a realistic scenario and that kept me from enjoying the story too much.

the romantic relationship in the film has no chemistry. i just didn't feel any chemistry between penny and maverick. that's a first because you do have two very good looking actors and i always thought tom cruise to be great action actor. so no chemistry between cruise and jennifer connelly is a bitter pill to swallow.

what i did like about it was the cinematography and some of the action sequences with the dog fighting. but i didn't think the dog fighting were any better than the original film. in fact, the original film might have had better scenes. this film just has a lot of choppy editing to imply action.

i think its a 6/10, but not a chance it's a 9/10. maybe if they added a tom clancy inspired screenplay to the film i might have given it a 9. maybe a team of seals to do recon before having the jets engage and with the aircraft carrier companied by a battlegroup flotilla. aircraft carriers just don't end up secretly off the shore of adversarial country completely alone, not in the real world.

i drove an hour each way to see this in a movie theater, my first visit to one a couple of years because i wanted to get the full cinematic experience. what i got was a huge pile of corn. if not for the flying sequences, which are awesome, the rest of the movie is a bit pants. ed harris is in it for a single scene, more of a cameo role than anything. val kilmer's scene was embarrassing. jennifer connelly is looking her age and plays a half baked love interest which frankly the film could have done without. is she supposed to be the kelly mcgillis role from the original movie? she lives in a very similar house and she drives a porsche so who knows? the plot revolves around a mission so uniquely unlikely that it makes the movie slightly preposterous. the cast of pilots don't hold a candle to the original cast and their characters are two dimensional and boring. it isn't tom cruise's best performance either playing the eponymous maverick, a man still plagued by the death of his buddy, goose from the first movie. come on, man. that was 35 years ago, get over it ffs! jon hamm, who i normally like doesn't look comfortable playing maverick's up tight commander and there's a scene of beach football which is supposed to mirror the volleyball scene from the first movie but just looks gay af. once again the flying scenes are unbelievable, by that i mean extremely believable. the actors must have actually been in the planes for at least some of the shots and cgi has been kept to a minimum which is great to see. but take away those sequences, which don't account for much run time, maybe 15% of total run time, and what you have left is quite poor.

all in all, its a by the numbers follow on which probably should have been made 15 years ago or not all. i'm sure part of my disappointment is how much of a pop culture effect the first one had on my generation and that this is a pale imitation compared to it. six out of ten might seem generous, but i guess i just don't want to "lose that loving feeling".

i'll say the positive thing first, lest you misunderstand my better-than-5 rating: in terms of reboots, this one does its job adequately well. in a sea of reboot flops that i've given way worse ratings to (movies like any star wars film after the original trilogy, and the matrix reboots, or tv shows like csi vegas, or star trek picard) this one isn't a complete waste of time. it tells a decent story despite a dearth of dialog, is visually beautiful, and is paced nicely.

now the tough love: this movie is as formulaic as it gets. interestingly, one of the main themes of the movie is that a pilot needs to be less conservative in order to do great things, yet the makers of this movie took essentially no risks. instead of new, bold concepts, they recycle old ones over and over. cast with a bunch of square-jawed, buff actors, and possibly written via blockbuster mad libs. tons of references to the 1980s original, good at times, but seemed overdone. even more self-referential in-movie callbacks, including cheesy one-liners, to the point of eye rolls that nearly detached my retinas. a simplistic, black and white world where one rogue cowboy with a heart of gold, who women can't help but fall in love with, defies orders from rigid superiors to save the day... you can practically hear lethal weapon dialog every time a commanding officer chews maverick out for breaking the rules while being the best. ed harris gives a speech that sounded stolen from agent smith in the matrix. the mission is recycled from the star wars death star fatal vent shaft flaw... i'm surprised maverick didn't make reference to bullseye'ing womp rats in his t-16 back home.

it feels like a script written in the 1980s, with a mysterious, faceless, generic enemy, that was mothballed until 2022... which is both a good and bad thing simultaneously. it does accentuate the nostalgia of rebooting an old franchise, one of the main reasons to even give the movie a try, so sure to please the older crowd.

i had high expectations for "top gun maverick", considering the hype and an imdb rating of 8.5. but it became all too apparent within the first few minutes of the opening scenes, that this "new" film was basically a rehash of the original top gun, with updated aircraft and a lot more focus on tom cruise. the dialogue was mostly average, and often cringeworthy, and very cliched. but it's not all bad news either. the fighter jet scenes are nothing short of exhilarating, and you can see that a lot of effort went into filming them. sound effects of the jets in action add to the immersive experience of this film. all in all though, i came away with the sense that i'd pretty much seen it all before (i just re-watched the original with my daughter before watching the new film), and the outcome was ever so predictable. i have no idea why this film is currently rated as the 58th greatest movie of all time. that's an insult to some truly exceptional films which are ranked well below this one. for a film to be ranked in the top100 of all time i think it needs to be more than a mere 2-hour entertaining diversion, it really needs a solid script, engaging characters, and a story that that we might still be thinking about long after the hype dies down.

this is a slightly modernized version of the original. it has the same essence and feel, which is impressive after 36 years. it's enjoyable and mostly well-made with certain scenes living up to the term "blockbuster." it's definitely worth watching in imax, especially with the expanded aspect ratio.

the flight scenes are once again fantastic, with the only flaw being too many cuts instead of holding on a shot. the story is investing with some good heart. the musical score is awesome. tom cruise somehow continues to do his own stunts, which adds a realism that we don't see as often these days. he even has a running scene like in so many of his movies. but i can't blame him, he's really good at it.

on the other hand, i'm generally not a fan of 80's movies so that aspect didn't do as much for me as it will for others. and some of the nostalgia stuff feels a bit forced. they still memorize and sing the same songs 36 years later?

in the end, i had a good time with this movie. big fans of the original will love it, and casuals will be entertained. (1 viewing, early screening imax 5/24/2022)

if you're taking into consideration all great films this is a 6 at best.
