to convey what i think of top gun: maverick properly, i'll make an analogy that will take a moment. i'm not sure if anyone has heard of the mythical kitchen, which is an off-shoot of the youtube series good mythical morning with rhett and link, but josh from the mythical kitchen is quite the craftsperson when it comes to making the most gourmet fast food you've never thought about. some examples include a "$249 wagyu beef panda roll from panda express" or "569 wetzel pretzel taste test" or the most recent video, "josh makes a six foot taco." josh can take a ton of ingredients, some i've never heard of and don't know what i would do with, and makes something that is absolutely spectacular looking and, of course, quite expensive - but the idea is that it's much, much more tasty and less like the school cafeteria taste you might get from your garden variety burger king or kfc or what have you. this is all to say top gun: maverick is a josh mythical kitchen special where you can tell this has been made with intense, high-quality care.... does it transcend being fast food? your mileage and/or colon may vary.

first off, let's get the good things (sometimes even better than good) into this review meal (ill stop with the food analogy i swear, maybe): tom cruise is still a charismatic five foot seven icon for this kind of movie, where he brings much more swagger but also a lot more natural vulnerability, pathos and (maybe reading closer into it) a bit of world weariness underneath all of those decades of movie star "i'll go further than you... and then another step more" chutzpah. so, if you want to see the movie for him more than any other reason, as i did, you'll get your money's worth.

i also think he has much stronger chemistry with jennifer connelly- or maybe it's a better written character she gets to play, or a combo of the two- so their scenes on the whole are pleasing. and my goodness is the one scene he has with val kilmer one that can... well, the berlin song isn't here this time (shock of shocks, the tiniest bit of restraint not with that song). it's certainly because the actor had his own cancer bout and so that had to be worked in to ice, but their scene is loaded with so much dramatic energy, like you can tell how far the actors have come as stars but also as just people that it informs their scene and tops anything by a metric ton anything in the first movie for honest emotional weight.

as for the new actors, they're mostly... swell. i don't know if i have a stronger word for it (ok, i like bob and that he's just bob and nothing more, good on you for not succumbing to a lazy nickname), buy they all fit their types - with h*ngm*n (hey, he scratched out the letters first) this movie's cocky iceman and rooster, miles teller's son of the late goose (is that a saying i dunno), is not.. quite maverick or goose, which is good, though he is saddled with the thing that we have seen in many other movies of this ilk of the son trying to live up to a father's legacy, or in this case what the best friend and confidant meant in that scenario. this isn't anywhere near the depth between cruise and teller that we saw in, say, creed, but there's also not as strong or solid of a legacy to have from there anyway. let's be honest, the death of goose wasn't some giant mythological nexus point, it was one of those beats in a predictable action movie.

ok, i still got a little more positive, or a lot depending on your point of view, in comparison at least to 86 top gun; both the central plot is executed and carried out with a clearer precision (though ill get back to something that bugs me about a detail with it in a moment), as the stakes are set up from early on and the pilots are working on just that one mission, as opposed to the prior movie with it being almost more like a hang-out flick (with all those towels.. ); and the action and flying set pieces themselves are far, far more engaging and exciting, in no small part because of how film and camera tech now make it so we have a quasi verisimilitude with these actors in the planes and whether they're doing piloting or not (i suspect cruise did because he's so bonkers, but did bob? shrug).

and the climax of the picture is bombastic and with at least a couple of turns that i should've seen coming, if nothing else from my umpteenth viewing of star wars (does that make it a mild spoilers? hell, this movie is like a new hope again... is it a better new hope than force awakens? i'll have to sleep on that).

but talking about stakes brings some issues to the table; even a gigantic hundred or several more million dollar popcorn vehicle for cruise and company should have some politics besides 'america, good - them, bad,' but this doesn't have that. maybe the first movie didn't either, but that at least had the cover of the usual typical bs reagan d-swinging cold war poltiic where the us navy pilots could clearly be seen as engaging those kinds of targets even if not spoken. but here, we are told that "the enemy" is about to do a thing that will make them capable of enriching uranium. hmm where have we heard that before in recent news? but there's no mention of any foreign adversary, like iran or north korea or even like borneo or some crap. it's just... *them* and it makes it purposely vague.

maybe that will be good for audiences who don't want tricky or thorny politics into the mix, albeit its hard for me not to ponder about the times in recent years america has come so close to getting some (ie iran) to draw back on uranium/nuclear weapons only to be thwarted by agent orange and so on. i do get it to an extent, like it's hard to sell and get so many millions all over the world to watch your movie if you're pointing someone as a villain. but the vagary points to something that bugs me about the movie, which is despite all of its entertaining masculine piss and vinegar and how much one can get caught up in a sleekly shot, near perfectly edited action sequence, it's all kind of safe and impersonal deep down.

is there more to it than "these pilots good, and as for you in the snowy mountains with your enemy pilots... shrug"? or what about the personality that could be put in by a director with a little more visual panache than what's required? it's a strange note to end here, but the one thing watching the two gunss in as many evenings is that tony scott really did bring a strong, smoky, painterly-but-super-commercially attention to lighting and compositions and, as dopey and silly as it all is, a kind of rampant hormone-driven miasma to 86 top gun (is it gay? sure, and that makes it *fascinating* in a bizarre way). i can't tell you a shot that tells me kosinski stands out from several others, which is a shame as he is definitely talented, and this is better than a number of other films he's made, but...

i'll close here (frankly my kitchen metaphors made me hungry). top gun maverick, for all of its bravura and, at points, heavily winking nostalgia (like the annoying thing we get now where scenes and moments replay here, with little *twists) is a $406 whopper with extra high-grade royalty cheese, or like a $300 bag of doritos. i love a good bag of doritos and i can dig a whopper. will i feel it later? well.... my wing name is colon, after all.

(ps: i kind of get, even though it sucks, writing off the female leads of the last movie, as kelly mcgillis was uh too tall i guess next to cruise and meg ryan whatever happened to her... no tom skerritt? he could've popped in here, no)

i didn't find the original one from 1986 too appealing, sure it was groundbreaking when it comes to the camera work in coordination with the pilots, but that was the only thing going for the movie, the story wasn't that rich and was filled with an over the top nationalism.

maverick is without a doubt a superior movie, which is not easy to do on a sequel - the obvious praise is of course the practical effects, the actors went through a great deal of training to prepare to withstand being on a jet plane during insane maneuvers while still acting for the camera. the results are worth it, no matter how good the cgi is your brain makes that connection immediately so when you see something real it's always refreshing, specially in action movies.

for me that's the highlight of the movie, fantastic action sequences, breathtaking scenes (literally) during the plane fights, it's one of a kind and one of the best practical approaches i've seen for an action film.

the story is not bad, they manage to design a good plot however, it has two major problems for me, it relies heavily on the story of the previous film (not necessarily a bad thing but also not original) and in all honesty it's not that great of a story, it's engaging enough to not make the movie all about flying jets but a bit dry.

it's hard to make a connection with the characters because there's not much back story and for me personally i wouldn't be emotionally invested mostly because, although they don't emphasize on the theme of war at the end of the day this is what these pilots are trained for, so all that risking their lives and having to do their mission, i don't agree or see the appealing in real life war, i understand the comradery between the individuals that fight but war makes no sense to me specially since most of the times soldiers are fighting for the interests of powerful people and for them to become even more rich, rather than actual interests for their country and its people.

with that aside it's a great cinematic experience and highly recommended to watch in the cinemas!

it was a brilliant move to push back the release of top gun: maverick, as it would have been insulting to the many people who worked so diligently to make this a truly unforgettable theater experience to see this on your home television during a pandemic. tom cruise somehow finds a way to go bigger and bolder with every new project he decides to embark on. i've never witnessed aerial stunts as visceral as those attempted in this movie, and the fact that they were successfully completed is nothing short of a marvel of filmmaking. cruise also displays an emotional range that he doesn't often get the opportunity to showcase, and miles teller is solid, if unspectacular. but there was no purpose for jennifer connelly's character to exist in the film. her storyline and presence were nothing but disruptive to the movie's plot and pace. yet the craft of the film is undeniable. the cinematography was gorgeous, and it could be a serious contender for that category when award season rolls around. in the end, if the oscar voters are on the same page as the general audience, it could win far more than that.

i feel like the praise for this film is a bit overblown in how people are saying it surpasses the original top gun, which i find it surprising because to me they are meant to be different kinds of films. the first film is unashamedly pure testosterone and is very much a product of it's time which i mean as a compliment. it was simply just fun. this new one by contrast is quite sentimental with how maverick still mourns the loss of goose, questions his value in today's society and rekindles a relationship that he knows he took for granted in his younger days. it goes for more serious moments and these are mostly well done, just some of the dialogue is a bit clunky and some of the new characters aren't that developed.

of course where the movie truly shines is in the action and in this area it surpasses the original immensely. they really ramped up the speed and aerial maneuvers performed and it was exhilarating to see on the big screen. there is an action scene at the end which is incredibly over the top and cheesy, but the action is so fun that you can't help getting on board and having a good time with it.

i would only rate this lower than the original as i have no detractions from that one. but as most modern movie sequels simply try to cash in on originals and rehash the same ideas, top gun maverick is refreshing in that it honors the original source material and does enough new things to make it a great film on its own merit.

this movie is excellent mostly because of the visuals, real life depiction of dog fights and realistic action.... but the director us not a filmmaker, he is an architect by trade, he is never being to film school and therefore his movies feel empty and without human touch, lets not forget his tron that was boring and without soul, then he did "oblivion" a movie that feels cold and without a heart... in other words... top gun: maverick is so good thanks to tom cruise...not his robotic director.

this film is not perfect, but i don't fault the reviewers coming out of the theater with a full rush of excitement, nostalgia, and adrenaline for temporarily feeling like it is. for a certain audience, this is the type of film they've been missing. the kind we've not been able to experience in a while, and the kind that brings up great memories and allows us to bridge generations.

it's definitely true that mileage may vary, depending on how stuck you are on accuracy in depictions of military life, aviation, etc. and i personally agree that the writing out of both kelly mcgillis and meg ryan's characters in such a way that neither actress even got a cameo, despite being as important to the overall enjoyment of the original film (and ryan's character being indirectly central to this one) feels "wrong," when you consider how much time and expense was taken to make sure val kilmer (who is unable to speak -- his voice was created digitally using ai in the film -- and has other physical challenges -- corrected with a variety of practical and cgi tweaks -- after a nasty cancer battle) would be included. is it the worst thing that the "surviving" female character is, while largely age appropriate, the one who is most conventionally attractive and young looking of the actresses and was barely a blip in the original film? no, not the worst thing, but it's a legitimate gripe and i don't begrudge others for whom it diminishes their own enjoyment/nostalgia of the film (famously, top gun did shockingly well with women, who were into the romance and ryan's grief in test audiences, leading them to play up both and shoot additional scenes and sequences, so it's legitimate that many women's nostalgic connection to the source may tie to those characters and scenes as much as it does to cruise and kilmer.)

but note i still gave it an 8, because at the end of the day, this is an extremely entertaining film.

it makes a refreshing change for a film to reach pole position and not be related to dc or marvel ideas it's a good film not without its cheesiness which helps it along in a strange way.mr cruise dies what he does best with a big dollop is nostalgia,fair play that he wanted to keep the film in the cinema and not gone the route of quite a few features,citing covid as the excuse.well done.

top gun: maverick is how to do a sequel. i wasn't expecting much from a top gun sequel but this blew me away. it has some of the most intense action sequences i have seen in the cinema and really is some of the best action scenes period. the choice to use as much practical work rather than cgi is there to be seen and makes it so much better. callbacks, ranging from the music to certain characters are worked really well here and shows hollywood how to make a proper sequel.

actually, it is. i think for the fighter-pilot enthusiasts among us it is truly a must see and a worthy sequel to the original top gun. it includes the old heroes and some of their family members, but in a realistic historic way. maverick is still maverick and he will do "whatever it takes" and a true hero we can all root for. val kilmer is there in spite of his medical condition and the movie is done around it and a respectable way.

the aviation hobbyists between us will appreciate the sky-high fighting actions, which are phenomenal and shows many kinds of planes and flying styles, all in-between constant action and solid progression of story-line. the movie-lovers will appreciate the solid character building, the dialogues and the quick pace up to its final conclusion.

on topic of diversity and inclusion, there is a defensible representation here, but not in a 'woke' way, which is way too common in recent hollywood productions. i feel many directors can learn from this movie how to appreciate women, and women of service in particular, without having to make the white male an immediate enemy.

overall very recommended, possibly this summer's greatest movie! i can see how a fan of the franchise will score this a '10' but for us, mere mortals, i feel it is a very solid 4 stars. exact score: 82 / 100.

it certainly helps that top gun: maverick actually has a plot with a beginning, middle, and ending that we can follow, unlike its meandering predecessor.

the story sets up a mission with clear-cut stakes and impossible odds very early on, and the threat and pressure felt by these pilots was felt by me for almost the entirety of the film.

after a clunky first act with very cheesy, expository dialogue, the story really gets going with interesting characters, extremely well shot and edited action sequences that put you in the center of the action, well-intentioned humor, and a romantic subplot that is a lot more believable and relevant than the one in the first movie.

plot-wise, there are certainly several elements that don't make sense and can't stand up to logical scrutiny. jerks like me on the internet will likely have a field day picking apart all the implausible material in this film.

but the filmmakers present this story in a way that oozes sincerity and care for all the characters both old and new, and with a passion for entertaining the audience with pulse-pounding action set-pieces.

this is an immensely satisfying film. not just as a sequel, but as a film in its own right.

color me surprised. it was worth the wait.

when top gun was released in 1986, it made quite the impression upon audiences. people flocked to cinemas time and again to watch groundbreaking flying scenes interspersing a particularly juvenile version of the hero's journey. the hero in question was maverick, played by tom cruise, and the original top gun was very much his film. it is therefore fitting that the sequel be in the same vein. top gun maverick provides us with a lot more flying and a lot more maverick. 36 years later, one can see how updated technology, of both the plane and camera variety, would make fresh flying scenes appealing, but surely, three-and-a-half decades later, tom cruise as maverick can not be the same heroic figure that he once was. well, no-one told tom cruise that and nor should they have. as a film star, he still has the presence and the bravura to remain front-and-centre of this hyper-charged vehicle.

of course he is much older now, although, in fairness, he really doesn't look it. in fact, tom cruise has defied the aging process much more successfully than the original top gun film. technologically, top gun maverick soars miles above its predecessor. gone are the miniature model plane shots and scenes filmed in aircraft simulators. this film sees its characters genuinely taken into the skies, and it's a marvel to witness such adrenaline and action captured on the screen. the poor pacing, uneven tone and unbridled machismo of the original film is also improved upon in the sequel. the pacing is helped by having a much more developed plot, which provides a narrative context for the copious flying scenes. each of the scenes is needed to move the plot forward and shows how the crack team are progressing towards their final mission. taking the lead from the 2nd half of the original film, the sequel is suffused with a sense of loss and a need for redemption. rooster (played by miles teller) is the son of maverick's late best friend, goose, and his character provides this redemptive arc. rooster is both a surrogate son and a potential best-friend-in-the-making to maverick. it's their complicated relationship and their shared connection to the late "goose" that forms the emotional core of the film.

as to the previous machismo, this time the film has a much more nuanced emotional palette. maverick is much older in years and he has become wistful and reflective over time. the best scenes in the film, for my money, are at the beginning, when maverick is surveying the generation of fighter pilots who have ostensibly replaced him. for a few brief moments, he's a good-looking older guy at the bar watching the young bucks cavorting and performing in the exact same way he once did. maverick is a man who has seen all of his former colleagues either pass away or age out. he alone is clinging to the rigors and audacity of a youth that belies his actual years. but, of course, this is the world of top gun, and in this world maverick is always the hero. the higher the stakes, the more heroic maverick will become. just as speed and space are no object, neither is time. it doesn't matter that maverick is now twice the age of all the other hotshot top gun pilots, he'll outpace and outperform them because that is what top gun requires, the hero must prevail at all costs.

there are many flights of fancy and there is a general sense of unbelievability regarding significant portions of the plot but there is always just enough risk so that the film never quite lets go of its emotional pull. thus, it does enough to immerse you in the fantasy and provide the emotional catharsis that comes from a sense of triumph earned amidst the genuine possibility of tragedy. in this sense, the film has an old-fashioned feel to it. it takes its audience back to a time before the rules of big budget actions films changed. it holds to sacred formulas of heroic triumph and ultimate redemption that are no longer fashionable in this genre. it taps into a pureness and simplicity that audiences still clearly yearn for but which is now extremely difficult to deliver in a manner that is convincing and satisfying.

more generally, both tom cruise and top gun maverick represent a generation of hollywood which is out-of-step with current trends. the film emphasises practical effects in an industry increasingly dominated by computer technology. it champions a white male hero in the face of 3rd-wave feminism, intersectionality and critical race and gender theory. it depicts ultimate triumph in a world which no longer believes in absolutes. and, yet, it finds a way to succeed.

this film demonstrates that old formulas can still work. if it's daring, it is so because it is so wedded to an artistic temperament that long preceded its release. to paraphrase the film, movies of this kind may one day be obsolete, but not today.

capt. pete 'maverick' mitchell (tom cruise) is assigned by his friend adm. tom 'iceman' kazansky (val kilmer) to return to top gun to train a group of elite pilots in a practically impossible mission to explode a nuclear plant. he meets his former affair penny benjamin (jennifer connelly), who owns a bar, and the son of his best friend goose, lt. bradley 'rooster' bradshaw (miles teller). maverick explains to the pilots that they will be pushed to their limits to survive the suicidal mission and only the best of them will be assigned. meanwhile he rekindles his relationship with jenny.

"top gun: maverick" is an entertaining blockbuster full of action and also romance. the plot recalls the attack of the rebels to the death star in the "star wars" franchise, where tom cruise would be luke skywalker. the audio is great and the scenes are breathtaking. jennifer connelly is still a very pretty woman and the sixty-year-old tom cruise convinces as a skilled trainer. my vote is eight.

it's saturday night and its tom cruise times. a smartest looking hero who would hit 60 this year just before us independence is out here flying all over the skyreen cruising on top in his most stylish and energetic look . the expectations on top gun was way too high considering it to be a sequel for the one that got released 36 years ago. the plot is quite understandable and easily guessable. unlike many other sequels this sequel doesn't mandate any one to see the first part. for me the movie looked so much straight fwd and ended too soon . top gun is definitely a grandeur and a must see in imax for all the visuals with some great re-recording. the vfx and screenplay was top notch and was quite exhilarating. the style and the class of tommy's acting just didn't drop a bit . it takes very little effort for tom cruise to handle jet flights since he's been flying in real for quite a while now with real pilot licence . val kilmer , jeniffer connelly and many others extend their best performance to make this movie quite enjoyable .

tom cruise (pete 'maverick' mitchell) appears in just about every scene, but he delivers the goods.

after disgracing himself by destroying a test plane, he is reassigned to train elite fighter jet pilots for a near impossible mission. the enemy is never named but think secret nuclear facility and you can probably complete the picture.

the young pilots are cocky and dismissive of their ancient teacher, but maverick quickly earns their respect with a mix of testosterone and flying skill. one of them is the son of maverick's old wingman, who died in the first movie. the strained relationship between the two and the build up to the final few scenes is a major subplot of the movie.

the two hour 14 minute time flew by (literally) with edge of the seat excitement and stunning visuals. make sure you watch it on a big screen.

a strong sequel 36 years after the original. bigger, bolder, faster!

the film opens up in the same manner as the originally with an 80s soundtrack blasting through. the opening scroll explains what 'top gun' is at which point you'll be forgiven for thinking they've put on the original film.

from there on out it's a perfect mix of old and new. whilst the story introduces a bunch of new characters and uses a familiar story beat from the original, it separates itself from the from the likes of the force awaken and jurassic world as it doesn't rely on the previous story beats to drive the central narrative nor does it try to beat down previous characters just to push the new ones forward.

the story continues the journey of pete 'maverick' mitchell, 36 years later, giving you some insight on how's he's dealt with the repercussion of the original 'top gun' and things that have and haven't happened since!

after receiving a call from an old friend, he's forced to confront all of this again. this, alongside the introduction of a particular character, played excellently by miles teller, adds emotional weight to top gun - maverick and is nicely balanced amongst the action.

speaking of action, top gun maverick has a lot of it and it's good. there is only so much you can do with with these planes but the nature of the training/mission really helped to notch up the intensity during the flying scenes. this is another check in the w column for cruise as he continues to prove himself as one of the last real actions stars in hollywood.

it's not all perfect, the romantic elements didn't have much time to develop and the focus on maverick meant that we didn't get an in depth look at many of the new characters but it was a worthwhile sacrifice.

if you born in my generation (1974) , i'll have a hard time believing you liked this better than the original. it's still a very strong movie. it lacks character development, and some of the big names are just throw aways. it dives right into the mission and there isn't much else to the plot other than that. it's the tom cruise, miles teller show. if they stuck to the formula of the original i could have cared more about the supporting cast, but they are nobodies. but i can see every generation outside of my own thinking it's better than the original. 30 years later.

30 years after the events of the first film pete "maverick" mitchell (tom cruise) has purposefully avoided advancement in the navy and continues to operate as a test pilot even in the face of pressure from the pentagon to shift focus to unmanned drones. following an incident where maverick takes a prototype jet passed the limit, maverick seems poised for a discharge however thanks to the intervention of maverick's former wingman tom "iceman" kazansky (val kilmer), maverick is instead transferred back to topgun to train a batch of 12 pilots for a mission to destroy a uranium enrichment facility in a hostile nation-state before it can be activated in three weeks' time. of 12 fighter pilots, bradley "rooster" bradshaw (miles teller) has a history with maverick as rooster still carries animosity towards maverick over the loss of his father and maverick's wingman goose and the fact maverick pulled rooster's academy papers and derailing his career. during this time maverick also rekindles his romance with an old flame in penny (jennifer connelly)

undeniably top gun is one of the biggest cultural benchmarks of the 80s as the film was not only the highest grossing film of 1986, but it's also responsible for launching the careers of tom cruise as an a-list leading man and director tony scott as a uniquely identifiable hand behind blockbuster filmmaking with his high-speed editing and magic hour photography influencing an entire generation of filmmakers. despite being tom cruise's first major blockbuster, cruise had initially expressed no interest in doing a follow-up as he said as much during a press tour for born on the fourth of july in 1990. during 2010 however negotiations began with producer jerry bruckheimer, director tony scott, tom cruise and paramount about a follow-up to top gun addressing the end of the dogfighting era and rise in drone warfare, but the development was curtailed with the unfortunate suicide of tony scott in 2012 leaving the projects fate in doubt. eventually the project regained traction in 2017 with oblivion director joseph kosinski reteaming with cruise as director and the film began production in 2018 but was delayed from its original 2019 release due to the complexity of the aerial sequences and became the poster child for covid delays as top gun: maverick much like the james bond film no time to die went through a cycle of release dates and reschedules as offers from streaming were rejected by cruise who insisted it be released in theaters. once released the film became the biggest of cruise's career making nearly $1.5 billion against its $170 million budget and has earned rave reviews from both critics and audiences to boot. top gun: maverick is not only a worthy sequel to top gun, but in many ways it exceeds its predecessor while also revisiting everything that worked about it the first time.

as with the previous film, top gun: maverick is a showcase for some incredible aerial photography. what really helps sell the illusion is that the actors actually were in the jets for interior shots during filming giving authentic reactions to traveling at those speeds while for exterior shots actual us navy pilots flew and to see some of the elaborate aerial sequences and know they're done without cgi is truly a sight to behold and really shows the enduring appeal of tom cruise as an action star because he dives (quite literally) into the action. top gun set the standard for how to approach aerial photography and despite attempts by imitators such as fire birds, iron eagle, or (heaven help you) stealth, no one has surpassed that standard until now as maverick features some of the most intricate and engaging aerial dogfights and sequences ever captured on film with the editing and filming making you feel as though you're in the seat of the action.

of course, if top gun: maverick just delivered on the spectacle it would just be an above average actioner, but the movie does give some solid story and characterization that was lacking from the first film and allows cruise to deliver one of the best performances of his career. with cruise's approach to maverick, it's very much a reflective piece as like maverick cruise is getting up in years and he's still the best at pulling these dare devil stunts (such as in his mission: impossible series) but eventually he will have to let go despite his best efforts to do otherwise. it's undeniably the character interactions that have made this movie as resonant as it has been as like many modern "legacy sequels", we do have a fresh faced batch of recruits playing against the veterans of this ip, but they're much better written than you typically see in this type of film and especially in miles teller as rooster who's the emotional core of this movie. with maverick and rooster there's something of an estranged father/son dynamic as maverick still carries the weight of goose's death very close and has tried to respect goose and his dead wife by protecting rooster even if that means rooster hating him, it's emotional scars like this that really held me with the movie, but easily the biggest was with val kilmer reprising his role as iceman who has been dealing with throat cancer (like the real life kilmer) and despite iceman's presence in this film being mostly via text, it's the buildup to the major scene where kilmer and cruise come together one final time in a scene that was heavy with emotional resonance especially if you know the off camera animosity between kilmer and cruise that came during top gun and there's something cathartic and emotionally cleansing about this scene that's already good in its own right but adds even more when taken into context for the real life undertones.

despite the strengths of top gun: maverick i do have some criticisms. i personally didn't feel the romance with jennifer connelly's penny was all that developed and it felt a little unnecessary given all the other elements on display. the fact that penny is an "old flame" of maverick's also struck me as a little odd as it seemed like maybe there was an initial draft where this character was kelly mcgillis' character charlie but now it's a wholly original character, but it doesn't feel like we have the attachment to this character that we should. connelly is perfectly fine in the role, but this is more a hiccup of the writing. i also felt it was rather humorous just how far out its way the movie went to keep its antagonist faceless because the enemy nation state is never given a name (not even one of those fake names with the "istan" suffix) and even in the climax where we get a look at the ground there's absolutely no identifiable markings, language, or even geography to identify where we are relative to the rest of the world so our antagonist is basically a faceless swarm of missiles and jets. i will say at least the movie is built up to this climax as opposed to the original where the climax was tacked on, but the lack of a tangible antagonist does seem rather odd but given the importance of the international market i understand why they did this, and there have been instances like this all the way back to the 1950s such as with captain nemo's "hated nation" from the disney adaptation of 20,000 leagues under the sea.

top gun: maverick delivers on the thrills of the original film and exceeds in the story and characters and making for a more enjoyable sit. while i did have issues with the film such as the lack of an antagonist character and the penny character feeling slightly extraneous, the film works well where you expect it to and delivers the action and entertainment that has become synonymous with cruise. i don't think i agree with this being cruise's "best" movie as i personally think live die repeat and mission: impossible 1,4,5 & 6 are more entertaining on the whole, but this is still really solid blockbuster filmmaking.

i remember liking the original "top gun" (1986). it wasn't high art, but it was good cheesy pizza. going back to watch that film again recently, sadly it has aged about as well a cheese pizza that has sat out for over 30 years. the film has lost that loving feeling, i hate it when that happens.

top gun: maverick brought back that loving feeling. it is undoubtably better than the original. the film is well paced, focused and full of good character decisions.

the film does not reinvent the wheel by any means, it follows a tried and true formula, but it does all these classic hits very well. the new characters also aren't as interesting as tom cruise. they aren't awful, just underdeveloped.

but the show stealer of the whole thing is the aerial action. the dog fights and flying sequences are second to none. they use real planes and real g's, and it feels real. it is filmed with clarity; it communicates to the audience exactly what is going on and why characters are doing it.

filmed with skill, what a thrill. goodness gracious great balls of fire!

you can literally see the dedication that tom has for film-making during the filming sequences- being able to see the physical pain that he is putting himself through for the role. miles teller also delivers a performance on par with the intensity he shows in 'whiplash'.

the action scenes are thrilling and the soundtrack matches perfectly, with some great 80's throwback songs.

however, the love interest side-plot didn't feel entirely necessary and i would have liked to have seen more female characters in the film, it feels a bit too much of a boys club at times.

definitely worth a watch on the big screen!

as per the storyline, tom cruise here is not 'the man' on the mission, but a test pilot (read super pilot) who trains a batch of recent graduates for a special and dangerous assignment.

given the fact that the protagonist here is an aging star (almost sixty) and reduced to playing a trainer and not the 'man of the mission', many of us (including me) got the impression that the movie would be sans the tom cruise magic (read death defying stunts) and more of an encashment of his brand as the last hurrah.

but please get rid of all such notions, as it's an out and out tom cruise movie, made very intelligently with proper business acumen and amazing special effects. also, not once does the star appears old or jaded.

herein, he is a maestro of supersonic fighter jets who can test them to record breaking speed and manoeuvre them like a toy with impeccable strategy to meet the concerned mission's need.

alongside, he also teaches his unconventional albeit highly effective flying methods to a new batch of military graduates bursting with youth, super confidence and passion to do something out of the ordinary.

and he battles the ghosts of his past and rekindles an old flame.

as an exceptional dancer makes the toughest of steps appear like a child's play, the combo of good direction, acting, cinematography and special effects in the movie, ably simplifies the world of supersonic jets, their architecture & manipulation and their limitation on different terrains and altitudes !!

everything is easily understandable and this is no mean feat.

you will find the movie thrilling & entertaining and around midway, you will start predicting it's end, but it will surprise you with an interesting climax.

in spite of woven around a top class military assignment, the movie is not gruesome to watch, as the bullet and bomb firing scenes are more on the lines of a hi-tech video game.

also, it's a family entertainer with no nudity or intimate scene.

top gun maverick is a 'tom cruise special' giddy cocktail of - adrenalin rush, emotions and nostalgia, which needs to be watched in a theatre for full entertainment of the senses.

please don't wait for it's ott release.

last but not the least, though the movie is a sequel of top gun (1986), a huge commercial hit by tom cruise and team, it can be watched as an independent film.

tom cruise knows how to construct a movie by now and this proves how good he is at it. i was expecting less and instead got more, a very pleasant experience. it covered all the bases a movie should include and what is outstanding is it is a decent script acted out reasonably well. it is not a movie i would see twice but rewarding the first time around as there are no memorable scenes. also, it is one of those flicks where the ending ends it for good! worth the price of admission and the time to view. good job to all involved. to tom cruise: keep up the good work. forget hollywood! give me entertainment! i will continue to pay you for your efforts.

i gotta first tell you that i'm not from the generation that experienced top gun when it first came out in the 90s, i'm a millennial. i saw top gun for the first time five years ago and i thought it was magnificent, a very period piece type of movie that works amazingly in all of its elements- actors, music, setting... and it is so iconic even i can understand it even if i didn't live during that time when it first came out. fast forward five years and the new top gun is here! the reviews have been amazing, many saying that this is the rare case when a sequel surpasses the first movie and that everything is perfect. i totally agree with these aspects but there was something that lost me a bit in the movie.

i understand that this is all 100% maverick's movie but a lot of the characters needed further exploration and development- i know they tried to make the secondary characters i.e. the team that maverick teaches as distinct as possible but the plot doesn't really have time for any of them which is a shame as i would've loved to see all of these new pilots get a team working relationship and try to overcome the task at hand which we don't really get, we get glimpses of this- after all this supposed heist is done in three weeks but due to the plot it gets shortened to two weeks which is a shame- i know they did this to heighten the stakes but a lot of the character development gets sacrificed... instead we get a lot of conflict that never really gets dissolved until after the heist which feels so forced. i was really bugged that we didn't get more scenes with rooster, hangman, phoenix etc. it's not that maverick's story isn't compelling per se, it is the emotional core of the story after all but goddamn could this movie have been better with further exploration on the other top gun crew, just like in the 80s movie. at least we got a hunky beach scene lol!

the music is fantastic, very great use of the older tracks from the movie and the older score vs. the new one which is good! the lady gaga song is really awesome as well!

all in all it is a good movie, not my favourite but it is good- i understand the praise but it needs a bit more work for me before it can be called amazing- nevertheless i had a fun time at the cinema! which is all that counts really!

i anxiously anticipated the release of top gun maverick, which for anyone who did, made for an even-higher bar of expectations because of the films' multiple covid delays. i don't know how much of that(if any) was calculated, but in hindsight, i suspect it only helped the film at the box office.

only a week removed from another nostalgic sequel, jurassic world dominion(5/10), i had become even hungrier-for(and more wary-of)something like this.

no worries here.

maverick is an action film-lovers' delight. the flight sequences are beyond amazing, and the film doesn't skimp at all in this regard. the film has other strengths as well.

it's kinda nice to not use or need as much cgi in a blockbuster action flick. the pacing and spacing of the action sequences is also well-balanced. the film never drags, and at the same time, it isn't sensory overload(think transformers). it also borrows some things from some other action/aviation films; firefox and iron eagle come to mind.

of course the film is very nostalgic, with many nods,references, characters, and plot continuations from the first film, but unlike force awakens, world dominion, and others; maverick takes very good care of most of these nostalgic moments. one nostalgic scene with kilmer is deftly handled, and a love scene(or a lack of one) with newcomer jennifer connely(newcomer to tg anyway) is tactful. the last 30 minutes of the film is nonstop exhilaration, and the film is worthy of repeat viewings. that's not to say that some scenes aren't a little too "safe", because they are, nor to say the film doesn't have it's fair share of unrealistic moments, it does. either way, the audience will be having way too much fun in the cockpit to care. some of the emotional chords do ring true. solid performances all-around never hurts.

miles tellers "rooster" is a perfect continuation of the maverick/goose storyline, but perhaps my biggest gripe with top gun maverick is that teller and his undeniable talent are perhaps under-used, and the film is one or two emotional scenes involving rooster away from a 9/10 for me. it's very close to 9, and i may revisit after another viewing.

overall, i can recommend maverick without hesitation - it exceeded already high(and even-further elevated) expectations. it shares some of the same strengths and weaknesses of the first film, but it's in that very rarified air where the sequel surpasses an already good original.

83/100.

i went into top gun maverick with a lot of nervousness because we know sequels rarely outshine the original, but to my amazement, tom cruise and his gang have actually managed to do complete justice to the top gun brand. sequels often go wrong in three areas which i think top gun maverick got right

1. nostalgia- right from the very first scene, you are transported back to 1986 when the first movie came out..and it's done so well!!.. not the cheesy flashbacks or remixed soundtracks..but instead, elements of the first movie brought in at the right time and place ..nothing too over the top. if there was anything that was a tad pretentious, it's probably the scene with val kilmer.. but then again top gun wouldn't be top gun if there was no val kilmer right?

2. the premise- in the first movie, aside from the adrenaline boost, when it came to storytelling, it felt a little flat in my opinion...but not 'maverick'.. in addition to thrilling adrenaline pumping sequences, the storytelling kept me engaged throughout with some timeless dialogues and funny scenes

3. the ending- so how did they end it? did maverick die? well, i won't spoil it but suffice to say, it was a satisfying end and to be honest a bit unexpected. this is where the movie shines for me and really went supersonic over the first one (excuse the pun) all in all, top gun maverick immersed me into a time when watching movies on the big screen was for that special experience while at the same time not diverging from story of this amazing character- maverick.

it would be easy to complain about a lot of this movie, everything about it is almost a straight lift from the original. half the soundtrack, half the cast, his bike and jacket, hell they even have scenes from the original in there and a pseudo beach "volleyball" scene of it's own.

but there are only so many ways to take a film like top gun and make a sequel work, either you create an entirely new vision and story and risk alienating the original fans or you go the other way and make a top gun movie.

the reason this works well as a sequel is because it very knowingly gives the same thrills and humour from the original. as far as the flying and actions scenes go, they are considerably better than the original due to the advances in technology and film making. tom cruise is still fantastic in the role as maverick, glen powell as hangman was an excellent choice to be the cocky rival, at times playing an inbetween version of maverick and iceman. he certainly wouldn't have been out of place among the original members.

my only real gripe with this sequel is that it is a little too heavy with the callback and memory of goose in the front end. while i'm sure younger audiences might not have known the character, they overplayed it a bit especially when iceman is in the movie and has his own story within it which is a little glossed over by comparison.

but in the end, the climax of the film and performance from miles teller as rooster does win you over.

it was a little strange to me why they decided to make a sequel to a film from the 1980s, why even bother when over three decades have passed. i still have to admit that i'm not a big fan of the original top gun. however, here tom cruise showed why he is the king.

we got a real quality summer blockbuster, in the best sense.

a lot of effort was put into every scene involving the flights of fighter planes, and there are plenty of such scenes in the film. they look really impressive. but that alone would not be enough for a quality film, we also have great characters, emotions and story. the sequel is based on the essential components of the original and a strong connection is built around it so that we can keep up with the characters even after thirty years. the characters have their own story, past and motivation, you can understand them, and that is very important for a well-written character. i wrote an interesting thing about the first part that also applies to this film, which is that there is no antagonist here, something that we don't often see in most films, but the film still makes sense. i believe it's down to the script that made it all possible.

a sufficient amount of emotion, even i felt it, is shown throughout the film, and it is based on the original, once again a great script. during the third act, it has great tension and action, which is exactly what a real action blockbuster should have.

kudos to you, tom cruise, you've done it again.

'top gun: maverick' was not on my radar at the start of 2022. i did not watch the original 'top gun', so i was not really invested in this universe. this all changed when it received critical acclaim. i watched it and i could not believe how great it was.

the action scenes in the first movie were awesome and with the camera tech we have now this movie moves that up another level.

the action sequences are absolutely amazing, this movie is a wild ride. i watched it in imax and 4dx and both are highly recommended. so great to see effects that were not all cgi.
just watch it. don't apply too much login and mind. it's an out-and-out entertaining movie. as expected cruise outshines everyone. visuals we're really good.

you certainly don't see movies like this anymore, and tom cruise wanted to ensure if a sequel was made, it was done exactly to these specifications.

the most impressive part of this film is just how much of it was shot live and not infront of a green screen. if you manage to watch the bonus features, you'll really appreciate the lengths not just tom cruise went to, to ensure these shots were truly real, but many of the other actors who participated as well. there are few actors who would go to such lengths for the sake of a movie's integrity and viewers experience, and this movie exemplifies his devotion to the craft.

all of that being said, i do feel like the hype around this movie is more indicative of hollywood and the woke culture lately. people have endured an intense malaise for over a decade, with a testosterone crushing level of man shaming and non-stop depressing stories that leave people walking away from the theatre with lower and lower expectations.

i did think the picture overall was great and embodied alot of the characteristics we used to know and love in older classic films. there was however alot of stereotypical scriptwriting and many scenes were very predictable. i found myself several times finishing the lines before they were spoken.

although i didn't think it was as worthy of the grandstanding others seem to be giving it, we still have to recognize that this is a sequel, and when it comes to sequels, i can count on one hand the number of times hollywood managed to make the second as good as the first. in some respects i would say this one was better, as you could tell tom had alot more freedom and control over making it exactly how he wanted.

if you can work out the entire plot of a movie within the first 5 minutes is that necessarily a problem? top gun maverick lays down a pretty good argument that it's not. the main reason for watching is obviously thje electrifying flight sequences which may be the greatest ever put to film due to choreography, editing and actors actually in the seats, which allow you to genuinely follow the flights instead of standing witness to meaningly jump-cuts. however maverick also has its tender moments especially the relationship between maverick and rooster (teller, son of goose) which grounds the film and fills in the emotional beats throughout which were only present in the 3rd act of the original. cruise rightfully is getting many plaudits for this continued dedication to the role of action star as he approaches 60s but teller really shines here and this may be the movie which pushes him into the true superstardom which anyone who has seen whiplash knows he has been destined for for almost a decade. this movie is a rollercoaster, you know it'll be safe and where you'll end up but it's exhillerating if you get onboard and allow yourself to be taken for a ride.

i didn't see the first movie, but today i saw the movie top gun 2022 and i enjoyed watching it. hans zimmer's music was legendary again, the filming and photography were at a high level, the direction and editing were correct, the set design and costume design were also very good, but i have one criticism and that is the characterization that could have been done better for me, except for tom cruise. and jennifer connelly and mills teller, the rest did not have good characterization. even jennifer connelly's character performance in the role of penny was not perfect, but overall, i saw a good action thriller and i recommend watching it. my score for the movie: 8.7 10.

this movie is soooo cheesy. i was on board an aircraft carrier 2 years after the original, and we used to make fun of that movie so much. i mean we liked it but the original was only fairly cheesy. this sequel is dripping with cheese.

normally, i can't stand movies like this. i can't stand when a movie is so cheeseball that predictions are easily made. but even though i knew "hangman" was going to save "maverick" and "rooster" at least 5 minutes before he did so, the scene still inspired a tear out of my eye.

i am at a loss for why i enjoyed it... but i did.

the original top gun was a fun film for what it was, with charismatic personalities and aviary action. i think it is safe to say that top gun: maverick brings things to a whole other level. there's a lot of heart in the story this time around. it is rewarding for fans by giving them what they would expect while also building upon the legacy of the last film. it delivers on the action and the third act of maverick made me feel tense at times. speaking of the action, it's amazing what you can still do with practical effects, as most of the aviation scenes were just that. without spoiling, there is one character that is brought back from the original film and i thought it was cool how they used them. for cons, there are some moments that can come across as cheesy and the love interest aspect i felt could've been stronger and more integral. you can tell a lot of heart was put into the production for this film and i think it will be worth the wait for those who have been long time fans of the original. if you want a legitimately fun movie experience, i can't think of anything better at the moment than top gun: maverick. verdict: 8/10.

the plot is simple, predictable, and.. not the best of work. i feel a little bit uncomfortable after too much patriotism. (i found out 'top gun: maverick' is supported by the us military.) it also directs and pressures the audience to feel a certain way, too much melodrama and tear-jerking moments. the problem is that it's working. i hate 'action action' movies which have no regard for the writing, the core of the film. 'top gun: maverick' is not that, but it's still true that the storyline is too hasty and has some holes. i also hate that the action part is so breath-taking that it covers up the weakness of the writing. my conclusion is that my eyes were joyful for the whole two hours.

i'm over 50 and i hadn't seen the original in all it's glory.

i had seen the berlin music video and bits and bats of scenes here and there but never the film.

that was because i was an insecure young man and really didn't get the macho bravura of the top gun men.

years later, the sequel arrived.

i decided to watch the original in preparation for taking my wife and daughter to see the sequel.

i watched it on my own and quite enjoyed it. surprisingly, the original hasn't dated. it's still a good film. kelly mcgillis looks gorgeous, sassy, fun. the cruiser (tm) hasn't changed a bit. that winning smile still doing it.

so, anyway, we went to the pictures and watched tg maverick that night. everything still fresh.

my wife and i really enjoyed it. my teenage daughter and her friend said they were bored. they didn't understand what was going on. i suspect it's their own fault because the film is far from boring. she did say she wasn't paying attention.

it is what popcorn cinema should be. full of action, wittiness, oozing sexiness....and above all thoroughly entertaining.

cruise still has that smile and it's still working.

miles teller is good in this too. quite a transformation from his roll in whiplash.

some very touching, tear inducing, scenes in there as well.

it's a lovely homage to the original.

one other mention, jennifer connelly effectively takes over the love interest from kelly mcgillis.

she's my age and god she looks fantastic. beautiful, full of charm and wit and has a great onscreen chemistry with the cruiser.

tbh, the cruiser looks amazing for his age.

anyway, this isn't going to win any major oscars. we know that but as post pandemic entertainment goes, it's great fun.

i felt that need, the need for speed for the last 36 years ... and it was definitely worth the waiting! thanks to the crew for this great picture... thanks to tom for creating the history.. and specially thanks to val.

every second of action in this movie is well earned and blood pumping. the references to the original movie are great and the tension between maverick and rooster is very real and tense. only problem i can see is the dynamic between maverick and penny seems forced and makes for a lot of cringey moments and overacting by jennifer connelly.

the movie is a great combination of action and feel-good. the action scenes were very thrilling. nice references to the prequel. cruise does a good acting job.

i cannot believe people who say this movie is the best ever.

there are too many clichés that make the movie less than perfect. also some unrealistic events. the cocky behavior in the bar. the driving on the motor without helmets on. the posing of the couple in front of a vintage car. literally flying apart a plane at mach 10 and then stepping in a bar as if you fell only 3 meters. being shot down and then meeting up with your wingman also being shot down in the forest after a short hike. conveniently near an airbase that you can walk into without special equipment (don't they have at least a fence around the airbase?).

an ancient plane in the airbase that is conveniently fueled and equipped with rounds and flares.

overall a solid movie, but nowhere near the best movie ever.

morethis film is adds a plethora of content and richness to the original which really completes the story and provides much needed closure for the characters. having only watched the original for the first time a few days before this one i could really notice just how much of an appreciative love letter this was to the first one. kosinski admires and respects the original film and that is clearly evident throughout the runtime. cruise reprises his role as maverick perfectly. he's not trying to play the exact same character in the first, he's playing an aged and lived maverick who has still been carrying his emotional baggage from his youth. this clearly has affected his relationship's and i believe makes him a more three dimensional character. he is no longer just a rebellious pilot who was overshadowed by his father's prowess as a legendary pilot, he's a damaged man trying to find meaning in his life and tie up loose ends within himself. i loved the stark contrast against cruise teller brought as rooster. i really felt their chemistry was organic and could tell just through their performances there was a deep underlying issue between them which connected them however ;also crippling them both emotionally. the best part for me about this film was the absolutely stunning and just overwhelmingly awesome cinematography. i found it much easier to navigate and understand the dogfight's in this film which is obviously due to the advancement in camera technology but at the same time it's the camera tricks used. the film is just beautiful to look at and is a great milestone for current cinematography limits. i would highly recommend watching this film, it would be much better to see the previous one to appreciate all the nods and references but i think it does a great job at providing enough detail and content that there isn't any point where as an audience member you feel distant if you haven't seen first film.

this movie is awesome! loved the realistic dogfights (it was quite obvious when it wasn't real at all or was faked)

score is freaking amazing. i mean they really tickle the nostalgia sensors here with the whole movie and everything, but the score puts this baby into the bedsheets. i just love how they (faltemeyer, zimmer, gaga) reprized the core top gun themes. its really ironic how refreshing this blunt dumb suspension of disbelief is conquering the superhero fatigue wave. oh boy, i was laughing very hard on many cringe worthy scenes: with disobedience from mav, "talk to me goose", the whole akira kurosawa "hidden fortress" star wars: the new hope vibes... i mean, sometimes i really thought this movie indeed takes itself seriously. oh boy and that very cringy conelly and cruise scene with "that look" omg :d

even though above all these, this is a must see for anyone who is up for a thrill and chill, especially with over dramatic lemonade.... cruise indeed the "xxxxxx men alive..." nobody else could carry on or get away with this much cheese to be honest.

tom cruise returns as the " maverick " in this sequel after over twenty years it marks a record of cinematic feet in propelling this piece as it has been most anticipated. the rivalry of the best as earlier seen in the prequel by iceman ( val kilmer ) pete " maverick " mitchell is been played by a new set of " kids " played by new characters they are nurtured under the tutelage of maverick.

long lost love is found again this could be split into two maverick's love for flying and finding his former love. the meeting between maverick and iceman is an emotional meeting, the pain is real as we notice val kilmer's inability to deliver his lines because of his speech impediment but he pulls through.

following the same direction cum cinematography as applied by the late director tony scott we are been reminded of his classic work. and when the sun comes sun we see " in memory of tony scott " once again our emotions are been touched. joseph kosinski direction may be fascinating but not original as earlier stated it is a derivative of tony scott. the stunt coordination excellently fantastic, this movie is a really great score for producer jerry bruckheimer.

most energy in this film is mostly in the jets as they glide in the sky, will they be caught by enemy power or not ? that's what causes tensions in our hearts but as all good stories the heroes must always prevail. so come and join this ride of wide entertainment.

i remember watching the original film in a kino theater in germany. i can't believe its been 38 years since that movie came out. maverick's return is welcomed and the movie is fantastic. it might almost outdo the original.

maverick is now a test pilot and his career has kind of stagnated because of his arrogance and over confidence. he is recalled to top gun school to train a group of recent graduates to perform a dangerous mission bombing a uranium enrichment plant in an unnamed country. the run to the plant is similar to the one in star wars (1977) in many ways. the graduates are all arrogant pilots like maverick, including rooster (miles teller), who is goose's son. jennifer connelly plays penny, a former lover of maverick's. jon hamm is the commander at top gun, admiral simpson. also returning is val kilmer as iceman who is now an admiral and has acted a maverick's guardian angel over the course of his career.

the flight sequences are amazing and the music score keeps the tension high. the secondary pilot characters in this version get about as much screen time and development as the ones in the original.

the weakest part of the gilm imo is the manufactured tension between maverick and rooster. don't get me wrong, i love jennifer connelly, but they could have deleted her scenes and focused on the relationship between maverick and rooster without detracting from the overall plot. rooster is mad and then he isn't. its that simple.

this was a fine sequel to the original. its a shame we had to wait almost 40 years to get it, but it more than meets expectations.

i have a confession to make. i'm not a massive fan of the original top gun. i think it is an ok movie but i don't think it is as amazing as it is as great as it is made out to be. nevertheless for some reason i get the urge to rewatch it from time to time.

now, 36 years later, there is a sequel. tom cruise is back as maverick with jerry bruckheimer as producer along with cruise and joseph kosinski taking over as director from the late tony scott. this time we see maverick returning to top gun this time as an instructor for a new group of recruits which includes the son of maverick's deceased friend.

the flight sequences in this movie are enjoyable, in fact more than they are in the first movie. i really liked the interactivity between maverick and goose's son rooster and the reasonings behind it. the friction between maverick and the top gun instructors also added to the movie. it was also nice to see val kilmer as iceman and the scene where they reunite was heartwarming.

the movie does however have its downsides. the storyline is a fairly simple one. and i didn't find it as thrilling or as impactful as it is made out to be.

overall it is a worthy sequel that is enjoyable and actually better than the first one although if i'm being honest, i don't think it is as great as it is made out to be.

hy everybody!

8/10 it is the real score.

tom cruise....this name guarantees qulity.

in the last scene, i was completely sweaty.:)) respect for val kilmer, he is respectable!

top gun: maverick was great! it was a great story about save lives, go out of your way to be the best of the best, don't be rude and arrogant, and really take care of your family and friends. the action and suspense with all the f-18s and the tomcat was cool. i liked how there was some funny moments. the scenery was beautiful. the instrumental music sounded very good. the only two corrections i'd make is the sexual immorality was unneeded and the foul language was unnecessary. still though this was a great movie and a great sequel to the classic film! have a great day and goooo top gun: maverick!

what else is there to say about this movie that a trailer wouldn't tell you? is it a soft reboot of the 80's cheese and us navy commercial that is the original top gun? yes. does it wallow around in its own nostalgia? a little. does this movie kick more ass then any other summer box office goliath this year? absolutely.

between covid stalling the release and a gimmick centered around real life cockpit shots of the beautiful insane man tom cruise and friends, as they pull--honest to god--real g's, thousands of feet in the air... it seemed like "top gun: maverick" was going to a be a shallow cash grab of a homoerotic fighter jet classic. this movie is a cash grab, but every second of the jet engines screaming across the screen and the camera mounted inside and out of these angels of death, more then forgive the nature of the films inception.

cruise--the endless charisma magnet--does nothing but ooze personality in every scene hes in. usually standing next to stock cardboard pilots on his air force suicide mission crew. miles teller as goose's son (hilariously dubbed rooster) does what he can with the role, and jennifer connelly puts in a subtle performance as a jaded bar tender. but the second cruise gets in the cockpit, the film is his.

sounds are explosive, delivering thrilling shock and awe. music is fine with requisite callbacks. editing is fast paced, keeping you involved, while begrudgingly pumping the brakes for softer character moments not taking place in an f-18. and the effects flipping between real life fighters and the in-cockpit performances are seamless.

the film is truly a shinning gem amongst superhero fatigue and animated musicals when it comes to mainstream box office fair. its story is forgettable but its moments are one of a kind. but all roads come back to cruise.

he is an enigma. a film making supernova. an utter and complete maniac. what he does to draw your eyes to a movie screen is nothing short of magic. he is the life of the party. he is hitting red on roulette every turn causing the table to erupt. he is jumping between buildings, actually flying planes, throwing his body out of cars.

"top gun: maverick" solidifies tom cruise isn't done putting an excited smile on your face every time he steps in front of the camera.

hangman reminded me of iceman. roostermiles made the perfect son for goose. it started slow but as soon as he climbed over that limit in the beginning and wrecked the jet it was like there's maverick he knows he is going to get into trouble and unbelievable that his friend through it all iceman was bailing him out. would have been even better to see some of the pilots from the first movie.

like it's predecessor did for a reagan's u. s., top gun: maverick gives an embattled society a hope and connection to what got us here. dripping with a purposeful nostalgia while connecting all of the dots, closing all the loops and giving nods to those who came before... tg:m does it all and more. even as cruise's production team has been under the pressure of the mission impossible franchise, as it shows in the third act, you are left with a warm heart and a peace of mind while being behind enemy lines. the specific detail to cinematography and charismatic cast line up well to close out a franchise 30 years in the making.

the sequel delivers and how. this is not a small feat to achieve to make a follow up movie after 36 years and still manage to make it this entertaining. with a solid story and knock out performance by tom cruise, top gun:maverick takes us through the fantastic ride through nostalgia while having a captivating story to tell.

captain phil mitchell aka maverick is assigned back to top gun, this time as a teacher to train a bunch on a supposed suicide mission and they include rooster aka goose's son. as mav makes it his mission to bring back all of them safely while achieving the mission's target, all of which needs to happen within 3 weeks. as they run against time, the training sessions give enough high moments whereas mav & penny's relationship adds onto the emotional quotient.

the tension between mav & rooster, the bond between mav & ice, everything is so balanced, kudos to the writer. not once did the film felt like it was dragging even when it was taking cinematic liberties in the final act, just couldn't stop rooting for maverick. the message it tries to convey is once again that of learning to let go and it hits hard.

upscale mediocre film. tom cruise built his entire career off these types of movies. upper average at best.

the united states owes its entire existence to its military. cruise plays to this truth like no other hollywood actor.

i thought this would be just another use of a big name title that never remembers why it was good in the first place. but here everything clicks for simple reasons.

1. you have simple plot and also a conflict between two characters that needs them to evolve.

2. the movie never tries to be more than it is a fun action-buddy movie.

3. doesn't overstay its welcome: no three hour movie just to collect a higher ticket price 3. nostalgia: just the right amount, honoring the original 4. here the original main character is not a grumpy out of touch annoyance like in terminator or star wars 5. it adds something new: no cgi crap you can feel those flight scenes. they are amazing.

the only thing you can critisize is that it is the tom cruise show. but i didn't expect anything else and he carries that movie perfectly.

the original 'top gun', released in 1986, has become a cheesy, incredibly entertaining classic, and it isn't hard to see why. the new film is better than the original, but still arrives with some flaws. as with the original, the film loses speed on the ground, but when it's in the air, it is absolutely fantastic.

the plot follows maverick (tom cruise), who's enlisted back into his old flight academy, where he is now 'top gun' (an instructor). it's pretty standard stuff, a few reunions, an old love interest and some great music are mixed along with it.

the characters this time around are mostly useless, with the main b story romance serving as more of seasoning on an entree meal. it doesn't need to be there, but certainly adds a little extra flavor and complexity. but as a whole, the whole love story is useless. it doesn't amount to anything, and is clearly there to live up to the original, but lacks the energy of the first film. another flaw: they kill off kelly mcgillis's character, committing a true filmmaking sin - killing off a character between movies, and adding a new one. and the new interest, this time played by jennifer connelly, doesn't serve a purpose, as i stated previously. tom cruise meets up with her for a slow reunion as we learn that they were once lovers. she's there sporadically for smiles, and of course, congratulates tom cruise at the victorious end. what does she do here? nothing. it's a flaw that dents the movie, because of how baffling of a decision it is.

the best part of the movie are the flight sequences, which go on for a very long time. they're wildly entertaining, constantly unpredictable, and, honestly, exhilarating. they're some of the best action sequences in years. it is too bad the characters are thinly developed and flawed, as this could have been the masterpiece that was so anticipated.

is the movie bad? absolutely not. is it entertaining? extremely. is it worth seeing, especially in a theater? very much so. is it the masterpiece blockbuster that could be compared to blockbusters like 'lawrence of arabia'? hell no. but it's a pretty fun time at the movies.

top gun: maverick (2022)

3 stars (out of 4)

directed by joseph kosinski

screenplay by ehren kruger, eric warren singer and christopher mcquarrie

starring tom cruise, jennifer connelly, miles teller and val kilmer

rated pg-13

130 minutes.

how long are we expected to wait for a sequel to a legendary movie? is it expected that as fickle as movie goers are; top gun:maverick is to be gushed over as a blockbuster or be treated as a pretty good follow up. i expected more than a mediocre rehash of hunks of the most liked scenes in the original. sure tom cruise is outstanding, mostly due to his work ethics and still being able to physically put his body through the rigors of making a movie.

maverick has a disappointing rank for his years in the navy; but of course his attitude and arrogance has pissed off numerous superior officers. he is more or less given a final chance to stay around even longer by returning to top gun and taking charge of training a squad of younger "best-of-the-best" to destroy an enemy uranium plant.

the flying scenes are stunning and choreographed flawlessly. the chemistry with jennifer connelly is smooth as magic. and the small part of val kilmer purely heartfelt. a very good popcorn movie. and for certain, maverick (cruise) still owns the sky!

before moving to the meaty positive parts, let me tell you the things i didnt like cuz you will hear everyone saying the good things first. first, the story is extremely ordinary and dated. i don't know how many times i have seen a film where an ex teacher comes back to business to train a bunch of unorganized students to accomplish a mission. guess the makers wanted to invest less in the story so they went in with an easy one. top gun 1 had a much better story involving personals. second, adding to the previous point, this time the students have no characterization whatsoever except rooster. you aren't attached to any one of them. this is again because makers wanted to invest more in the stunts. third, the romance in this film does not work and is forgettable.

now coming to the part which you must have read everywhere, the positives. i watched it in 4dx and had an absolute "out of this world " experience witnessing the stunts and this is where i give this film brownie points. everything is real. no cgi, nothing. with 4dx, the stunts were feeling so realistic that i got completely immersed into the climax. the 45 mins climax is a treat for cinema lovers. heres a little spoiler without spoiling much- there is a sequence in the climax that is a total rip off of tom cruise's own mi 7 (the last one which came out in 2018 with only difference that in that film, it was helicopters). just breath taking. from next time, if a film releases with 4dx , i am not settling for anything less than 4dx.

tom cruise, man how does this dude look exactly like he was back in 1986?? xd. nevertheless he's done a terrific performance. his chemistry with rooster only gets going in the climax. others have done a good job as well. ice has a small sequence.

overall, a movie only to be witnessed in theaters and that too, try 4dx . if you miss it in theaters, don't even think you will enjoy it on tv.

i have never seen the original so if you haven't either don't let that put you off watching this one.

the movie is fun, the minute i see tom cruise on the poster i immediately want 2 things, a crazy stunt and a big explosion. i got all of the above in this !!

firstly what i liked, most of the movie to be honest. i thought every single character was played perfectly, i thought the action was great and i guessed i would be bored of watching them fly around but i was completely wrong, knowing most shots were 100% real in the plane drew me in so much. the story was okay, the pace was pretty good and there were some very nice hearty moments

not much i didn't like, you can just enjoy a movie without it being a masterpiece, i would have liked a little more in plane time but other than that i can't complain!!

i can see myself watching it again some time, an 8/10 for me.
