top gun: maverick is without a doubt a classic blockbuster, and for me it checked all the marks that it needed to as a action drama flick in 2022. notably though this movie tends to lean in to being sentimental a lot more. i could see this being taken the wrong way but in my opinion it was done respectfully.

directing is something else here, i can't deny that every single fighter jet scene gave me goosebumps. this movie just nails that feeling of overcoming challenges, speed, intensity and everything else that comes to doing something extreme. everytime we get back in that pilot seat i'm in. pacing and editing also need a huge shout-out. this is a movie with incredible highs and lows. and there's a balance just right to make the pace for this 2 hour movie more than bareble. visually it tends to lean to lots of sunsets and yellows. making it have quite a distinct and warm look, fitting to the desert.

this takes me to sound design, fighter jet movie, you have expectations. and yep they're met. incredible sound, punchy, impactful and crisp. dialog sometimes the only thing that sounds a tad mumbled. music, hans zimmer gives a solid en trustworthy score. it does what it needs to do but doesn't innovate.

acting is top notch, everyone does their best. some roles felt a bit small and i do feel that john ham was miscast in his role. but it's a minor personal nitpick. pilots are great, but cruise is the standout no doubt. fantastic range and just great during the many emotional moments.

story, flashbacks have been done well i think, there's a few callbacks, but for me they didn't become too cheesy though it was on the edge sometimes. story realism etc was kinda meh, the enemy are basically bots, no personality. and some plot points like walking into the enemy base and getting out so stealthily whilst there's and alarm going was kinda silly. also how tom just does things in the navy as if he is walking there alone.

that said, a cinema worthy experience.

it is always hard to do follow up with a good sequel, especially if the original was a popular film in the 80s. top gun: maverick defies the odds and soars. tom cruise carriers this film effortlessly and shows he's still got it. i really liked the plot, throwbacks to the original and great flight action sequences that brought it to life. this is a good film but i am pleasantly surprised it has received such a high rating on imdb and grossed so much revenue. i enjoyed the original and also this film. this proves that a great sequel can be made if everything lands well (good plot, acting etc) and should act as a benchmark for future sequels.

with its musical and photographic callbacks to the original "top gun", this film is a marriage of old and new. like many marriages, it contains "something old, something new, something borrowed, and something blue".

tom cruise may not be "old" but his pete mitchell is 36 years older than the brash young pilot we all enjoyed in the first film. in "maverick", mitchell is mostly unchanged: still a captain, still indulging his need for speed.

quite new are the visual effects. though the film features actual scenes of flying-and is notable for that---modern technology figures in the weaponry and the displays.

both the original film and the sequel include scenes of dogfights. "maverick" also includes a secret mission involving a team that must train to surmount nearly impossible odds. this is a plot point "borrowed" from many military films, like "the dirty dozen" or "the dam busters".

as for the blue, consider the wild blue yonder that is the backdrop for most of the film. it is both a place and a state of mind, where most pilots live some of their best hours.

the cast does a fine job of filling their uniforms. though his film focuses less on romance than the original, jennifer connelly plays love interest penny, owner of the bar where the pilots hang out. the film would not have suffered if her character were given more screen time.

the film is fast-paced and emotionally involving, including some moments of real tenderness. i doubt another sequel will be made, and that is fine because "maverick" feels like a fitting ending.

this movie was delayed for so long because of covid and cruise could have easily had this moved to streaming. thank god he didn't!

this was a solid sequel to an old movie which doesn't happen very often!

i actually don't care for a lot of the work cruise has done for 20 years now but this one was solid! not going cgi, thank you! i really hope many other movies follow suit if they're able to.

the story was ok, nothing special but who cares, you're not watching a movie like this for an in-depth story! great job on this one!

i enjoyed top gun maverick more than the original. it had a story which had a lot of potential and director used it very well. after you watch the movie for a while, the story will fade but the feel and the mode of the movie is what keeps you interacted. the soundtrack was nice and aircraft scenes were nicely shot. the movie at some times feel little bit long but the action sequences cover it all. this is movie which you may enjoy at cinema but not that at home. the action scenes are of next level when you experience it in cinema.

overall, you should give this movie a try especially those who love airforce.

tom cruise, and the rest of the crew, went out of their way to give us an unparalleled amount of realism when it comes to parts of the movie recorded in the cockpit, and then they did complete 180*, and created a story, and air combat which are idiotic, and borderline science fiction.

the story itself is fundamentally flawed, because the whole story is propped on an idea that the enemy uses gps jamming, so the target can't be hit by gps guided munition. ok... so how the hell did enemy radars which guided the aa missiles were working if the area is flooded with jamming signals? or how did e-2 hawkeye had not only no problem performing overwatch, but also had tactical map working via gps with all sam sites locations being displayed without any issues? as far as movie goes, there was so jamming of any sort in the area where they were attacking.

what was much better was the level of interactions between the characters, and the amount of respect being paid to the first top gun. this part i enjoyed completely.

in the end, i did enjoy the movie, but it could be so much better if they go through with most of the movie being somewhat realistic, because realism can be even more dramatic, and emotional that made up stories. just look at the case of air force major e. t. tullia who was flying f-16 during desert storm, and successfully defended from 6 iraqi sam missiles in relatively rapid succession, while his automatic countermeasure system wasn't working. if real life can create amazing stories, why can't you?

top gun: maverick is the sequel to the first top gun movie from 1986. this sequel is directed by joseph kosinski, the director of oblivion and tron: legacy. in the film, pete "maverick" mitchell (tom cruise) is called back by the navy after more than thirty years of service as a top gun pilot. here he is asked to train new top gun pilots for an important and dangerous military mission. during these training sessions, maverick tries to train the young pilots in his own ways, so that they can push their own limits. in this way he hopes to send them more successfully on this mission and to be able to see them alive again at home base. due to the difference of generations and the clashing arrogance between maverick and the younger pilots, this is just not as simple as maverick had hoped.

after about thirty years, they manage to present this second top gun film in a modern, yet also recognizable way. there are many moments in this new film that fans of the first film can recognize and appreciate. furthermore, there are also enough moments to make the film more approachable for the younger generation. so young and old can both enjoy this film. it's nice to see tom cruise now in a leadership role teaching younger pilots. compared to the first film, for example, he has now changed from student to teacher, who tries to do everything in his own way. because of this, he sometimes gets into trouble with the people above him, but he tries to stand his ground for a successful end result for himself and his students. they have beautifully portrayed this sequel and actually filmed it all at the request of tom cruis. for example, no green screen or cgi recordings were used. thanks to improved filming techniques and this way of filming, the film feels more realistic as if you are actually in a cockpit during these aircraft training sessions and missions. for this realistic feel and way of filming, they used real airplanes. a large part of the film cast also had to meet many physical demands such as undergoing real g-force training sessions. as a result, most new members of the film cast deliver better and more realistic work during their airplane scenes. only a few have used a stunt double, but fortunately this is not reflected in the film. the actors who play the pilots in training come across well as a joint group of students. because of the script, the film also focuses on other things besides their group, so that the group does not always come across as strong as a joint group. things went a bit better with the older group from the first film. with this new group you only really get to know the students who eventually go on the dangerous mission. in addition to the training scenes and final mission, the film is also about maverick trying to work on a new romantic relationship with peggy benjamin played by jennifer connelly. tom cruise and jennifer connelly have good chemistry with each other in the film, but it just isn't as strong as the chemistry tom cruise had with kelly mcgillis in the first top gun film. kelly mcgillis is unfortunately not in this sequel, because the director and writers couldn't really think of a role for her character in the front of this sequel. kelly mcgillis herself has indicated that she probably has not been asked back either, because she has grown older and did not want to train herself again for the role. returning actor val kilmer has more of a cameo in this film, as due to his declining health he is unfortunately no longer able to do much acting.

there has been lots of sequels in the past where it made things worse from the original film, especially this original film has been released 36 years ago. but tom cruise and joseph kosinski really understand and know what they want from the sequel...it's a really long waited for making a sequel, ( and also because of the pandemic for making this release date putting another year ) but they have done such incredible job for making it right.

for the whole visuals and cinematography, hands down the flight sequences are the next level from the original film ( or any flying sequences in any film ) the long wait to the technology for capturing the actors and actresses inside the fighter jet is breath taking experience. the whole experience brings much more intensity in those flight action sequences. ( must watch in imax )

the storyline is also quite convincing, even the story has been 36 years ago. this sequel really brings lots of connections in the story of the original film, such as val kilmer of iceman, miles teller as rooster who is the son of goose ( tom cruise flight partner from the original film ), using few of the main original soundtrack of the first one, and some similar classic sequences from the first, etc ( you can probably see them from the trailer ) it brings lots of old memories back and they have done it right in this.

the only thing i may complain to this film is also the similarities, where there's really been little too much similarities from the original film, which may not bring me any freshness in terms of story wise. but other than that, the whole excitement watching this film in imax has been amazing. so i won't mind with those little tiny complain. overall this film really brings practical flying visual sequences into the next level.

what makes tom cruise the biggest name in action movies worldwide is the daredevil persona he has carefully maintained over the years, combined with his almost vampiric ability to delay the ageing process. making a sequel to an era-defining film like "top gun (1986)", 36 years after the original would have been taxing on any other actor but this man makes it seem like a walk in the park. when "maverick" takes to the control of that fighter jet, you are sucked in again to the mesmeric, fast-paced world of "top gun", with the adrenaline-pumping and goosebumps-inducing narratives only strengthening in this brilliant sequel.

we rejoin captain pete "maverick" mitchell (cruise), a daredevil fighter pilot who still refuses to play by the rules and keeps turning down promotions that would see him grounded instead of being in the air where he belongs. tasked with rejoining the famous "top gun" naval fighter pilot academy, this time as a trainer, the movie follows his journey as a highly unconventional teacher, teaching a bunch of rag-tag hotshots that it is not the plane, but the pilot that makes a difference in high-stakes air combat. director joseph krasinski stays true to the vision and world building so painstakingly done by the original film's director, the legendary tony scott, by paying rich tribute to some of the most memorable motifs and elements used by his accomplished predecessor.

miles teller is expectedly terrific as the troublemaker from the class of students, while glen powell and monica barbaro ably play the other cadets that "maverick" has to beat into shape for a crucial real-world mission. the fighter plane dogfights are painstakingly filmed, with the perfectionist in cruise insisting that each member of the cast portraying a pilot in the film mandatorily fly in one of the fighter jets built by boeing co. so they could fully comprehend the physical and emotional duress undergone by a pilot operating under the strain of immense gravitational forces.

despite losing his voice to throat cancer, i loved the way the makers still managed to include val kilmer back in his iconic role of "iceman", maverick's bête noire. jennifer connelly is enthralling and captivating in equal measure as maverick's love interest and i'm glad the director went an age-appropriate way in the romance than pairing up the 59-year-old cruise with a young actress.

the iconic bgm and the music of the original, composed by the legendary harold faltermeyer can never be matched and the makers smartly recreate the same with minimal changes, to doubly recapture the blend of soul-stirring music, bone-crushing action and exhilarating aerial combat sequences that made "top gun" such a cult classic action blockbuster.

the cinematography from claudio miranda captures every dip, swerve, dive and turn with panache and realism, so much so that you feel all the tension and anxiety of the protagonists on screen. while the screenplay follows a familiar road, hitting all the feel-good high notes and redemptive arcs you would associate with such a movie, the "top gun" junkie in you can forgive the makers as they more than live up to the credo of this mother of all action franchises, that still makes you scream "i feel the need, the need for speed", 36 years on! highly recommended! catch it on the biggest screen possible because maverick, he is back baby, in all his legendary glory!

maverick is a sequel that's better than the prequel. maybe because of the passage of 36 years in between films, the second one has less glossy, more serious approach. the cold war machismo was replaced by a more reflective (although no less action-oriented) attitude. tom cruise, playing the title character, has supplanted delovee3d here a nuanced performance. in top gun, he was preening. here, he's acting. the differences relate also to the screenplay, with less testosterone and to the tone, that is more grounded.

i was preparing to be disappointed as i didn't see how a sequel to top gun would be able to work. they somehow figured out how to portray an older and a little wiser maverick, still exciting, larger than life, reckless and charming while not ignoring his age. it immediately felt like a 30 year later or so maverick would be!

the ties to the original were not too much and not too little, with a new group of hot shots sharing the spotlight with the past. the new characters, (rooster and penny in particular) were worked in seamlessly and perfectly cast. jennifer connely was immediately a perfect fit for the love interest as well.

in summary, i am not a serial high-ranker and a 9 is high praise, which this film deserved. this was my first time in a theater in over two years and this is absolutely one to see on imax, or at least in a theater!

it can be said that this work has been created in parallel to the previous work! . the screenplay keeps moving us as a page of maverick's beautiful love, a page of indescribable sadness at the loss of his friend, a page of training to master students. the director has given back the classic scenes, shots and light flow featured in the previous work! . the truth is that "tom cruise" continues to dedicate his body and life to his art without the slightest thought! . make no mistake about going to the theater to see jennifer connelly's striped diamond eyes! .

hey, streamers, let's fly off into the danger zone. yes, it's top gun: maverick time. the sequel you have been waiting almost 40 years for, which was supposed to come out 2 years ago, is finally here. now, i have never seen the original film, but i was keen to see what all the hype around this sequel was about. tom cruise has made good choices over the years and he's always going full tilt in these action roles, so i didn't expect for this to disappoint. here's how it goes.

even though top gun: maverick is a present-day sequel to the original top gun (1986), the movie really leans into that old-fashioned, 1980's action film vibe. also, there is a big spoiler from the original film that is central to the story of this sequel - maverick's wingman, goose, died. here, goose's son, rooster (miles teller), is one of the elite navy aviators, who maverick (tom cruise) is tasked with training for what's considered an important but impossible mission. there is tension between maverick and rooster because of their fraught history. there is tension between maverick and his superiors because he is notorious for going rogue. nevertheless, maverick is the best and the mission requires the best. high-flying hijnks ensue.

top gun: maverick is the kind of movie that begs to be seen on a big screen. in my opinion, the story is not really great or innovative, so the actions sequences, stunts and camera work have to justify the price of admission. luckily, they very much do. the aerial shots and all of the fighter jets flying have to be seen on a big screen to truly be appreciated. the rumble of the jets and the perceived danger add to the tension that builds up through the movie and explodes in the final sequences. while there is an attempt to build an emotional core to the film by focusing on maverick and rooster's relationship and also a slight love interest on the side, those relationships barely register and seem almost superfluous. honestly, they could've cut the love story and the film would have been the same but 10-15 minutes shorter - that would have given them the ability to cultivate the maverick and rooster relationship, which would have been more impactful.

some of this movie is so retro as to be kind of corny. glen powell plays hangman. he's one of the cockiest aviators in the top gun program. powell plays it like the quintessential 1980's movie villain, which was groan-inducing at times, but some may love it. tom cruise is at his tom-cruise-iest, which isn't a bad thing. movies need stars and tom cruise is still a movie star. he still has the charm to pull off maverick's character. as the movie leans into the nostalgia, tom cruise makes it worthy of being on a big screen. this movie desperately needs that.

nevertheless, what was presented was certainly entertaining. there will be times when the flying will have you on the edge of your seat. that's why a movie like this is made. in that way, it is quite successful.

ultimately, top gun: maverick is tailor-made to be seen in a movie theater. the feats of stunts and action are worthy of the big screen. there are times when you may be on the edge of your seat. although the story is a bit lacking, the rest of the movie makes up for it and the 2-hour runtime flies by in a *wink*. grab a box of popcorn and enjoy this spectacle on a big screen.

pretty awesome sequel with tom in awesome form. unbelievable action sequences and interesting story that balances nostalgia, new ideas and the expected hokiness. teller is a great actor, and successfully matches the cruise intensity. shameless money spinner, but we greedily lap it up, as this film reminds us of how good films used to be. 8/10.

top gun: maverick is a great movie, one of the best movies to watch now in theaters so go watch it! it is a great love letter to the original one and gives a nice closure to the story of maverick.

i kind of anticipated from the first trailer that maverick (tom cruise) will be taking the position of training pilots. not just regular pilots but the best in the u. s. navy.

the main struggle and conflict of course is between maverick and bradley bradshaw, a. k. a "rooster", a. k. a goose's son from the first movie who died. goose was maverick's co pilot and best friend who died and ever since, rooster has been blaming maverick. so you know there is a lot of tension between them. especially when maverick is supposed to train rooster and the other pilots for a mission they might not come back alive.

the other pilots are also very interesting, i found much interest in them as i found in maverick. my only concern that thankfully didn't came true was that they would be annoying characters that won't cooperate. but they have proven to be great pilots with great skills, their cooperation with maverick was truly awesome to see near the end of the film.

of course the final battle sequence was amazing, a bit to hollywood type of ending but for now i'll pass over it.

overall i'm really happy with this film, i'm glad my hype didn't die during the whole two-year wait and that i'm satisfied with the final product. go watch it now and thank me later.

an epic adrenaline rush created by some of the most unbelievable high-octane, real-life aerial sequences ever made. you feel like you've been in the jet the entire movie (prepare to sweat!). calling this an action movie doesn't really do it justice - it's more of an immersive thrill ride.

top gun: maverick pays homage to its original on multiple occasions, filling you with nostalgia. a few of the characters are rather one-dimensional and some of the dialogue feels predictably simple, but the storyline delivers. tom cruise defies physics and his age once again, delivering on his promises of using real planes and no cgi.

this is what a big blockbuster film can be! the bar has been raised and everyone else has been put on notice.

verdict: watch it.

excellent moviemaking! some fun for nearly everyone. story of a man who is the undeniably the goat, proving that he's still got it and whipping the young bucks into shape to be the next generation. they should not make more, but this was great.

some quick "is this worth it?" math... tom cruise running? check. ok, we're good. because everyone knows - tom cruise has *never* made a good movie where he wasn't running.

all the obligatory tc "man of action" requirements are met: authentic stunt work, motorcycle, planes (obvi), some form of pg-rated pda with the girl... all set to a good soundtrack.

ample homages to the vhs source material as well (so much so that you don't need to re-watch it, thank you) without insulting anyone's memory of intelligence - yay!

some genuine tear-jerking moments here (val kilmer, man), a well as some uniquely military-based fun, a "dad" moment or two and a weird "immortal grown teenager" scene that made me laugh for lots of reasons and it's a wrap: traditional old-school movie gold, truly.

oddly enough, the best thing tg:m did here was to advertise the next tom cruise movie - mission impossible 146 (or whatever). i now can't wait to see that.

bottom line? go see it in the theater and get popcorn.

for fans clamoring for a modern & significantly better sequel to top gun, lo and behold, maverick is the answer to our prayers. with one for the books kind of action sequences, this film completely blew away the original, a rare feat for reprised titles.

before we rave about the action however, worth to highlight that the casting done for maverick was on point. the new faces were solid in their roles particularly miles teller, whose resemblance to anthony edwards was uncanny. glen powell & john hamm as anti heroes, were perfect complements to tom & miles as the scenes they share were electric. to top it off, seeing val kilmer as iceman sent shivers down my spine as it was surreal.

as for the action, absolutely epic! great work by joseph kosinski and tom cruise for producing an authentic "aerial warfare" experience that rivals that of christopher nolan's dunkirk. amazing that they weren't conservative with these scenes either, as these tension-filled & intense sequences were abundant, resulting to an edge of your seat experience that the original plainly lacked.

my only knack in maverick is the unavoidable cheese-fest. it does add substance to the storyline and i'm glad it was dialed down compared to the original, but yes, the drama is a tad predictable and a buzzkill at certain points. nevertheless, the fun and excitement are impossible to be spoiled!

overall, maverick has definitely cemented its place as one of the best action films of 2022. the hype and build up to its release was well worth it as it is really a well executed film, brimming with energy, authenticity and well intentioned bravado. sorry for doubting you tom cruise!

very entertaining, engaging and action packed sequel. having seen the original in theaters back in the 80's, then enduring the loss of the theater experience during covid i was greatly anticipating the return of great filmmaking and big screen entertainment.

tg maverick is one of the rare sequels that outdoes the original in almost every respect while remaining true to the original narrative. the characters were authentic and the actors were well cast. the sentimentality was perfectly executed without becoming sappy and the new storyline and writing was even better than the original.

very well done film all around and easily some of the best action ever produced for the big screen. the final 45 minutes is a heart pounding thrill ride.

get your popcorn 🍿 ready!

86/100.

i loved the original top gun and it inspired many of us to buy a ninja rocket and feel the need for speed.

this film is very entertaining and tom cruise is still hanging in there looking good at his age and jennifer connelly is the perfect 80s leading lady - even if her part is not very well developed and rather pointless.

the film has fantastic action in the beginning and then sort of peters out in the middle with melodrama yet makes up for it in the 3rd act and has a wonderful ending that always is most vital to an action film. joe kosenski does a fantastic job directing the film.

the only complaint is that the film easily could have been 110 mins like the original and the 2nd act felt tired and the writers hit us over the head too many times doing the rooster/goose to the point of exhaustion.

and as many have mentioned the plot was completely stupid with the cruise ship missiles only taking out the airstrip and not the mountain top sar missiles. and the 5th generation planes with stealth mode fighting in visual mode against a 1970s f14 is laughable. like a tesla trying to race a tricycle with trainer wheels.

but hey its tom cruise and the only part that was really missing was his motto of "i feel the need for speed". .

otherwise it is a fantastic film and loved seeing the old relic pushing mach 10 at age 60. and of course the navy could not ask for a better promo ad to get more kiddos in the seat of a fighter jet. too bad nowadays the f35 is a nightmare failure and most pilots are flying drones inside a metal box in nevada.

a solid 8 and surely it will make loads of money yet sure hope there is no more sequels. great balls of fire!!! enjoy the film with low expectations. old 80 school fun!

i am not a big action genre fan. i prefer realistic action scenes when they are needed in plot. such as heat or tdk. this one is easily the best movie of 2022 so far.

tom cruise deserves an oscar nomination just because he is killing in those non stunt f-18 scenes. just wow!

story is formulaic. there are some cliche characters and expected plot twists but acting and chemistery save it all. i can't complain for cliche dramatic character arcs. topgun maverick is all about crazy fun and thrilling action.

you shouldn't miss this one if you like classics because this one is already a classic! 8/10.

look, it's better than the first one, and it's a good action popcorn flick. tom cruise continues to stick the landing. but "masterpiece"? "best movie ever"? come on. have these people never watched actual amazing films?

the flight scenes (especially the beginning) are indeed very well done. the classic feel of the first movie is there and improved upon. the movie is an action roller coaster ride. the acting is solid, and the dialogue is funny and engaging. but the romance portion is weak, and some of the other interpersonal drama stuff is contrived too. the plot also gets a bit ridiculous and unrealistic to the point i was having trouble suspending disbelief.

all in all though, it is worth the watch, and i do consider it an improvement over the original. it's fun, gripping, and intense. just here to say the 10/10 hype is absurd and i can't believe it's currently sitting at #50 on the top 250. it's not that good.

much much better than i was actually expecting. i find the original to be a very mixed bag, but this was a really great sequel. i was surprised at how much of an emotional punch this one had with tom cruise's character revisiting old characters and memories of his early top gun years, especially with iceman. the flight action sequences are incredible and so well done i was hooked the entire time and on the edge of my seat. there's a few nods to the original too and the music still rocks. honestly this might be the biggest surprise of 2022 for me so far.

8/10.

for the years i've been attending movie theaters, this has to be the best one i've seen in a long time. over the past few years, most of the movies i've seen in theaters have been unoriginal and predictable stuff that this generation of film has become known for. however, in this movie, the people involved in this film seem to have actually cared. from the opening thank you message from tome cruise, to real jet fighters being used instead of cgi. the movie also had a patriotic feeling to it as the american flag can be seen everywhere. the movie was tense, having you at the edge of your seat unlike the superhero movies with the same plot but new coat of paint. this will definitely be one of the best films this year.

thirty-six years after the original top gun took the world by storm, tom cruise is back as pete "maverick" mitchell in this high-octane sequel that delivers on all fronts. with its stunning cinematography, exhilarating action sequences, and compelling character development, top gun: maverick is a must-see for fans of the original and newcomers alike.

the film picks up decades after maverick's heroic exploits in top gun, where he is now a seasoned test pilot, pushing the limits of what is possible. when he is tasked with training a new generation of top gun graduates for a dangerous mission, maverick finds himself facing his own mortality and confronting the ghosts of his past.

tom cruise delivers a career-best performance as maverick, once again demonstrating his undeniable charisma and screen presence. he captures the character's unwavering confidence, his underlying vulnerability, and his unwavering dedication to his craft.

the supporting cast is equally impressive, with miles teller as rooster, the son of maverick's former rio goose, glen powell as hangman, the cocky rival trainee, jennifer connelly as penny benjamin, maverick's former love interest, and jon hamm as cyclone, the tough-as-nails mission commander.

joseph kosinski, who also directed the 2013 film oblivion, delivers a visually stunning film with breathtaking aerial sequences that will leave you breathless. the film's use of imax technology is particularly impressive, immersing the viewer in the action and making you feel like you're right there in the cockpit with maverick and his team.

top gun: maverick is a thrilling, action-packed sequel that honors the legacy of the original while also forging its own path. it's a film that will appeal to fans of the original and newcomers alike, and it's sure to leave you wanting more.

this show provides all the nostalgia for those raised on the original but different enough to maybe inspire a new generation to be fans. none of the new pilots have much character development as their roles feel rushed. however, maverick is clearly more conservative except for when he flies; ignoring orders, pushing known limits, and of course pushing back against authority. all leading the older generation, to have a feeling of nostalgia and reminiscence. pictures of goose, his family, his jacket, his bike, and even some of the photography serve as reminders to the first top gun. we also get a little on the ground, a bonding, and a new love interest in this one. we don't get much of the back story to their previous relationship, but it appears by the end that maverick may begin to no longer fly solo and may settle down after the events of this movie.

good: new photography, new jets, new conflict, connections to previous movie bad: less character development and attachment, story is rushed/jumps at times.

this film is basically the original top gun but better in every way.

the stuntwork and acting is phenomenal along with the jokes and characters.

the connection between rooster and maverick was done very well although i would've liked to see it a bit more.

the film is one of the best looking films visually of all time along with the last jedi and kong skull island.

the buildup to the final battle is awesome and so is the battle itself.

it pays homage to the original in very nice ways while just being better.

overall just easily one of the best films of all time and easily the best film about flying and planes of all time.

top gun: maverick is a surprisingly good action film. it has got great action-sequences, good actors, and a well-written plot that echoes its predecessor.

i have been sceptical towards modern sequels to classic blockbusters, which also affected my initial attitudes towards this film. however, i was pleasantly surprised at how well the film honoured its source material and built on the story.

the film really feels like top gun. this is of course intentional, but it never feels cheesy or out of place. the character dynamics, the shots, and of course the soundtrack works to really set a familiar tone.

the plot builds on the original film in a good way, adding emotional weight. it doesn't feel forced, but it creates a good link between the two films.

it is a very "clean" action film, and it could have benefited from some more dramatic moments. still, the film makes for a fun, engaging ride which might actually outshine the original.

i usually say that a sequel can't/shouldn't be better than the original. however, this fantastic movie blasts that out of the sky.

with top-notch speeds and blindsiding emotions, simply put, top gun: maverick is my film of 2022.

that soaring sound of fighter jets ripping through the desert salt flats and the fuel injecting roar, as the familiar kenny loggins's danger zone track blasts out, wasn't hampered by my only regret of not seeing this movie on the biggest screen possible.

bottom line, i knew i would enjoy this film from the trailer but i never expected this movie would remind me of the summer blockbusters from my childhood.

an absolutely amazing sequel especially considering it's been 30 years and it was far better than the original. the story line was much more clear cut and the action was exceptionally better. teller and cruise crushed it but i will say my only con was literally every other actor who played a pilot was bad. great movie though.

i wanted more from rooster. unfortunately his character felt a little thin to me. i think a scene with rooster (miles teller) and his mother (meg ryan) would have fleshed out the animosity between him and maverick.

yes offcourse there are clichés. yes offcourse this is a commericial profit endeaovour. yes the plotline isn't much. yes, al lot of unnecessary sentiment and drama. but come on. appreciatie it for what it is. it is a great, visually stunning action movie. it is hard to say wether it is accurate towards the navy and aviation in generaal. most people do not know and do propably not care. respect for tom cruise for being in such fine condition in his sixties. even if you have no clue of topgun part one, this is still a very enjoyable watch. go watch it on a big screen if possible, it adds up to tegen effect.

i thoroughly enjoyed this!!

watched the first movie a long time ago and i personally liked that but the sequel hits it out of the park.

we the viewers expect a tom cruise project to be easily distinguishable from other action movies. his movies push the limits of many technical boundaries, are entertaining and almost never dull. and this delivers in all fronts.

the aerial cinematography was amazing and the sound paired with that made the action sequences emmersive. this movie should be experienced in theater.

the music was good, the nods to previous movie was done in a tasteful way. all the actors did their job very well.

one can argue some of the plot might be unnecessary, some forced, some too optimistic but when all the small and big things come together this movie just feels great!!

tom cruise returns to his popular role of pete "maverick" mitchell, arrogant but goodhearted and incredibly talented navy fighter pilot of the original 1986 film, now some 30+ years later much the same thank goodness, though he hasn't risen above the rank of captain and is currently a test pilot when he is ordered back to the top gun program to teach prior top graduates on a secret and dangerous mission to destroy a rogue uranium plant in a canyon on foreign territory, and deal with the estranged son of his late best friend "goose" killed in the first film, and now a pilot himself. jennnifer connelly plays his current love interest penny, who was mentioned in the first film, and val kilmer returns briefly as "iceman" now a respected admiral nearing the end of his life.

surprisingly superb sequel surpasses the first in every way, though pays its respects to it most satisfactorily while still telling its own story and introducing interesting new characters who could possibly star in future installments, if this turns into a franchise. a huge blockbuster hit that troubled hollywood could learn many lessons from, as this film is most exciting and emotional, not preachy with the "message", but an old-fashioned patriotic feel-good adventure that hasn't been seen for far too long. not at all surprising story wise, but well-acted and directed (joseph kosinski) picture hits all the right buttons.

after 3 years of delay, the much awaited top gun sequel is finally here. i've never really been one of the die hard fans of top gun but i thought it was a fun watch with some memorable moments. and i enjoyed this sequel just as much. if you're a top gun fan, you're probably going to love this. though, i don't think it is as much of it's own movie, it does a good job tributing and celebrating the 1987 top gun.

i like the direction. action-wise, this feels like a modernized top gun. while there is more use of cgi, the shots are wider and you get a clearer view of the dogfight scenes. i also found the final mission and the environment pretty cool. i liked most of the characters but some of them are just there for you to forget, and some feel like exact replacements from the original. there were also plenty of jokes and it's a fairly light-hearted and fun movie, which i didn't expect. tom cruise is, well tom cruise, and that's enough. the rest of the actors did a good enough job too.

i loved the first half. it felt fresh and i loved the direction it was heading. the second half goes pretty much exactly as you would have thought, which was a bit disappointing. though the second half has some great action scenes and crowd cheering moments, it's also predictable. and the final act has many similarities to the original. like there are scenarios that felt exactly like certain scenes in top gun. the story in the second half is very similar to the original. that, i thought, could have been better.

but in the end i walked out happy. i enjoyed this movie and i can understand the hype. if, even after 35 years, you get a sequel of your favourite movie, it would certainly be a special feeling.

maverick skywalker (tom cruise) ends up teaching a dozen aces how to hunt bump rabbits in a canyon and shoot a target down a ventilation shaft in order to destroy death star. seems an unnamed rogue nation has build an underground facility to enrich uranium. the us is going to commit an act of war against them by attacking the facility protected by surface to air missiles and superior fighters. there is some human drama.

i was not overly impressed with val kilmer. his relationship with penny is rekindled. otherwise, good characters, unbelievable plot.

i'm so happy i went to see this in the theatre. we went as a family and even my teenage daughters enjoyed it.

loud action packed and tom cruise was awesome. jennifer connelly did a great job as well.

loved the actors who played rooster and hangman. my only complaint is that there was no character development of the new crew. i remember watching the original, i bawled my eyes out when goose died. i felt like i didn't care about any of the new characters.

overall is was a great start to summer film definitely worth seeing in the theatre.

a well made sequel in which it surpasses its predecessor . top gun 1986 was a commercial hit , eventhough it had weak plot and was not much engaging . but this time it's different , in this movie right from first movie had proper goal and traveled towards the goal . plot was pretty simple a asusual team on mission story , but way they build tense around the mission by showing its difficulties makes more intresting . joseph kosinski's as director done a spectacular job . cast wise each and every cast gave their best . tom cruise doing this role after 36 years delivered marvelous performance . miles teller playing as roose ( son of goose character in top gun ) was literally show stealer . jennifer connelly done her part well . relationship between roose and maverick was emotional . each and every action sequence with flight jet was very well made , especially last 30mins literally gave me a seat edge experience . only drawback i felt was romance track . they missed to explain the absence of charlie's character . overall a must watch movie . please don't miss it to watch it on big screen .

top gun: maverick (2022) directed by joseph kosinsky is a surpringly original sequel and takes a highly successful retro step to hollywood film making.

the story is set 30 years after its predecessor, and follows maverick's return to the united states navy strike fighter tactics instructor program (also known as "topgun"). the plot is very simple; here, he must confront his past as he trains a group of younger pilots, among them the son of maverick's deceased best friend lieutenant nick "goose" bradshaw, to eliminate a uranium target. that's it. but the sheer finesse and bravour with which cruise, connelly, teller and kosinsky pull this off is impressive.

spectacular action, stunning cinematography, a great score paying homage to it's original predecessor topgun (1986), is all perfectly executed, and that justifies its cheesy style and simple plot. highly recommended!

as usual tom cruise is always at his best in what he is supposed to deliver as a lead actor in any movie offered to him. it is so unbelievable that even at 59 he looks hell young as someone of 45 years, or even lesser. his down to earth attitude with a smart personality is always a winning point.

for those who haven't watched 1986's masterpiece and original top gun, i strongly advise you to watch it, because it has emotional and eventual connection with this sequel. val kilmer's short yet impactful role of admiral iceman, now a sufferer of throat cancer, shares emotional bonding with pete in a part. role of young pilot trainees and graduates played by miles teller, glenn powell and monica barbaro are outstanding and performed exceptionally brilliant.

last but not the least, jennifer connelly deserves a strong applaud for her performance as pete's new love interest penelope and a single mother. her presence alongside tom adds a slight comfort and helps in moving the story forward.

overall, this one is a highly recommendable sequel and more powerful than the original.

maverick is worth seeing in the theater. it has a well thought out storyline and it is visually amazing. plus the sound effects are unreal. i now know why tom cruise wanted to wait to release it in the theater and not a streaming service. i give it a 8 out of 10.

i don't get it why this review was declined at first. do the review-revewers just toss a coin? is it not allowed to review this film positively (to the bigger part)? or is it because i said something about "us world police prop***anda"?

anyway: i enjoyed this movie a lot. it has a straight and simple and yet captivating story and a lot of very good top tier action, and wich was done by using mostly practical effects and filmmaking and was not a cgi overkill, unlike so many blockbuster action movies nowadays.

the movie also stands out as an example for a very good sequel, which might even be superior to the first movie.

if you can see past the blatant and yet relatively sparingly inserted "us world police" prop***anda (which was in the first "top gun" as well), this movie can be a very fun ride for you, especially if you are into a somewhat cons*rv*tive action movie experience. thank you, tom cruise, for giving us such a movie in the 2020ies!

a very good sequel, maybe even better than the first "top gun".

i was glad i saw the original film first and, i saw it multiple times. i have it on an ancient laserdisc format and watched it a lot after it was first released. having done that, it made the experience of top gun maverick a whole lot more complete and understandable.

making this movie required hours upon hours of film making and, sadly, much had to be cut out to make the movie fit the industry's 2-hour model. that is readily apparent. this movie could have been a whole lot more with some of that cut footage being restored.

this was a school teaching pilots for their next mission. but, there wasn't a lot of school in the film -- on the ground or in the air. aerial teamwork never comes into play until the grand finale to the story. at least the beach football game offered a glimpse but not enough. like, when they climb out of the hole, why do they roll over to go down the other side? it has to do with g-forces but, that's never mentioned. pilots will understand but the audience, well not so much.

a lot of character development between mav and penny would have also contributed greatly to the film. do people who never saw the original know who penny benjamin is and what her relationship to maverick is all about? what about the other pilots? anything there? there is a gaping hole in that regard.

i have read that joseph kosinski doesn't plan on a "directors cut" but, i hope he seriously reconsiders this decision. another half hour of material can transform this excellent film into a superior film easily.

i thought "top gun: maverick" was very fun. better than the first to be honest. the dogfights were great. tom cruise still has it too. it's a very good action drama movie with a lot of heart. nothing that'll knock your socks off but it's an entertaining 2 hours.

it is truly amazing how a movie, done right, can make you fly. top gun maverick took us to new heights, quite literally. it took me away, just for a moment, and made me experience something that i will never be able to in real life. i left the theater feeling just a little bit cooler than i felt before, just for an instant, as if i were part of something bigger.

granted, i did not enjoy the original "top gun". but this sequel surpassed my expectations-of sequels in general, but especially as the sequel to a movie that i do not particularly enjoy.

i especially liked how maverick took the audience with the pilots into training to teach us something while toning down the "broness" of the original that i found so unappealing. maverick is funny while retaining some emotional depth and gravitas gained from its source material. and the stakes in maverick are still high. in this case it is not so much the anonymous enemy that keeps tensions high, but the fight against physical limits, the natural constraints that we battle against to reach our target. these are the qualities that make top gun maverick a truly captivating movie to watch.

definitely would recommend.

wish we didnt have to wait 30 years for this . its a fabulous sequal, really good story , brilliant . really enjoyed it, although its not as fast pacing as top gun its more mature , but absolutely phenominal , think its gonna be one of the best movies of this year perhaps .there are some similar characters,,and some remembered parts , and some very sad parts , but its well worth watching and very exciting and has some real nail biting moments ! im glad i watched it . tom cruise is every bit as good as he was in the original top gun, and i must say for a male his age he looks incredible, he still looks as young as he did the first time around i really dont know how he manages to keep so fit ,? amazing movie !

what an experience! top gun (1986) was not bad for being an 80s movie, but top gun: maverick (2022) really pushed the limits of today's modern movies. the flying scenes were unbelievably amazing, which literally gave me goosebumps! the visuality, the sound and the music together are a real masterpiece. i didn't know if i was going to smile or cry of enjoyment during watching. you can't get any better action scenes from a movie. the actors were mostly good - especially tom cruise. i have to say that the story was kind of the typical, american military story, and some of the dialogue scenes were a little too long for my part, but the flying scenes made up for most of it. anyway, strongly recommending for every action-movie lover!

top gun came out at a time when smart phones only existed in science fiction and computers were more expensive than cars. relationships didn't start with swiping right on the screen, and teenagers left hand written notes, not facebook messages, for those they had a crush on. the world was a very different place without the suffocating abundance of technology.

so, what have we got in top gun: maverick? we got drama, we got rivalry, we got romance, we got some funny moments, but above all, we got character. i couldn't help but notice the similarity with the recent bond movies, where an aging bond is considered obsolete and to be replaced by technology. in one scene, tom cruise's superior tells him tom wasn't his first choice for the given mission, and he couldn't fathom what tom might have left to give. again, i was reminded of a scene from the dark knight rises, when selina (catwoman) begs batman to come with her. she says, you don't owe them (the people of gotham) anything, you've given them everything. to which, batman says, not everything, not yet.

tom cruise was 24 in 1986, and in top gun: maverick, he shows how much he appreciates what we no longer have in the midst of all the things we have. he takes us on a journey on which the things that make us human are on full display. the cinematography is outstanding, the story not outlandish, and although there are a few moments where a willing suspension of disbelief is required, those are precisely what makes the movie stand out from the daily grinds of life. it's about flying, and for a change without a cape, but it's not the plane, it's the pilot.

go watch it; it'll take your breath away.

theres something so nice about a sequal thats been so many years and yet still maintains the charm that the original movie had. you could say that its probably not as great as the original but it still had the same great songs, awesome vehicles and othes that are nice to look at. there is some new cast up this time around following cruise and kimore. a new love interest jennifer connely is here and its always lovely to see her in films. we also have ed harris, john hamm and miles teller as one of the new recruits to mavericks training program. they get off to a rocky start but after understanding who he is they are alright. so overall it was a great action packed sequal that had a lot of heart but was sad aswell.

help me help you to take the highway to the danger zone...i even rode into the danger zone just to bring you this review of "top gun: maverick".

well truth be known i was in a comfortable movie seat and the only danger i faced was running out of drink & food before this over 2 hour movie marathon finished so i started rationing my snacks while some of the best dog fights zoomed across the big screen in xd.

this has to be some of the best aerial photography of fighter jets i've ever seen.

however manage your expectations with a script that isn't as good as the original and a bar room scene that drags on past its use by date.

this top gun took 36 years to finally be exclusively released in cinemas thanks to its star & producer tom cruise strongly recommending it not go straight to streaming in a covid-19 world.

the late bob hawke was prime minister of australia and reaganomics was rife in the usa the year this story of a naval academy flight school for elite pilots first came to light.

tom cruise has been acting for 40 years and has once again strapped in to play the beloved lieutenant pete "maverick" mitchell in this top gun sequel.

one of the running gags is at his age, nearly 60, he should be an admiral by now, but he's a bad boy who doesn't play by the rules.

i guess you could call him a maverick...oh that's right they do.

from being a shirtless arsonist in "endless love" to a shirtless ball playing pilot on the beach in "top gun: maverick" he's gone the full circle.

that's right there is no homo-erotic volleyball scene in this movie, but don't worry director joseph kosinski managed to film a scene where cruise gets to flex his middle age pecs.

this time he's teaching the next generation of aviators, including miles teller as "bradley bradshaw" aka "rooster" aka the son of "mavericks" best friend "goose".

he teaches them how to let their egos write cheques their bodies can't cash.

the macguffin that propels this story along involves going into combat training on a level no one's ever seen, not even "maverick".

also watch out for other characters maverick butts heads with including vice admiral cyclone played by jon hamm and ed harris as a rear admiral.

keep the tissues handy when val kilmer's "ice man" returns as an admiral with throat cancer, the same disease afflicting kilmer in real life.

guess who isn't back in this sequel?

kelly mcgillis as his love interest "charlie" instead jennifer connelly steps up as "penny benjamin" who's character only got a mention in the first "top gun".

by the way if you are playing top gun bingo the word 'dangerous' could win you the game...again.

your mission, should you accept it, is to see this movie on the biggest screen near you, because this film doesn't just complete me, it completes the top gun journey.

great movie and lots of fun but tom cruise wrote himself in as luke skywalker. too many references to add here but it became so laughable especially near the end. this could have been a movie telling the story of the training before the destruction of the death star mission. right up to the 3 foot opening of the vent shaft at the end of a narrow corridor they need to fly through. i swear, in one scene as they were entering the canyon, they cgi'd an actual x-wing in for a few milliseconds as they were banking left. the "enemy" pilots even looked a lot like tie fighter pilots. still, a good movie to watch but come on lmao.

i really enjoyed seeing top gun 2 last night. it was in fact better than the first one. i liked all the action they included to it. it was more action packed than the first one with all the jets they raced in with today's computer generated effects made it more realistic than ever and how maverick got to know goose's son.

what i liked: popcorn humor, it got off to a promising start, beautiful jennifer connelly, iceman cameo, nerve wracking final mission, callbacks to top gun 1986, the cool fighter jet imagery when the anti-missile tech is released, and the very end was a nice happy ending that is applaudable.

what i didn't like: the middle where maverick comes out of nowhere on the radar while they are in class and they can somehow all observe him even though he was dismissed as teacher and his subsequently being brought back felt rushed and unrealistic, picking the 6 pilots felt rushed and slightly confusing for a big moment, the soundtrack was nowhere near as good and iconic as the 1986 original (it could've used righteous brothers "you've lost that lovin feeling" at the end or somewhere), the tacked on "behind enemy lines" ending became cartoony and literally made no difference in the end other than for another deus ex machina (only because they didn't inform the viewer that hangman was sent, which they should have) hero-twist, and even though this was an impossible mission not one pilot died, which made it lack drama and believability.

this is a decent-good movie. it's like ripping out the cliff notes of a good book and only reading them, but moreso it's like the mission tom cruise led his pilots on: the mission was to vertically clear the mountain on the way out at the end of the mission in order to succeed, but for the movie during that ending, the aircrafts never quite cleared the peak to be truly great. it did reach the good range though, and for movies today, maybe that's the best they can do since it seems it's all been done before.

6/10.

i just watched the film and truly enjoyed it. it as engaging, old school action fun the way they don't make them anymore. tom cruise was born for this role. the supporting characters, everything was perfect, but the disease of too long endings stroke again. the film was perfectly set for maverick to die an honorable death and get absolution, go out guns blazing, a dinosaur in ai era, take your pick. the whole movie was perfectly set for an epic death and absolution to the character. but then he lives, and he stole an f-14 taking off from a 50m runway, only to fight fighter jets 30 years more advanced than his. anyway i don't mind the extravaganza, in the end that's what the character is all about, but it really felt like the movie was about to finish and some executive just ordered another 20 minutes because of the potential for more sequels. especially now that it's smashing the box office. nevertheless, great fun, highly recommended. 8/10.

had reservation about watching part two! top gun is a movie icon, and usually part two comes out flat after watching a movie classic. i remember watching temple of doom after the classic raiders of the lost arc. i was wondering if seeing maverick would be deja vu again? well maverick starting out kind of woke. the odd white guy, the white jerk, over macho female character and fill in the blank other blank characters, (i thought oh no preachy non relatable movie characters) but maverick got out the tail spin with believable/likeable characters. maverick has believable characters, with pete being the test piolet push the envelope guy with personal demons. gooses son is a tribute and a crux of the story a younger mitchel character from the last movie. hangman is the new ice character. the gamer which make us understand the new skills of a modern military with the calming ebb and flow of the rest of the characters for the military machine. there is a recruiting part with all the new state of the art air craft, which mixes with a star wars story line. but un like star wars there is a few good plot twist with homages from the old top gun and a homage to iceman. i left maverick actually feeling good, with out having a woke or hollywood formulated movie hang over. well directed, written, and original script. 8 stars, best summer movie so far!

finally went and saw this latest long awaited installment of the "top gun" franchise, and i must say that "top gun: maverick" did not disappoint the scenes and camera work were thrilling as the film was fast paced and exciting and a thrill ride of high flying fun. i saw the original as a kid in 1986, and liked it, as many young men had tom cruise as their idol.

now after 30 years pete mitchell(in a standout and classic performance from tom cruise) returns as a top navy aviator and he's chosen to teach younger up and coming test pilots. the test is working with young rooster(miles teller) the son of pete's late friend. plus watching i got a throwback legendary feel seeing val kilmer and ed harris also jon hamm is a good supporting cast member, and jennifer connelly is just fine as pete's love interest. the flying scenes with jets are thrilling and stunning it has you pumped this "top gun" sequel was made well with passion and fun.

top gun is something that shaped a generation, but it was a pretty silly movie, from the premise to the plot, the characters and the love scenes, the dogfights and the navy terminology. top gun: maverick, on the other hand, is surgical. everything that can be problematic is removed, while the action is focused on the flying.

can we bring back kelly mcgillis? no. she is 9 years older than cruise, which makes her 65. so we'll go with connelly, who still looks stunning at 51. would it be weird to show maverick wooing a woman the way he did 36 years ago, following her into bathrooms and what not? of course. let us say they were already a thing from before, just estranged. could people get their panties in a twist because women are allowed to be pilots now? sure, so let's add a female pilot that does absolutely nothing the entire film except participate. same with some black folk. make one an admiral and the other a pilot and give them two minutes of screen time. can we show dogfight scenes like in the first movie, where everyone who knows anything about flying would laugh out loud? no. let's montage everything from short sequences showing maverick is the best of them all. should we name the enemy country who went "rogue" like they detached their territory from the earth and are trying to fly away? no. let's not call it iran in any way. and when we show a coordinate on a screen, let it make it the most neutral place in the world! not switzerland, but the pole of inaccessibility.

so instead of characterization, setup or any portrayal of an actual human being, it's a film made of significant cutouts who suggest what the story is, without an actual one. the plot is super silly, also, basically one of those "so crazy it might just work" ideas combined with the "old man who can do it better than the young'uns" concept and sprinkled with the star wars attack against the death star. but it works. it is entertaining, lacking any controversy, depth or moral. after feeling good for a second, you will forget the film ever existed.

and just so we can call it a sequel to a completely different film, let's call back cruise and kilmer (for a few minutes, too), use the same music, bring in the son of goose (who is somehow a rooster?) and use some of the same lines in top gun, so we can pump up the nostalgia. but it's not a sequel, only a color neutral reimagining of a similar concept, lacking the impact that the film had. and released now, when iran is not as much an enemy as russia and china are, it shows how much the world has changed in three years.

bottom line: it is worth watching both top gun films back to back just in order to feel how much things have changed (and how much they stayed the same). it's a well produced and executed film, but it has no real soul. entertaining, but without impact. i doubt young people will climb over each other to join the navy after this film.

as any avid cinephile will tell you, a film's original score or theme song has the power to ground that film into a classic. top gun from 1986 has this distinction, not just from making that film a classic, but because the theme song went on to be called top gun anthem. it starts with the synthesised but faint chime of a church bell, before the melody escalates into a crescendo of 80s instrumental rock music. as symbolic as it sounds, the church bell here is a dual tone for both grief and glory.

calling maverick a sequel would only be half-truth. from the moment you hear that synth church bell in the opening sequence, you feel like the last 30 odd years didn't happen. it even begins with a frame-by-frame recreation of the original film's iconic intro on the decks of an aircraft carrier. we see the silhouettes of navy personnel dispatching and receiving warplanes against a low-lit but vivid sky, followed by a familiar text caption explaining the us navy's weapons school programme. this sequence is more than just the cool beginning of top gun: maverick, this is the start of an instantly familiar feeling that will immerse you into nostalgia for over 80 percent of the film's running time.

making this umbilical connection to such a beloved film in the first few minutes, especially after 35 years, is both risky and rewarding at the same time. part of that nostalgia also includes flimsy one-liners and corny jokes among characters, but also a half-baked and implausible story. and part of that is an inside joke as to why pete "maverick" mitchell is still captain, while most of his colleagues are either top brass or have retired. only tom cruise can answer that question with the cocky recklessness but godlike flying skills of the legendary maverick. which is why maverick has to now train a bunch of crème de la crème navy pilots for a daring mission that is pure suicide. although the "enemy" country is never mentioned, encountering a mi-24 superhind and fifth generation migs during the mission tells us the objective is in ivan's backyard. but sending navy pilots without hardened combat experience in last generation f/a-18 hornets against the aforementioned enemy, in a mission impossible mission, is like taking a knife to a gun fight. implausible narrative silliness, but who cares, right?

then comes the remaining 20 percent with fresh content - grief and glory, and a lot of closure. one of the advantages of such a long gap after the first film, is that screenwriters can now fill in the blanks. one is the introduction of "rooster", son of "goose", who maverick lost to an accident in the first film. prepare for some emotive tantrums and chip-off-the-shoulder baggage between maverick and rooster (miles teller). the other is probably the most genuine, bitter-sweet, heart-breaking moment in the entire film and easily the best, and this is when maverick visits and old friend - iceman. i won't say anymore. glory is reserved for the last 30 odd minutes and it's a high octane adrenaline rush for the audience as well as maverick and his team. even if it's big bucks cgi, it just feels real. unlike recent blockbusters with mind-numbing visual effects and eye-popping camera angles (looking at you marvel movies), top gun: maverick has some of the best white-knuckle air combat displays ever seen in a film, and it all feels real. tom's cruising charisma does the rest. all you have to do is sit back, buckle up and enjoy your supersonic flight with 100 percent fan service.

say what you like about tom cruise the guy knows how to make film...wow

it's cheesy (maybe a bit too much) but the action sequences are outstanding. natural camera movements

just a great blockbuster movie - saving the cinema from possible doom.

i only watched the original "top gun" movie earlier this year, so my wait for this follow-up feature wasn't as long as it obviously was for its long-term fans.

i must admit that i enjoyed the original with its mix of high-flying thrills, clichéd characterisations and situations on the ground and loud rock music and given that "maverick" was pretty much more of the same, i'd have to say i enjoyed it equally as much.

tom cruise returns as our hero captain pete "maverick" mitchell still flying dangerous aeroplanes in this man's air force, to and beyond their limits, naturally cocking a snook at authority in the process, which is of course why he's still only a captain 36 years on as he's constantly reminded throughout the film. that is, until he's suddenly plucked to train this year's intake of young fliers to carry out a dangerous bombing mission to take out a uranium plant in an unnamed foreign country. of course, mav's first instinct is to aspire to lead the squadron himself but in this he's thwarted, at least for now, by his censorious new c. o. played by john hamm. worse yet, amongst the wannabe pilots is the son of his late lamented partner goose, handily called rooster, played by miles teller and it's no great surprise to witness the simmering tension between the two.

after numerous simulated training exercises with his young charges, maverick has to choose just the select crews who will go on the near suicidal mission. will mav get to fly on this, his proclaimed final flying mission, will he win the respect of his not-quite-adoring pupils, will he find love with jennifer connelly's old flame bar manager at the airbase and lastly will there be a big man-hug between him and rooster before the end?

well, you won't need a heat-seeking missile to direct you to how it all turns out, but it certainly does so in an exhilarating and highly entertaining fashion. bar one new lady gaga song over the end-titles, the soundtrack is very much retro-rock comprising the who, bowie, t rex and even foghat which makes you wonder who locked these prospective fighter-aces up with their dad's record collections.

anyway, there's lots of double-speak technical talk, amazing simulated flying stunts and as you'd expect, tear-jerking catch-ups and look-backs at iceman (a brave cameo by val kilmer) and goose, with the recreated "great balls of fire" wig-out by his son, under maverick's detached, baleful gaze.

cruise literally cruises through his part with his million dollar grin and glint never far away, the mostly young talent around him provide strong support and i liked connelly as the love interest.

never mind that the film makes the viewer complicit in another highly covert u. s. military operation and instead rejoice that nobody dies this time, at least not in action anyway.

somehow i suspect it won't be another 36 years before old mav flies into the great blue yonder again...

good fun. i thoroughly enjoyed it. tom cruise hasn't lost his touch at all! stunts were excellent, and the cast well put together!

catch this movie when you can!

i feel the need for speed - again... yep, some 36 years after the original 80s blockbuster, top gun gets a sequel, and "it's good, it's very good"!...

an absurdly ageless tom cruise (60?!) re-appears from his cryogenic chamber (no doubt sponsored by the church of scientology) as captain pete 'maverick' mitchell, this time heading back to top gun in order to train up a new batch of annoying, jingoistic ego-maniac fighter pilots for a mission impossible (doh) against the world's common -unnamed- enemy... and so we take flight once again to destroy some dastardly world destroying hidden nukes (with many updated nods to the original film, including music).

typically, the cruiser lights up the screen throughout, aptly co-piloted by an on-point supporting cast headed by lovely jennifer connelly, ed harris, val kilmer and stand-out miles teller as his old buddy goose's disgruntled son (you have to suspend the reality that he would be in his 40s now though!).

the real star of the show however are the spectacular non-cgi plane sequences, and there are plenty of them! it's a real rocket ride of adrenaline as the 2 hour runtime literally flys by and the need for mindless, nostalgic blockbuster popcorn munchers proudly rises like a super hornet in overdrive.

much like the first flick it's big, cheesy, over the top, full of improbabilities... and one helluva 'mach ten' fun ride. a refreshing and much needed change from the overplayed marvel-verse et al, top gun maverick is one summer blockbuster (and by far the biggest earner of the year) that has and will thrill film fans old and new...

so strap yourselves in, disengage brain and enjoy your long awaited flight back into the danger zone, you won't regret it.

i got my hopes up a bit too high when i saw it had an 8.6 on imdb. i'd put it at more of an 8.2, which is still a really good rating. overall, this paid homage to the first film and expanded on its themes in a more mature manner.

pete mitchell aka maverick goes from an ambitious, self-absorbed, flirtatious (well, he's still all of that)... but the point is he had more of a character arc than the first film. he wants to make peace with goose's son rooster (who acts towards maverick with hostility) and he needs to forgive himself and move on. he's torn between penny benjamin, who rekindles his motivation, and adm. simpson, who justifies an end to his career. miles teller's goose must forgive his father's friend's decision to delay his training and is influenced by phoenix and hangman (reminiscent of ice from the original). it's an adequate arc for both characters (but mainly maverick) to ground the aerial sequences. i was surprised how many non-aerial scenes i enjoyed. the bar scene, the iceman reunion, and pete's visit with penny all added emotional weight compared to the lackluster story of the original. from a plot perspective, the story and pacing maverick isn't dramatically different from the original: starting with a semi-perilous aerial scene, transitioning into numerous training scenes with a romantic side plot, and concluding with a combat scene. it's just the filmmaking for maverick was more successful in just about every way. the hans zimmer score immersed me and inspired me in a way i haven't felt since watching interstellar. it wasn't all electric guitar and rock music. the authenticity of the cinematography and vfx is undeniable. there are interior shots, exterior shots, extreme close-ups and pan-outs. the original didn't lack these qualities; but, due to the dialogue and the capabilities of modern technology, the action scenes were much easier to follow. the final half hour of the film really ramped up the vfx and suspense to a mission impossible level; and, i can't help but admit how fun it was to watch those scenes in the theatre. the ending was certainly feel-good (if not a bit cheesy) with maverick and goose coming home alive, reconciling with one another, and maverick going off with penny. the message of letting go of the past is nothing new in cinema; but, it was the center of a strong story aimed at completing pete mitchell's character arc from the first film in a satisfying manner. complex characters, a cohesive story, and some of the most immersive and suspenseful action scenes in recent times prove that maverick soars above the original.

tom cruise returns to the role that arguably put him on the cinematic (i would say '83's risky business got there first) map. looking like the ghost of tony scott (who directed the first film) & even in the opening title crawl we see don simpson's name (he was jerry bruckheimer's partner back in the day), who's been dead for more than 25 years, we appear to have never left the world of pete 'maverick' mitchell, still behind the stick as he's test piloting a new stealth fighter hoping to break that magic mach 10 speed barrier. no sooner does his superior, played by ed harris, steps foot on the base, we know maverick is up to his old tricks by breaking all the rules in order to win the day. deemed a success but a failure (he crashes the plane) he's demoted (sideways?), to return to his roots so to speak & become an elite fighter trainer where one of the cadets in his rank turns out to be his old wingman's (goose, anthony edwards) son, miles teller, who w/a number of others have been selected to run a treacherous mission to destroy a plant that has nuclear weapons in mother russia. tension brews during the training between cruise & teller (over cruise hindering his career's momentum in order to protect him) w/the outcome of the final mission never in doubt as cruise's determined pearly whites & ray banned facade assure us all along. never having been a fan of the original (remembering back in '86 watching it on home video muttering to myself 'i don't get it!"), but damn, this film does everything right when it was so easy to get wrong. bringing back val kilmer as iceman was definitely a step in the right direction even though he & cruise have only one scene together, his presence (& his real life hardships as a throat cancer survivor) looms in the background so large that if the film ended after he & cruise's tete a tete, i would've been satisfied but even the mission itself is a popper (even though the final movements might be too much icing on the cake).

hollywood, take notes, this is how you "remake" a classic movie for modern audiences, this is how you diversify your casts, this how you tell your old audiences to be aware of how time has changed, this is how you should do it!

classic yet modern, sad yet hopeful, top gun: maverick proves that the old 80's movie formula still works in the middle of woke ideology messaging in the modern western entertainment. in the middle of fresh and young faces, cruise almost does not waste his time telling the young kids he's still the boss around here. though i have to say that by coating it with the vibe of his mission impossible series, i'm afraid his action flicks for years to come would bring nothing new to the table. still, i hope for dead reckoning part one and part two, he'd deliver something special as a love letter to long-time fans the way this movie does, or the way infinity war and endgame did for mcu fans.
