in these rather somber and worrying times, what better than to resurrect a hit formula from the 1980s? in fact, this 'sequel' to one of that decades biggest hits outdoes its predecessor massively in every respect, however, it still feels oddly stuck in that previous and perhaps more reliable era. the plus points here are the aerial sequences, which are stunningly well done, a coherent plot and a good cast, including tom cruise as good as before, and its also a film that doesn't take itself too seriously. yes, there are some obvious cliches, but this is solid big screen feel good entertainment.

top gun: maverick is the perfect popcorn movie. suspend your disbelief, don't expect any deep meaning and just have a good time.

virtually nothing in this movie would happen in the real world. maverick couldn't wreck an experimental plane and walk away from it. a critical, secret mission wouldn't be thrown together in three weeks, nor put in the hands of an unpredictable rogue pilot (no matter who his protecting admiral is). he'd never get away with stealing a jet fighter (twice). he wouldn't survive a crash in enemy territory, much less defeat far advanced fighters to make it home. and so on, and so on. but who cares? it's fun.

production and acting are about what you'd expect. brilliant visuals and effects. lots of call-backs to the original (and a star wars homage). tom cruise is tom cruise, with all his ramped up charm and bravado.

this was a tough job for the whole crew. the original top gun is iconic for a lot of people born between 1970 and 1990, maybe even beyond!

honestly, i have never met a person that has watched the original and didn't like it.

with tony scott's passing this sequel seemed like it would never get done, but step in joseph kosinski who had a relationship already with cruise, who didn't want to do the movie. i could definitely see why cruise signed up for this.

yes, the movie isn't perfect. yes, the plot is a bit thin and there isn't a lot of (if any) character or plot twists, but the executions was something else.

cruise steps into the maverick skin like he's never left it. absolutely perfect here.

the new roster of pilots aren't groundbreaking but some strong performances there and overall group chemistry pull it through.

lots of practical effects and real flight shots of the actors actually flying in jets (not piloting, naturally).

a third act that was straight out of a bond movie also spiced things up a bit.

i really do hope they go on and make more movies like this one in terms of the production and using cgi only when absolutely necessary.

don't get me wrong, i am not advocating they continue reviving old franchises for sequel/prequels, but more make original movies set in these times and use more real props and locations.

over the last 20 years cgi has become so so overly-used that some movies border on computer games, and as much as people don't want to admit it, it still doesn't look close to real!

big thumbs up for the crew involved in top gun: maverick and go see it in the cinema, you won't be be disappointed.

the movie is done right on so many levels and i can tell the huge effort put into it. the skill put into work is outstanding - visuals, sound, directing and acting. the movie follows a similar formula as the first even if obviously up to modern day and age. whoever did tom cruise's make up deserves a special award. that man does look 40 at most. the movie is really enjoyable and the only downside is that is actually quite predictable.

they knew just how to dial up or dial down the throwbacks (leaning into soundtrack, but actually helping us understand the mission this time). they knew just when to dial up or down the realism (showing hyper-accurate flight sequences initially before releasing all pretense of feasibility over the last third). and perhaps most importantly, they knew when to let cruise shine and when to make this ensemble (hamm, teller, connelly) the star. nobody's life will be changed because they finally released another top gun movie, but that doesn't stop it from be an absolutely perfect summer blockbuster.

in 1996, a disgruntled brigadier general hummel and a group of marines took over alcatraz prison the hopes of forcing the government to pay reparations for men he lost lasering targets during operation desert storm. 25 years later and this time ed harris is a rear admiral, who believes maverick is a relic, which considering the original top gun was released 10 years before the rock would seem likely.

the main bulk of the film is about the same mission hummel was doing in desert storm, and constructing and training a team to carry out that objective. yes, compared to the original film, it's as contrived as luke skywalkers attack on the death star, but part of the contrivance is to provide some wonderful flying shots. tom cruise has gone all out on providing aerial action, and there's plenty of reports regarding the boot camp training he put the other actors through to give the viewer the sensation of being there. and it helps that sony developed imax compatible cameras small enough they could fit six in a cockpit. watching on a big screen, with a full dolby atmos setup - another suitably stirring soundtrack from hans zimmer - is a joy.

i think the only disappointment was how much the peril was telegraphed. the set piece scenes flowed beautifully, but predictably, though that was to be expected going in.

a great cast, fantastic performance's and a story you can buy into top gun maverick is not just a fanboys dream. there's a lot of great writing and 30+ years after the original the team has done a fantastic job of creating a seamless follow on. plenty of great camera work and music makes this a modern day equivalent of the original classic. if you were worried that the fa18 could never surpass the legendary tomcat you won't be disappointed. certainly worth paying the extra and watching this on the big screen. 10/10.

top gun: maverick is a flawed improvement. its story is straightforward, which works. maverick has one last mission, his relationship with goose's son is complex, and his romance has baggage. none of this is inventive, but it's enough to fuel the climax. however, top gun: maverick changes paths and loses steam. a dramatic peak is nicely set up, yet the film backtracks on that, introducing a new layer to the mission. this second climax is action-packed, but also fatiguing and muddied. had top gun: maverick kept its bittersweet climax, it would've been more meaningful. instead, its emotional mediocrity feels like a missed opportunity.

meanwhile, top gun: maverick has solid filmmaking. first, visuals are polished (utilizing focus, lighting, and mounts), acting meets the material, and the tone is clear. the soundtrack balances nostalgia, and the production is authentic. plus, the editing employs montages, dissolves, and energetic action. next, the sound design mirrors emotions, using symbolic echoes, silence, and j-cuts. finally, the effects are the star of top gun: maverick because its stunts are impossibly real. overall, top gun: maverick advances its drama and thrills, but still lacks a core message. unfortunately, without a conscious theme, it feels like war glorification.

top gun: maverick (2022) -

they might have been able to sell this as a separate film, but i think that the existence of its predecessor'top gun' (1986) was probably necessary to make this one truly work and to give it some awesome marketing power. with that said, this was certainly the better of the two films in the franchise.

yes, it was more of the same and pretty darn predictable, but i enjoyed it a lot more.

i really hadn't expected to like it, because having rewatched the first film recently i found that i couldn't understand why i had ever liked that one at all.

what i could appreciate about this film was the maturity of the story in comparison and tom cruise's improved performance as the titular character. it really helped that maverick was more grown up too.

i always seem to point it out in my reviews of his films, but the new calmer, 21st century version of tom has far more going for him than any of his younger 1980's castings. in this film he returned to one of those previous shouty man roles, but with a more easy disposition and he had definitely improved with age, especially physically in my opinion, woof-woof, hubba-hubba.

the charm of maverick was easier to see and so it made sense that jennifer connelly, who was just enough in the part of penny would realise that he wasn't the same as he had been before. she wasn't playing kelly mcgillis' part from "tg", but another lover from an occasion in the interim. i liked the fact that they didn't fixate on this romance, but instead used it as a way for him to have at least someone on his side, as no one was particularly keen to learn flying and tactics from such a "maverick".

the admiral beau "cyclone" simpson, played by jon hamm, definitely needed persuading of the benefits of tom's rogue pilot ways, but he wasn't such an over the top hard ass that he was unbelievable or stereotypical and he was a very sexy beast too.

playing the part of mav's old wingman goose's (anthony edwards) son "rooster" was miles teller. i did feel that he had the right look for it and he seemed to have taken on some of the other actors mannerisms too, especially towards the end of the film.

it hadn't necessarily endeared me to him however, because he was still miles teller and i was frustrated that his character still held a grudge about his father's death, even though he was only about 3 at the time. and the backchat between him and mav was quite cheesy at times.

for me there is just something so inherently unlikeable about miles and the characters he plays. maybe i'll meet him one day and he will show me that i'm wrong about him, but while i could appreciate how he played rooster and his outstanding delivery of andrew in 'whiplash' (2014) too, both characters are essentially unpleasant to start with, semi-underdogs or not. i will say that he did grow on me by the end, but i will need to see something more than his 'mr fantastic'* to truly warm to him.

initially i'd thought that the obnoxious machismo still needed calming down a tad, but after a while it seemed to be more realistic and less about banging on their chests and pissing contests, although i did like seeing all of their gorgeous glistening, sweaty pectorals on the beach in an homage to the volleyball scene from the 1986 instalment. and actually that wasn't the only example where they repeated certain scenes and even specific shots from that one, but it was all done in a way that was kind of clever and enjoyable, definitely with an eye for the fans that would appreciate the nods they had made.

in fact there were a lot of moments that could have been straight out of george lucas' 'star wars' (1977) saga too, because, although it wasn't the only bit or even dialogue that they seemed to steal from that film, the bombing run scene was almost as if they had extended the drama of the last 30 minutes of it and set it in a real world situation. i thought that made it a more interesting finale than i'd got from "tg" though and there was an extra feeling of threat. i certainly felt the tension of what they were going through, possibly because i was more interested in the characters this time, due to better acting performances, or because the directors and writers had done their job well in the first place, probably both.

i was genuinely emotional by the end of the film, but i was having withdrawals from years of taking anti-depressants at the time, which could have been a factor of that too.

i had expected more of the same and that was essentially what i got, but this one certainly had more polish to it, mostly because of tom's more mature performance and i would imagine that he had a lot more say in how things were done this time around too.

it was actually a very appropriate sequel and one that worked better for the distance inbetween, a more grown up storyline, structure and better acting. obviously it also had an interesting display of aerial acrobatics and what could be done, with the right pilots, akin to 'the red arrows' i suppose. that wasn't something i had remembered from the original and i hate to keep referring back to that one, but that was always going to be the case from any film critic, even barry norman would find it hard not to at least reference the og tg.

unlike that first one, i would definitely sit down to watch this one again. it lost points for not being the most original storyline, but gained some for doing it so well.

it is easy to be enthusiastic, nay, rapturous about top gun: maverick. the feel-good hollywood story of the summer; top gun 2 is the first movie in a long time to feel like a proudly american cinematic spectacular. its major box office success and public popularity is impossible to root against. the celebratory energy of top gun: maverick will enrapture plenty. but even accounting for tom cruise, jerry bruckheimer, and director joseph kosinski's shrewd spell-the influx of timing and properly placed ambition, giving a starved audience the kind of entertainment they needed-top gun: maverick is still a super-charged rush of fresh air; a summer blockbuster both jaw-droppingly thrilling and emotionally fulfilling.

maverick doesn't rewrite the "legacy sequel" rules. 36 years after top gun, tom cruise's pete "maverick" mitchell has graduated from hotshot young stud to seasoned legend. brass wants him to retire from flying and train the next generation, for there is a real-world mission to an unnamed place against an unnamed enemy that must be carried out. it's a thin premise, but not any more so than the original movie. in fact, maverick is very much the same story as top gun. miles teller plays rooster, son of goose, the maverick proxy. he competes with a handful of others for something like the top gun prize, as they train for the upcoming mission. the movie's first half is basically a remake, a criticism we've heard before of certain legacy sequels. you get the same action beats and the same emotional flavors, repackaged with varying levels of success.

where this movie really starts to cook is in the second half, when the money, talent, and ambition truly hits the screen. you expect the aerial filming technology to improve in the three decades since tony scott's impressive outing, and maverick's second half opens up those possibilities. the training runs work out similarly for both films, with some magnificent real-life aerial footage mixed with ubiquitous cockpit close-ups. maverick does it without the clunky blue screen gimbals, but that doesn't make its scenes discernibly better. no, it's the dogfights where the new film pulls ahead. on a gigantic screen, with thunderous sound, maverick reaches action highs that few others have ever reached. i can't say what these filmmakers did, or how they did it, but it sure as hell looks like cruise, teller and the rest are actually flying these machines, dodging missiles, and pulling heavy gs. the sustained tension and endless narrow escapes of the final chunk of the movie signify the type of action that really thrills. the kind that fixes your eyes to the screen and juices you up instead of numbing your senses.

don't discount the human factor, though. maverick isn't a lesson on character writing by any means, but it does have a charming collection of pilots, led by cruise and teller. tom cruise leverages his stardom without coming off as vain. he's fun. a bit of an underdog, where someone else might have seemed too-good-to-be-real. in the sky and in his relationship with jennifer connelly's penny, you want him to make it out alright. miles teller is the other important cog, heading the new crew. the breakout shot has been eluding teller since his explosion onto the scene in whiplash, but with top gun: maverick, he may have finally found that star-making role. he's charismatic and emotionally well-shaded. when he's in the cockpit, you're thinking about more than just the plane. the movie hits some easy emotional targets (how hard is it to feel choked up by a touching tribute to val kilmer?), but that's a great deal more than you can say for other movies of this type.

if top gun 2 isn't quite the movie its predecessor is, it may only come from tony scott's absence. his original film is the sexier movie; more mature, more confident, and better looking. but maverick is the thrill-seeker's choice. a feature-length theme park ride, complete with pre-ride set-up and fist-pumping finale. people will wax hyperbolic about top gun: maverick, and with good reason. it's a mammoth action spectacle involving human beings, on a universe we recognize, done (mostly) for real. i don't think that necessarily makes it a great film, but it does make it worth seeing in a movie theater. an experience like this one is what those big screens are made for.

always thought the original top gun (1986) was a wonderful coming of age story about a young fighter pilot securing his manhood by conquering his past so that he can soar off through the danger zone into the future! director tony scott skillfully shoe-horned you into the cockpit with the cocky hot dog aviator pete mitchell so that you could get a tense grip on his misgivings and feel his need for speed. there was a great camaraderie between the students in the top gun class and later in scenes at the bar or on the beach. the antics of tom 'iceman' kazansky as played by val kilmer and anthony edwards as nick 'goose' bradshaw come particularly to mind as memorable. kelly mcgillis as astrophysicist charlotte 'charlie' blackwood is also easy enough on the eyes so that you don't lose that 'lovin' feelin'.

flash-forward then thirty-six years to now. captain pete mitchell is still his authority defying self even though he has been maneuvered into instructing and prepping a group of top gun graduates for what appears to be an impossible mission. yeah, i know, i get the reference, too. the influence of tom 'iceman' kazansky, now an admiral in charge of the u. s. pacific fleet, swoops in to save maverick's bacon on more than one occasion when he's in conflict with his superiors over flight strategy and aerial tactics. but the mere fact that mitchell can walk his talk, or should i say fly past their reasonably assessed objections, proves to be a winning point in more than a couple of suspenseful encounters.

this film also makes important points about instructing and teaching as its principal actors soar beyond the horizon. sometimes the best instructors and teachers do not teach so much what they know as what they are. the mission on paper that maverick prepares his top gun graduates for appears logically undoable. the look of consternation on their faces all say the same thing, such as '-so why are we even talking about this?!'. but maverick is able to demonstrate through his exceptional flying ability during an unauthorized test run that what they thought was impossible and undoable, is in fact barely possible and doable. all that is left for the top gun graduates is to duplicate his energy frequency as team leader. this is something that both einstein and jomo kenyatta have spoken about albeit from different cultural perspectives, but i am sure would heartily approve. jaime escalante's assertion that students will perform up to the level of the teacher's expectation also comes to mind. but there is no doubt that maverick's expectations of his crew of pilots perhaps raises the bar to places no man or woman has gone before in a cockpit.

while the technical wizardry is dazzling and more than confirms the notion that cinema has more to do with its ancient ancestor the circus than the theater, this film also scores a few points in the human dimension with its characters. maverick's rekindling of his romance with jennifer connelly as penny benjamin and his poignant reunion with val kilmer as now admiral tom 'iceman' kazansky are particularly elegiac. but his scrambling on the run in and out of harms way with pilot bradley 'rooster' bradshaw as played by miles teller, resentful son of the late nick 'goose' bradshaw in a kind of hastily improvised surrogate father and son relationship keeps the narrative justly going at breakneck speed. this mixture of an enlarged human interaction between the characters with state of the art visual and aerial effects and stunts is what makes this sequel an improvement on the original.

where i would qualify my praise for this film has to do with the confrontation of this team of aces with a nearly faceless enemy whom we never get to see grappling with the effects and aftermath of its high-tech victimization. this is something that i groused about regarding pulp fiction (1994) and the wolf of wall street (2013), and is even an issue that can be raised obliquely about the birdman of alcatraz (1962). but many would simply regard this as nitpicking, as these three films certainly have won the love of its audiences around the world. pete mitchell, aka maverick, an engaging boy-man one notch above a comic book hero as the poster airily suggests, may one day have a yeager-like catch with his son or not. but tom cruise showed the guts to play this character at warp speed, warts and all, and who knows that one day he might take penny up in his mustang only to barely hear her declare that she's pregnant with his child!

stranger things have been known to happen in the danger zone as i am sure you have witnessed.

the sequel is very similar to the 1986 flick in that it has the same strengths & weaknesses, however with the welcome difference in that its strengths are even better executed, and go on for longer...while its weaknesses are less jarring, and shorter!

the personal-drama and camaraderie stuff is standard predictable fare we've seen a thousand times in other movies. quietly effective at best, eye-rollingly simple at worst. it does pay to have seen the first top gun, to at least appreciate the more effective elements.

now on to the good stuff, and the main reason we all watch this movie: the flight action! and it's even better than the first film. it's easier to follow, takes up more runtime, feels ambitious, well-shot & great sound. the main mission is clearly described & understood, so we really feel the tension as the team attempt it! the only negative i have is the usual for modern action films: the editor cuts too quick, we have hundreds of great shots but they're barely a second long...not enough time to really saviour the grand achievements of the camera crew.

the plot is good, and it ends well. overall 8/10, superior to the 6/10 for 1986's top gun.

i had little interests in seeing this movie at first. given the trailer, what i thought was going to happen, and the over-saturation of sequels/remakes, it seemed like a recipe for disaster. i am so glad to say that i was wrong. tom cruise still has the same charm as maverick along with all the other actors, the story was engaging and flowed smoothly, and the movie had the right amount of tension that never broke and maintained it to the end. few things did keep me from giving the movie a 10, but i'll let you see it to figure out why. all in all, a very good movie that gives a refreshing sense of pride in the usa and it's military (which can be good from time to time).

i was a big top gun fan (as was mostly everyone i knew) back in the late 80's and early 90's. it was the highest grossing movie of 1986 for a reason. so i was very excited to finally get a chance to see this sequel a day earlier than the advertised release date. we went at the very first matinee and everyone in the theatre enjoyed it. it was fun and triggered lots of chuckles and laughs with subtle humor.

i cried at probably at least five or six scenes, whether from nostalgia, heavy hearted references to either character deaths or character relationships, or the romance scenes. in addition to the humor and sad scenes, there was also some good drama and intense jet fighter sequences. the director and writers blended the concept of a difficult fighter jet mission with fun training scenes, romance, and callbacks to the original.

i'm not going to lie- this is a good movie. i'm not exaggerating that i barely blinked during the entire run time of 2 hours and 10 minutes, with which most of the time when i wasn't being tear-jerked, i had a silly grin on my face or was chuckling at the subtle humor. however, i will say that if i wasn't a big fan of the first one, i might not have liked it as much as i did. that's because it was a great as a fan of the first one to have so many references to anything in part one.

the ending was good, but it could have been even better, even though it was intense enough to have me sweating a little. but one of the biggest drawbacks of top gun 2 is also one of its strengths, in my opinion, in a way. i got the impression that ultimately this is a movie that is more made for kids and teens than adults, and what that means is that the content is mostly light and shies away from any kind of violence or sexuality, which would have made it feel more mature and realistic. for example, in the original top gun, it has heavy profanity, really intense romance and sex for a pg movie, a pilot dies depicted with a face covered in blood after ejecting, and the dialogue by actors like tom skeritt make the stakes seem higher and more realistic: "what we do up there is dangerous". maverick's dad's fate in vietnam is also discussed to paint a realistic picture of the stakes. overall, it just felt more gritty, whereas "top gun maverick" keeps it ultra "clean" considering the dangers of flying and the explicit nature of locker room talk and sexuality.

what this means is you get a sequel movie that is much more appropriate for teens and kids than adults, yet being an adult i kind of wish the stakes would have felt as heavy as they could have been. it would have been sadder, but it also would've been more mature and realistic. it is what it is. it's still a good movie, but it could have been better.

i'm glad that i saw it early. as a nostalgic, emotional, fun summer popcorn movie, it was a blast, but if you're expecting a best pic contender or something remarkably original and profound, unfortunately the writers and directors "had the shot, but refused to fire it", and for that the movie comes up a bit short in cliches, cheese, and yes even lacking believability at key moments. i think there was an oscar-contender somewhere in this story, but the creators of it decided to go another direction, more into a "popcorn" and feel-good movie of the summer. that's fine and i don't blame them since the target audience was clearly younger kids, which makes it a nice, wholesome movie for a change.

jennifer connelly, despite a small supporting role, was the key to this movie. other than cruise, who does have a few stumbling moments at times, her confident experience as an actor makes every look she gives and line she says add credibility to what is an otherwise rather superficial script for supporting actors. the other good role that stands out is val kilmer's pleasantly surprising (and funny at times) reappearance as admiral iceman. then, teller does a pretty impressive job as goose's kid.

at the end of the day, "top gun maverick" succeeds and soars as a nostalgic, deeply emotional surprise triumphant action flick, with flight battle scenes so intense it'll make you sweat in your seat, while it also crashes into some of the mountainous cliches that have been built and established by hollywood throughout the years. so grab a seat and some popcorn and take a trip back to the 80s and 90s, a much simpler time, with some updated special effects and tech upgrades.

the structure in this first moment is very similar to that seen in "top gun: indomitable aces". even the instructor's arrival is the same: maverick stands before the students exactly as charlie (kelly mcgillis) did almost four decades earlier. so will the dynamics between the members of this cutting-edge school. if before the rivalry was between maverick and iceman (val kilmer, responsible for one of the most exciting passages in the new film), those who now take on these positions are rooster (miles teller, revealing an interesting dramatic potential) and hangman (glen powell, showing with charisma goes beyond an attractive print). but times are different, and if in the 1980s all pilots were white men, now we have on the teaching benches a black man (jay ellis), a latino (danny ramirez), an oriental (manny jacinto) and even a woman (monica barbarian). it is regrettable, however, that the film is not interested in them, as they only serve to create scenery, however, this is a type of "inclusion" that occurs naturally and not forcedly, such as a change of profile and, mainly, ethnicities of classic characters to please the fervent political militancy of modern-day social networks, which occurs mainly in comic book adaptations. the focus, after all, is on the protagonists - but not just them. and this is where "maverick" begins to differentiate itself from the original.

instead of subverting what was already known from "top gun" or revisiting this universe with a critical eye, the sequel is more interested in reliving a moment that was so significant for action cinema. knowing that fans of the franchise will return to the cinemas looking for the same adrenaline with touches of humor and romance, the sequel has no shame in recreating entire scenes from the original production. from the aforementioned epic opening to the repetition of the chords of the memorable "danger zone" theme, the sequel proposes constant rhymes with the original - to the point that even a new character like penny benjamin (jennifer connelly) is, in fact, a name mentioned briefly in the original feature.

these parallels reach a deeper level, placing the protagonist back on the fringes of the system. more than 30 years later, maverick continues to have problems with authority in both his professional and personal life, a theme marked by constant reminders that he remains stuck in the rank of captain, even though he has every opportunity to evolve and reach the highest positions in the northern navy. -american. it is at this point that the continuation finds its reason for being. of course, pete could have evolved and grown - professionally and mentally - like everyone in his class did, but then who would be left to roll up their sleeves and teach the new generation the ropes? a question that fits with the space that the franchise has come to occupy in the history of action films. while some of its peers have sought to update themselves to keep up with the public's changing sensibilities through drama, social commentary or even self-parody, "top gun" refuses to change. and he doesn't do this as if he were saying that the past is better and the world should have stopped there - on the contrary, the production takes into account the world that surrounds it today. but this modernity is used to boost the rescue of an experience that only its fast planes and obstinate pilots could provide to the public. of course, this refusal brings openly corny moments, like when pilots prefer to have relationship discussions aboard machines that cost billions. however, the production does not try to justify this tackiness, which is also part of the identity carved out in the 1986 film.

this conversation between the script and the context in which "top gun: maverick" is set is the film's greatest asset. this plot that talks about freeing yourself from the bonds of the past to evolve is something that dialogues both with the characters and with the moment in cinema itself, and all of this makes this revival a pearl in the midst of a lazy nostalgic invasion that invades the movie theater. this is because "maverick" manages to tie up the ends left in "top gun" very well to create completely new situations that make room for both new and old characters to grow. so, in the same way that we have a new generation of pilots understanding that the old guard still has a lot to offer, we have this veteran pilot realizing that he has less and less space in this world and that it is necessary to let the newcomers fly for good. for this reason, it makes a lot of sense that the new film carries the codename "maverick" in its title. this hero's journey to accept his role in this new world, leaving the past where it deserves to stay, is the same as the film itself, which realizes that a revival is not just repeating the structure of the original features, but making space for new ones. names occupy that space. of course, compared to the first film, a lot will sound familiar. the patriotic tone is still there - although less pronounced -, as are some 1980s mannerisms. how long has it been since you see the opening credits of a film, with a music video? that's why everything is in maverick's dna.

but none of this is the essence of the film. there are small references and homages inserted organically or even in a more comical way, but they do not summarize what the new film is. the american football game during sunset on the beach is as cheesy as it was 36 years ago, but it's just a joke amidst what really matters in the plot. the core is about moving forward and leaving some things behind - like nostalgia itself. this becomes very clear when we see pete "maverick" mitchell himself, who has been trapped in this past for almost 40 years. he may be stagnant as a captain, when he could have a much more brilliant career, or even in this relationship of mourning and guilt over goose's death back there. and the character's entire journey is not just returning to the top gun academy to train a new generation of pilots to participate in an apparently suicidal mission, but understanding that it is no longer possible to live in that past. and that goes for both him and the cinema itself.

this is very well punctuated in two moments. the first one is when pete is in the bar with all the younger drivers and ends up being kicked out of the place for not being able to pay his bill. outside, he watches a mirror of a scene from the first film, with rooster (miles teller) doing the same piano performance his father did so many years ago. but this time, tom cruise is on the outside and realizes how much space he no longer has in that world. this scene reinforces the second great moment of "top gun: maverick", when the protagonist goes to the house of admiral tom "iceman" kazansky. in addition to being a very emotional moment due to val kilmer's condition, it makes it very clear what the central message behind the entire plot is: letting go of the past. and the script is very happy and competent in also assimilating the message. after all, at the same time that he resolves mitchell's issue with his own past, he uses the same issue to evolve the new characters, giving space for this new generation of actors to shine. this is the case with teller himself, who delivers a very interesting and well-developed rooster. he is this young pilot with a lot of potential, but who is limited by living in the shadow of his own father's death, in the same way that his relationship with mitchell is troubled by things the hero did in the past - also motivated by this attachment to what it's already gone. thus, both generations need to learn, in their own way, to move forward.

at this point, it is important to highlight that even though it enjoys the legacy left by tony scott's film, the production stands out by refining its qualities so that the show becomes even more complete. firstly, the big mission is established right at the beginning and its great risks make the challenge palpable and rewarding. a danger that also sets the tone of gravity for the new story. while the first brought death as a sudden and unpredictable event, the second leaves its shadow in the air from the first scene, which makes each flight have an extra dose of tension. especially when maverick's big arc includes a reckoning with the past, embodied in pilot rooster (miles teller). a major focus of the production, the duo's relationship is one of the emotional anchors of the story, which brings a new conflict for the protagonist. even though pete refuses to change, he is now the responsible adult, a role that brings internal and external conflicts that take top gun: maverick beyond the shadow of the original.

this gives joseph kosinski's ("oblivion") direction the chance to use every cinematic technique honed since the '80s to film stunning aerial action sequences. if "top gun" did an excellent job of bringing exciting training and combat to life, "maverick" goes further and uses technology and the commitment of a cast that even underwent aviation training to expand the possibilities of what can be put into screen.

"top gun: maverick" is one of those must-see cinematic experiences that reminds us of the practical and sophisticated magic of the seventh art. filmmaker joseph kosinski creates his own visual narrative with dances in blue and mountains, breathtaking aerial combat and the sensorial intensity of what it is like to fly top gun fighters. in the midst of plots that constantly seek to adapt to the sensitivity of current generations, who go as far as to demonize films, accusing them of being "full of testosterone" as if this were something wrong and prohibited for today's cinema, " top gun: maverick" celebrates the cliché and an old school way of making cinema, with an astonishing quality, and its box office, which surpassed the billion mark worldwide, is proof that the public wants, above all, a good story, not political militancy.

maverick's hype is well earned. i'm glad i watched the original first, despite really not enjoying it, because otherwise so much of maverick's nods would've been completely lost on me, but maverick stands in its own right as a solid action movie. this is some of the best dogfighting ever caught on camera. the authenticity of every shot is through the roof and goes a long way to really selling the intensity. top gun sought to put the audience in the cockpit with the pilots, maverick actually does while also capturing some breathtaking stuntwork at the same time. they could've built a mock cockpit in a studio in front of a green screen and filmed the actors normally and cgi'd the planes in the sky, but then they'd be missing the real effect of those gs on the actors faces, they'd be missing the palpability of flight at those speeds, they'd be missing all the little imperfections impossible to recreate. tom cruise deserves all the praise for this movie's monumental success, financially, critically, and artistically. he offers that which action movies have been sorely lacking for decades - authenticity. while i'm not quite at the point where i'd put it on the same pedestal as fallout or fury road, it definitely has a strong claim. i give top gun: maverick an edge-of-your-seat 8/10. this is definitely a movie i could see myself rewatching before the end of the year.

the movie is a worthy sequel to the 1986 original, it pushes all the right emotional buttons and occasionally brought a lump to my throat. i like the film and would see it again.

but while the flying scenes are thrilling, you could not help get the feeling that something is being rushed or missed here.

the following, which appears elsewhere but is likely to be poorly shared, explains it all:

"while very entertaining to watch, there were several issues with the way the mission was planned and executed that would likely have played out very differently in real life.

in the film, maverick assesses the operational problem based on a quick survey of some photos and determines the method for destroying the target almost instantly. in real life, an entire cell of joint planners would analyze the problem for days if not weeks and come up with multiple courses of action that could achieve the goal, and the decider for a target such as this would probably be the president (since the enemy is very clearly supposed to be iran).

maverick airily assumes away the stealth capability of the f-35 (as well as air force assets such as the b-2), and immediately assesses the job can only be done by f/a-18s for reasons unexplained. there is no discussion of using electronic warfare aircraft and/or cyber attack to shut down or at least hinder the enemy's integrated air defense system.

the navy uses cruise missiles to strike an enemy airfield to keep additional enemy fighters from taking off but does not seem to consider striking the enemy surface-to-air missile systems, radars, and command-and-control nodes by the same method. there is no combat air patrol (cap) of f-35s to engage enemy fighters and protect the strike aircraft on egress from the target (even if we agree with the basic assumption that f/a-18s were necessary for the strike, f-35s, not more f/a-18s would be the clear choice for the cap).

there is no reason why the strike aircraft would be loaded exclusively with flare countermeasures instead of chaff when the threat was clearly understood to be radar-guided weapons.

finally, the strike aircraft were loaded out with laser-guided bombs requiring a diving delivery, high-g pulloff, and spotting of the target with a laser from the wingman; gps-guided munitions could have hit the target with a higher probability of success and lower-risk level delivery over the target.

all of the above issues added more drama and action onscreen but also severely eroded the military realism."

tom cruise is getting on now. he looks fit and has looked after himself but like me, now at the same age, he needs to become more of an actor than an action star.

the question is asked, early in the movie, by cain, played by ed harris, why he is still a captain and not an admiral. it is the most critical question of the movie. ed harris must be way past military retirement age himself.

it turns out that maverick is a test pilot. still taking risks that should have killed him years before. defying all the rules hollywood style. this is a tale of miracles throughout.

the problem of a sequel more than 30 years in the making is how to reference the old movie. there will be two audiences. one that saw the original, bought the vhs tape, maybe even watched on tv. the other is the younger audience that never saw or remembered the original.

the callback was the subplot of being returned to top gun by iceman. played by val killmer and both showing and acting his age. killmer is an admiral and has progressed while cruise is determined to keep his boyish charm.

the tension in the new generation is rooster. the son of his wingman that died in the original movie. flashbacks follow. the son is even wearing his father's 1980s moustache. it seems out of place and distracting.

your alternative was just to enjoy the action sequences. they were fun and thrilling. once sitting in the plane with maverick and his team you could forgive most of the subplot and the mustache. enjoy the flying - which is what you came for anyway.

love or hate tom cruise, you must admire his efforts to heighten the authenticity of paramount pictures' long-awaited sequel "top gun: maverick," co-starring val kilmer, ed harris, and miles teller. cruise stands front and center for making "maverick" not only entertaining but also as realistic as possible. for example, when the pilots are in the cockpit, the actors and the actresses are actually airborne! they're riding in the rear seat, typically occupied by the radar intercept officer (rio), while an actual naval aviator flies the supersonic boeing f/a-18 super hornet. the cast weather genuine g-forces. ultimately, whether or not you enjoy "top gun: maverick," the movie serves as both a triumphant naval recruiting endeavor as well as an example that touts the navy's combat capability. primarily a mission-oriented actioneer with minimal comic relief, "top gun: maverick" depicts intrepid navy aviators dispatched to obliterate a target which poses a threat to world security. incidentally, paramount pictures never reveal the identity of the "rogue" adversary whose uranium enrichment plant is the target. nevertheless, the signs are unmistakable that the enemy is iranian since they're the only country which still flies f-14 fighters. pay close attention to the hopelessly, far-fetched "maverick" finale if you've any doubts.

in his informative slate. com article, "a quite serious military analysis of top gun: maverick's tactics," aviation expert fred kaplan ridicules "the whole thing" as "crazy." according to kaplan, "f/a-18s don't have the range to pull off this stunt, especially at fuel-draining high speeds. but more than that, it would have been much easier simply to send a couple of b-2 bombers at very high altitude-beyond the reach of the enemy's surface-to-air missiles-and fire a handful of gps-guided smart bombs. or if there was a chance the sams could shoot down a b-2, their radars could be blinded or tricked in a cyberattack." alas, armchair aviators need not feel cheated. nobody should confuse hollywood heroics with real-life heroism. basically, kaplan's sensible scenario wouldn't have drummed up much drama. audiences want to ride the edge of their seats while the heroes risk their necks. this is where the gee-whiz forces of adventurous storytelling come into focus! cruise, kosinski, and oscar-winning lenser claudio miranda of "life of pi" (2012) deserve kudos for hurling us headlong into the skies for a tumultuous rollercoaster ride of a lifetime! the only thing more sizzling than real life is spectacular storytelling, and "maverick" keeps its audiences clinging to a wing and a prayer throughout its' brisk 131-minutes of pg-13 rated havoc!

insubordinate navy captain pete mitchell (tom cruise) is the only aviator qualified to train the best pilots for the rigors they'll encounter on this critical mission. admiral tom 'iceman' kazansky (val kilmer of "true romance") runs interference for mitchell. were it not for 'iceman,' mitchell would not have been ordered back to top gun. one of mitchell's contentious superiors, rear admiral chester 'hammer' cain (ed harris of "appaloosa") roasts him not only for his aerial antics but also for his failure to wrangle a promotion. irritably, cain complains, "thirty-plus years of service! combat medals! citations! only man to shoot down three enemy planes in the last 40 years! yet you can't get a promotion, you won't retire, and despite your best efforts, you refuse to die! you should be at least a two-star admiral by now, yet here you are. captain." when he arrives at top gun, mitchell thinks he'll be leading the mission, too. admiral beau 'cyclone' simpson (jon hamm of "the town") crushes any such hopes. simpson makes it clear to mitchell that the latter is the last man he would have chosen for this assignment.

naturally, "top gun maverick" bristles with callbacks to its predecessor. kilmer and cruise are the only original cast members to reprise their roles. the opening aircraft carrier scene with crews hustling to launch jets ranks as a nostalgic homage to tony scott's unforgettable "top gun." "tron: legacy" director joseph kosinski designed this opening scene to recapture the essence of the first film. one aviator struggling desperately to make the cut for the mission is lieutenant bradley 'rooster' bradshaw (miles teller of "only the brave"), the son of mitchell's former radar intercept officer (rio), lieutenant, j. g. nick "goose" bradshaw. "rooster" bears a grudge against mitchell. pete refused to recommend him for the naval academy, torpedoing bradley's plans to become an aviator. nevertheless, pete had a legitimate reason. meantime, kosinski recycles flashbacks of goose (anthony edwards of "zodiac") and his wife carol (meg ryan of "the women") cavorting with mitchell. furthermore, the sequel draws on dialogue exchanges about an original "top gun" character that we finally meet in the flesh, admiral benjamin's daughter penny (jennifer connelly of "blood diamond") and her relationship with pete.

not surprisingly, the attack on the uranium plant in "top gun: maverick" generates heart-thumping suspense. the pilots must wing their way along a meandering trench, like the one in the clint eastwood warplane epic "firefox" (1982), to avoid surface-to-air missiles. afterward, they must soar over the crest of a towering mountain range, plunge precipitously toward a barren arena of flatlands that conceal their underground target, drop their ordnance, and then throttle up for a vertical, spine-tingling ascension over an even higher mountain! clearing this craggy gauntlet, they wind up exposing themselves to both missiles and enemy aircraft. mind you, mitchell has barely three weeks to train them. our heroes must complete the flight through that treacherous trench in 2 minutes flat! anybody who craves aerial combat epics will spot the resemblance between "top gun: maverick" and "633 squadron" (1963) with its suicidal bombing run where a squadron of plywood mosquito fighter bombers assailed a heavily defended nazi factory. happily, "top gun: maverick" emerges as a charismatic escapade about gallant aviators, not a tragic world war ii epic about heroic pilots who sacrificed their lives to pull off an impossible mission.

'maverick' achieves it all. as a spectacle it is an easy 5/5. producing set pieces of unprecedented beauty. sequences sent straight from the heavens (or maybe a deal with the devil?) not too mention the scale, the goddamn scale!

in short, action cinema soaring high on a level of its own making.

buut, this movie gives just as much time to its characters when they're on the ground and here, it's a mix bag of well rounded development and nauseating cheese.

miles teller gets the better end of it. a rich character with plenty of heft behind him to compete with cruise's already guaranteed hero statues. some of the strongest scenes involve only the two of them.

the worst is jennifer connelly (a great actress), who while everyone else gets to soar in the sky, receives 'unoffending female love interest'.

this would be a minor issue if she weren't given a mountain of screen time, and the scenes between her and cruise ...just need to go! just cut, it's okay. no one cares. get to the jets please! (they might as well be playing brother and sister with that lack of chemistry) also that's a really stupid rule for a bar...

i'm impressed. great shots, good camera work and, for me the most positive thing, a good story with emotions! i like how they portrait maverick and his ongoing conflict about the clash in part one. he gets a real character with great development. the lovestory also has it's moments. still, some critic from my side: the beginning is exposition dumping and not well made. mach 10 is completly unrealistic and maybe, it is a bit too much heroism in the end. however, i had a lot of fun watching.

this movie is an unabashed love letter to tom cruise as well as to gung-ho hoo-aa style military action movies favored by the production houses of tony scott and jerry bruckheimer (the movie is also dedicated to tony scott).

tom cruise is almost in every scene and the production goes overboard to ensure that everything - from the dialogue to the lighting to the dazzle of his smile to the whiteness of his teeth to the sun setting exactly so correctly behind him to the blackness of his hair to the agelessness of his physique - all of that continues to provide frame after picture perfect frame of more tom cruise than you can handle in a lifetime.

in short this is the tom cruise production fanboy equivalent of what the hallmark channel does for romantic christmas movies.

you know exactly what you are going to get - there are zero twists in the story, no one gets so much as even a scratch, there is zero action on the ground, and there is not one villain you can see in the movie. all of the action takes place in the air, the climactic battle is a cakewalk for everyone and barely lasts 10 mins with just two enemy aircraft showing up to ignominiously bite the dust. and the ending is well....even romance movies could not come up with a better hea ending!!!!!

the entire movie is a stringing together of tom's greatest hits moments - with every scene setup so that he gets to have the last word with the best punch or emotional line. of course almost everyone is against him but secretly worships the very ground he walks on and of course everyone hides a golden heart with eyes ready to turn moist. dialogues are corny puffed up and cringeworthy or make for a good laugh.

so why did the movie work obviously? there is just one answer and it is the obvious one - because of tom cruise and because he is a superstar. this is what he does best and no one comes even close. he is the last great superstar from a forgotten era that no longer exists - that of the superstar action hero that the whole world immediately recognizes who channels macho action in a bloodless old fashioned boys' adventure style movie making the way no one does. that is why tom would never be in a movie like braveheart or saving private ryan.

no one probably remembers the boys action hero biggles book series anymore (by capt we johns) but for those who do tom is the biggles avatar. he is also the hardy boys come to life - that is the era and image he speaks to.

and yes the production has done a beyond awesome job of all the aviation and aerial action sequences and puts you into the aircraft - that is how good it is.

so go watch it for your love of aviation and for tom ......go tom, you got this!!!!!

top gun (1986) was a phenomenal blockbuster, and the second one, 36 years later, is top gun maverick (2022) in theaters now. there are a lot of advancements in technology in the second movie. the computer generated imagery (cgi) made you feel you were really there, and it also made you feel like the actors were flying the jets themselves, because they were! let me explain. this "flying" was a combination of cgi and the actors actually flying the jets, because the movie crew couldn't go out to the himalayas or the arctic and start shooting footage of the actors flying around mountains in super hornets, so they picked lake oroville, feather river canyon and made the place look like it was snowing. at the end of the movie, maverick flies off into the distance while lady gaga's "hold my hand" is playing. however, the movie characters have too much plot armor. maverick went crashing down at mach 10 and survives, not to mention that both mav and rooster blew up, and both of them survived! afterwards, maverick gets targeted by a large enemy helicopter and every single bullet misses him! overall, great movie, but could've been better.

it is common to think that the second film cannot equal or even equal the first one, but top gun: maverick is the example that this can happen. the plot of the film is well structured and the trend becomes more and more compelling. the special effects and the scenography in general were perfect, making the settings and action scenes something fantastic and overwhelming, all accompanied by a thrilling soundtrack. tom cruise's performance is worthy as is that of the other actors. the director also found a way to make the events of the first film fit together and influence the dynamics of the second in an apt and never banal way. get ready to fly high in the sky.

it was a lot of fun seeing maverick back in action. compelling story with interesting new characters. the testosterone and bravado of those top guns as they vie for approval and position. watching goose's son battle through his own insecurities and the realization of what those around him have done in love for him. so sad to see the iceman in such an unhealthy state. really glad he made good on his career. the flying and maneuvers the pilots had to make to complete there mission was nothing short of a scene from a star wars death star destruction attack. just as thrilling and intense. great watch.

but there was some maaaaaajor flaws regarding accuracy and logic: -why they didn't use american 5th gen fighters (f22 & f35) at least to suppress the sam sites.

-and the f-14 start sequence is way much longer... a fighter won't start with a flip of a switch.

-also .. a plane hits a building during takeoff with its front landing gear and continue like nothing happened .. i mean c'mon for god's sake mate!!!

the list goes on and on... but in total .. i really like this movie style and wish to see more of it.

what a great film, updated storyline that really works, truly amazing dog fight scenes, the flying is epic, and just a few bits of nostalgia. you get a real feel for the characters in the movie.

the actions scenes will absolutely take your breath away, it's so fast and amazing, it's tough to keep up with it.

soundtrack is not as memorable as the original but is still very good, it's what you come to expect from hans zimmer. tom cruise is great in this as the experienced maverick, jennifer connelly is beautiful as always and plays her part well as the love interest. the other pilots play their parts well and you get to see the grow into a team.

to sum up then. an excellent sequel that a lot of people will love and a lot that loved the original movie will also really enjoy.

i watched this movie for a 2nd time tonight. originally i scored the movie 6/10, stating that the first movie was much better and struggled to see how such an "average" movie could score so highly by other reviewers. how wrong i was, and what a pleasant surprise 2 years make to one's positive outlook on life.

who knows, maybe i was in a tunnel of cynicism when i first watched it the first time. having enjoyed my childhood in the 80s, i have a great fondness for the original, it's one of the truly iconic movies of that decade. and this sequel has all of the elements required for a great sequel - cruise is as good as ever as maverick, less cocky, still vulnerable from goose's death, but still the top gun we know and love. miles teller is convincing as goose's son, he even looks like him, absolutely perfectly casting. and glen powell is another ice man. jennifer connelly adds a wonderful touch as the love of mavericks life.

i upgraded my rating from a 6 to a solid 8. great movie, highly recommended, and apologies for my original review. the good news is, i seem to have navigated myself out of my cynicism tunnel.

over all i do enjoy it however here are my issues: too similar to the first that it feels like a reboot as appear continuation.

not enough character development for the team. i wouldn't remember who and what their call names are.

like every other tom cruise movies he comes out on top at the end. in real world scenario, fighting is not so staged.

everyone is perfect and good looking. have you looked around your surroundings? when do you ever see that in the real world.

yes i realize it's just a movie, that's why i'm not giving it a 10.

enjoyed this movie much more than i thought i would. cruise confronts much more than the bad guys here, he actually fleshes out and becomes a human being as well. that is a significant accomplishment in any movie, let alone one that previously was a relatively mindless summer blockbuster.

one actually sees the human side of the character "maverick" and comes to actually like him despite his many flaws. in fact he grows larger as he continues despite his flaws. that resonates much more than one dimensional super hero type characterization because one realizes the price that has to be paid to achieve the extraordinary.

there is great cgi in this movie interspersed with actual flight scenes. it's pretty seamless and will age well over time.

downsides? a few- knowing a small amount about aerodynamics and friction at high mach numbers lells us that hypersonic mach speeds are not ejectable and survivable conditions. the limiting factor on the sr71 blackbird aircraft was not the engines, but the fact that the leading edge of the airframe could not survive speeds much beyond mach 3. a bit of artistic license yes, but one that pretty much strains believability in any realistic scenario.

the other downside is that one has to wonder, if the navy possessed sufficient firepower to crater and render enemy runways completely destroyed they could not do the same for the surface to air missile sites that guarded the exctrance and exits to the nuclear processing site.

flaws aside it's easily one of the best from hollywood in the last five years.
the first top gun is an awesome great cheesy film and top gun:maverick does not disappoint , i enjoyed every minute there is a great cast proper cheesy story what's not to like ........8/10 ....!!!!!

pretty good action movie, love rooster and maverick dynamic. hangman obviously has some story to be developed, reminds me of a young you know who. the female pilot and her beta male co-pilot added nothing to the movie, was obviously a progressive quota filling situation. only other glaring issue, if the cast of the movie is anything to go by, white people are the minority in america now.

having rewatched the original in preparation, i can safely say this is a neat 2022 restoration. the plot slightly tweaked, each scene touched up and carefully put back in place, all with the exception of the main mission, which is essentially the same tactical plan luke skywalker and the rebellion had to destroy the death star.

all this doesn't matter though, cause this film is a film. loud, fun and intense. i had a fantastic time watching it on the big screen. the third act is what action movies are all about. edge of your seat excitement.

top gun (1986) premiered the same year my mum pushed me out into the danger zone. tom cruise may not have grown as much as me in 35yrs, but his balls certainly did!

great film, great plot although it's a bit like the navy meets star wars, great flight scenes and a compelling story, if you don't think too hard about it.

cruise, and connelly, both are in motorcycle scenes with no crash helmets or any other protective gear. this is a very poor role model and illegal almost everywhere. theses scenes definitely detracted from the overall enjoyment.

i only watched top gun this year for the first time in preparation for maverick. the first film i can see why it was so popular back then and maverick really brings it into the 21st century. i'm not normally a tom cruise fan but i did enjoy this even if it is basically the same storyline as the first.

there are some cool call names in this (fanboy, payback, bob, rooster, hangman) and the aesthetics are brilliant. i love that they bring the old soundtrack back as well, some really iconic songs. it made an absolute killing at the box office (1.4 billion) and became the highest grossing film of the year. it's not the best film i've seen this year but i'm glad i watched it.

the good: as someone who despises the original top gun and thinks it's amongst the most overhyped films ever...color me surprised that i really liked maverick. i feel like virtually everything was done better with this film than the original. the plot feels more purposeful and cohesive; there's a mission, there are stakes, there's a reason maverick is brought back.

the characters are more grounded and relatable. yes, there still mostly clichés (the jerk, the nerd, the good hearted son-of-the-alum, the uh...girl), but they're not actively irritating, like the first one. cruise is actually really, really good here. unlike the first one, maverick doesn't feel like an a******e. his arrogance feels earned, the way he acts is drawn from a legitimate (and selfless) place: he wants to ensure the young top gun students survive a dangerous (and almost impossible) mission. miles teller is also really good here; perfect casting as goose's - hilarious named - son, rooster.

but of course, it's the flight scenes that steal the show. plot notwithstanding, these are legitimately exhilarating and worth the price of admission alone. again while i get there were technical limitations in the 1980s, the reason these scenes are better isn't the cinematography. it's that there's a better story and better characters involved. but yes, they're also filmed very well: you can tell what's going on, the scenes feel real, and they're unlike anything i've seen in a long while.

the final 30 minutes of this movie are just pure awesomeness. it's great to see the mission built up this way and to see it live up to the hype. i can totally see why this film resonates with so many people. it has the spirit of an 80s blockbuster, with the technical and storytelling finesse of a contemporary film. it brings you back, but it far, far surpasses the original in every way (almost like the inaccurate memory of the original).

the bad: i thought, just like the original, the worst aspect of this movie is the romance. cruise and connelly are nice to look at, but they don't really have a genuine or well-developed romance. cruise just sorta shows up and it's clear the script wants them to get together, but there's no reason they actually do. it just feels very half baked.

i also have to acknowledge while the film is self-aware a lot of the time, there are moments when it leans a bit too much into the cheesiness. a bit to over sentimental, you know? the use of flashbacks was highly distracting and unintentionally funny at times. for example, when rooster is playing "great balls of fire" and cruise is having vietnam flashbacks about goose doing so, i legitimately felt there was some cruel prank being played on him or something. that's at least how it felt.

oh, and i just have to nitpick here: did the final mission really have to have a video game esque "weak point" for the jets to target? come on.

the ugly: so, as in the original top gun, the "enemy" country isn't revealed (for more obvious reasons today than back in 1986, honestly). however, unlike the original, where there's nothing in the plot that could possibly suggest who the enemy was, here we get tantalizing clues:



it's iran. definitely supposed to be iran. that we're not explicitly told that is kind of reflective of the "good patriotism" of this film. it's obviously pro-american but it's not all up in your face with it.

for films produced in the 1980s, the first top gun film succeeded in showing stunning fighter plane scenes. after watching the first film, you are guaranteed to be even more amazed by the various fighter aircraft attraction scenes shown in top gun: maverick. moreover, maverick and his team face a much more dangerous mission in the sequel.

in the sequel, maverick and his team get a mission to blow up a uranium enrichment facility. however, they have to face terrain that is not easy to reach and leave their target location. even during the training period, you can watch various cool and thrilling fighter aircraft attractions.

the audience can feel a thrilling sensation during the fighter plane scene because the camera angle is so right. the camera angle makes the audience feel the excitement and tension of being in the pilot's seat, like maverick and his team. top gun: maverick proves that you can get the sensation of watching 3d films without using 3d glasses.

there is no doubt that top gun: maverick is a complete package for those of you who want to experience various sensations in just one film. you can feel nostalgia, emotion, and the sensation of being a fighter pilot while watching this film.

the covid pandemic delayed the release of top gun: maverick (2022) for a few years. having only watched the original a few days prior to seeing this in the theaters, it was definitely worth the wait to see something like this on the big screen. the trailers only hinted at the spectacle that could be achieved over 35 years after the original wowed audiences with great fighter jet footage. that's not to say that this film doesn't lean heavily on its nostalgia-or plots that come strikingly close to other famous franchises.

part of the appeal of top gun (1986) was all the footage of fighter jet acrobatics. most civilians never get to see these things outside an occasional air show, so there's an amount of awe involved when seeing what these marvels of modern engineering can do. over three decades of advancements in cinematography allowed this sequel to surpass the original. cockpit footage of these actors actually in these fighter jets, combined with high-definition shots of amazing maneuvers, made this movie quite exciting to watch. these scenes shown in the trailers made me-a top gun skeptic-want to see this film. i was not disappointed.

plot-wise, top gun: maverick felt slightly more developed than its predecessor. my favorite part by far was the experimental aircraft test at the start of the movie. however, the rest of the film's plot felt familiar, but not in a good way. about a third of the way through, i realized, "wait a minute. this is just star wars (1977)." don't get me wrong, star wars' climactic battle against the empire is a cinema-defining moment. it just felt weird packaged in this way. add to that a few moments of blatant nostalgia and it was clear this movie was at least in part made for fans of the original.

improving on the visuals and story of its predecessor, i give top gun: maverick 4.0 stars out of 5.

i'm not a tom cruise fan, nor was i fan of the first top gun movie, but i have to say i thoroughly enjoyed this. it's a great flick, with a simple story, it's good fun with plenty of action. there's no silly gender ideology, pushing agendas or cringy woke nonsense. there are characters you actually care about and who make you feel things, which is what movies are supposed to do. modern filmmakers please take note! this is the sort of good old fashioned blockbuster that people are missing nowadays, we don't go to see movies to be lectured to. we just want simple escapism and a bit of entertainment for a few hours.

if i had one problem i'd say at times it can be a little bit cheesy and some of the dialogue is a bit lame and there's a cliche of the characters moping and doping but to be fair it's only for like 2 minutes. but aside from that this is a fantastic movie. the emotional weight is done very well. i didn't see the original but i actually understand maverick's relationship with his late friend goose and he doesn't want to see his son die unlike his friend from the first one. that conflict is very well handled. what is worth seeing about this movie though are the flying sequences. they have fantastic cinematography, sound design and stunt work but what i think mainly works about the movie is the editing. like the dark knight these scenes do have some quick edits but you can still see what's going on in these scenes and they're done impressively well. even if you haven't seen the first one like me i'd still recommend the movie and you can still understand what happened in the movie even if you haven't seen the first one. that's what i feel like sequels released decades after the first movie should do. and this is one of those sequels that gets it right. it may not be one of the greatest sequels of all time but it is still a good time with drama that's handled extremely well and fantastic flying sequences that i think is worthy of a viewing.

ok -we may well of seen similar scenes of action in much earlier action films . such as the opening , when we see maverick attempting to beat the elements as we saw by chuck yeager in "the right stuff" in 1983. i believe that the the right stuff won a number of academy awards .this tom cruise production may well pick up one or two as well.

yes ,we are back to top gun territory ,right left and centre. but that tom cruise smile is always infectious.

see this great entertainment on as big a screen , with the noisiest sound affects you can. it's terrific entertainment. and this old codger clapped at the end !!

just like his work on the mission impossible franchise, he knows exactly what this movie is supposed to be and he delivers accordingly. he plays the role to the perfection and supporting cast, directing, writing and absolutely thrilling action sequences all come together to make this a wild ride with just the right amount of nostalgia sprinkled throughout as additional fan service. for 10 failed reboots or remakes there's always the one exception that is very well done and top gun: maverick is that one out of 10. i definitely recommend it, whether you've seen the original or not but let's be real... who hasn't seen the original?

i recently went to watch the new top gun movie with some friends and below is what i thought. i thought the new top gun film (top gun maverick) was a very enjoyable film, the characters were good, the chemistry was quite good and the acting was alright for tom cruise. however, it is not true cinema. true cinema is stuff like martin scorsese, stanley kubrick and so on. overall the film was enjoyable but should not go down in history as a masterpiece. looking at the reviews now, i think the film is a little overated but definitely worth a watch.

top gun doesn't innovate but it successfully delivers outstanding action and successfully continues maverick's story 20 years later with a style. while it may lack originality and unabashedly borrows from its predecessor, the film admirably embraces its spirit.

top gun is so stunningly similar to the original one, it could be called total copycat.

there is a scene in a bar at the beginning - check.

then there is a song in a bar - check.

and yes, it's great balls of fire, appearing at approximately the 20th minute of the film.

there is a cocky, iceman like character type - check.

he even uses a toothpick as iceman did.

there is a romantic episode with maverick involved - check.

you thought tony scott's volleyball scene on the beach was left off out of this?

yes, it was.

they are playing football, not volleyball.

you get the point.

this is one of the most déjà vu films i've ever seen.

is it necessarily a bad thing?

from the point of paying tribute to the original and continuing story while delivering great actions top gun maverick passes with a straight a.

it knows what it stands for and doesn't pretend to be larger than life. it steals from the original without shame and delivers superb action scenes.

miles teller gives a good performance as goose' son to create tension between him and cruise and besides that his physique is strikingly similar to goose's.

tom cruise does what he does the best - drawing you closer to the action. sometimes his puppy eyes on the point of tears look forced, cruise - connelly chemistry doesn't work so well at moments, partly due to sometimes cheesy dialogue, but we won't mind.

why?

top gun mix works so well you'll forget some things that might have been better.

action is outstanding.

"it's the one you need to see in the cinema" is a cliche appropriately used for maverick. i enjoyed being blown away by fast pace camera pans and audio effects. i was literally on the edge of the seat.

it doesn't rely solely on cgi and it's going to grow old as well as the first one.

it's so refreshing to see a classic hero of the flesh and blood.

it's also the hero america needs right now. although i'm not an american i'd pick maverick over other marvel heroes any time.

success maverick had on box office shows there is still hope for classic genre heroes like this.

before end credits start, there is dedication to tony scott and rightly so. without this master of action films, top gun maverick wouldn't be what it is today.

it's nice that the team behind a film was humble enough to recognise this and give him credit. well done.

this is a great film to see one large screen with an appropriate audio system. i would have been sorry if i hadn't seen it in cinemas before reviewing it one more time.

oh, and one more thing.

if you wondered how real action scenes are, here's the answer.

david berke, top gun instructor and probably one of few if not the only one who can fly on all fs says everything seen on the screen was something he's done during his career.

that's enough for me.

great action, respect for the roots of the story and small issues you'll be willing to forget.

mission accomplished.

full disclosure: i've never seen top gun (and yes, i was born when it was released. i just never bothered).

i watched this movie because i'd heard it was a call back to the great action movies of the 90's & 00's. before the mcu & star wars turned our favourite popcorn flicks into mindless, cgi choking, woke nonsense. movies with likeable characters you care about, real stakes and an aspirational & uplifting tone.

and yes maverick absolutely ticked all these boxes. now is the plot/story perfect? no. is the primary romance of the story well developed? not really. did i pick exactly how it would end really early on? of course.

but maverick does deliver 2 things in spades.

one, it keeps you engaged the entire time.

the flying sequences are pretty great, in no small part because of the practical sets. and the cinematography is stunning.

and say what you want about cruise but he's still got the juice to carry an action film. sure this movie didn't stretch his acting chops much but he delivered.

and two, i got the hit of positive, aspirational feelings i was looking for. i was on the edge of my seat when i needed to be and cheering when it all came together.

in a time of soulless reboots and modern re-interpretations of beloved ips, top gun maverick appears to be the usual suspect and prime offender: an 80s cult movie, filled with antiquated ideas of masculinity and absurdly fetishized militarism worthy of james cameron's wet dream. what a temptation it must have been for the studio and the creatives to board the en-vogue subversion-train and give top gun a 'modern' makeover that online trolls could go to metaphorical war over.

yet, top gun maverick withstands those temptations and instead chooses to honor and respect its cinematic predecessor and give us a true to formula action film, with a refined structure, believable character development and state of the art flight sequences. all while remaining free of excessive misfires of comedy or the urge to make us feel ashamed about liking 'that sort of entertainment'.

tom cruise fully embraces his aged hero figure while gracefully passing the baton to the younger generation, replacing the unintentional-seeming homo-eroticism of the original film with genuine themes of brotherhood, friendship and forgiveness. with top gun maverick and following the reinvention of tron in 2010, director joseph kosinski certainly has established himself as the man to honor and preserve an ip while giving it a fresh new layer of paint. all these things combined make top gun maverick is a standout in 2022's action film offering.
