final thoughts: picture it, prescott, late 1980s. summer camp for christians. believe me, that'll be important later. they called lights out like normal at 9pm. about 15 minutes later, the lights all came back on and they invite everyone into the large room for "movie night!" and they're showing top gun! well, only 40-minutes of it. they edited out any "curse" words or what they deemed was immoral dialogue, any sexual relations or innuendos and anyone dying. but, when they edited it, it was like 3-5 minutes before and after the alleged sins. this was my first "viewing" of top gun and i wouldn't officially see it whole until 2015. needless to say: it was so choppy and badly spliced together; it was a hot mess that made little sense. barely a c for effort, christian counselors!

the film from 1986 that pretty much summed up 1980s film for me in that it is a series of montages, style over substance in every scene if you like.

it doesn't have a deep storyline, far from it. it is about a u. s. navy fighter jet pilot school where the students vie to become the 'top gun', the best of the best.

in one corner you have reckless but dangerous pete mitchell (tom cruise) and his aviator/best buddy nick 'goose' bradshaw (anthony edwards).

in the other corner you have straight down the line tom 'iceman' kazansky (val kilmer) who is just as brilliant a pilot as maverick if a little more reserved and/or seemingly professional.

interlinked you have a series of soundtrack highlights intermingled with scenes that are questionable about their inclusion such as a beach volleyball scene where the pilots play in sun drenched scenes (in jeans?) and several dressing room scenes that make you ask what are you watching.

maverick has a romantic relationship with a character called charlie (kelly mcgillis) to add to proceedings before the main event in a lacklustre screenplay.

the flying/dog fight sequences are some of the best yet put to film and add a layer of danger to the proceedings.

the film for all its style over substance is one that is an easy watch all these years since production.

what i like most about top gun is how it really puts you in tom cruise's shoes. if you enjoyed the old propaganda movies about the underground resistance in nazi-occupied europe, you'll probably like this one. as students at the navy's elite fighter weapons school compete to be best in the class, one daring young flyer learns a few things from a civilian instructor that are not taught in the classroom. the airplane they use is so advanced that it seems like it can read minds. top gun is not by any means a classic; it is, however, a nice snap-shot of a society. the plot is fairly generic, but the buildup has enough suspense to make the whole movie worth a watch. this was so-so, one of those films that could have been a lot better had the editing been tighter.

this movie has long been on my shame list of super popular movies that i have never seen as a cinema fan i had to see for myself what the hype is all about. it was everything i expected: 80s montage scenes, the infamous strange beach volleyball scene, planes, and 80s tom cruise. while it had a great soundtrack and was an entertaining ride i couldn't help but me overwhelmed by the amount of 80s cheesiness. and i am someone that loves 80s movies. i was curious to see where the hypeness of this movie came from so many 80s movies similar to it. it felt very much like a jean claude van damme film of the era. some of the camera shots mid-flight had me uneasy. what really drives the movie is the arrogrance and pompous of young tom cruise as maverick and his rivalry with kilmer's iceman. while it was not my favorite movie of all time, it was a cool ride, gave me a feel of 80s nostalgia. it will be interesting to see cruise's reprisal in the upcoming sequel. i can finally say i have been able to see top gun. good not great.

no political correctness. no focus other than on the main protagonist. the typical downfall of a dying friend and the "why do we fall so that we can learn to lift ourselves up" theme. i miss these simple entertaining movies so much. tom cruise always has a way of acting the character in the most convincing way; maverick reminds me of my typical army friends with their all arrogant, too confident masculine attitude that would probably just get cancelled and criticized today on twitter, yet it's just so dumb that it keeps you entertained for how he'll interestingly keep being both idiotic and competent alike.

considering this movie was released the year i was born it stands up pretty well. guess practical effects and putting your body on the line really do hold up. watching this now, it's interesting to see how it was the blueprint for action movies and the tom cruise persona. only difference is, he has not looked this short in a movie since.

"the best shooter" directed by tony scott was created as a typical literate film of the mid-1980s today. an interesting era in cinema, an interesting picture with tom cruise in the title role. this is a very beautiful visual realization of the boundless skies, where the heroes are their conquerors, who time after time soar up on winged combat vehicles.

the film gave a lot of pleasant impressions thanks to the diverse cast, where almost every name is known in one way or another. tom cruise, val kilmer, anthony edwards, meg ryan, kelly mcgillis, michael ironside, rick rossovich, tim robbins and others. a fairly simple plot, where there are a lot of brave guys in the center of events. each of them is ready to serve the motherland, achieve their goals, soar into the skies, conquer beautiful women.

in the center of the plot is the self-confident hero of tom cruise, nicknamed the tramp, who, already being a skilled pilot, goes to the best squadron to join the most skilled military pilots. he has a best friend and partner goose, who was embodied on the screen by anthony edwards, playing a wonderful comrade. meg ryan in the role of the latter's wife named carol performed just brilliantly. even though her appearance in the film was not long, the girl gave a beautiful scene of a conversation with a tramp closer to the finale of the picture, from which it was hard on the soul. val kilmer is also good. his ice became a worthy competitor to the tramp, the tension from the confrontation of which hung in the air for almost the entire picture.

the plot of the film does not shine with something extraordinary. this is a good film, even in its philosophy, where brave military pilots are ready to serve their country and valiantly fulfill their duty. the picture is ready to impress with several interesting moves, but no more, remaining a pretty creation of its reagan time. the picture is intended primarily to show the story of the hero tom cruise, the evolution of this character, who is used to winning everywhere and in everything, breaking the rules, coming out victorious from any situation. life becomes a harsh teacher, throwing an unprecedented test to this young man. the tramp is changing, evolving, thanks to the help of his comrades, he finds his place in the sky again, where he has always been a master and felt confident. it should be noted that the script and the game of cruz perfectly convey the story of this new formation of the main character, allowing you to empathize with the heavy thoughts of the tramp. after all, he loses faith in himself, having fallen painfully from a kind of olympus of life. however, sometimes such a fall is necessary for everyone to remember - we are all human beings, we tend to make mistakes. falls only strengthen and allow you to rush up with renewed vigor.

the picture is really simple. but it teaches you to be an admirer of your work, to be able to love, to be a good friend and a support in a team, where even with rivalry, everyone remains a true comrade to each other. there is no tearful drama here, but there is an understanding of what it is like to be a true friend, someone's true love. the film successfully combines excellent visual solutions, high-quality sound, an interesting plot and a good denouement, where the antagonists will finally appear.

7 out of 10.

united states naval aviator lt pete "maverick" mitchell (tom cruise) and his radar intercept officer (rio) ltjg nick "goose" bradshaw (anthony edwards) stationed aboard the uss enterprise are sent to attend topgun, the naval fighter weapons school at naval air station miramar. once there maverick strikes up a romance with civilian contractor and topgun flight instructor charlotte "charlie" blackwood (kelly mcgillis) and a rivalry with lt tom "iceman" kazansky (val kilmer).

top gun was inspired by the article "top guns" by ehud yonay, from the may 1983 issue of california magazine which detailed the lives of fighter pilots at naval air station miramar in san diego, self-nicknamed as "fightertown usa". a high priority project for producers jerry bruckheimer and don simpson, the draft written by jim cash and jack epps, jr. was heavily adjusted with the input and cooperation of the u. s. navy. tony scott had directed the commercial for saab wherein a saab car races a saab jet leading the producers to hire him, with tom cruise eventually cast for the lead of pete "maverick" mitchell. when top gun was released, it became a breakout success staying in theaters for six months and going on to become the highest grossing film of 1986 and spring boarding the careers of tom cruise, director tony scott, and even meg ryan in a smaller supporting performance. in hindsight the movie is unashamed in how much of a showcase it is for the u. s. navy, but thanks to tom curise's performance and the immersive direction of tony scott it's also unquestionably a well made one.

while risky business was tom cruise's first time headlining a leading role, it's here in top gun where he cultivates the daredevil rogue persona that would define many of his future acting roles. maverick is brash, abrasive, and arrogant, but unlike many imitators that tried and failed to do this character type (such as charlie sheen's hawkins in navy seals) the movie builds a character and story around it rather than just plopping it in front of us. with top gun it is a showcase for impressive aerial stunts and photography, but we also learn what drives maverick as a character and build his relationships with other people such as anthony edwards' goose, kelly mcgillis' charlie, or rivalries with others such as val kilmer's iceman. many movies that tried to ape this character archetype only took the surface level of maverick (with the brash arrogance) and didn't add any substance to it which left many of the imitators insufferable at best. here cruise is not only a solid actor, but he's given some good meat to chew on character wise.

the other star of top gun is undoubtedly the aerial photography with the f-14a tomcat probably deserving of a second billing behind cruise. despite the hunger being tony scott's debut feature, top gun is what most people think of when they think of tony scott as a director: the "magic hour" shots, dynamic camera work, multiple cuts and angles to get the maximum impact of an action sequence, this is where we see tony scott start forming his identity as a director. the aerial sequences are amazing as they used real jets with cameras mounted on them and scott uses all these different angles to give you the feeling of flying through the air. even though most of the movie is training exercises the movie focuses on the psychological and physical strain that comes from piloting these jets and you feel both the exhilaration and the danger that comes with it.

now despite the positives of top gun there are a lot of silly moments to the movie. some of the romance subplot between charlie and maverick is pretty corny, there's also some pretty cheesy scenes interspersed throughout the movie (volleyball scene anyone?). top gun is graceful when it's flying through the air, but on the ground it often goes into hokey, albeit still visually beautiful, melodrama that's pretty hard to take seriously.

top gun is a showcase for both cruise's skills as an actor in his breakout role as well as the direction of tony scott. the movie does a good job of giving the audience the feeling they're in the air with these fighter pilots and at the time this was some of the highest level aerial photography ever seen in a blockbuster release. of course in between scenes of exhilaration there's scenes of pretty hokey melodrama or corny line deliveries but that's part of the appeal of a movie like this.

"on march 3, 1969 the united states navy established an elite school for the top one percent of its pilots. its purpose was to teach the lost art of aerial combat and to insure that the handful of men who graduated were the best fighter pilots in the world."

so starts this action masterpiece from director tony scott. hot shot pilot maverick (tom cruise) gets a chance to attend fighter weapons school or top gun in miramar when his lead cougar loses it in the air. he's met by cold as ice iceman (val kilmer) as his calculating competition. he always has his navigator goose (anthony edwards) by his side. he constantly tries to prove himself running on instinct against his father's perceived failed mission. top gun commanding officer is viper (tom skerritt) and jester (michael ironside) is an instructor. charlie (kelly mcgillis) is a civilian instructor.

the action is great. tony scott shoots the action like a music video and it looks amazing. he gets great access to military hardware and locations. this is not the older generation military movie. movie star tom cruise is perfectly suited as maverick. the only minor hiccup is the limited chemistry between mcgillis and cruise. it's not bad and it doesn't detract from anything. this movie just has all the fun 80s stuff. it's funny. it's fun. it's a great popcorn movie.

pete "maverick" mitchell flies f-14 tomcats for the us navy with his radar intercept officer nick "goose" bradshaw. maverick is a bit of a wildcard with a certain contempt for the rule but when the unit's number one pilot has a panic attack during an encounter with a pair of migs he finds himself sent to the prestigious 'top gun' school where he and goose will train and compete with the finest pilots in the navy. once there he quickly ruffles a few feathers but also impresses with his flying and is one of the favourites to be top of the class. away from the flying he gets involved with instructor charlotte "charlie" blackwood. a tragic accident during training means he considers whether or not to quit but when a situation arises in the indian ocean he takes to the skies again and must put what he learnt into practice.

i first watched this film in the eighties, loved it and watched it many times but having not watched it for several years i wondered how it would have aged. thankfully it was as enjoyable as ever. the story itself is a little cliché but it is well told and the aerial scenes are some of the best in any film i've seen no cgi here. the romantic subplot does feel a little forced as the two leads don't seem to have the right chemistry the relationship between the pilots and rios, especially between maverick and goose are more interesting than the romance. when the 'tragic event' occurs it is quite a shock and genuinely emotional. the cast do a decent job and it is no surprise that this launched tom cruise's career as an action star however the real stars are the grumman f-14 tomcats. director tony scott did a great job capturing the action both in the sky and on the ground. overall i'd say this is a must see for anybody who likes modern military aircraft and those who like decent action.

maverick battles his fellow pilots to be best in class, but his daredevil attitude lands him in trouble.

it's definitely one of the most iconic films to come out of the 1980's, and it's no surprise to me that it still has a huge following, and spurned a sequel decades later.

it's one of those easy to watch films, it's full of romance, competition, action and egos, it really is a film packed full of energy.

i'm surprised by how good it still looks, you can't argue with those action sequences, and best of all, that phenomenal soundtrack, which still sounds awesome.

love him or hate him, tom cruise has always had something, not just his looks, or charisma, whatever it is, he has it, and he's great her, the only thing i'm not totally convinced by is the dynamic between him and mcgillis,

tim robbins, val kilmer, anthony edward all so good.

it's a film that's quite hard to review, as it's one i know inside out, and have watched so many times, it just never gets tired, i think anyone watching it for the first time, would still thoroughly enjoy it.

8/10.

i didn't care much for tom cruise early in his career, i guess because i equated his real life personality with those of on-screen egotistical characters like vincent lauria in "the color of money" and 'maverick' pete mitchell in the film under consideration here. his jumping up and down on oprah's couch while advocating for scientology in 1990 certainly didn't win him any favors in this viewer's eyes. i really have no idea how he is in real life, so it's unfair to paint an unreasonable picture of him based on early observations. i did like him as nathan algren in "the last samurai", and i've enjoyed his take on the jack reacher character. "top gun" was a major breakout role for cruise and you can see why. his hollywood good looks stand out strongly and he does have charisma on screen. as a hot shot pilot tapped for advanced flight training at the fightertown u.s.a. base in miramar, california, 'maverick' mitchell joins an elite group of flyers, some of whom have an outsized ego as big as his.

what follows is a fairly formulaic story that follows maverick as he pursues his air combat maneuver training and rivalry with iceman mike kazansky (val kilmer), not to mention a romantic tangle with civilian instructor charlotte 'charlie' blackwood (kelly mcgillis). the chemistry between them didn't work for this viewer, but that might just be me. i thought the repeated strains of 'take my breath away' got a little heavy handed at times, as if you couldn't tell the couple was hot for each other. but it did win best original song at the oscars, so i guess it fulfilled it's purpose. when mitchell faces a crisis of conscience with the death of his best friend and co-pilot goose (anthony edwards), he has to summon up the courage and determination to move on. though he misses out on the top gun trophy at miramar, maverick pulls through when it really counts in well orchestrated battle action over the indian ocean, which re-earns him the respect and admiration of his fellow pilots and officer trainers.

seeing as how this film is over three decades old as i write this, i can appreciate how far tom cruise has come as an actor and i have to admit, he's not bad. he's not a favorite, but you can see he's developed his craft. what i would say in criticism of the picture is the casting of meg ryan as the redneck wife of anthony edward's character goose. who at the time thought that was a good idea?

i always heard and read about top gun every time i'm looking for a movie recommendations but never give it a try until the sequel came out and got tons of positive reviews. i'm finally interested and immediately like it, it was better than anyone thought it would be. my only problem is the relationship between maverick and charlotte, it just seems kinda forced, no chemistry and felt corny at times. it's just doesn't work for me, i think it would've been better if they just make it a simple bromance and competition movie between naval aviators with more action, or just write a better romance story.

the dogfight sequences are great considering the time this movie was made, they managed to make it look as real as possible when the actors are inside the aircraft. but some scenes can be too confusing to make out what happened because it was too shaky and a lot of weird jump cuts.

my favorite is undoubtedly the final dogfight and yeah the soundtrack are the best part as well.
top gun is a classic!! tom cruise and val kilmer makes a fantastic duo!! it's sad at the end but if you have the urge to see a movie, go see top gun. top gun 2? can't wait to see it.

the top 1% of the nation's flyers gather for fighter pilot training. outstanding maneuvers in the sky. great soundtrack embellishes the hi-jinks, action and drama. you walk away from this one proud and pumped. this had to be a godsend to the military recruiters! i can watch this one again and again.

tom cruise, in probably his best role. kelly mcgillis goes by the name of charlie, but looks all woman to me. wow!! val kilmer plays a good hard ass villain type. anthony edwards, tim robbins and john stockwell are air jockey buddies. tom skerritt plays the mentor. meg ryan has a small, but very noticeable part; cute, funny and loud.

excellent photography and sound that will not let you snooze. don't miss one of the best of its kind. top gun is tops.

this movie was surprisingly good, and i thought that it was a really good movie about top gun. there really is a top gun, and it is the best of the best, and this movie really showed the viewers that it was! i liked how there was a little bit of romance included in the movie because it made it a little bit better. tom cruise was the hottest in this movie!!! today he is still good looking for his age, but in this movie, there are no words to describe him!! the movie was really good, but the one thing that made it amazing was him in it!! in this movie, to me, he is hotter than shia laboeuf and alex pettyfer (they are still really hot)! even though he made the movie even better, overall the movie its self i would give and 8 out of 10 with or without him in it. i would definitely recommend watching this, especially if you're a girl because you will not be able to keep your eyes off of tom cruise!

i have lost count of the number of times i have watched this movie and it never disappoints when i get to see again.

switch off the brain, sit back and be entertained is the easiest way to describe it. do not overthink it.

tom cruise, anthony edwards, tom skerrit, michael ironside, meg ryan, val kilmer, tim robbins and the list goes on, the movie is packed to the rafters with good and great actors.

it has comedy, drama, romance and action all the way through.

if you haven't seen it already and like action packed movies do yourself a favour.

i was a child when i watched this film and it was great fun. actors that i loved playing around with big noisy dangerous toys in a context that i couldn't possibly understand in other terms than the very basic our guys vs their guys. i couldn't have possibly understood what mav and charlie were doing, other that it was cute, and at the time, watching the film illegally from behind the iron curtain, this was my version of harry potter.

the plot is that hot-shot pilot pete mitchell, which from then on will be named maverick, goes to the school for top pilots to prove he's the best of the best. he trains a lot, acts all hotshotty, gets the girl, is brought down by misfortune, then gets back up and bags himself a few bad guys in the process. then... he becomes an instructor. wait, what? he instructs other pilots after he want into one single battle?! i would like to see potter doing that after the first book in the series.

anyway, at the time it was amazing. girls were swooning after cruise, boys wanted to be him and get more mature girls like kelly mcgillis and everybody was happy that the commies got their asses kicked. navy enrolment increased 500% after the film, which was one of its main objectives anyway. fast forward 36 years later and everything is different. the manly banter between pilots is seen as overly sexual, borderline homosexual. mav's straight to the jugular flirting style is seen as plain harassment. try serenading a girl in a bar with all the other guys as backup, then follow her into the female bathroom today and see what happens. even the passive roles of women in the film would get at least a raised eyebrow. the political situation is also hard to stomach, even if the russians are at it again these days, as one cannot possible imagine a scramble between u. s. and russian planes without so many breaking news that tvs would physically break.

not to mention the technical side of the film, which i believe was ridiculous in 1986 and now it would be laughable. pilots doing whatever they want, flying my instinct, and their backers checking where the enemy planes are by looking through the windows in 3 vs 5 plane battles from aircrafts that conveniently have their ramps malfunctioning and with officers that can only say "god damn it!" in frustrated powerlessness.

so how did we change so much? is it a good thing or a bad thing or just normal? is it ok to not be able to recognize the world - and worse, the people in it - in films only a few decades old? top gun is a cheesy film with silly lines, inaccurate depiction of navy life but also a joyous celebration of boyish maleness and of the american way of life. it was an instant financial success back in the day, regardless of the lukewarm critical reception. (even then movie critics were useless, heh!)

i can't wait to see how they did the sequel in 2022. i do feel i am going to learn something here. certainly not on how to woo women and fly planes, but on how the world can change so fast we can hardly remember or accept how it really was.

troubled by accusations that his deceased father was somehow disgraced as a pilot in a fateful combat sortie during the vietnam war, "pete 'maverick" mitchell" (tom cruise) exhibits a reckless nature while at the same time trying to be the best fighter pilot in the u. s. navy. so, when an incident disqualifies another pilot from attending the elite school known as top gun both he and his partner "nick 'goose' bradshaw" (anthony edwards) are elated to be chosen instead. yet as good as the two of them are, neither one of them is prepared for just how grueling the competition will be to earn the honor of being top of their class. now, rather than reveal any more, i will just say that i thought that the selection of tom cruise was a perfect choice for this picture as he exuded the necessary cockiness required for this role. not only that, but his acting, along with that of val kilmer (as "tom 'iceman' kazansky") and tom skerritt ("mike 'viper' metcalf") was equally impressive as well. in short, those viewers looking for an excellent action film might want to consider this particular movie and i have rated it accordingly.

even in 2023, "top gun" remains thrilling and entertaining. while the plot may be a bit predictable by today's standards, the action sequences and aerial photography are still top-notch. tom cruise delivers a charismatic performance as pete "maverick" mitchell, a hotshot pilot who pushes limits in the air and on the ground.

the flying sequences are some of the best ever filmed, and they still have the power to excite and amaze. also, the soundtrack is packed with 80s hits, perfectly capturing the film's energy and spirit.

unfortunately, the plot (in 2023) is a bit simple and predictable, especially in the film's second half. at the same time, some of the female characters are a bit one-dimensional.

overall, "top gun" is a classic film that is still very watchable today. it's a fun, exciting, and visually stunning movie that will indeed please fans of action films.

rating: 7.5 out of 10.

this is probably a top 10 80s film through and through. an excellent cast, story, and special effects for the time are phenomenal. tom cruise leads a stellar group of top gun pilots through the most rigorous flight school known to man.

tony scott pulls off one of the greatest visual feats of the 1980s that still looks excellent today.

the music and score can be a little cheesy and the cliches are surely there but this here is a real piece of americana. for the time, it was hands down the greatest flight film of all time.

this film alone pretty much molded tom cruise and val kilmer into household names.

i decided to rewatch this movie before watching the new one (top gun maverick) that came out this year. not that it was really necessary as i remember most of it. i'm surprised some reviewers weren't impressed by top gun. for 1986, you have to consider the year it was made, it's a pretty spectacular movie. it's not really the story that is impressive, even though it's not bad, but the flying shots. the air time scenes are just top notch. as for the acting with a cast like that it just can't be bad. top gun was a sensation the year it came out, and that was justified. even after all those years as soon as the first tune can be heard you immediately get nostalgic of the eighties. the oscar for best music, even though not really my genre, is deserved you could say as it stood time. next top gun maverick, looking forward to it when you see the extremely high ratings it gets.

so i aim to watch top gun: maverick this week and in my preparation i thought i would go back and watch the original top gun and here is my review for it. the premise of the film sees a young cocky upstart join a school for fighter pilots where he has to learn plenty about himself in order to truly thrive.

main character tom cruise plays maverick and this is one of his more iconic roles and he gives a really fun performance. his young, confident performance fits the character really well and you can't help but gravitate towards maverick, the film then explores more into his character and you do end up caring for him and want to see him have a good ending.

supporting characters anthony edwards plays goose, him and cruise are fantastic together and have a great on screen chemistry. you feel this relationship and friendship has been crafted over many years and the two actors are really good with edwards giving as energetic a performance as cruise. val kilmer places iceman and you can see how he is the polar opposite of maverick, he is more cold and calculated instead of the risky attitude of maverick. though he is pretty much the villain of the film, you understand where he is coming from and he is just trying to do the best for himself and his wingman. kelly mcgillis plays charlie who is the main love interest and she is good in the film. i like their relationship and how it develops throughout the film, she is a cool character and a good love companion. tom skerrit plays the main instructor and he is just a really cool guy, who treats his students fair but clearly cares and wanting them to succeed.

story the story is pretty basic, it really focuses on the romance and it works pretty well. the dynamic between the two actors work well and it is a well functioning romance. the dogfights are pretty cool and the characters do get time and it feels like they are fleshed out well enough. i just wish the film had spent more time focusing on the training school and a bit less on the romance, i felt like actually seeing them work through top gun more would have been really cool.

script the script is pretty well handled, yes it is extremely cheesy and at times that does come across too much but it fits the film. the film has decent drama and humour, it is just some of it feels too much and like it isn't serious enough.

style for a film that came out in 1986, the plane fight scenes are fantastic and feel really epic in scale, you feel like you are sitting with maverick & goose in the cockpit. the film also has an amazing soundtrack which has become iconic over the years, it really gets you into what is happening on screen.

overall overall, top gun is a great film that has stood the test of time. if you are one of the few who hasn't seen it then i would suggest a watch, especially with the great buzz around top gun: maverick.

rating - 8/10.

top gun is a good movie with a decent storyline and a good cast.it was my first time seeing the movie,i since its so well known i expected it to be a lot better,tom cruise did deliver a great performance however,but this movie is so cheesy,there's constant singing to feel good songs and a cliché love story to it as well.i don't really like val kilmer as an actor,mainly because he was the worst batman ever,but he delivered a pretty solid performance as iceman.

the only thing i disliked is that it is basically propaganda for the military. i can't even imagine how many young men watched this movie as young boys and dreamed of becoming fighter pilots (a dream many boys share, apparently, but very hard to do. i was horrified at the very thought of trying to fly over obstacles (mountains in nevada in the film) while trying to evade another aircraft, all while being subjected to extreme g force at over 800 miles an hour) so i must say this film did increase my respect of the men (and a couple of women) who are able to accomplish this feat.

typical hollywooded, larger-than-life blockbuster from the mid-80s. this movie is a must see for cruise fans. one of the best soundtracks of the 80s. kelly mcgillis, val kilmer, and tom skeritt give one of the best performances of their careers. of course it is not an accurate depiction of top gun as some have pointed out .... it is a movie made for pure entertainment value.

top gun was the "king of cool" in the 1980s thanks to the self-satisfied performance of tom cruise as hotshot "jock" pilot peter "maverick" mitchell. the film revels in mitchell's arrogant disregard for rules (he is a walking section eight), from his absurd guidance of a terrified comrade onto the deck of the uss enterprise (this despite the fact maverick's f-14 lacks the fuel to land itself) through the remarkably weak punishments he gets for breaking such rules as hitting on his dod instructor (kelly mcguiness) to getting his radar intercept officer "goose" bradshaw (er's anthony edwards) killed in a thoroughly stupid contest with tim "iceman" kazansky (val kilmer) over who will be first to "kill" the enemy plane late in the navy's top gun dogfighting exercises; the film wimps out badly when, in this incident, maverick's flying through iceman's jetwash (thus killing his own engines and leading to the ejection punch-out where goose slams into the cockpit canopy and severs his windpipe) is more accidental than anything; the scene should have been clearly 100% the fault of maverick, since he practically sticks his f-14's nose into iceman's thrusters.

but if it were thus portrayed accurately, then the film comes to an end, with maverick grounded or even dishonorably discharged, thus underlining the weakness of playing up maverick as incapable of discipline. throughout the film maverick acts in thoroughly unprofessional manner (any pilot who performed a close-in flyby on a tower would be court-martialed) and never is called on it except in the most perfunctory and insincere fashion, not even when goose bradshaw pleads with him early on that he, goose, can't afford to blow the opportunity presented to him.

cruise and mcguiness are not worth investing the time needed to watch the film; the real stars are the supporting cast - tom skerritt, michael ironside, anthony edwards, val kilmer, and rick rossovich - and the superb aerial dogfight footage; the use of f-5s as soviet migs is a bit distracting, since the f-5s don't look at all like soviet warplanes. also annoying is the lack of role of the backseaters, who do more than just read radar screens in the f-14's cockpit. kenny loggins' famous theme song is a treat, but not really appropriate for the film.

if you can overlook the weak leads and focus on the supporting cast and the aerial footage, you're in for an entertaining dogfighting spectacle.

even though 1986's top gun received mixed reviews from critics upon release, it is one of those feel-good movies that is fun, fun, and even more fun. imagine it is 2010 and you are in the midst of watching a michael bay movie. a movie with striking cinematography, expertly crafted action scenes, but middling human character development. yeah, this film is one of the precursors to bay-directed movies, but this film definitely works. some people may complain about the film's machismo or pro-military stance, but i always been told it is one of those required viewings for any male. it definitely was in my household. even though the characters are middling and not fully developed, they are really memorable. after all, the film launched tom cruise's hollywood career. the action sequences, more specifically, the aerial dogfights are incredible. they are expertly shot, and it made you feel like you were a part of the action.

the film received its humble beginning from a magazine article in a 1983 edition of california, which was written by ehud yonay. his article went into detail about the life of fighter pilots on a naval air base in san diego. producing partners jerry bruckheimer and don simpson were very interested in the content, which featured some outstanding aerial views. they hired jim cash and jack epps jr. to write the first draft. they hired tony scott as the film's director. yes, that is ridley's younger brother. scott impressed the producers with his commercial featuring a turbo racing a fighter jet. it is impressive that the producers made this big-budget film scott's first film. in terms of action, scott definitely delivered.

pete mitchell codenamed "maverick" (tom cruise) is a very talented pilot who is accepted in the nation's top school, known as "top gun." maverick has to compete with the best of the very best in order to earn top honors. he meets a possible romantic partner in his astrophysics professor, charlie (kelly mcgillis). also, he meets his rival from the get-go, the intelligent and studious iceman (val kilmer). also dealing with the people associated with his school, he is also haunted by his father's death and legend, which may or may not seem as heroic. maverick wants to be the very best. will he reach that status?

the film is at its best when the jets are in the air. but we cannot forget the film does have human characters. the screenplay does not give much time to develop the characters. the relationships with one another are paper thin. do not get me started on the relationship between maverick and charlie. it was ludicrous. with all that said...i had a great time watching these characters because the performances are solid. cruise has always been great playing the cocky womanizer and continues that sort of character here. too bad he couldn't show much chemistry with kelly mcgillis who previously exceled with harrison ford in 1985's witness. i did like the chemistry between cruise and best friend, goose (played by anthony edwards). val kilmer as iceman makes a great antagonist for cruise. i did like tom skerritt who played viper, a father figure for cruise.

the soundtrack! i really enjoyed it. kenny loggins contributed with his rendition of "danger zone", a high-octane song! the song that won the oscar was berlin's "take my breath away." that song introduced them to the music world and it really is a good song. those two songs are some of the reasons why i enjoyed this movie. alas, we cannot forget the scene where maverick and goose sings the righteous brothers.

personally, i found top gun to be excellent entertainment. i know some people think the film is hot garbage because it does not have a credible script and the characters are poorly developed. but come on, there is an awesome volleyball scene! that has to count for something, right? despite the characters, at least the performances were on point. the aerial sequences were something else. when the airplanes are in the air, that is when to keep your eyes peeled. the studio shelled thousands of dollars to use these planes so they made it worth the high bill. the movie was the highest grossing film of 1986. it gave people new reasons to be "cool."

my grade: b+

to appreciate the full effect of this movie, i think you have to have seen it in the theater, with the bass track vibrating your seat. tom cruise wasn't yet as crazy off-screen. the balance of action, humor, and a little love story makes it the perfect weekend night/date night movie. both, it may not be oscar worthy, but it never professed to be. this is the movie i watch to make sure my sound is where i want it (along with the opening of star wars). if i can't feel it, it isn't right. watch and enjoy. some of it is forgettable, but it has multiple iconic scenes that will always be with me.

after decades, i watched top gun again (i saw the 3d version, and by the way, the conversion is incredibly well done) and i'm both deeply impressed and, on the other hand, quite shaken.

the editing is still impressive, as are the scenes, for example, on the aircraft carrier and in the air, which still hold up even today.

add to that the brilliant and timeless music (action scenes: e.g., "danger zone").

when was the last time a film came out of the usa where every song became a timeless hit?

less good, and at times downright embarrassing, is the overacting of the "cool" guys. some scenes, like the one in the bar, are genuinely cringe-worthy.

however, there are also scenes where they toned down the exaggeration and pseudo-cool nonsense. and those scenes are really good: for instance, the moment when tom cruise (who still had a lot to learn as an actor back then) meets the wife of his deceased comrade, played by meg ryan, after his death. instead of overblown emotional outbursts, the scene is crafted in a way that you can see cruise holding back his tears. meg ryan rounds off the scene perfectly. it's a truly great scene that brilliantly shows how less can be more and how realism has a timeless impact.

it also shows what the film could have been if they had avoided the overblown, embarrassing macho scenes and instead stayed realistic.

i was shaken, however, when i saw the still-iconic "take my breath away" scene with the motorcycle ride to his beloved, where cruise knocks on the veranda: that's exactly how things were in the 80s and 90s!

it was, after the dull, drug-riddled, and downtrodden 70s with their shaggy hair and awful music, a wonderful time: full of zest for life without drugs, sunny, where the youth could still discover life for themselves!

what's so unsettling is that looking back through this film made it painfully clear what the youth have been robbed of over the past 20 years or so: the sexualization of children, feminist indoctrination starting already in schools, and the flooding with foreigners, so that no sense of belonging or home remains. it shows how the usa went from being a great role model that everyone aspired to emulate to a place where the lowest is elevated to the top, and the bastion of freedom has been transformed into a politically correct tyranny.

even hollywood!

because, as weak as some scenes may be: back then in hollywood, the people in charge still had a sense of aesthetics and an appreciation for beautiful people! even that is something hollywood can't manage anymore today.

a film from a truly better time.

this movie is one of my favorite of all time. it's a classic. =) i mean, you have fast planes and hot guys. what could be better?? with tom cruise playing maverick, val kilmer playing iceman, and anthony edwards playing goose, you have an all star cast but before they were stars. an all around great movie.

tony scott's exciting romantic drama about a pilot school has often been deemed a modern classic, and a quentissential part of film history - and i would very much agree.

tom cruise is a good actor, yet somewhat uneven, sometimes being dragged down by less-than-stellar scripts - but when he's good, he's very good, and this film is one of his better roles, giving a great performances and being complemented by the supporting cast to expertise.

"top gun" is a 1986 action drama directed by tony scott starring tom cruise and kelly macgillis. over the years and against my own expectations, tom cruise has by now become one of my favourite actors of all time. while jake gyllenhaal still wears the crown and will forever defend the top spot, cruise is very close behind him and comes second place. even though many people complain that he isn't quite the most versatile and talented actor in the business, i still got to say that he has an incredible acting range and makes a variety of films that are all extremely enjoyable to me. from his undying, action orientated role as ethan hunt in the "mission impossible" franchise over his dramatic performances in films such as "interview with the vampire" or "magnolia" to his fairly underrated ability as a comedy actor, as seen in "tropic thunder", the man is more talented and versatile than people declare him to be. that's why i love him as an artist, he has the skills, is charismatic as hell and always a joy to see on screen. by now, every single film of him i have seen so far has been at least entertaining, and on the fifty-eighth birthday of this apparently immortal legend i have tackled probably his most iconic film of all time. to my utter astonishment, the flick wasn't even as well-received as i thought it was, from what i have heard before, the film is generally located in the airspace of mediocrity. is it really that unbearable, though? i got down to the bottom of this question and i have personally drawn the conclusion that i understand both sides and all the points of criticism, but boy, i unexpectedly loved it so much. in this film that basically depicts the competition of students at the flight school for extremely gifted pilots, we get everything a well-balanced pop corn flick from the mid-eighties needs. the focus of course lies on the glamour boy peter "maverick" mitchell, charmingly portrayed by the twenty-four-year-old cruise, and how he wants to be the very best (like no one ever was) in the naval aviator business. i definitely cannot speak on the behalf of everyone, but his character is utterly likable and someone i immediately could find a connection to. as if it was done purposely, he lives up to his own name and is quite an idiosyncratic personality. regardless of his apparently god given talents as a pilot, he is extremely reckless, arrogant, cocky and a true daredevil writ large. despite all of those rather negative traits and being a tremendous danger for himself and everyone around, he still manages to bring the audience on his side with his sheer charisma and, most importantly, by the other side of his overall pretentious nature. against my own expectations, beneath all his outward coolness, also a severe turmoil of a haunted soul lies dormant. as the son of the myth-enshrouded pilot duke mitchell who mysteriously vanished on his last mission, he tries to follow in his own father's footsteps and always wants to be the best to both make his father proud and make up for the lack of acknowledgement of a father figure that has never been there for him. yes, behind this overconfident and smug smile hides a disturbed boy who still struggles to cope with the unresolved death of his dad, and hence does all he does in an extreme manner, just to come as close to him as possible. it is only a minimal undertone, but if you are aware of it, it gives every breath-taking scene in the sky a subliminally saddening meaning. as one of his fellow pilots remarks, he is indeed always flying against a ghost as soon as he is in the air. this tragic effect increases even more after the devastating death of his co-pilot and best friend goose, the man he claims to be his own family he has left, and even though his passing seems to not bother him that much on the outside, you can see it in mav's eyes and by cruise's acting that he is extremely tortured by the fact that he has no one left in his life, except for maybe one. speaking of relationships, another aspect that made me fall in love with this film is how it establishes its individuals and its overall character constellation. what mav and goose have is another prime example of friendship goals, his rivalry with iceman is defined by subtle aversion and yet full of professional respect and his relationship to love interest and instructor charlie feels pleasantly genuine. in terms of romance, amity and enmity the film has done everything right and i liked every single iconic character here. even if they without a doubt contribute a lot to the film's reputation of being a classic, it is not the critical factor for its status. the scenes that take place in the air deserve this honour. i am not sure if its true, but i have the feeling that this kind of cinematography must have been ground-breaking in eighty-six. the camera work and visual effects (if there are any) are undoubtedly breath-taking and simply stunning to look at. as if the dogfights in the beginning that are part of the training are not already utterly exciting enough, the film steps up its game in the final act when the newly graduated students have to go into their first serious combat, and this is also the moment when the inner conflict of maverick concludes. once again, on the outside it is still a serious mission and an extreme danger to the rookie aviators, but it also functions as a confrontation for mav, the perfect opportunity to face and leave behind his past. still reminded of his own mortality and vulnerability after the tragic incident, he is still traumatized and not confident enough, but as soon as his mates need him he brings himself to overcome what haunts him the most and do what is necessary: fly like a maverick. of course, the film has a happy ending, but it was the only proper way to let this personal catharsis end. all in all, this iconic flick manages the balancing act between awesome and stunning action and touching and profound drama, between airborne excitement and grounded greatness. it works as both, a pop corn flick to shut your brains off to and a subliminal character drama, and thanks to likeable characters, a talented cast and a decent leading performance by cruise, it becomes something that conjures a smile on my face. of course, it isn't flawless and has some minor issues, as it is rushed at times and confusingly edited, but it has enough other factors that make up for it. on top of that, it is surprisingly metaphorical, as it also deals with serious question that its protagonist asks himself throughout: will you stay on the ground or will you fly back up? it is an uplifting tale about overcoming grief and loss, and yet it is popcorn cinema that also knows to entertain in a straightforward way. it cannot be denied that it is cheesy, but like a wheel of cheddar, it isn't only good-looking but also utterly delicious and simply too good to pass on. it has a phenomenal soundtrack, a packing and touching atmosphere and is extremely enjoyable. this isn't only a film to watch and forget, it is the feeling of a generation, a movie that elevated itself in the list of favourite films of cinephiles around the world. even if i am a professed admirer of tom cruise and it might appear a little overrated to some, this film is without a doubt one you must have seen at least once in your lifetime.

i saw this film in 1986 on a big screen with state of the art thx sound. i remember admiring the technical achievement but not liking the movie all that much. i thought it glorified a bunch of arrogant self-entitled brats. this was before the millennials came along!

saw it again yesterday and was surprised by how much i enjoyed it. part of it was because it validated the sensibilities of my youth. today's young people might find it tacky and the jokes corny. but this was my generation, and yes, we were cool once!

although it now looks somewhat humble compared to the production value of today's blockbusters, there is a certain innocence and sweetness to this movie that did not come across at all the first time. it was a simpler time back then. one interesting observation is that the interactions among the pilots is now perceived as homo-erotic. back then, it was seen as just good clean camaraderie and friendship.

the one problem that now i have with this film is the way it treats the token non-white character. as if referring to the black aviator as sundown isn't offensive enough, he also turns out to be the only character that maverick gets physically rough with. that is the one thing about the period's sensibilities that i don't miss.

looking forward to seeing the new one when it comes out on home video!

top gun. a classic 80s movie i meant to see for years. it had super familiar music like "danger zone" and "take my breath away". i heard that they were making a sequel to the film, and i made it a mission to see the original first. i checked it out from the local library and watched in on my ps4. unfortunately for me, when i saw it the first time, i didn't like it. i think that was because i had just come back from a long exhausting day and i couldn't dive into the movie.

top gun is one of the defining films of the 80's. it was released in the summer of 86 and just marketed as a summer fun at the movies with cool fighter jets and cool dudes. along with back to the future(s) and arguably indiana jones raiders of the lost ark, top gun was another barely pg-rated hit and one of the most successful and iconic films of the 1980's. it epitomized the high testosterone, military hero-action genre that went on to inspire many similar movies that proceeded it (though none were even close to achieving top gun's success and popularity).

top gun is an underdog story. it magnifies how rebels and misfits can be ostracized from their due credit for not playing by the rules, while in the end, anyone acknowledging the truth can't deny they may be more talented than the actual winner. it's depicted toward the end when one of the pilots asks the flight instructor if maverick was really the best (and they seem to know it), even though he had emotional problems for several reasons. this is the kind of story that people who like underdog stories can be a fan of, although it's not anywhere as stark as the rocky underdog boxing story.

this is a movie whose only purpose is to entertain by making a cool action blockbuster that at the time was fairly impressive visually. it delves into camaraderie, brotherhood amongst military members, competition, and pursuit of being the best, as well as how thinking outside of the box can have its benefits. there are definitely some emotional scenes in it and lots of quotable lines.

back in the 80's, studios didn't churn out as many films as they do today so when a movie hit the theatres, it was going to be one of the few for that year. it was an attempt at quality over quantity, which eventually set the stage for the 90's hits and successes. so imagine being a kid or a teenager in the mid 80s with no streaming sites, only movie theatres, and your family or friends just want to go to the movie theatre for fun one night and you went to see this. it was a cool movie to watch. it had stunts, action, explosions, cool lines, cool actors that many young kids wanted to be as cool as (everyone had their favorites whether goose, iceman, viper, hollywood, merlin, or maverick), and a somewhat cringeworthy sex scene.

but most of all, perhaps, it had a truly awesome soundtrack. to this day, it can be argued that this is the best movie soundtrack of all time. from the theme music to berlin's smash hit, "take my breath away" to other really classic rock hits of the 80's, it was really popular. nobody can hear tmba without recalling top gun. it was essential 80's viewing for 80's movie fans.

so it's a very iconic, successful, and nostalgic 80's summer blockbuster action flick, but don't expect to see anything oscar-worthy in way of performances or story. it was more like an "event" where you had to be there to understand its notoriety. it also had a truly star-studded cast with meg ryan, tom skerrit, mcgillis, edwards, kilmer, rossovich, and cruise.

the sequel being released this week will be nostalgic, and i wouldn't be surprised if it's hugely successful at the box office. if it really is an improvement of the first one as many critics have put it, then it would deserve to be.

a fun well made tom cruise film from the 1980s. the flight sequences hold up really well, real jets, filmed from the air. it's amazing to watch those sequences. the actual story itself wasn't as good as the rest of it. still a good film overall. the film has a great opening, which could have been the finale of the film but it's just getting started. the colours and uses of filters in the beginning look amazing. it's like in half the film the sun is either setting or we're in the magic hour.

top gun in 4k is a picture that is a touch rough around the edges but still looks fabulous. most of the film takes place in clear daylight and it looks fantastic. you can see every drop of sweat on a characters face in the closeups you see. the films action is so well directed, i'm thinking of the aircraft sequences, the way it's shot, the director gets the camera up into the air with those planes, it's not all shot on the ground or with some awful 1940s rear projection, or purely from the cockpit.

colours are very distinctive in this film it's like one perpetual sunset, a great use of filters, the soundtrack is fun. the look of the film is also pretty iconic, with big aviator sunglasses, motorbikes - it's jingoistic and proudly pro american the story is one of rivalry, maverick - tom cruise is a hot shot super talented pilot, but must learn to control his ego and work better as a team player. in that sense it's a lot like an officer and a gentleman.

the antics though of what goes on outside the cockpit resemble more something from a high school zany antics and mad characters with attitude. kelly mcgillis is excellent in her role and gets a great character to work with. a common critique of this movie is it's more an armed forces commercial than a film. colours look incredible, lovely warm hues, sunset, great detail in the picture, the clothing, the hair texture, the soundtrack is awesome berlin - take my breath away is used for the steamy romance stuff.

it was silly the lengths the film went to in order to cruise look taller, just accept him for his height. the dialogue is so direct it's quite cheesy but again it's of it's era. they weren't trying to make a serious drama but a fun action film. it was pretty influential as a film, in terms of fashion too, which means you know you've mad an impact. you can sort of see why this film was so popular in the 80s reflecting american military confidence and strength, a recovery of national pride of events in the 70s. i never cared too deeply about maverick but it was still an excellent transition for cruise away from the teen role towards more adult material. two years later he was in rain man one of the best films of the 1980s.

so, here we are in 2022 and top gun (1986), finally gets a sequel, with top gun: maverick (2022). tom cruise returns for more fun in the skies. that doesn't really matter so much when it comes to this film. i personally didn't need a sequel to this film, in order to get excited about watching this film again. i already have seen this film, at least, a half-a-dozen times in my life, but i watched it again, just the same, for the purposes of this review. this film hasn't changed much at all for me, since i saw it in the theaters back in 1986. i have the same respect and the same concerns today, that i had for it back then. that includes all the repeat viewings i've done on the film since then. this film is what it is. it is a 1980s-charged, action film, complete with the biggest actor from the modern age of film leading the way, an mtv styled pace, great music and plenty of action to go with it.

this film is still a good film. it is an iconic film also. it represents some of the best elements found in 1980s action dramas. it is still a cheesy film though. you could even see the cheese elements in the movie back in the 80s. it wasn't fooling anybody back then either. i remember going to the theater with my high school buddies, when the film was initially released and chuckling at it, for being slightly silly. it mostly stems from the overemphasized romantic plotline, that brings the film to a screeching halt in some places. but, once those aspects get out of the way, the film rocks on, with some great music from kenny loggins, great aviation action and tense military situations, perfect for the cold war atmosphere, that was prevalent in the 1980s. it also has plenty of testosterone nonsense for the ladies to enjoy as well.

maverick (cruise) and his partner goose (anthony edwards), get accepted into the elite aviation training program known as top gun. a place were the best of the best pilots vie for the coveted title of being the top gun. during their training, they run into all the other tribulations of life, such as love, family, death and disappointment. the cast is perfect, consisting of talent like tom skerrit (viper), michael ironside (jester) and val kilmer (iceman). tom cruise's maverick impresses you as much as he annoys you. his talent is immeasurable, his bravery is excellent, but his ego makes you want to smack the crap out of him. kenny loggins "danger zone" theme and berlin's "take my breath away", won many awards and made a lot of money. berlin would go on and win the academy award for best song. now in 2022, as the great critical reviews and amazing fan appreciation come out for top gun: maverick (2022), the more superior sequel proves the theory, that if you remove the cheese, you may have a huge hit on your hands. as for this film, it paved the way towards a better future.

top gun is one of the most iconic movies of the 1980s, a story where the navy's elite fighter weapons school students compete to be the best in the class. one of the students, maverick (tom cruise), fights the attitudes of the other pilots and struggles to be the best pilot, all the while forming a relationship with civilian instructor charlie blackwood (kelly mcgillis).

this is one of those movies i saw once when i was a little kid. while i don't remember much of it, i do recall finding maverick's daring character interesting as he strives to stand out and the romance between him and charlie to be a good piece of chemistry for this action-adventure movie. the dogfighting scenes with the f-14a tomcats are well-choreographed and tom cruise is a "go getter" in his maverick role. his love/hate friendship formed with his comrades provided a nice touch of sportsmanship and heartfelt drama. actors tom skerritt, val kilmer and meg ryan all rounded up what is a pretty good cast of characters with some stellar acting.

tony scott is out of his mind. i love this movie.

from the magnificent soundtrack packed with several 80's hits and chart toppers to a notoriously memorizable script start to finish, top gun epitomized blockbuster movie making in the 80s. tom cruise's stardom took off because every boy or guy for that matter wanted to be as cool as maverick and get the girl (kelly mcgillis) while flying mock 10 with their hair on fire and getting caught up in 4g inverted dives with mig-28's while keeping up foreign relations by giving them the bird (yes, we know it's the finger, goose).

meg ryan makes one of her earliest if not first major roles as goose's wild wife. goose is played by a young anthony edwards (er) and was a lovable character whose fate leaves no one with dry eyes. the star studded cast also included val kilmer and tom skerrit.

this is a movie that welcomes cheesiness for all the right reasons, and it redefined what a summer blockbuster could be and what audiences liked in an action film. newcomers and younger generations will find this hard to believe, but people who grew up in the 80s understand that the movie doesn't have just one, two, or three memorable lines and dialogue; nope- the whole entire movie can be memorized- that is, every single line from beginning to end. it's one of those movies that will never get old. like many, i probably have seen it over 200 times since 1986. it had to be one of the most rented and shown on tv films from the late 80s to 90s on both basic cable and cable, and it is always a fun watch. just pure entertainment that never lets up.

top gun is pure quality for many reasons, be it the hard hitting ballad soundtrack, the magnificent camera work or the great pace of the film. many fans of aviation and aspiring pilots were made purely through watching this classic as children, and after you've watched it, it's easy to see why...

tom cruise stars as maverick, with his youth and charm flawlessly suiting the hotshot protagonist of the film. cruise strikes the perfect balance in presenting maverick as a pilot who lives life on the edge, but isn't totally out of control. kelly mcgillis does a good job too, yet her lack of any truly memorable scenes gives her the appearance of being in cruise's shadow somewhat. the movie's pace is poised well, with quieter, slower scenes slotting in between the more intense action sequences. this neatly brings us onto the camera work, which is simply out of this world. the f14s are shot in splendid aerial sequences where they perform all manner of crazy manoeuvres and stunts in summery locations. the scenes involving maverick's bike in particular seem to evoke the strong sense of youth found throughout the film. the soundtrack is marvellous and remains famous to this day, with vintage classics by artists such as the righteous brothers intermixed with 80s rock ballads and quieter melodies for the more sombre scenes. unlike many modern action films, tony scott gives maverick genuine obstacles and tribulations to overcome, which invokes a much greater sense of fulfilment and maturity by the picture's conclusion.

top gun has inspired future pilots all around the world and continues to do so. it's a film of passion, energy and youth, but also of learning and coming of age. those born after the film's era may find themselves wishing they'd been alive through it, as not many films capture the vibrancy of the 80s, or the excitement of being a pilot, like top gun does.

pete mitchell, a.k.a. maverick is known as a navy pilot who's not afraid to take risks. mostly because he creates the risks himself. his controversial reputation should get him kicked out, but instead he gets accepted into top gun, an elite fighter school. but to get accepted turns out to mean more just being a joyriding daredevil...

top gun is without a doubt the most macho movie ever made. i could name all arnold action movies on one arm, and none would even come close. you get everyone talking tough towards each other, sweaty half-naked bodies, lots of shower discussion sequences, everyone acting like their own ladies' man, and absolutely fearless attitudes. save for goose.

of course, this means it's going to be very cheesy. i found myself laughing at points because of how hard everyone tried to be cool, and the music choices for the romantic scenes. best of all though has to be maverick pulling off his smile every time he get uncomfortably close hitting on charlie. oh, charlie is a woman. don't worry though, there are plenty of homoerotic undertones throughout anyway. i love the friendship between maverick and goose, they are the kind of friends who get silly with each other as often as they act endearingly sympathetic towards each other's struggles.

it was actually pretty sad when he died.

which brings me to arguably the most interesting section, that being when maverick starts to feel some guilt. he's not invisible anymore. and he realizes jet pilot flying is not a game. cruise shows some of his refined acting skills when we see him unable to move on, his confidence dropping like a domb in hiroshima. it makes him more sympathetic, since we know that anyone who goes through a tragic event can get to that point.

the best performance goes to tom skeritt, who is very likeable as the instructor viper. he avoids being the cliché character who makes life even tougher for maverick, instead serving as his mentor. when everyone else thinks he's nothing more than a dangerous nutcase, viper believes in him.

kelly mcgillis does a good job as the love interest charlie, and her character is also decent for the most part (i'll get to the latter later on), and while the scenes between her and maverick do follow the regular conventions, you believe in the chemistry between them.

the music is welldone, with lots of memorable tunes playing (especially during the training sequences), really managing to get you pumped up. they do overuse danger zone a little, but it's still a great song.

do i have anything bad to say about the film? i guess the first thing would be that at first i didn't really get into the characters. it felt like they were just showing off to each other or doing spit-takes at first, which made me feel like the writers were having a little too much fun trying to be clever. but after a while you start to like them, and iceman goes from ice cold to well... medium-temperature water.

i thought the only weak part of the last act where maverick feels guilty over himself is how charlie reacts to it. it's like, wow! ease up! the man has been through a lot of shìt! maybe the best way to motivate someone who's been through a tragedy isn't to harshly call them a coward. i would've liked to see her offer an apology at the end. but thankfully, viper comes with some very nice advice and understands how he feels.

i think that's all i have to say. it's unpretentiously fun, go check it out.

pros: 1. tom cruise (maverick), val kilmer (ice), anthony edwards (goose) and kelly mcgillis (charlie) all provide incredibly magnetic performances.

2. there is electric chemistry between tom cruise and kelly mcgillis, to the point where even the prolonged pauses between them sizzles with energy.

3. the jet fighter scenes are amazingly choreographed and edited masterfully to create a lot of tension and excitement.

4. the death of goose is suitably heart-breaking particularly with the aftermath of it seeing maverick being deeply afflicted and affected from the loss.

5. the film delivers an inspiring message of never giving up despite how tough it gets as well as highlighting the importance of learning to improve and show humility, even when you think you're the best.

6. the editing with its fast cutting helps to imbue the action scenes with more virility.

cons: 1. the soundtrack is far too incessant.

2. occasionally the dialogue is a little too cheesy and annoying.

well known as the picture that turned tom cruise into an international icon and coming with one of the great memorable soundtracks, "top gun" is an enjoyable first-rate eighties movie.

maverick (cruise) and his best friend goose (anthony edwards) are two cocky, talented pilots working in the us navy. after they succeed in rescuing a fellow pilot who nearly died in mid-air combat, their commanding officer stinger (james tolkan) decides to send them to top gun, a top flying school that trains the best of the best of the us navy's fighter pilots...

the plot is in some ways a parallel to "an officer and a gentlemen", which was made much earlier in the decade. both movies are set inside a flight school, both have a troubled central character (in that movie it was richard gere, here it's tom cruise) who must confront their past and negotiate a romance in the course of the movie. the main character in both movies has a best friend who comes to a tragic end, and both movies feature a very memorable romantic theme song.

in terms of plot and characters, "top gun" is ever so slightly inferior to the earlier movie. the main strength in the cast is cruise, who holds the movie up with likable charm and strong inner intensity. kelly mcgillis is slightly stilted as his love interest. she performs the role well, but she cannot really compete with cruise. because of this, the romance holds no real frisson and it is only the soundtrack playing in the background of their love scenes that allows the relationship to generate any chemistry.

anthony edwards does well in the role of goose, but his character is too underdeveloped that when he eventually meets his tragic fate it lacks the impact that it should. tom skerrit, micheal ironside and james tolkan are fine as the flight school commanders and val kilmer is enjoyable arrogant as maverick's rival iceman.

the brilliantly shot dogfight sequences give a stirring and disorienting realistic feel of real-life airborne combat, and these combined with the searingly memorable title track "take my breath away" are the picture's technical highlights.

flashy 80s, glossy 80s, voice-over with a raspy virile voice 80s... the reagan era or the time where business meant success and success meant business, and the days with moody depressing post-vietnam auteurism were over. it all started with "rocky"; and in a way there's a lot in the story of "top gun" -written by jim cash and jack epps jr., and inspired by an article titled "top guns"- that follows the pattern of "rocky iii": rise to success, accomplishment, doubt, overcoming your demons, and in fact getting even better than if you had stayed in your zone of comfort.

now, there are reasons why "top gun" is such a cult-classic. think about it: "iceman", "maverick", "take my breath away" or just the first synthetic notes, there's also that death i won't spoil but that still upsets many fans because the character was so damn likable... the uniforms, the special effect, the motorcycle rides, hell, the face of a young baby-faced cruise... the fact that these elements, these brandnames of coolness, are still celebrated today by legions of movie fans and even mentioned in no-less memorable movies and tv shows, or that many us navy pilots enlisted after watching the film, say a lot about the cultural impact of "top gun"... and many other things.

and yet "top gun" was dismissed at the time of its release and maybe the release of "hot shots!" was the final blow to the film's legacy as a legitimate drama, but we're in 2022, and maybe this is one of these cases where you can paraphrase that old saying about doctors "roger ebert criticized the love story and the parts on the ground, pauline kael called it a 'commercial' film, but what do they know?" i have the utmost respect for these two distinguished critics but they missed the mark that time. the film is far from being flawless but it is designed in such a way that it's like it knew it was going to be relevant. and yes it was commercial but who cares when the story is the placed product (except maybe for "the emoji movie").

indeed, it's not about tom cruise alone, not about the cool-sounding call-names not even about the aerial effects which are impressive (and still hold up today) but it's the combination of these factors, the story it tells, the way for one hundred minutes, the film makes you want to be part of a team, where everyone's young, competent and take the job seriously. so seriously that one doesn't hesitate to quit when he feels like losing the edge. indeed, in our self-deprecating victimhood time, there's something fresh about a film where everyone wants to be at the top. like an oasis of idealistic competence emerging out the crass averageness. why and who they fight is totally immaterial to the story (something its own parody "hot shots!" insisted to show), the point is that these guys love their jobs.

i'm not surprised that the film contributed to an increase in applications to the us aviation forces. if you grew up in the 90s, you remember these old cheesy commercials with men running in slow motions, engineers working with a misty sunrise in the background, that's the "top gun" effect. any ad for joining an army borrows from that opening scene in "top gun". now i must say i saw "top gun" once when i was 10 but i had "hot shots" recorded, so rediscovering it was like finally getting ahold on the source and yes everything in this film is begging for being replicated: the rivalry between cruise and val kilmer, the tension that is certainly more palpable than the chemistry with kelly mcgillis, the past secret, the nervous sweating and cigar-chumping commander played by james tokian who was born to play angry authority figures and maybe the homoerotic subtext of the volley ball that has been quite exaggerated to tell the truth.

but what the film gets right is the spectacular action sequences, i just watched 1949 "twelve o'clock high" and i was frustrated by how desperately lacking in battles it was, that's not to say that the fight are always easy to follow but we know what is a radar interceptor, a wingman and we know way too well what the troubles caused from an canopy malfunction... the narrative in the film is pretty linear and conventional but it's done in a way that works because unlike the peck movie (take my word for granted), we care and we know the characters.

maverick is the cocky rebel who's got something to prove, iceman the rival who never loses his cool and hides behind an enigmatic smile the fear that this wise-guy might steal his thunder, he's not actually an antagonist but perhaps the competitive guy who acknowledges his worth, in others situations, they would be best friends but that spot is occupied by anthony edwards ,with more facial hair (and less hair period) than in "e. r.", steals the show as goose, tom skerrit is the respected and caring superior and meg ryan was a brief little sunshine.

i agree that the romance isn't exactly the film's strongest suit and seems like designed as an afterthought in order to plug the "take my breath away" song, (good call, it won the oscar) as it's true that if she was just a friend and a coach it wouldn't have made the film any less good and wouldn't have provided arguments for dismissing it. but apart from that little malfunction, the film's got the right stuff and as showy and commercial as tony scott's directing was, it sure worked with the content.

you'll struggle to find a more cheesy film, even so 'top gun' is a super film.

i need to check out more of tony scott's work because he has yet to let me down from the flicks of his that i've seen; on that note i'd put this below 'crimson tide' and unstoppable', but it is still one of his best i'm sure. the action is great, as is the pacing and music; even with "take my breath away" being slightly overused at one point.

tom cruise is excellent in the lead role, no doubt the perfect choice to play maverick. kelly mcgillis, val kilmer, anthony edwards, tom skerritt, michael ironside... ace cast! tim robbins, andy dufresne himself, is even involved too. they all commit to their roles and give noteworthy performances.

'top gun: maverick' is literally right around the corner. i'm expecting positive things from that sequel.

i think the title says it all. tom cruise has never bettered this performance in my eyes, val kilmer has never achieved quite this level of cool and kelly mcgillis is as fantastic as always.
