i finally got around to watching this in honor of val kilmer and while i'm not usually into these kinds of pro-militaristic action flicks, director tony scott did the most with the material given out. i think the best way to describe top gun is melodrama at its most purely macho, aided largely by the chemistry between tom cruise and anthony edwards' characters. some people have made theories about possible homosexual undertones between the top gun academy students, but i mostly viewed them as sticking out for one another throughout the course. that said, it is strange that cruise's character ended up romancing mcgillis's character so smoothly given their roles as student and teacher, something that i'm sure would easily get you banned from any academy in real life.

if people don't always care too much for the story, at least the actual arial combat sequences are fun to marvel at. one can tell how much time and effort the crew put into elevating the stakes in and outside of the planes, complete with the top notch editing and expertly choreographed sound mixing. plus, harold faltermeyer's score keeps the momentum going with the appropriately fitting action tracks that allow top gun to age well as a cheesy 80s cult classic. all in all, the movie is fun at points but doesn't fly high enough to be truly special, which is still fine in its own right.

"top gun" is a classic from the 80's and before watching the sequel released in 2022, i wanted to refresh my memory. the airplanes sequences are tense and dynamic, you never know what to expect for sure. the photography and the editing are always on point because they looked credible. i was completely immersed in the moment. a lot of modern productions should take this as an example on how to direct good action scenes. the plot has some elements that aged very badly: it has plenty of clichés, typical of that period. the love story between maverick and charlie takes too much screen time, instead of being just a background plot element, as it should be. at times it is cheesy and slightly annoying to go through certain parts, but this has been made more than 35 years ago, so it is perfectly normal to encounter a few things that today would be difficult to see for today's standards. the character development is pretty sloppy and extremely boring. despite everything, this remains a cult. if you are seeking something simple and you want to play it safe i would definitely suggest "top gun". it will entertain you for a couple of hours.

this movie was a great action flick. it had all you ever for an action film between the actors and the action - but that's all it was - action.

perhaps i have read too many drama comments but there are many more action movies out there that are better than topgun but it will always have its cult following. including me sad to say.

i do not agree that this is a 'chick flick' i think it is for us all. looking back now it is interesting to see val kilmer and tom cruise when they were much younger.

all in all a good film but there is better action out there.

as students at the navy's elite fighter weapons school compete to be best in the class, one daring young flyer (tom cruise) learns a few things from a civilian instructor (kelly mcgillis) that are not taught in the classroom.

"top gun" is just one of those must-see 1980s films, very quotable, with a classic cast of tom cruise, anthony edwards, meg ryan and val kilmer, among others. it spawned the popular parody film "hot shots", and remains a hit today despite the fact it focused on a cold war theme that no longer seems relevant.

both john carpenter and david cronenberg allegedly turned down the chance to direct, and we have to wonder how it would have been different. cronenberg would have brought in a whole new audience, probably reducing the popularity while improving the style.

tony scott is first and foremost an action director, which makes him ideal for this film. the film could have been trimmed a bit by reducing the stock footage of the military stuff. and it definitely needed a reduced use of "danger zone" and "take my breath away" (why play the same songs repeatedly?). but overall, it is a fun, light and rather exciting film if you are into dogfights.

if you have not seen "top gun", you really should. it ranks, at least for me, as one of tom cruise's top three most enjoyable films and is definitely at the peak of his career. a good actor he is not, but an essential part of the 1980s he was.

this film, when viewed in retrospect, is symptomatic of the 1980's yuppie culture. when mavrick's best friend dies his girlfriend virtually disowns him and only takes him back when he has some earning potential again (when he regains his mojo, so to speak).

in fact, the phallus plays a crucial role in the film, from it's embodiment in the physical shape of the airplane all the way through to cruise playing with his stout beer bottle in the final scene. and why is it that you have semi-naked men playing beach volleyball hugging one another as often as they possibly can? probably to keep julian clary (and graham norton (if you are american and do not know who julian clary is)) happy....

still, saying that, if you take your brain out of gear and marvel at the production values rather than the script then it's an ok way to pass a couple of hours of your life. do remember though, you'll never get those couple of hours back - so be warned if you hate it and realise after you should've watched a rerun of citizen kane.

top gun is very similar to the movie predator starring arnold schwarzenegger in many respects. when i say that, i mean both of them are pretty mindless movies that basically just serve as popcorn entertainment instead of something that is going to make viewers think intelligently. there's nothing really wrong with this, it just means you shouldn't expect to find some hidden, deeper meaning to this film because you won't find one. at the very least, these types of movies are good solely because of the amount of action scenes put in them which are sure to keep people watching. it's a double edged sword though, because i always feel like the more movies like this i see, the faster my attention span will fade when i watch something more slow-paced. the story of the movie revolves around a pilot in the us navy, lieutenant "maverick" mitchell (tom cruise) and the challenges that come with being a part of the world's most powerful military. as a pilot in the us navy in the 1980s, he is assigned to fly the grumman f-14 tomcat interceptor, a highly advanced jet fighter originally designed to provide cover for aircraft carriers by shooting down soviet bombers with extremely long ranged missiles. right off the bat, there is action in this movie, but no real explanation as to why. enemy mig 28 jets (not a real aircraft) have been spotted close to the carrier, and maverick is sent to stop them. one of his wingmen, cougar, is too stricken with ptsd to land his plane, causing maverick to disobey orders and fly after him. he walks him through the landing process, and once back onboard the ship, cougar resigns. maverick's superior officer then sends him to the navy weapons school in california, named top gun. once the class begins, maverick manages to beat one of his instructors in a mock dogfight, but uses dishonest tactics to do so. this leads to him getting scolded by commander "viper" metcalf. meanwhile, another pilot called iceman does not view maverick in a positive light, and considers him foolish and reckless due to his tendency to ignore orders and fight aggressively. later on, maverick is shown not to be as tough as he appears to be, since viper manages to bait him into a move that puts an enemy pilot on his tail. this demonstrates how important it is to stay with your team when you're in a combat situation. during a similar mission that pits maverick against iceman, maverick's f-14 flies through the jet wash of iceman's plane, causing both his engines to stall. this was a real life (potentially fatal) flaw in the early f-14 models since the pratt and whitney engines were not designed to have their airflows interrupted. maverick's plane goes into an unrecoverable spin, and his radar intercept officer goose is killed after the ejection seat smashes his head against the plane's windscreen. maverick initially has the death of his friend pinned on him, but is later said to be not guilty. still, the death of his friend makes him perform worse in the air, and although he still graduates, he loses the top gun competition to iceman. at the end of the film, maverick and his fellow pilots are called upon once again to shoot down more migs that are threatening a ship. after being in the heat of battle with both their lives at stake, maverick and iceman gain respect for each other, and maverick returns to top gun to teach new pilots. much like tons of other movies made in the 80s, top gun in many ways is full of problems. even if you choose to overlook the fact that has basically no story outside of the action scenes, the action scenes themselves are not done particularly well and get old fast. the footage of the f-14s flying around is probably all stock, and when all the characters are out of their planes, the plot just falters. maverick does get a love interest later in the movie, but there really isn't any point. nobody watching this cares about that, and only wants to see things explode. the movie is also hilariously unrealistic at times, most notably during the very beginning when it shows an aircraft carrier in non-american waters completely alone. everyone knows carriers are the most important type of naval warship in today's world due to their ability to project airpower basically anywhere on earth. the sight of one traveling with no escort whatsoever is ludicrous. there's also the scene that involves maverick's plane having its engines die because of a disruption in airflow, when this was remedied by grumman in the new f-14 models by replacing the pratt and whitney turbofans with ones made by general electric. only the early versions of the plane used the former engine, and because this is the mid 80s, i find it hard to believe they're still flying the old version. in general, movies like this are hard to talk about because almost the whole story is centered on action and not much else. cruise is in a lot of movies like this that don't require much thought and can be explained pretty easily, but top gun launched it into the mainstream. of course, you can't ignore the fact that america coming out of any fight on top is a hallmark of these movies. the only reason i watched this is for the plane scenes, and i think the majority of people will say the same.

the skilled, but reckless, selfish and rebel pilot maverick (tom cruise) and his partner goose (anthony edwards) are assigned to go to top gun, a military school for top-notch pilots. soon he has an affair with the instructor charlie (kelly mcgillis) and a rivalry with ice man (val kilmer) and slider (rick rossovich). but when goose dies in an accident, maverick decides to quit school. will his friends allow him to quit?

"top gun" is an entertaining popcorn with a commercial and silly story, but great action scenes made with the support of the american navy. there is a shallow romance between the gorgeous kelly mcgillis and tom cruise but in general the movie entertains. my vote is six.

everyone is familiar with "top gun". yep, it is one of those movies that everyone has seen. perhaps it is because of tom cruise, or perhaps because of its cheesy and cliché filled storyline. or perhaps it is because of the music, or even because of the beach volley scene. whatever the reason, you just have to admit that it is one of those pseudo-classic movies.

the storyline is so predictable that even a blind man sees what is coming a mile away. but despite its predictability, then there is still something enjoyable about "top gun". for me it was the dogfight scenes with the jet fighter planes.

the story is about maverick (played by tom cruise) a young hotshot fighter pilot student who takes on the burden of his fathers legacy as he attempts to prove his worth at the academy. love and loss are two things that strike hard in his otherwise perfect life. when a conflict of war is at the threshold, maverick has to make use of all his skills in order to pull through.

there is a good ensemble of talents in "top gun" with tom cruise and val kilmer in the lead roles. and the likes of anthony edwards, tom skerritt, tim robbins, james tolkan, meg ryan, rick rossovich and michael ironside really helped put "top gun" on the map.

if you haven't already seen "top gun" then you are missing out on one of the most memorable movies from the mid-eighties.

abandons his wingman lieutenant rick "hollywood" neven (whip hubley) to chase viper. maverick's flying abilities impress viper, but he still defeated when manoeuvred by him. viper's wingman jester as much as you want to dismiss "top gun" as one of the cheesiest movies ever, it simply cannot be done. there might not be a lot to love about the film, but i challenge anyone to find something to hate about it.

the story of pete "maverick" mitchell (cruise) and his partner "goose" (edwards) as they are selected to attend the navy's top air academy for dogfighting is classically structured. there are so many archetypes (the mission gone wrong, the rebellious pilot, the instructor-student romance) that "top gun" has both an eye-rolling quality and yet a comfortably familiar quality. it's so easy to follow that you get bored through most of it, but you never once stop rooting for maverick and goose and you laugh at the completely implausible yet successful courting tactics employed by maverick on his love interest, "charlie."

another thing that can make a movie fun that "top gun" has plenty of is music. a rockin 80s soundtrack that can't be beat, from "danger zone" to "take my breath away," the film is partially as lovable as it is because even if what you're watching is boring, what you're listening to is fun.

"top gun" could be a totally forgettable film, but it is that innocent, charming quality that lets it get away with the fact that everyone's who hasn't seen it thinks it is one of the best films of the 80s, when it is by no stretch of the mind in that category.

classic 80s action which focuses more on cool action shots of fighter jets than any storyline. there isn't a lot to top gun, an aptly named 'maverick' fighter pilot who competes to be the best in his class as he completes the highest standard of training. before the halfway mark that is about all there is, just shots of jets going fast coupled with cockpit quips, but developing into an afterthought love story and emotional turmoil. it's fine as a plot, but not exactly gripping or hard-hitting. more just a long advert for the us navy.

as someone with zero knowledge on military aircraft, the film provides no clarity on what goose and all the other backseat pilots actually do beyond say "look out". plus, it's never even stated who the us are fighting here, you can assume, but its almost as if all political context is removed and the bad guys are just the pilots with less colourful helmets.

a killer soundtrack, tons of quotes now embedded into pop-culture and a volleyball scene no one asked for, top gun provided a lot for the 80s whilst contributing absolutely nothing.

i'm sure that if tony scott ever imagined his 1986 blockbuster top gun would be taught in film studies curriculums, it would not be under the 'ironic/alternative/reappropriated viewing' week. indisputably, the film's slick, macho posturing is now legendarily lampooned/revered as a classic of unintentional(?) homoerotic camp, and more lampooned than revered for its glibly brazen patriotism, militarism, and daftly monolithic cold war politics. nonetheless, there is a moment, after the deluge of plane-porn, shirtless, oily volleyball romps, curiously lizard-like makeout sessions, repetitive musical cues that appear blatantly designed for comedy, and endless discussion of "hard-ons", where even the most sophisticatedly distanciated viewer is likely to have the gall to stop and think, "gee whiz – this movie is actually kind of fun. like, fun-fun, not just 'i'm-laughing-because-it's-so- ridiculously-hyperbolic' fun. what is happening? tom cruise, how have you bewitched me so with your voodoo magic and dazzling, cheshire-cat grin?!" this, surely, is the 'danger zone' kenny loggins keeps so helpfully cautioning us against.

yes – begrudgingly as it may be, the simpson/bruckheimer mystique is infectious, greasy-beer-ad-reminiscent as it may be. even nearly thirty years on, the film's mtv-flashiness is energizing, the flying sequences remain exciting, and even the ra-ra-military propaganda throughout is somewhat cute in its hokiness (bear in mind how unironic an enlistment tool the film served as to return to the solemn world of pooh-pooh-hood). and, despite spawning decades of jeering, patriarchal frat-boy morons and lazy halloween costumes alike, it's virtually impossible not to be won over by the cruiser's million-dollar grin, so hypnotically charismatic that even his smarmy swagger starts to (fairly disturbingly) become strangely seductive. bonus points to val kilmer to somehow cobbling an iconic codename (i've lost count of how many icemans have bested me at laser tag through the years) out of a lazy, moralizing drawl, kelly mcgillis for somehow remaining sassy instead of sappy, meg ryan for somehow remaining on the right side of annoying, and anthony edwards for stealing all the best (unironic) lines as adorably subservient perennial wingman goose. also, playing 'spot- the-tim-robbins' is always good for a lark.

yes, top gun will 'take your breath away', whether from laughing, genuine enrapture, or a bashful mix of both. if nothing else, the film remains an essential piece of cinema history for evidently discouraging sir cruisealot from taking part in a movie musical after his cringeworthy karaoke bout here (at least until rock of ages, which is loathsome for reasons far beyond him). danger, danger, pete mitchell.

thirty six years ago witnessed the release of top gun; a film which was destined to become a classic of its era. it centres around maverick (played by tom cruise), a bravura naval aviator who plays by his own rules and almost always finds a way to win. maverick's unique skill-set sees him enter top gun, a training programme for elite naval pilots. here he will come up against his stiffest competition yet, he will also find himself in a cat-and-mouse pursuit of one of the female trainers at the academy, charlie (played by kelly mcgillis). alongside telling the story of maverick's constant ability to overcome the odds, top gun is notable for its copious, often groundbreaking, flying scenes and its provision of a plethora of semi-naked, glistening male bodies. there is also, of course, that classic '80s soundtrack, the crowning element of which is berlin's melodramatic anthem "take my breath away".

deemed as the film which best epitomises the reagan era, top gun is a flashy, attention-grabbing, toxic male fantasy on steroids. that is not to say that it doesn't have its plus points. there are some impressive flying shots (i say shots rather than scenes as the scenes often feel interminable and made exclusively for aviation obsessives). there is also a slight element of depth to the film when an event of genuine tragedy occurs which finally makes maverick doubt his preternatural abilities. on top of this, there is something oddly entertaining about the ridiculously crass and unconvincing dialogue, and the unashamed brashness with which the film presents its spectacle of total masculine triumph. on that note, it's worth looking at the background to this triumph in a little more detail.

maverick's major obstacles in this film are, firstly, the top gun top-brass; he needs to prove not only that he is the best pilot, but he needs to prove to them that he can only be the best by doing things his way. then there is charlie, the object of his romantic attentions, he must totally conquer her to demonstrate his supreme masculinity. we also have unresolved father issues stemming from a murky death during aerial combat: maverick must solve the mystery of his father's final acts to conquer the past as well as the present. naturally, he must also overcome himself when doubts begin to swarm about the nature of his true abilities. but maverick's greatest obstacle comes from the man who is both his most prominent rival and critic: ice (played by val kilmer). gaining his approval is what will truly cement maverick as a leader among men. i will not reveal the resolutions of these plot strands just in case there are some who have not yet got around to seeing this film, but suffice it to say that maverick's arc very much plays out as a hero's journey.

the greatest objection i have to this film, besides the incessant flying scenes, is the solipsistically obsessive attention it pays to its main character and the toxic message this plays into when it comes to defining and understanding masculinity. when watching this film, i challenge you to find a single piece of dialogue which takes place outside of the flying or teaching scenes which does not reference maverick directly. every utterance, every snipe, every chance interaction is based around establishing the fact that maverick is firmly at the centre of this narrative. i understand that maverick is the hero of this journey but to force this concept so incessantly risks moving the film from being mere fantasy into the category of wildly-unrealistic aspiration. insecure, directionless men may look to maverick as a pin-up for their own arrested psyches. they can perhaps imagine that one day they could be a fraction as important as maverick clearly is in this make-believe world.

a particularly egregious consequence of the maverick obsession is that we are fed diabolically underdeveloped and underwritten supporting characters, the worst example of which is charlie. she starts out well enough as a young, driven woman who refuses to be impressed by maverick's irrepressible cockiness and insufferable self-assurance. but then she completely falls for him, because... because she must... because... because who, after all, could resist this paragon of masculine excellence? the problem is that she very quickly becomes an appendage to maverick. the story is so obsessed with him that there is no room whatsoever to provide her with any agency, character or even particularly discernible characteristics. then comes ice, who appears to be the saltiest and most cringe-worthily obsessed individual you could ever not wish to encounter. he can not resist any opportunity to criticise and undermine the noble, brilliant maverick, until, of course, he too is won over. when it comes to maverick, even the haters can't keep up their hate.

the seemingly overt homo-eroticism of the film is worth remarking upon due to its notoriety and quirkiness but it is, in my view, often misunderstood. the reason there are so many scenes of shiny, sculpted male flesh is to show us what all real men should look like and what all aspirational women should be blessed to be in the presence of. top gun is about boys and their toys. it's about "real men" fully expressing themselves and finding a way to have it all. it's about a jet-fuelled hero who is supercharged and supremely able. it's a g-forced geeing up of dissatisfied males who feel the need for something larger-than-life to aspire to. as long as the film is taken as a corny fantasy, it's harmless and enjoyable enough. my only concern is that it seems to have the potential to be taken not quite literally but perhaps a little too seriously.

maverick mitchell, a young and fearless pilot, determined to be the best at the army aviation academy, even if he has to step over his colleagues. a very different attitude from charlie, a teacher who maverick is totally dazzled by, and who will teach him some things that are not learned in class.

probably the film's biggest legacy is that it launched tom cruise's career. from this point on he became the go-to lead actor for blockbuster action movies, as status he still carries as witnessed by the success of this film's sequel, top gun: maverick (2022).

'top gun (1986)' is, essentially, a recruitment video for the us navy and is largely responsible for the 500% increase in people applying to become naval aviators that reportedly occurred in the months after its release, which equates to over 20,000 young men enlisting in the navy because they watched a movie about fighter pilots, sweaty men and subtextual homoeroticism. it's as jingoistic as most movies about the us military, albeit in a slightly less obvious way (it doesn't even think about the implications of its messaging), and it actively conforms to expectations set by that establishment, pleasing the powers that be in order to have access to its authentic equipment. that equipment is vital in creating the film's most exciting and memorable moments: those that take place high in the sky. the jet sequences are pretty spectacular to behold, as tangible as they are kinetic. the editing maintains a sense of geography while still being ever-so-slightly disorienting, making you feel as though you're up in the air with the characters and trying to keep up with their high-speed manoeuvres. most of the flying focuses around training scenarios, but that doesn't stop it from occasionally bringing you to the edge of your seat. what keeps it from doing that more often is the fact that you never truly care about the characters inside the aircraft. in fact, you're more concerned with the real-life stuntmen actually doing the manoeuvres (one of whom sadly died during production). the script doesn't really concern itself with doing anything other than establishing the outline of its characters, but the actors do a good job bringing them to life. even this early in his career, tom cruise seems more like an action figure than an actual actor. there's just something not quite right about him; he almost seems dead behind the eyes. don't get me wrong, he occasionally manages to convey something close to genuine human emotion and he's typically charming enough to get the job done, but he's always more physically convincing than he is emotionally compelling. for some roles, that's more than enough and, luckily, this is one of them. pretty much all the core players coast through the piece as glorified frat bros, engaging in relentless banter and seeming to spend more time in the locker room than in their own homes. they aren't especially compelling, but most of them are likeable enough. besides, they're totally secondary to their mechanical co-stars. tony scott treats both with the same semi-romantic aesthetic, crafting a big-budget blockbuster by way of lovelorn rock ballad. the music is as corny as the cinematography, but both are actually kind of delightful in this context. the flick is charmingly cheesy, but it's also genuinely enjoyable for the most part. it isn't great, but it's fairly fun and its stunt work is often exciting. having said that, it isn't quite gay enough.

my take: a good look, but not as good as its box-office status made it look.

one of the highest-grossing films of the 80's. the film which gave name to tom cruise a "superstar". it also features one of the most exciting aerial sequences ever lensed. so, is tony scott's 1986 popular blockbuster top gun worth all the attention? judging by action, star power and breathtaking aerial photography, it does. top gun is grandeur of sound and fury, but once it settles down, it turns rather slow and weak. while he blows us away with top-notch energy, director scott and "kaboom" producers don simpson and jerry bruckheimer can't find much more to offer when aerial action and top-notch photography rest backstage. the romance subplot between cruise maverick and his flight schoolteacher (kelly mcgillis) is fairly competent, but other plot elements fall on a flat note. but top gun has pretty much more elements that get us going and, for a mission that only wants to bring us a big-budget star-vehicle for a well-named cast list, top gun still has enough juice to keep us quenched until the end credits.

although rather overrated and quite childish- top gun manages to squeeze some charm out of its macho premise making it a forgettable but not entirely pointless action spectacle that has continued to grow overtime. i'm gonna be honest and say i truly don't understand the hype or appeal of this movie to so many people. sure, maybe it's just a nostalgia thing, but to many it seems much more than that when there is really so little to remember about this one. to start off with the things i didn't enjoy, the script is wire thin- but honestly that was to be expected. some of the dialogue is so incredibly cheesey and played out, and much of the conflict on screen seems uninspired- and very derivative of other action films of a similar nature. the cinematography is an orange sunburn tan the entire course which has its moments, but certainty doesn't make it stand out. the soundtrack is rather good, but its overuse of the same two songs over and over again can be played out. not to mention the second half of this movie takes a sharp right turn itself toward dramatic territory which is both unexpected and kinda undeserved. so what if anything positive is there to say about this one? well for one, the actors do try their best. tom cruise is a delightful lead, as well as love interest kelly mcgillis as charlie. the film can be entertaining to watch at times, and there are even a few moments that had me smile and even laugh at times which was surprising to me to say the least. if you turn your brain off and just go along for the ride, it's not half bad. in the end, top gun is no masterpiece but it is pure popcorn fun at times. despite its struggles it manages to cook a half baked story into an entertaining action film just enough to leave you more satisfied than not. it may not deserve its popularity and high praised status but there certainly is much worse out there to compare it to.

re-watching this film after 10 years has made me realise how flawed and ordinary it was. i was in college 10 years ago when i saw top gun for the first time. by that time, i hadn't seen thousands of classics, so i enjoyed watching it. i enjoyed the aerial action, the adventure stuff, tom's handsome looks and kelly's sexy appeal. i didn't know much about the art of filmmaking. i didn't know there were aerial action classics like the oscar-winner "wings" (1927) and good films like grant's "only angles got the wings" (1939), master billy wilders's "the spirit of st. louis" (1957), and a few more in the 40s and 50s. but today, when i am through with almost 5000+ films right from 1901 to 2022, and those films mentioned above, i can easily notice the flawed aspects in top gun. re-watching this film today has made a big difference in my viewing experience, and it has also shown me how mature my taste has become in the past 10-11 years. top gun looks so ordinary when i think about it as an aerial action drama and compare it to those old classics from the 30s and 40s. not just story-wise, but many other factors too. first the story - what mediocre writing it is. not a single moment of thrill. it was so predictable and cliched. having a good friend and then losing him, a past that isn't known, a jealous colleague, a girlfriend who's in the same profession, getting nervous and that guilt after losing someone, i mean, all these things were outdated in the 70s only. what a great mess that love story angle was. and then, they had that typical reconciliation too. seriously? one day in the 1980s, top producer jerry bruckheimer sat in his office in hollywood, flipping through the "california" magazine. he was mainly interested in an article about the us navy's flight instruction school at miramar air station in san diego. the so-called topgun program had started 20 years earlier (during the vietnam war) and was rumored to be the place where the world's best fighter pilots trained. which gave bruckheimer an idea. so, he contacted the magazine's editor-in-chief and acquired the movie rights to the piece.

but it would be a challenging picture to make. in order to get the footage right, it was necessary for the film crew to cooperate fully with the us navy. for the same reason, jerry bruckheimer (and his director tony scott) also had to allow the military's censor complete script approval. no wonder then that the picture became so strongly pro-armed forces. ultimately, the us navy actually used "top gun" as a recruiting tool in their search for new fighter pilots.

unfortunately, in the '80s when "top gun" was made, cgi was still in its infancy. tony scott therefore had no opportunity to use computers to animate the many aerial sequences. the director briefly considered using miniatures instead, but dropped the idea because he suspected that it wouldn't look realistic enough. consequently, actual planes performed real stunts in all the flying scenes in the movie. tragically, though, a veteran aerobatic pilot was killed because of that.

despite rather lukewarm reviews, "top gun" became a gigantic, international triumph. it was number one at that year's box office, while the film's soundtrack topped billboard's hot 200 album chart for five consecutive weeks. and the success just went on. before he made "top gun", actor tom cruise had "just" been a hot commodity among others in tinseltown. the movie elevated him to the next level, starting a decade of high-profile blockbusters.

tony scott's "top gun" is arguably the most american movie ever made, which by pop culture laws translates to also the coolest movie ever made. this is about kenny loggins' brand of rock'n'roll, fighter jets, leather jackets, motorcycles, sunglasses during the night, macho rivalries, bromances and, of course, passionate love. what a thing.

the movie stars tom cruise as maverick, a hotshot us navy fighter jet pilot who is equal parts skill and attitude. he is a single-and-ready-to-mingle twenty-something years old ambitious but reckless and authority-defying young man. his partner goose (anthony edwards) is the polar opposite--already married, he has no interest in showing off, but his friendship with maverick is way too powerful to let that get in the way.

the beginning of the movie finds us flying, as we see maverick and goose flipped upside-down about two meters above a russian mig with maverick flipping the russian pilot off just because he can. obviously, this reckless behavior doesn't go well with the brass which sends them to the us navy's elite fighter weapons school to master the art of aerial dogfighting and also to get it out of their system. in there, maverick meets iceman (val kilmer). with his stiff hair and constant chewing--just to make sure he is cool enough--he is an equally brilliant pilot but also composed and by-the-book. quickly, the two settle into a rivalry because rivalries are cool and you have the ultimate recipe for a full-blown cliché. there is just one thing missing: the girl. enter charlie (kelly mcgillis), astrophysicist and civilian top gun instructor with whom maverick flirts before eventually both falling in love with each other.

now, when "top gun" is in the air, it is unmatched. scott uses the freedom of the open sky to his advantage by moving around at violent speeds, unbound by physical walls and surrounding the planes. the editing is based on generating brief shots of the pilot in moments in which he is put under pressure before furiously returning outside the cockpit freewheeling around shootouts. it does a great job at simulating the nauseating and overwhelming feeling of being in a dogfight--something which few people have ever experienced for real.

unfortunately, after it lands, "top gun" simply doesn't know what to do with itself. the relationship between maverick and goose is honest but bland, the rivalry between him and iceman--while containing obvious polarizing ideas--it's lost to a few brief interactions in which maverick parades around like a child. but the biggest issue lies in his relationship with charlie. at first, their flirts are combative--he uses his words to reel her in, she uses them as defenses and eventual counterattacks. but even after they get past adolescent woes, and share personal feelings--maverick tells her about his missing father who was also a fighter jet pilot--they don't give in to each other, and it's maverick the one who takes a step back.

i assume director tony scott took this strange decision to show us the guy is not all about "scoring" despite the fact that he wears aviator sunglasses more than 50% of the time. he is trying to tell us that maverick is all about real love but i am pretty sure that by that point everyone believed that anyway. and also, when they eventually make out, it looks more stylized than a synth-pop track playing saturday night at your local disco. this is also a pretty predictable movie--which comes naturally when you've got clichés--as when maverick is on the verge of giving up on flying after suffering a personal loss, it's charlie the one that picks him up and dusts him off. to be fair, i don't mind the predictability as by the time the movie gets to this point, it was clear to me what it is all about. i also like the message: it was love that saved maverick--that, to me, is the biggest take from "top gun".

this is a spectacle to behold--a movie which is all about style, visually evocative despite being emotionally flat; it is brooding, dramatic, self-pitying and self-centered. these things don't particularly make for a good film, but at least they do factor in to contribute to what can only be called the american cool--which happens to be the best one.

"top gun" seems to have just one purpose: to elevate then-candidate hollywood star tom cruise to stardom and, consequently, gross millions at the box office. and the uncreative script, written by jim cash and jack epps jr., explores several clichés without any shame to achieve its objective. we have the promising young heartthrob who, due to the trauma of his past related to his father's death, has no fear or sense, but who, on the other hand, is incredibly good at what he does. we also have the girl (in this case a more mature woman) who will obviously get involved with the good guy and the annoying antagonist, who seems to exist only to generate conflict with the protagonist without apparent justification, and who will obviously become friends with him in the predictable ending. finally, we have the jovial and romantic songs from harold faltermeyer's beautiful soundtrack, which remain stuck in the viewer's memory, reminding them of the film whenever they hear them (and at the time the romantic "take my breath away", by the group berlin, was played extensively on the radio). just to reinforce the argument, notice the numerous times in which scott uses close-ups of tom cruise, often wearing sunglasses, alternating with american shots (from the waist up) of the shirtless star, clearly exploring the charisma (and muscles) of the young actor to attract the female audience, as is evident in the volleyball game scene, which is nothing more than pure exhibitionism by the young heartthrobs. even goose's tense and sad death does not escape the cliché of the death of a best friend that serves as a turning point in the protagonist's life, perfectly symbolized in the scene in which maverick throws his partner's ashes into the sea. and not even the pilot training sounds convincing, never conveying the expected difficulty that a pilot should face to reach the level of excellence required in a profession like this.

but "top gun" also has its positive points, starting with the excellent sound work, noticeable especially in the sensational aerial sequences, perfectly capturing the noise of planes tearing through the sky. good editing by chris lebenzon and billy weber collaborates in these exciting sequences, where director tony scott creates beautiful shots, also helped by jeffrey l. kimball's photography direction and visual effects. the director takes advantage of the beautiful visuals during the flights, taking advantage of the universe of beautiful images that the sky provides to film from interesting angles such as the front, wing and tail of the planes. in another moment, scott gives a close-up of cruise when he talks about his late father, highlighting the sadness on his face when thinking about his mysterious death. tom cruise, in fact, has a good performance, demonstrating the usual energy as the rebellious maverick, despite using endless smiles (obviously, trying to establish himself as a heartthrob). notice how he smiles slightly when he hears that he is going to the special "top gun" school, as he knew that this was the opportunity of a lifetime to prove his quality as a pilot, in addition to being able to face his traumatic past. his performance grows in the final part, after losing his friend and leaving to overcome the trauma of the enigmatic loss of his father. but unfortunately, the predictable script doesn't demand much from the cast.

goose, played by anthony edwards, has the sole function of causing forced laughter in the viewer and most of his weak dialogues with maverick are not exciting, such as when they talk about the inverted mig. val kilmer is caricatured and exaggerated as the one-dimensional tom kazanski, the "iceman", who only has two human moments throughout the entire narrative. the first is when he respects maverick's pain for losing his friend ("i feel for goose") and the second is the predictable ending, when he finally recognizes the quality of his rival. kelly mcgillis plays the mature charlotte and has her good moments, like when she tells cruise that she didn't want to let their relationship get in the way of her profession ("i don't want you to know that i fell in love with you"). her charlotte, despite being completely in love, is very aware that assuming that passion could compromise her performance as a team instructor. tom skerritt is excellent as the intelligent commander mike "viper" metcalf, who knows very well where maverick can go and fights to get the best out of the boy. and finally, meg ryan steals the show in the few minutes she appears, playing goose's wife, carole bradshaw. totally loose and laid-back, she is clearly the best performance in the film, still conveying a lot of emotion when she loses her husband. it is with her on the scene that goose and maverick experience one of their best moments, when they sing together at the piano.

when maverick approaches charlotte and sings, helped by everyone in the bar, the song "you've lost that loving feeling", tony scott's film seems to excite. the excitement increases in the wonderful sequences starring fighter jets that cut through the sky at high speed. but unfortunately, when the action takes place on the ground, it is not successful, limiting itself to a common and uninteresting narrative. there's no problem using clichés, after all, they didn't become clichés for nothing. the problem is the way these are used, and unfortunately in this case the uncreative result is not pleasing, being saved only by the aforementioned aerial sequences. with exciting and impactful aerial sequences, "top gun" shows the danger and excitement that await each of the pilots at the navy's prestigious fighter aviation school. rewatching the film decades after its release still gives you that incredible, thrilling sensation with the wonderful aerial action scenes. even though, nowadays, these scenes are not perfect, we must recognize the impact of the time of their release, however, the aerial scenes often seem confusing, filmed from a distance where we notice the use of models and other effects, especially in the destruction of the aircraft. the editing, in most of the aerial scenes, fails to create a visual game in which it shows the viewer who the character is under the pilot's outfit and the entire construction of the events that culminate in maverick's impulsive and courageous actions, in the death of a character. or in conflicts between pilots in full training. when we see it, the scene concludes and we accept what we only heard over the pilots' communications radio and from the navy control cabin.

interestingly, even before cinema took over the language of video games, "top gun" uses strategies to momentarily transform the viewer into an excited pilot shooting at enemy aircraft. some of the moments with the greatest tension and sense of adventure are precisely in the aiming process that places our gaze directly on chasing the "villains" until everything is ready to detonate them with missiles. tony scott uses certain dramatic situations as mere subterfuges to accentuate an exciting vision of military equipment. in this sense, there is even an exaggeration in how maverick is falsely trapped in a structure to rebel against. the instructors who reprimand him have deep admiration for him; the wife of a partner who dies on a mission is more concerned with consoling him than paying attention to her own pain; maverick's questions about his beloved woman's opinions result in one thing: he's right. even iceman, the only one who seems realistic about his recklessness, is led to give in to his rival's exceptionalism. therefore, the film exists to glorify tom cruise's character, to the point that his romantic advances are not considered. you don't have to go far to understand how problematic the invasion of the bathroom and the insistence on transforming a "no" into a "yes" are.

there are exciting situations in the production and nostalgia during the revisit can be responsible for relativizing certain problems in favor of a less demanding experience. however, if we look a little more carefully, we can see that not even the romance between tom cruise and kelly mcgillis' characters makes much sense. she is an officer openly flirting with a cadet and no one says anything, that is, breaking the rules is not even seen as a transgression; she is a figure that exists only to confirm how incredible he is, both in terms of his knowledge of flight and the intricate logic of love; in the isolated sex scene between the two (filmed months later, as it did not exist in the first version of the script), the only thing emphasized in the prudish dynamic of the shadows making out is the french kiss. but, continuing in this vein of scrutinizing the main points of the film, not even the rivalry with iceman is well worked. the evident homoeroticism that exists in this relationship (see the malicious looks during the presentations, the scenes of horniness in the locker room and especially the blatant volleyball game between the shirtless men) does not serve to mobilize anything. in the end, "top gun" leaves no important message or reflection, it doesn't have a creative script and it doesn't even recycle old clichés. tony scott prefers to follow the opposite path, abusing formulas and recipes to achieve box office success. therefore, he explores action scenes involving fighter jets to attract the male audience and romance involving the heartthrob of the time to attract the female audience. in the end, the director managed to achieve his goal, but unfortunately, he didn't achieve anything more than that. unlike the powerful planes we see throughout the film, "top gun" never takes greater flights.

this film will always go down as an 80s classic with its appeal to both the lads and the ladies. the lads go for the action, the women go for the love story.

no doubt about it, the film has some amazing dog fights as well as a sturdy plot to emphasis its reasoning.

the overall cast was chosen well, tom cruise suited the cocky hero heart throb, as always. kelly mcgillis was the perfect choice to play the intelligent love interest, val kilmer played his best role to date as the rival ice man and tom skerrit was well chosen to play the warm hearted mentor.

it is not usually my cup of tea, but the romance side of it was not as bad as i expected because it for once had a realistic approach.

what let the film down for me was the stupid musical numbers, such as "you've lost that loving feeling" and "goodness gracious great balls of fire". as not only did it make the actors look stupid, but they were also unrealistic, how many times do you see that in real life? the film is also backed up by an awesome soundtrack, which gave the film that atmosphere.

overall, a film that everyone should watch at least once in their life time.

the highway to the dangerzone is a road filled with cliches, bro-love, adrenaline and cheese and your enjoyment of top gun is entirely dependant on your love for, or tolerance of, these things. tom cruise is at his most charming as this is the film which cemented his star status following the brilliantly fun risky business and the supporting cast try their best with a script filled with high-fives and laddy 80s banter mixed in with a light sprinkling of tradgey which elevates the movie in the third act. the plot is however notoriously thin as the producers famouly post-engineered drama into the film via over-dubbing lines in scenes where characters had helmets on. this film relies almost entirely on the sensational action sequences which look great for the era due to a clever use of real naval air force training footage and as mark kermode posits these sequrences play out like the song and dances in a musical which give good pacing to the film despite its light plot.

this is a fun movie, if a little cliche. it keeps your attention and entertains, and i think that's the whole point of it. the stereotypical macho-ness was a little off putting and could have used some nuance, something i'm really hoping for in tg: maverick.

all things said, top gun is understandably a classic movie. maverick is charming, some scenes are emotional, and the action is tense. however, top gun is narratively disappointing.

the plot tends to jump around without much care for where the story leads, and it never feels consistent. a movie does not need to be predictable, but it should at least have a solid narrative. more than anything, top gun feels like a montage of scenes from a well-structured movie. had the narrative been better, i could have found myself more engaged in the story. instead we are left with a fun movie that leaves little room for thought.

gosh, i wish i liked this more than i do. i mean, it's technically accomplished, there are some nice performances, it looks good, but the story is just so wane, the stakes so completely absent for so much of the running time, and the romance so generically dull that it seriously limits my enjoyment of what the film does well. it's just one of those films where the technical side of things is so high that it really does just come down to a balance between that and everything else that is just kind of...boring.

pete mitchell, maverick, (tom cruise) is a hotshot naval aviator flying f-14s with his radar intercept officer, nick, goose, getting sent to top gun, the naval school for elite aviators to teach them dogfighting. the one piece of screenwriting that i actually appreciate in this film is how the beginning, where we watch the best aviator on the aircraft carrier, cougar (john stockwell), get so spooked by an encounter with potential enemy migs that he just outright quits. this gets repeated later in the film with maverick which is the one bit of screenwriting structure that feels like it has some real thought in it. because, otherwise, this is just pete up against tom kazansky, iceman, (val kilmer) about who's the best pilot at top gun.

when i say that there are no real stakes here, i really mean it. there's little sense that what they're doing is actually dangerous to them personally because none of the pilots are self-reflective enough to realize that they're doing incredibly dangerous things that can end their lives for roughly the first hour and twenty minutes of the film. aside from the opening with cougar, it's just a bunch of hotheads arguing about who's the best of the best. if it weren't matched with some incredible aerial footage of these aircraft dodging around each other, expertly edited together, it'd be a slog of boring machismo without any stakes.

and then there's the romance. pete meets the civilian contractor, charlotte (kelly mcgillis), and the two have this will they won't they relationship that's just honestly never that interesting. it's rote, at best, all the while we know that they'll get together in the end, that pete's recklessness will temper just enough so that charlotte can love him...except we don't even need to get that far. they' fall in love by the halfway point. i suppose it's a small mercy that she isn't one of those, "i'm always worried about losing you every time you go up," movie wives, but they've replaced that trope with almost nothing instead. it's just a dull as dishwater romance that eats up minutes and minutes of screentime.

things get amplified during one of the training exercises when something terrible happens to a character, shaking maverick's confidence to the point that he thinks of quitting the whole thing. finally, there are stakes. this honestly would have worked better if the sense of danger were more palpable through the whole preceding couple of acts instead of just relying heavily on how awesome it is to fly fighter jets (which, admittedly, seems pretty awesome). and then it really becomes, can maverick get over the fact that he's not really responsible for a tragedy and fly again? it's kind of an odd moment.

and the final act is actually, finally, a clearly defined dramatic situation where tensions are running high with some unnamed foreign power in the indian ocean, and there's going to be potential for violence during a rescue mission. combine that with maverick still trying to get over his mental blocks, and you've got the makings of a quality third act. it almost feels like an accident that it gets to that, to a third act that actually does kind of work, but there it is.

also, the whole final moment with iceman feels so unearned because the rivalry between the two was never that deep, just simplistic rivalry type stuff.

so...i'm mixed on the whole thing. the technical side of things is top notch. the third act works quite well while combining nicely with the prologue. however, everything in between is thin and dull, especially the romance. it's a rewrite away from giving the majority of the film stakes, diminishing the romance appropriately, and tying up the whole film with a stronger emotional throughline. maybe a decades-later legacy sequel could do...all of those things?

top gun, despite receiving mediocre reviews from critics when it was released, was a blockbuster for paramount pictures, and the highest grossing movie of 1986.

the good: the visual effects still stand up nearly 40 years after its release. the biggest star of the movie is arguably the f14a tomcat and best scenes are in the cockpit. val kilmer shines as iceman, and anthony edwards and meg ryan put in solid performances.

the bad: nearly everything else. stilted script and frequently wooden acting. tom cruise's character is a hopelessly arrogant pilot, who, in reality, would have been stripped of his wings for dangerous flying, not sent to top gun. the chemistry between tom cruise and kelly mcgillis is nonexistent, the entire soundtrack is 80s cheese. there are so many technical gaffes that is seems as though director tony scott didn't even bother to bring in technical support from a former fighter pilot. some glaring examples: throttles work in reverse (pilots pull the throttles to idle when supposedly throttling up) and dogfights that take place just off surface of the desert, when there is supposed to be a 10,000 ft hard floor that was important enough to be a plot point.

it's good, but not great. director tony scott was much better than this. for a better tony scott experience, revisit "enemy of the state" or "true romance".

"top gun" has a fabulous sound track. very few from the 80's generation don't get their heart racing when they hear about the "danger zone". tom cruise delivers a good performance, but val kilmer's performance was more notable in my opinion. the movie blends the thrill of aviation with the challenge of military life mixed with the heated emotions of young "guns". these guys are just like military guys i met when i was young; dedicated to their profession, but always ready for a thrill. the girls are always looking for these guys, and the plot is true to the drama and reality of what it is like to be a man in uniform, excuse the old-fashioned reference, but the comment embodies the spirit of the movie.

1986's "top gun" had a lot going for it: a first rate production staff featuring the action partnership of don simpson and jerry bruckheimer, direction by tony scott, and lead acting by a young tom cruise and a still youthful kelly mcgillis, backed by a solid supporting cast that included val kilmer, anthony edwards, tom skerrit, michael ironside and, in cameos, meg ryan and tim robbins. couple this horsepower with a superb popular music score, lots of action sequences featuring the navy's hot f-14 fighter aircraft, and hijinks and angst among young naval aviators, and you have a great action movie that spent months in the theaters. the storyline centers around navy lt pete "maverick" mitchell (tom cruise), a brash, immature, but gifted flier. in a close encounter with enemy migs over the persian gulf, maverick saves his wingman and earns a slot at the prestigious fighter weapons school for himself and his backseater, "goose" (played with everyman humility by anthony edwards). at the school, maverick quickly develops a rivalry with his chief competitor, iceman (played with suitable demeanor by val kilmer) and a romance with one of his instructors, "charlie" (kelly mcgillis). however, maverick's willingness to push the flying envelope gets him and goose into an horrific flying accident. the accident robs maverick of his self-confidence and threatens to take him out of the cockpit altogether. some gentle mentoring by one of his flight instructors (tom skerrit) gets maverick back out to his carrier, right in the middle of an confrontation with the bad guys. in a vicious aerial dogfight involving an outnumbered maverick and iceman, maverick must finally grow up and become a team player. an absolutely terrific music score and action sequences involving dog-fighting f-14's and "red team" aircraft (cutting edge at the time) tend to mask a sometimes incoherent script. the romance between maverick and charlie gets worked in around the flying sequences, as does a rather obscure sub-plot involving maverick's mia father. the jumpy editing causes supporting cast to sometimes wander in and out of scenes without real introduction or explanation. minor flaws aside, "top gun" continues to hold up well as a highly enjoyable action movie twenty years on.

following his shocking suicide earlier this year, director tony scott's legend was cemented, with actors and fellow directors flooding to pay tribute to the man that delivered the likes of the last boy scout (1991) and crimson tide (1995). personally, with the greatest respect, i feel his death has overshadowed what was a relatively average career, in which his finest achievement, the tarantino-scripted true romance (1993), was possibly his most low-octane film, given that he is most fondly remembered for his work in the action field. therefore, it seemed the perfect time to re-visit his most popular film, top gun, the high- fiving homoerotica-fest that cemented the careers of both scott and star tom cruise, a film that they are still, 26 years later, best remembered for.

with top fighter pilot cougar (john stockwell) losing his nerve during a dogfight and dropping out of the air force, hot-shot pilot pete 'maverick' mitchell is offered the chance to join the top gun flight school. fancying himself as the best of the best, maverick, along with his rio lieutenant goose (anthony edwards), sets about establishing a name for himself with grand stunts and a cocky attitude, almost coming to blows with his fellow elite students, namely iceman (val kilmer). he even finds time to romance instructor charlie blackwood (kelly mcgillis). but when a tragic accident occurs, maverick must do a bit of soul-searching, and question his ability to live up to the legend of his father.

for a film that remains so immensely popular, top gun is shockingly bad. the almost unbearable swagger of the now slightly creepy scientology dwarf tom cruise leads to many moments of teeth-grinding anger- inducement, with the much-imitated you've got that lovin' feeling karaoke moment being simply embarrassing. but with most square-jawed, reagan-era 1980's action films comes much hilarity, with the best- selling soundtrack proving to be the king of synthesised cheddar, and the near-constant homoeroticism questioning the era's view of a 'man's man'. the volleyball scene is especially jaw-dropping, with slow-motion arse-slapping and greased-up torso's aplenty, playing out like a pre-sex ritual by cruise and kilmer.

the film is real justification of tony scott's reputation as a great action director. the dogfight scenes are filmed beautifully, with rapid editing and spectacular framing generating real excitement between all the crud (especially impressive given the cost of flying these machines and the heavily-restricted time-frames in which the crew had to shoot within). yet whenever the film is in danger of getting quite good, it delves into another cliché or shifts the focus back to the uninvolving romance between maverick and charlie, with scenes involving maverick's inner-demon fighting especially causing the fists to clench. with a film having the ability to be so bad and rather good in equal measures, it's hard to really justify it's massive fan-base and endless imitations, yet it's also difficult to deny.

every time planes take off from an aircraft carrier - almost every time we step outdoors - the skies are obscured by a heavy tobacco graduated filter. sooner or later we forget what real skies look like. it's a simpson/buckheimer trademark. it tells us, i suppose, how important it all is, how something of moment will be, is being, has been decided in this small theatre of human affairs ... it's not just filters: an air of self-conscious importance and cheap grandeur pervades their whole corpus. and, hey, sometimes it works. it depends chiefly on whether something of moment really is being decided. "crimson tide" is enjoyable because we end up getting the kind of confrontation we were promised in a context where the outcome really matters. here, a mission simply arrives out of the blue for the top gun jet fighters. the military tells us that the outcome is important, but i don't believe that for a second. even if the military is right it's all incidental to what the rest of the movie is about. all the portentous hints earlier on were about maverick's emotional life and personal skill. had he died and the mission been successful due to someone else's efforts, we wouldn't have thought, "well, at least the americans prevented the russians from doing whatever it is everyone was so worried about." no: we didn't give a toss about the russian/american conflict. it's hard to give a toss about the emotional life of maverick, either, but that's for other reasons: the whole situation was hard to swallow, and no-one did anything to hide the fact that it was artificially sustained. it could so easily have been prevented by diverting the trillions of dollars of public money that went into the private chariot races, towards - i don't know - a better script, perhaps.

top gun is about this super cool guy named maverick, played by tom cruise. he and goose, his funny-best-friend-with-a-family-and-a-little-boy- and who's-death-you-could-predict-within-the-first-two-minutes are at the top of their class in flight school. they go to the big boy's league where maverick meets and fall in love with his teacher, charolette, played by kelly mcgillis, and the two of them have about as much chemistry between them as cruise has had successful marriages. it's pretty funny how there's much more sexual tension and chemistry between maverick and goose and maverick and his rival iceman, who's the antagonist because the film tells us he is; however his only crime for ¾ of the film is being the only character who tells maverick he puts his squad in danger without kissing his butt in the same sentence.

an american action drama; a story about a rebellious u. s. naval air force pilot who is accepted into the air combat training programme, where he finds romance with one of his instructors as he battles for top pilot status. it is difficult not to recommend this film for its style, verve, blistering sound design, a winning soundtrack and song, the ideal casting of tom cruise, the visual photography which captured the awe of the fighter jet spectacle. one may feel spatially disoriented by the aerial scenes, but the fighter pilot lives in a world of 360-degree turns so it gives us a good sense of what it might be like to be in a dogfight. the narrative promotes a fantasy about eliteness and male narcissism at the expense of a realistic depiction of war or brinkmanship. however, weighed against it, are plot holes, corny dialogue, and a bunk romance which owes more to teenage adolescent fantasy than its intention - genuine romantic value. all in all, in the air, it's fair; on the ground, it flounders.

if you like action movies simply for the sake of the action, you'll probably enjoy this movie a lot. it is full of action (and even a bit of combat). however, if you expect at least a bit of a believable story behind all the action, in the end this movie will disappoint. in essence, there are three different stories told in this movie, and all of them either lacked suspense or believability.

the first takes up about the first three quarters of the film. maverick (tom cruise) is a navy fighter pilot sent to a special school for the navy's elite pilots. to the extent that there's a story here it seems to revolve around whether maverick or iceman (val kilmer) will end up at the top of the class and win the top gun award (and essentially be declared the best of the best). the problem is that the competition really didn't interest me. the movie didn't really offer any particular reason to root for one over the other, and when tom skerrit (playing the commander of the school) offers a voice over (by radio to the pilots) saying that only 2 points separates maverick and iceman, my honest reaction was "who really cares?" in fairness i guess kudos have to be given to the writers for avoiding the temptation to turn iceman into the embodiment of evil, which would have made the story even more ridiculous (even though it would have given us someone to root for.) as it is, though, watching this competition between the two was a bit like watching a world series between the arizona diamondbacks and the seattle mariners (or substitute any two teams that you don't care a whit about.)

the second storyline was about the romance between maverick and one of his civilian instructors at the school (played by kelly mcginnis.) the relationship wasn't sufficiently developed and just didn't strike me as believable. how did charlie (mcgillis) survive as an instructor at this school when she was so easily swept off her feet by a hot shot student (given that the only students she'd ever have at this school are hot-shots?)

the final storyline was the most interesting of the three, and revolved around whether maverick could regain his form after the accidental death of his buddy goose (anthony edwards.) again, though, there's a predictability to this. you know in the end that he'll come through. how he came around was a bit problematic to me (entertaining though it was, i admit). if the sort of thing that happened in the last little bit of the movie was really the sort of thing that might have happened during the cold war, then it seems to me that the cold war would have become "hot" pretty fast. this is clearly a plot line that worked very well in the 1980's, when cold war-themed movies were common (think "red dawn" or even "rocky v" - although "top gun" is certainly less over-the-top than those two), and that historical context might be a problem when watching such a movie almost 20 years after the end of the cold war, when the passions just aren't there anymore.

anyway, i'd give this a 5/10. action-lovers will love it; others might be disappointed.

this was one of my favourite movies when i was a young boy; as it was for a whole generation of young boys. not only was it a neat action film with charismatic characters and thrilling action sequences but was also the absolute reference in terms of fighter plane action and slick, cool, awesome military action. i don't think there has been any movie or piece of media where fighter jets, aircraft carriers and the navy itself have looked as good as in top gun. this movie is the epitome of the military being cool: where you're goofing around, hanging out with the boys and occasionally blowing stuff up. there has been a number of films in navy settings: under siege which was claustrophobic and tense; the hunt for red october which was precise and technically inclined; an officer and gentleman which was dramatic. none of them were as fun. top gun is a celebration of flying and of the fighter pilot lifestyle. full of motorcycles, hot babes and old r&b songs. there is a sense of juvenile fun. that is why this movie works, and also why is has endured as a classic movie.

on the other hand, you could argue, and i am leaving the music and cinematography aside for a moment, the overall vibe is the only thing this movie does competently. every other aspect of this film, be it the characterisation, the plot, the love story, or the overall story is either poorly done, left unanswered or simply lacking.

watching this as an adult, you quickly realise there is no story to speak of. maverick starts the movie as being already the best pilot there is. as a punishment he is sent to top gun, where there can be only one best pilot for some reason. there is no inner reflection nor growth. his interactions with others, iceman his rival, charlie his love interest and viper his mentor never successfully challenge his character or his actions or even his worldview. in typical 80s fashion, they instead kind of confirm that maverick the best there is, and that he has always been. the only thing standing between him and his greatness was his own self-doubt.

the shallowness of the film is both a hindrance and a stroke of genius. the movie directs all its craftsmanship, efforts and therefore the audience's attention to the sexiness of the planes and the awesomeness of sweaty men in uniform. it does feels like a never ending music video. and as such it is frankly glorious. it is one of the best looking movies ever and the endless scenes of jets taking off in golden hour is a delight.

the relative emptiness of the movie also allows it to be the ultimate propaganda film. as well as the most subversive gay romance of all time. but that is more involuntary than anything, and i think it makes the film less interesting. the subtext ends up being more interesting and exciting than the actual plot. however, even un-intentional meaning cannot replace the absence of actual meaning.

it is a weird time capsule of the 80s, a film archetype of that era. at the same time it is unique and a type of movie that is not made any more.

it's fast paced action sequences and aerial cinematography are top notch, simply breathtaking and stunning for the most. the drama of the shooting is the backbone of this film, the adrenaline it can induce is spectacular and some of the shots are simply haunting.

the humour is laugh out loud funny and it featured some bloody good looking men and great looking women so the eye candy is never far away. the film has very few lulls and the action is never far away. it has emotion and feeling but always gets back into the danger zone pretty quick with characters that are likable and fun to watch. the casting was very well done and you can sense that the cast and crew must have had a riot while making this film (with the exception of iceman/val kilmer, who actually kept himself apart from the crew for the most to allow for his character to be felt as a true outsider.)

as may be apparent i'm a top gun fan, have been since i first watched this film, i was gripped from the opening chimes of the epic top gun theme followed by that big haired 80's guitar riff and the initial sounds of engines winding up as the steam drifts across the deck of the aircraft carrier. i'm a firm believer that if this film doesn't get your stuff going at some point, your stuff is broken. it's not a film to be taken seriously, it's meant to be enjoyed with friends and laughed along with.

the film may have a few plot holes, there are about a million goofs, it spawned more than a handful of web sites to point out all the goofs and flaws in the film, dialogue and all other things top gun related but it's got a fan base the size of a massive army and for a reason, it's just a good movie because of all that.

the soundtrack and aerial footage really are the stars of this film, even though the cast was pretty huge, the director tony scott really went all in and made a huge effort with top gun (even at his own personal expense considering he ended up hiring a us aircraft carrier to get a shot just how he wanted!)

it's just one of those films if you like it, whenever it is on, you can sit down and watch it no matter where you walked in, or turned over and found it was on. it's like a really comfortable pair of slippers that always feel good to slip on when you get the chance. i often wish i could turn back the clock to being a teenager again to watch it for the first time all over again and get the chills down my spine as each action sequence gears up; the rush as the roar of the f-14 engines scream and howl. i envy the people who have not seen this film as they have experience the roller-coaster ride that this film can offer.

it's funny as i was inspired to come write this review after meeting someone the other week who had not seen top gun, which for me has been a rare experience. in fact i don't know many people who do not own either a copy if the vhs or a dvd of top gun, and most of my friends have the ost in their music collection or the larger part of it as singles/mp3's.

if you have not seen it, get on ebay or amazon or wherever, spend a few quid and buy a copy, get some friends around for the night, snag some beer, popcorn, pizza or tofu if that floats your boat and have a great night in. if you don't take it too seriously you should have a good night.

if you have seen it and enjoyed it, get on here and give it some love and vote it up, if only to get it ranked above a lot of the rubbish ranked highly.

it's also worth watching the dvd extras/making of top gun if you liked the film as it's pretty interesting stuff and very funny in parts, as some of the trivia about the film is fascinating.

in the opening moments of "top gun," an ace navy pilot flies upside down about 18 inches above a russian-built mig and snaps a polaroid picture of the enemy pilot. then he flips him the finger and peels off. it's a hot-dog stunt, but it makes the pilot (tom cruise) famous within the small circle of navy personnel who are cleared to receive information about close encounters with enemy aircraft. and the pilot, whose code name is maverick, is selected for the navy's elite flying school, which is dedicated to the dying art of aerial dogfights. the best graduate from each class at the school is known as "top gun." it turns out that maverick's dad was a brilliant navy jet pilot during the vietnam era, until he and his plane disappeared in unexplained circumstances. and it also turns out that one of the instructors at the flying school is a pretty young brunet (kelly mcgillis) who wants to know a lot more about how maverick snapped that other pilot's picture. it's pale and unconvincing compared with the chemistry between cruise and rebecca de mornay in "risky business," and between mcgillis and harrison ford in "witness" - not to mention between richard gere and debra winger in "an officer and a gentleman," which obviously inspired "top gun." cruise and mcgillis spend a lot of time squinting uneasily at each other and exchanging words as if they were weapons, and when they finally get physical, they look like the stars of one of those sexy new perfume ads. there's no flesh and blood here, which is remarkable, given the almost palpable physical presence mcgillis had in "witness." in its other scenes on the ground, the movie seems content to recycle old cliches and conventions out of countless other war movies.
