why have superman when tom does all day just about anything s-man could do?

the film is like a ship without a sail and headed in a direction full of sidetracks.

ethan hunt (tom cruise in a tom cruise production) and his team jane carter (paula patton), benji dunn (simon pegg) and william brandt (jeremy renner) are racing against time to track down a dangerous terrorist named kurt hendricks (michael nyqvist), who has gained access to russian nuclear launch codes and is planning a strike on the united states.

undaunted, ethan and his team chase hendricks to dubai, and from there to mumbai, but several spectacular action sequences later, they might still be too late to stop a disaster.

it all starts in budapest with the assassination of trevor hanaway (josh holloway) by sabine moreau (léa seydoux), proceeds to a prison breakout (ethan hunt has been imprisoned for killing some serbian guards), the russian secrets are discovered, aborted plans lead the team form the kremlin to dubai (for tom cruise's reportedly self performed scaling of a glass tower) and subsequently to mumbai and on and on an on for well over two hours.
tom cruise shows us once again his depth by playing tom cruise as usual, as he did in so many films before.
ethan hunt, after breaking out of a russian prison, is sent on a mission to retrieve vital information about a russian terrorist from a kremlin.

there is awesome cgi like the kremlin's destruction and the sandstorm in dubai and some cool chases and a few interesting stunts(tom cruise climbing the burj) but there is not even a small amount of tension.

it's the fourth mission impossible action spy drama set in 2010 featuring ethan hunt (tom cruise) and the impossible mission force.
ethan is being held in a russian prison but escapes with the help of jane carter (paula patton) and benji dunn (simon pegg), a new imf computer wizard.
hendricks bombs part of the kremlin, but the russians think ethan did it, as does the president, who now disavows the imf.
the russians kill imf secretary (tom wilkinson) in a car while talking to ethan and william brandt (jeremy renner), an imf analyst.
now on their own, ethan and the surviving imf folks try to stop hendricks and escape sidorov's pursuit.

the story moves between budapest, moscow, dubai, mumbai, and seattle.

this "mission impossible" has the usual chases (one wearies of watching tom cruise run) and spectacular derring-do by cruise climbing, leaping, and fighting.

after not only a 36 year wait but a painful few years in amongst that awaiting the covid-19 pandemic to be tolerated enough for cinemas to be back open for business as per usual, the sequel to iconic 1986 action thriller top gun has finally landed in the form of the much-hyped maverick.

a follow-up that has absolutely no right being as good as it is, director joseph kosinski and his star tom cruise have blown expectations out of the water for their return to the high flying world of american pilot extraordinaire captain pete "maverick" mitchell, a talented and confident loner who is still haunted by the death of his best friend and facing a changing world where his kind of pilot is no longer considered necessary in a changing landscape where man are too be replaced by machine.

perfectly balancing homages to the past that is sure to please die-hard fans, respecting the era in which top gun was birthed into, bringing in new characters to mitchell's world and giving us a story we can invest in while gifting us the adrenaline rush a film like this should inject into our eyeballs, maverick is a highly functional balancing act of pure entertainment, thrills and heart and while there's nothing out of the ordinary about the story being told in this venture, kosinski and cruise's commitment to the cause and ability to be at one with itself allows maverick to succeed where so many similar ventures have failed in recent times.

to call maverick one of the most successful sequels of all-time may seem far too over the top but with all things considered there's reason to be so buoyant about such a statement and the fact all involved with maverick were up for doing things the old fashioned way when it comes to stunts and set-pieces, ensures that the spectacle found within kosinski's fast-moving and constantly entertaining exercise is one of the best examples of hollywood filmmaking seen in the last decade, on par with the likes of mad max: fury road and cruise's other beloved property mission impossible when it comes to bang for buck and top-tier blockbuster outings.

it's extremely rare for a film of this kind to somehow give time and place to all of its components, giving them time to shine and work alongside one another but that's what happens here as the story of mitchell's grief and desire to find peace with his life comes full circle, all the while giving us a birds eye view of being a pilot in a generation of advanced military machines, culminating in one of the most memorable finales in some time that is sure to have audience members gripping their seats and swaying their heads left and right as the exploits in the skies take hold and kosinski and cruise's imaginations come to a stunning conclusion.

throughout all of this is a collection of memorable performances with cruise once more displaying a rare ability to possess hollywood charisma almost unlike any other peer while new additions to the top gun world such as miles teller as goose's son rooster (with teller looking uncannily like his fictional father), jennifer connelly as mitchell's love interest penny and glenn powell as the cocky hangman all making memorable appearances while a touching and important cameo from iceman himself val kilmer will be a significantly memorable moment for many children of the 80's.

final say -

old school hollywood filmmaking makes a triumphant return in the unexpectedly thrilling (and even moving) experience that is top gun: maverick.

when it was first announced that this would be happening, bringing back a now nearly 60 year old tom cruise as character maverick, i was highly skeptical.
shouldn't maverick be retired by now?

with the completely dependable tom cruise not missing a beat, easily stepping back into the shoes of maverick, and high flying, practical action that will...ahem...take your breath away, this 36-years-later sequel surprised the hell out of me.

the film's overall structure is pretty similar to the original film, with lots of training at top gun followed by a tough mission.
there's also an emotional elements established outright, with maverick still filled with guilt over the loss of his friend and roi from the first film, goose.
this is compounded by maverick having a soured relationship with goose's son, rooster, played by miles teller.

we also get some familiar character types here, the most notable being hangman, who is the pilot that most comes across as how maverick was in the first film.

the film's emotional and more visceral stakes are well established and keep the film feeling like more than just another retread of the original film, but even if you don't feel a strong connection to those aspects, you'll likely still find yourself entertained.
cruise wanted this done with practical effects and it really translates into an adrenaline pumping, well shot, exciting time.
i figured the film would lean hard into the nostalgia and give us a little bit of action, but i should have trusted tom more.

his high standards show here and director joseph kosinski, who's body of work (including previous tom cruise collaboration oblivion) would never suggest he would deliver something of this caliber, has certainly left a mark demonstrating his action filmmaking capability.
kind of like maverick, there is still a place for old fashion movie making.

"top gun: maverick" is nothing short of an instant cult classic and a much-needed cultural phenomenon for the modern cynical age!

while the trailer looked surprisingly impressive, tom cruise in a movie about an ageing jet pilot didn't exactly scream relevance.

this is not a competently made cash-grabber, "top gun: maverick" is what happens when people who love what they do put their heads together to try and make a great movie for the audience.

the last time a movie made me leave the cinema in such glee was way back in 2012 when "the avengers" took their deserved center stage.

i can only conclude that (the living icon) tom cruise, (the always on-point) mcq, and the (never again) underrated joseph kosinski have masterfully hacked into the collective subconscious and gave the world exactly what we didn't know we so desperately needed.

the entire cast and crew achieved the impossible and not only made one of the best sequels ever (!), but the movie itself is a living example of everything that we have been missing in movies for the last 10-15 years: viscerally real practical effects; a delightful throwback into simpler, saner times; and unapologetic fun.

hollywood will undoubtedly take notice, but only a handful of smart copycats will fully comprehend that this movies's magic formula is anything but easy.

"top gun: maverick" is so darn good precisely because it was not easy to make, because the cast and crew had to invest real-life sweat, blood, and perhaps even tears to bring it to life, because it doesn't pander to the audience.

it looks like the effort will be rewarded as tom cruise's love letter to cinema is on track to become one of the biggest box office blockbusters of all time.

top gun: maverick is a proper blockbuster that reminded me how important extra effort for practical effects can make.
top gun: maverick is just a fun movie, taking great lengths to ensure a truly cinematic experience, tom cruise's attention to detail and passion can be felt throughout.
maverick abandons the idea of capturing the feeling of a time period like how its predecessor did.

og top gun is filled to the brim with 80's energy, while maverick feels more timeless, harkening back to the past instead of living within it, and of course, it does, it's a sequel, that's what it's supposed to do.

but without the focus on capturing any sort of period, maverick has a lot more runtime to focus on other areas, and oh, does it use that time well.
all top gun: maverick centers around one mission, and builds up the tension and its characters to give the death-defying flying much more impact.

this way of centering everything around a singular goal works well for maverick, it gives everything a definitive reason for happening and gets the audience invested.(something i feel the original lacked.).

however, the biggest flaw has to be the lackluster side-story.

the relationship between maverick and penny is a low part, while it's not inherently bad, it just lacks when compared to whats around it.
i enjoyed what it did for maverick's character, and how it gave the tone and pacing a break so that the audience wasn't overwhelmed with action and high stakes.

so that just leaves these moments empty and lacking compared to the rest of the film.

top gun: maverick has an air of quality and dedication to it.
while i won't say maverick feels "21st century" in the same way the original feels "80's", it has all the other things audiences love, now with the volume cranked up.

most of the cast wasn't explored very much, but i still consider maverick to have a superb cast, both because of the actors' top-notch performances, and the dialogue, which sets the tone and shows the characters' personalities perfectly.

i loved how top gun: maverick made callbacks and handled the source material in its plot, instead of overt and cheesy callbacks that feel out of place, maverick instead slips in little continuities with the original that only fans will notice.

in particular, i have to commend the writers for plotting around val kilmer's (iceman) condition respectfully and realistically.

any complaints i can make amount more to missed potential than actual flaws which hamper the experience, top gun: maverick is a movie that plays on its strengths and downplays its weaknesses to create a film that, while nowhere near perfect, will stick with audiences for years to come and change the perceived level of quality movies should have.

in conclusion, the movie overall delivers what everyone liked about the original but through an updated lense, new characters; emotional, visual and musical references to the past while building a strong concluding future; and finally and most importantly, while delivering an enthralling and gripping actions stunts and mission very reminiscing of those "impossible missions" of the latest tom cruise involved mi.

tom cruise's personal views, but there's no denying he's a very strong actor, and he definitely comes through here, as does the rest of the cast.

the story develops nicely and logically, and the build-up is steady and gradual.
i don't like depressing endings, nor ones that leave you hanging, and maverick had neither of these issues.
the coyness and sass is all there to go toe to toe with maverick's personality, but still has that softer side that makes her realistic and fun.
as for maverick, cruise must have never left the role, because he hits the marks on every aspect and it works so well.
he pulls everything of maverick from the 80s and evolves it to the times, and in doing so accomplishes much with his character's revival in this story.
top gun maverick takes the elements of the original again, beefs them up with the visuals and gives you the combat school experience of the top gun program.
maverick's tale has evolved and like the acting, combines the old and new together to make that familiar feeling story.
the new age group going against the old, the military squabbles between maverick and the top brass, and plenty of history trying to find its place in the character lives.
maverick's opening flight gives you an idea of what is to come, and once the training is underway thing ramp up and go back to the familiar plane fighting antics you want.

however, compared to so many franchises this day, maverick really does achieve the balance for me and managed to take the energy of the original movie, advance it somewhat, and yet not make it something completely different.

again, a bit nitpicky, but something that gets me given how the rest of the movie flows.

the verdict: top gun maverick is a mission success in my book, in that it handled the big expectations quite well for me.
for something that could have crashed, tom cruise and the squad managed to balance old and new to levels i hoped we would see and made this soar.

tom cruise returns as pete "maverick" mitchell and assumes the role of flying instructor at his former academy, topgun, where he has to train the next generation of jet pilot recruits for an impossible mission.
can maverick train the new recruits to complete the mission successfully and make it safely back home?

that remains to be seen.

as a sequel to "top gun", "top gun: maverick" packs an emotional punch along with plenty of tense moments to keep the audience on the edge of their seats where the flying sequences and sound effects alone make the film worth seeing in theaters.
the action is great but there are also heartfelt moments involving maverick's relationship to characters and events from the first movie, including the tragic loss of his wingman goose.

although not many cast members from the original "top gun" reprise their roles in the sequel, val kilmer returns in a supporting role as iceman and even though his cameo in the sequel is relatively minor, you can still feel iceman and maverick's strong bond from the original movie which further adds to the sequel's emotional core.

overall, "top gun: maverick" is a fantastic sequel that retains the coolness factor of the original as well as delivering an emotional impact which makes it a sequel well worth the long wait.

in the art of filmmaking, execution is critical in keeping the audience hooked, and maverick successfully did it from start to finish.

the scenes on the beach can signify good times, like when the pilots play football, or uncertainty and sadness when maverick tells penny he's going on a mission.
but maverick makes all the pilots important by first showing them their nicknames and the goal of picking the best of the best.
that maverick's old partner, goose, died; in this movie, he's dealing with the conflict he has with goose's only son, rooster.

even iceman was essential for maverick's arc and the arc of the audience that people may come and go, but what's important is what they left behind.

with top gun: maverick, tom cruise and joseph kasinski delivers a thoroughly engaging, riveting and emotionally impactful sequel to a classic blockbuster, while simultaneously managing to improve upon the original in every possible way.

there is perhaps no other actor other than tom cruise who has managed to consistently maintain the same level of global stardom and public relevance for over four decades.
nearly 35 years later, cruise returns to his iconic role of pete "maverick" mitchell, the role that solidified his global stardom.

cruise once again showcases his acting talents and his unparalleled dedication to the craft as he along with other cast members, perform complex and difficult flight/aerial combat sequences that is all done practically by the actors themselves, with little to no usage of cgi.
the rigorous flight training undergone by cruise and the other cast members totally paid off, as all the aerial sequences, particularly the entire third act, forms the strongest aspect of the film.
instead, these are perfectly incorporated with the story and are even necessary for the development of maverick's character.
the impact of goose's death in the first film is present throughout this film and the effect the event had on maverick was perfectly portrayed.
maverick trying to be a surrogate father to goose's son, played by miles teller and his subsequent relationship with him, forms the emotional center and the true heart of the movie.

val kilmer's return as tom "iceman" kazansky was a truly delightful inclusion and resulted in one of the most emotionally powerful moments in the film.

the cinematography by claudio miranda was another noteworthy aspect as the film is filled with gorgeous visuals.

may it be a heart to heart exchange between two characters or an intense dogfight sequence, the music always manages to perfectly fit and elevate the impact of the sequences.

with exceptionally crafted aerial combat sequences, beautiful cinematography, emotional weight, nostalgic callbacks and a spectacular central performance by tom cruise, top gun: maverick succeeds at being one of the best legacy sequels ever made along with the likes of mad max: fury road and blade runner 2049, while simultaneously paying respect to the original film and further solidifying cruise's unrivalled starpower.

every cast member was special, unique, and added beautifully to the balance of the characters.

tom cruise did a phenomenal job, and i could see his hand throughout the whole movie.

top gun: maverick is the truly epic blockbuster we needed this year and it's everything that a good legacy sequel needs, it's one of the best movies i've seen this year and it's absolutely a movie that needs to be seen in theaters, you're missing out if you don't.

top gun: maverick is the reason you go to the movies, it's filled with outstanding action, incredible cinematography, riveting action, brilliant acting, and a solid heart beating at its center, miles teller, tom cruise, and jon hamm are all absolutely amazing here and it's got a truly epic 3rd act, it's a truly hilarious and heartwarming film that absolutely can be viewed on its own, the film reaches new heights and immerses you in the entire experience, similar to sequels like blade runner 2049, another absolute banger, i had an absolute blast with this film and i think it'll go down as one of the best legacy sequels of all time.

"top gun: maverick" is the sequel to the 1986 action drama film "top gun".

directed by joseph kosinski ("tron: legacy", "oblivion", "only the brave") and starring tom cruise, val kilmer, and miles teller, it exceeds the original film in every way possible by delivering a follow-up worthy of being considered one of the best sequels ever made.

thirty-six years after the events of the first film, pilot pete "maverick" mitchell (tom cruise) still remains in the rank of captain due to him intentionally avoiding promotion, which would result in him being grounded.

under the orders of his friend and former rival tom "iceman" kazansky (val kilmer), maverick is given the job of training a group of newly graduated members of the "top gun" program to undertake a dangerous mission.
upon meeting the young pilots for the first time, maverick notices that one of them is bradley "rooster" bradshaw (miles teller), the son of his deceased best friend "goose" (anthony edwards).

in spite of the initial tension he has between rooster and the rest of the pilots, maverick eventually earns their respect in the air as a skilled tactician capable of leading them through enemy lines.

if you are ever required to name movies that define high-octane 80s action to a tee, i'm sure "top gun" would be fairly high on many people's lists.

here, the film keeps its 80s roots to a minimum by presenting a more modern look at how much naval technology has advanced over the past three decades.

one scene in particular shows maverick flying his old fighter jet, complete with all the archaic bells and whistles, alongside the high tech present-day jets piloted by the younger crowd.

despite being a technical dinosaur by today's standards, maverick is able to manoeuvre his jet through the air with relative ease, showing these young folk that he is still a force to be reckoned with.
here, on the other hand, maverick is still just as confident and level-headed as he was in the first film, which is a refreshing change from that old formula.

with that said, it isn't entirely necessary to have seen the original to understand the full scope of the sequel's story, except for one major thing.

in order to fully grasp the importance of maverick taking rooster under his wing (pun very much intended), you need to be familiar with maverick's close friendship with goose in the first film.
since rooster is goose's son, the audience needs to know why maverick is so insistent on ensuring his safety.

aside from that, everything else in the film is conveyed very effectively, especially with how maverick is able to have remained such a skilled pilot after so many years.

i'm sure many will agree that one of the best things about the original film was its brilliantly shot dogfights.

reportedly, these creative decisions were made at tom cruise's insistence so we have him to thank for that.

even after more than three decades, tom cruise is more than capable of delivering another exciting performance here that, like everything else in this film, is better than the original.
his take on an older maverick is quite satisfying to watch, showing that despite the whole world changing around him, he has remained true to himself throughout even the worst of times.

regardless of what you may think of his personal life, you've got to hand it to someone this committed to giving the audience exactly what they want.

i also liked miles teller as rooster, the young and ambitious son of maverick's late best friend goose.

when he was first introduced, i half expected him to be arrogant and unlikeable given the hostility some of his fellow pilots initially show towards maverick, but for the most part he tries to remain respectful.
as the movie progresses, you really get the sense that maverick and rooster are forming a surrogate father/son bond, which makes their interactions so much more interesting.
many years from now, people will look back on "top gun: maverick" as a textbook example on how to do a sequel right, from the action scenes to the character motivations.
bravo tom.

tom cruise returns as pete "maverick" mitchell, and he hasn't lost an ounce of his charisma or edge.
his performance is a perfect blend of nostalgia and growth, as maverick grapples with his past while trying to guide the future.

the chemistry between cruise and the younger cast, particularly miles teller, who plays rooster (the son of goose from the original), brings an emotional depth to the film that complements the action.

what's refreshing about top gun: maverick is its straightforward, no-nonsense approach to storytelling.

his arc with maverick is one of the film's emotional highlights, and their evolving relationship brings a satisfying depth to the narrative.

the film is also a love letter to the original top gun, paying homage to key moments and characters while updating the story for a new generation.

yet, top gun: maverick stands on its own merit, delivering an experience that feels fresh and exhilarating, even for those who may not be familiar with the 1986 classic.

in a world where many blockbusters come with heavy-handed messages or convoluted plots, top gun: maverick is a breath of fresh air.

this is the kind of movie that reminds us of the magic of cinema, where the combination of storytelling, acting, and visual effects creates something larger than life.

overall, top gun: maverick is a spectacular achievement that's sure to satisfy both longtime fans of the original and newcomers alike.

whether you're here for the action, the nostalgia, or the incredible visuals, top gun: maverick delivers on every front, making it one of the best action movies in recent years and a worthy sequel to a beloved classic.

"top gun: maverick" is the long-awaited 2022 sequel to the iconic 1986 blockbuster "top gun," which turned its then-24-year-old star tom cruise into an international megastar and pop culture icon.
pete "maverick" mitchell (cruise) as he is reluctantly called back to topgun by his former rival adm.

tom "iceman" kazansky (val kilmer) to help train twelve elite naval aviators for what would otherwise be a suicide mission to bomb a secret military facility in a foreign - possibly russia, or russian-occupied - country.

this is why maverick is called back to train them, due to his experiences 36 years earlier in the first movie.

but training these new pilots for this mission won't be easy, since amongst them, is bradley "rooster" bradshaw (miles teller), the son of his late rio and best friend nick "goose" bradshaw (anthony edwards, from the original "top gun").
bradley resents maverick for stalling his flight career for four years while he was still at the naval academy and he also blames him for the death of his father in 1986.

tom cruise is at the top of his game, as always, and he uses his age - cruise just turned 60 today - to great advantage in showing us that while he is way past the prime of his youth (and he knows it) and many of his peers have succeeded him in the u.

of course you have the arrogant and pig-headed "hangman" (glen powell, filling in for "iceman"); ace female pilot "phoenix" (monica barbero), who is arguably the best and most level-headed of the bunch; her nerdy rio "bob" (lewis pullman); and then of course, there's miles teller's "rooster," who bears an uncanny resemblance to his father and even does his own live rendition of jerry lee lewis's "great balls of fire."

one of my greatest concerns going into "top gun: maverick" was the authenticity of the film's flying sequences.

here, it's even more authentic: the actors are actually in the cockpits of real flying f/a-18 hornets (the actors reportedly had to sign waivers attesting that they did not in fact have a fear of flying), which succeeds in re-creating the dizzying, vertiginous flying scenes that were made so famous in the 1986 original.

"top gun: maverick" is a long-delayed sequel that was well worth the wait.

the return of a now-60-year-old tom cruise, vertiginous flying sequences, a new generation of young naval aviators, and the delightful callbacks to the original "top gun" all made it worthwhile.

"top gun: maverick," the long-awaited sequel to the 1986 classic, delivers a thrilling ride that captures the spirit of the original while soaring to new heights.

directed by joseph kosinski, the film sees tom cruise reprising his iconic role as pete "maverick" mitchell, now a seasoned test pilot who is called back to train a new generation of elite fighter pilots.

from the opening scenes, "top gun: maverick" immerses the audience in breathtaking aerial sequences that are nothing short of spectacular.

the film balances high-octane action with emotional depth, exploring maverick's struggle with his past and the evolving nature of aerial combat.

cruise delivers a compelling performance, seamlessly blending maverick's daredevil spirit with a newfound maturity.
the supporting cast, including miles teller as bradley "rooster" bradshaw, the son of maverick's late friend goose, adds emotional stakes and new dynamics to the story.

jennifer connelly and jon hamm also provide strong performances, enriching the narrative with their characters' complexity.

while "top gun: maverick" pays homage to its predecessor with nostalgic callbacks, it stands on its own as a modern action epic.

us naval aviator captain pete "maverick" mitchell (tom cruise) still feels the need for speed and has turned down opportunities for promotion for fears of being grounded.
maverick is still passionate about flying and he still continues in the role as a test pilot.
maverick still continues to push the envelope and this time he defies orders not to fly a hypersonic prototype resulting in a crash after he successfully reaches mach 10.
rear admiral chester "hammer" cain (ed harris) manages to have maverick reassigned to nas north island in san diego to train a new group of top gun graduates.

vice admiral beau "cyclone" simpson (jon hamm) and rear admiral solomon "warlock" bates (charles parnell) feel that the presence of the aging aviator is unwanted, despite the fact maverick was only brought in at the request of former adversary turned friend admiral tom "iceman" kazansky (val kilmer who makes a welcome return to his iconic role despite his health issues) who is now the commander of the us fleet.

maverick is tasked with training the new group of top pilots for a secret mission to destroy a nuclear facility in an enemy compound.

one of the pilots is bradley "rooster" bradshaw (miles teller) who is the son of maverick's friend nick "goose" bradshaw (anthony edwards who appears in archive footage) who was killed in an accident in the original movie which still haunts maverick many years later.

other pilots brought in for the mission include jake "hangman" seresin (glen powell), robert "bob" floyd (lewis pullman), natasha "phoenix" trace (monica barbaro), reuben "payback" fitch (jay ellis), mickey "fanboy" garcia (danny ramirez), javy "coyote" machado (greg tarzan davis), brigham "harvard" lennox (jake picking) and logan "yale" lee (raymond lee).

maverick also rekindles his romantic interest with penny benjamin (jennifer connelly) who now owns a bar and is a single mother to daughter amelia benjamin (lyliana wray).

the fun and excitement continues just like the first movie and things get more intense and thrilling in the second half.

tom cruise shows that age will never slow him down as he returns as pete "maverick" mitchell.

as said before, maverick is still haunted by the death of goose but still cherishes the friendship that he since developed with iceman.

the rest of the main cast include jon hamm, miles teller, ed harris, glen powell, jennifer connelly, and val kilmer who are fantastic.

producer jerry bruckheimer turns everything up to 11 as he does what he does best.

along the way, maverick faces personal and professional challenges, including training a new generation of pilots, dealing with the loss of his former wingman goose, and reconnecting with his past.

tom cruise returns to his role as maverick and delivers an impressive performance, capturing the same charm and intensity that made his character so beloved in the original film.

additionally, the supporting cast, including miles teller as goose's son and jennifer connelly as a new love interest, brings depth and heart to the story.

the aerial sequences in top gun: maverick are nothing short of breathtaking, with stunning visuals and pulse-pounding action.

the film also features an updated soundtrack, with a mix of new and classic tracks that perfectly complement the high-flying adventure on screen.

overall, top gun: maverick is a worthy sequel that pays tribute to the original while carving out its own path.

cruise was in his early 20s when he first played pete "maverick" mitchell, the cocky young navy pilot with the aviator sunglasses, the kawasaki motorcycle and the need for speed.

and so the three screenwriters of top gun: maverick - including cruise's regular mission: impossible writer-director, christopher mcquarrie - have taken the threads of the original and spun them into an intergenerational male weepie, a dad movie of truly epic proportions.

for all of us who enjoy such excursions and want more of them in the future, top gun: maverick is the film we all needed.

for a very basic overview, maverick tells the story of the titular pete "maverick" mitchell (tom cruise), still breaking in cutting-edge flying machines with no designs on sitting behind a desk.

but in a world that has perhaps moved on from his ways, maverick is sent back to top gun to help train a new class--including one bradley "rooster" bradshaw (miles teller), whose name may sound familiar to fans of the original 1986 effort--for a seemingly impossible mission.

along the way, he rekindles a relationship with an old flame (played by jennifer connelly) and comes to terms with some unfinished business--both emotionally and in the skies.

first and foremost, tg: maverick is a 10/10 film--and easily, at that--because it perfectly balances the "new stuff" with the legacy material.
five minutes in, i knew that cruise and director joseph kosinski had the right formula.
not only that, but the focus is squarely on cruise's maverick pretty much throughout (as the title might suggest).
this isn't some cheap handoff to a "new crew" with cruise shepherding the transition.

there is something here for everyone (another cinema hallmark, come to think of it).

it is easy--and sometimes popular--to write off cruise's work due to some of his personal foibles.
unanswerable question, of course, but top gun: maverick puts him in the conversation, to be sure.
the future of cinema is still murky, to be sure, but as maverick himself intones about his supposedly impending extinction: "maybe so, sir...but not today".

set more than 30 years after the original top gun (1986), the film follows pete "maverick" mitchell (tom cruise) as he continues to defy expectations and push the limits as a navy pilot.
while his peers have moved into administrative roles, maverick remains a test pilot, refusing to be grounded.
maverick is not just training these young pilots; he's grappling with his own mortality, regrets, and the idea of passing the torch.

the film masterfully balances high-octane action with deep emotional stakes, making it much more than just a thrill ride.

tom cruise delivers his best performance yet

miles teller's rooster is equally compelling.
carrying the emotional baggage of his father's death, rooster's tension with maverick provides some of the film's most gripping moments.

their dynamic evolves beautifully, from resentment to mutual respect, culminating in one of the most satisfying character arcs in recent memory.

booking to see it on the manchester printworks vue imax (the largest screen in europe), i got set for a top viewing,of the new top gun.

view on the film:

reuniting with the lead actor after they had made oblivion (2013), director joseph kosinski is joined by his tron: legacy (2010-also reviewed) cinematographer claudio miranda in staging astonishing, high-octane action set-pieces.

specially developing imax-certified sony venice 6k full frame cameras just for this film, kosinski & miranda brilliantly place the audience in the cockpits right next to the pilots, with blazing wide-shots and tightly edited close-ups emphasizing the breath-taking views,and high risk of being shot down by an enemy pilot, seen from the air.

when on the ground, kosinski balances the thrills in the air, with ultra-stylized wide-shots following maverick bonding with the new recruits in a slo-mo beach sequence.

whilst keeping all the pilots ready to fly at any moment, kosinski wisely scatters quiet, more personal moments across the film, from the nicely understated, lingering romantic glances between hangman and rooster, (played with a sweet charm by glen powell and miles teller) and a heart-warming reunion maverick has with a old rival.

making it a condition when signing on that all the flying sequences would be done for real,and not cgi, the cruise missile gives a mesmerizing performance that hits every target, thanks to tom cruise visibly showing happiness when training the new recruits in the air, (with tom cruise designing a real 3 month program to train the rest of the cast to fly) and a weight of intense responsible upon the shoulders of maverick, over coming back home, in search of the next top gun.

top gun: maverick soars back onto the big screen with a bang, delivering an adrenaline-fueled sequel that captures the essence of the '80s classic.

however, i'm thrilled to report that top gun 2 not only lives up to expectations but surpasses them, offering a thrilling spectacle of aerial action, heartfelt drama, and nostalgic charm.

tom cruise reprises his role as the charismatic pete "maverick" mitchell, reminding us once again why he's the master of on-screen charisma.
cruise effortlessly slips back into the cockpit, radiating maverick's passion for speed and his unwavering dedication to his craft.

it's a testament to his acting prowess that he can still captivate audiences after all these years, infusing the character with a mix of humor, vulnerability, and undeniable charm.

joining cruise in this high-flying adventure is miles teller, who portrays goose's son, a talented pilot known as rooster.

the dynamic between maverick and rooster adds an emotional layer to the story, as the torch is passed from one generation to the next.

director joseph kosinski and cinematographer claudio miranda deserve accolades for their masterful work in capturing the essence of the original film's visual style.

the decision to use practical effects and real aircrafts further immerses the audience in the heart-pounding action, creating a genuine sense of awe and excitement.

while top gun: maverick pays homage to its predecessor, it also charts its own course, introducing new characters and storylines that blend seamlessly with the established universe.

the film strikes a careful balance between nostalgia and innovation, offering fans plenty of callbacks and easter eggs while still delivering a fresh and engaging narrative.

jennifer connelly delivers a standout performance as maverick's love interest, infusing the film with a touch of romance and vulnerability.

her chemistry with cruise is palpable, and their rekindled connection adds an emotional anchor amidst the adrenaline-fueled sequences.

the film is not without its flaws.

nevertheless, these minor shortcomings do little to dampen the overall enjoyment of the film.

top gun: maverick may not be a thought-provoking war film, but it never claims to be.

the movie's focus on real stunts and practical effects, coupled with tom cruise's unwavering dedication to the role, creates an exhilarating cinematic experience that will leave audiences on the edge of their seats.

in conclusion, top gun: maverick is a triumphant sequel that pays homage to its roots while forging its own path.
so buckle up, embrace the need for speed, and get ready to take flight with maverick once again.

we see several recruits and navy men on the ships where the pilots take off or make their returns.

captain pete "maverick" mitchell (tom cruise) rides his motorcycle to a base where he is set for a scramjet flight demonstration, but he is told that rear admiral chester "hammer" cain (ed harris) is on his way to shut the program down to redirect funds elsewhere.
not feeling deterred, maverick takes the jet just as cain arrives, and he flies it into the sky, taking it past its original mach 9 projection and hitting mach 10, to the delight of the crew.

however, maverick tries to take it faster and ends up wrecking the jet, but he manages to eject in time.

cain chews maverick out for his actions, but while he wants to have maverick grounded, cain instead informs him that he has been called back to nas north island by his former rival/colleague, admiral tom "iceman" kazansky (val kilmer).
maverick heads to the base to meet vice admiral beau "cyclone" simpson (jon hamm) and rear admiral solomon "warlock" bates (charles parnell).
cyclone makes it clear that he doesn't see in maverick whatever ice sees in him, but he informs maverick of the task at hand.

a rogue nation is operation a uranium facility, and maverick must teach a new group of recruits to find a way to make it to the base and bomb it.

maverick goes to a bar where he reunites with penny benjamin (jennifer connelly), an ex-girlfriend that he left a while ago, which pissed off her admiral father.
she bears no ill will toward maverick, but she ends up making him pay a round for everyone at the bar.
entering moments later is bradley "rooster" bradshaw (miles teller), son of maverick's late best friend goose.
after maverick's card declines, penny has hangman and payback playfully throw maverick out.

outside, maverick watches rooster playing the piano and is reminded of goose, but maverick still feels guilt over goose's death.

maverick later meets with the pilots to introduce himself and go over the mission.
since the facility is located deep at the bottom of a canyon, maverick's plan to take it out involves having two jets destroy the entrance to the facility before hitting the base itself.
rooster resents maverick because he pulled rooster's application and set his career back by four years.
maverick then goes on with the dogfight exercises with the pilots, showing off his skills to mess with the younger crew.

later on, hangman discovers rooster's connection to maverick.

maverick goes back to the bar to pay penny back what he owes her.

he then spends the afternoon on her boat with her, and there is clearly still a spark between them.

in the next round of exercises, maverick explains to the pilots about how they may lose oxygen and consciousness if they fly too high, reminded them of how high and low they will need to go when they carry out their mission.

hangman brings up maverick's friendship with goose, which provokes rooster into nearly attacking hangman, but the other pilots split them up.

ice requests maverick go visit him.
maverick expresses his concern over working with rooster, fearing that something will happen to him like with goose.

ice tells him he must work closely with rooster, and he manages to speak to maverick and tell him that the young pilots need him more than he realizes.

cyclone steps out onto the runway to find that nobody is there.
he finds that maverick brought the pilots over to the beach to play volleyball as a bonding exercise, which appears to work since they are all having fun.

maverick later goes out with penny and tells her that he pulled rooster's application because his mother asked maverick to look after him before she passed away.

the pilots then undergo a training exercise to strike the target at a certain altitude and in a certain amount of time.
maverick chastises rooster for how he handles his exercise, leading to them arguing over maverick hindering rooster's flying career.

a funeral is held for him days later, with maverick, penny, and the other pilots in attendance.

cyclone decides to take over instructional duties from maverick.

outside, the radars detect maverick flying his jet to complete the exercise, where he is able to fire at the target on the ground with seconds to spare, impressing all the pilots, including hangman.

the mission is carried out, with maverick picking rooster as his wingman, and being joined by hangman, phoenix, fanboy, payback, and bob.

the pilots start to fly back, but maverick's jet is shot at, causing him to crash.

rooster turns around and goes to save maverick.
a chopper begins firing at maverick while he is on foot, but rooster shoots it down, just before his own jet is shot down, but he manages to eject himself in time.
maverick and rooster reunite and devise a plan to get out of there.
although maverick manages to take two of them out with bullets and flares, they run out of weaponry just as a third jet comes their way.

rooster is also unable to eject himself, so the two accept that they are about to die until hangman comes through and destroys the last jet.

maverick and rooster make it back to the carrier, where their crew congratulates them.

rooster and hangman have a newfound respect for one another, while rooster looks at maverick the same way his father looked at him.

rooster helps maverick work on a p-51 mustang in maverick's hangar.
penny shows up, and maverick takes her for a flight in his plane.
rooster sets down a photo of himself and maverick right next to an older photo of maverick and goose.

top gun: maverick outdoes top gun in every conceivable way, and is the single best legacy sequel of all time, bar none.

the premise revolves around an aging maverick, who is called yet again to instruct new recruits at top gun.

joseph kosinski does a masterful job of directing this movie.

fighter weapons school finally feels like an actual military academy rather than a mere high school for adrenaline junkies.

tom cruise is quite literally the greatest movie star of all time.
i love how his character of pete mitchell has expectedly grown more nuanced and complex over the last 30+ years.

he appears tortured by events from the first movie, and his dynamic with bradley bradshaw (cast and played excellently by miles teller) is undoubtedly the film's most riveting aspect.

jennifer connelly has an astonishing amount of chemistry with cruise, and i don't think people give their on-screen relationship enough credit.

other pedigreed actors like jon hamm and ed harris, and lesser known ones like charles parnell all play their characters in memorable fashion.

maverick is also absolutely hilarious, and i can probably remember about 15 times when the audience around me burst into hysterical laughter (including myself, no doubt).

seriously, the final act alone is on par with any of the recent mission: impossible movies (also starrimg cruise), and even mad max: fury road.

maverick veritably dethrones the original movie's all time greatest aerial fight scenes with even better ones.

some segments of this film were so edge-of-your-seat thrilling that i'm surprised no one (especially me) got a heart attack or at the very least, passed out.

the end product is so well presented, it's rather difficult to pinpoint where the cgi ends and tom cruise's stuntwork begins (although, knowing him, i'm willing to bet he played his part in some of the stunning aircraft-mounted shots).

on top of that, the production of the non-action scenes was done well too, just like in the original.

i certainly enjoyed the restrained use of the first films music and score, incorporating some pretty good original songs like "i ain't worried" by onerepublic and lady gaga's spectacular "hold my hand".

top gun: maverick, directed by joseph kosinski, delivers a soaring return to the skies, eclipsing the legacy of its predecessor with thrilling aerial action and a poignant exploration of legacy, honour, and redemption.
set more than three decades after the original top gun, the film follows pete "maverick" mitchell (tom cruise) as he trains a new generation of elite pilots for a perilous mission.

with its breathtaking visuals, remarkable practical effects, and a performance that captures the essence of maverick, top gun: maverick is a captivating and emotionally resonant experience that elevates the franchise to new heights.

tom cruise delivers a standout performance, embodying maverick's fearless, rebellious spirit while adding layers of depth that showcase his character's growth over the years.
cruise expertly balances the physicality and vulnerability of maverick, portraying him as a man grappling with his past and navigating the complexities of mentorship.
the emotional core of the film is further strengthened by the chemistry between cruise and miles teller, who plays bradley "rooster" bradshaw, the son of maverick's late friend goose.

their dynamic adds a powerful layer of emotional depth, underpinned by themes of friendship, forgiveness, and loyalty.

kosinski's direction heightens the impact of top gun: maverick with awe-inspiring visuals and meticulously crafted aerial sequences that immerse the audience in the heart-pounding action.

the score, featuring contributions from harold faltermeyer and hans zimmer, provides an epic, nostalgic backdrop that complements the film's adrenaline-fueled pace.

beyond its spectacular action, top gun: maverick honours its origins while expanding on the original's themes of camaraderie and courage.

the film's focus on maverick's personal journey-balancing his role as a mentor with his need to reconcile with his past-imbues the narrative with emotional depth, allowing it to resonate beyond the spectacle.

by blending nostalgia with fresh perspectives, top gun: maverick stands as a powerful, self-contained story that speaks to audiences across generations.

in conclusion, top gun: maverick is an exhilarating, emotionally rich sequel that combines spectacular action with a heartfelt narrative, capturing the essence of what made the original iconic.
after more than three decades, top gun: maverick not only delivers a worthy sequel to the 1986 classic but surpasses it in nearly every way.

with breathtaking aerial sequences, emotional depth, and a powerful performance from tom cruise, this film is an unforgettable cinematic experience that balances nostalgia with fresh storytelling.

the story follows pete "maverick" mitchell, who, despite his legendary status, is still pushing the limits as a navy test pilot.

this emotional core drives the film, making it much more than just an action-packed thrill ride.

one of top gun: maverick's greatest strengths is its ability to blend heart-pounding action with genuine emotion.
the practical aerial stunts are nothing short of breathtaking, with cruise and the cast undergoing real-life flight training to ensure authenticity.
maverick's interactions with rooster are filled with tension and emotion, creating a compelling father-son dynamic that gives the film depth.

the balance between old and new characters is handled brilliantly, respecting the legacy of the original while paving the way for the future.

the film's soundtrack, featuring an epic score by hans zimmer and lady gaga's emotional song hold my hand, enhances every moment, making the experience even more powerful.

final verdict: top gun: maverick is more than just a sequel-it's a cinematic event.
with stunning visuals, an emotionally charged story, and a career-defining performance from tom cruise, it's a film that makes you feel proud, nostalgic, and exhilarated all at once.

"top gun: maverick" is the long-awaited sequel to the 1986 film "top gun," which starred tom cruise as pete "maverick" mitchell, a young naval aviator who is sent to top gun, the navy's elite fighter weapons school.

the sequel, set 34 years after the original film, stars tom cruise once again as maverick, now a flight instructor at top gun.

the film also stars miles teller, glen powell, and jennifer connelly.

the movie takes place decades after the original film, and follows maverick as he faces the challenges of modern air combat, including the use of unmanned drones.

maverick is also mentoring a new generation of pilots, including teller's character, bradley bradshaw, the son of his late wingman nick "goose" bradshaw, who died in the first film.

the film's visuals are stunning, with breathtaking aerial footage and state-of-the-art special effects.

the interactions between the characters are well-written, adding depth to the film.

tom cruise delivers another strong performance as maverick, showing the character's growth and maturity over the years.

he is surrounded by a talented supporting cast, with miles teller in particular delivering a standout performance as bradshaw.

overall, "top gun: maverick" is a thrilling and visually stunning film that is sure to delight fans of the original.

top gun: maverick is a love story about pete mitchell, call sign ''maverick'' (tom cruise), a distinguished pilot/naval aviator who uses his tough life situation to his advantage in order to re-ignite the past love with a stunning owner/bartender of a local military personnel favored bar penny benjamin (jennifer connelly).

penny benjamin was only referenced as a character in the original top gun, so bringing her on the big screen in the sequel was a great decision as is shown in the movie how much potential her character had.

due to the facts that maverick and penny have a shaky history and that penny is now a single mom, meaning her priorities have greatly changed, maverick realizes right away that he's going to have to really dig deep in order to achieve his goal, which is of course, to win penny's heart again, this time once and for all.

thus he puts an epic, extatic and romantic plan in motion in order to achieve his goal.

with the help of his old friend/wingman tom kazansky, call sign ''iceman'' (val kilmer), maverick gets reinstated back as the instructor in the famous top gun school in order to be close to penny's bar and therefore close to penny.
penny forces maverick's hand with the bar rules and puts maverick in a situation where he's forced to pay for everyone's drinks at the bar.
unfortunately for maverick, his card gets declined which reveals to penny that he doesn't really offer the financial security she, as a hard working single mom, deserves.

however, penny immediately shows why she got a hold of maverick's heart by showing she doesn't mind and thus reveals, although very subtly, that maverick still managed to lay a very much needed foundation for the achievement of his ultimate goal.

upon arriving at top gun school, maverick enters the second stage of his plan.

throughout the movie, maverick goes all out and over the top to achieve this crucial part of the plan - he gets really into it to the point where he even saves rooster's life at the end of the movie even though he didn't have to since penny was not there to see it.

by the end of the movie, maverick and rooster bond like father and son, thus showing maverick's second stage of his plan is complete.

and while completing the second stage of his plan, he also completes the third and final stage of his plan - the mission he was sent to do for the navy which he manages to do in a spectacular fashion, therefore solidifying himself as the man penny has been waiting for.

the message of the movie is beautiful and clear cut - it's never too late for love or, if you want, all you need is love.

whilst there are clear elements of nostalgia, they do not detract from the story, in which cruise's expertly-acted fighter-pilot ace "maverick" must confront and overcome past trauma in order to perform his duty and mend his broken relationships.

though the script was not particularly notable, powerful lines were delivered and the actors seemed to sink into their roles, conveying a lot of meaning through non-verbal communication.

the final act is an absolute goldmine of all-time wide-eyed cinematic awe, and that's not to undersell the earlier action scenes.

full of heart and surely satisfying fans of the original whilst also forging a new path for the franchise, top gun: maverick was an immensely enjoyable and satisfying experience.

besides being a powerful military recruitment tool, the film captivated audiences with tom cruise's charismatic performance as maverick, captivating aerial dogfighting scenes, and a now-iconic soundtrack.
that said, as a fan of tom cruise's action films, i was most certainly looking forward to seeing the sequel.

maverick is back as a flight instructor, and has to instruct a new class of fighter pilot recruits (among them the son of goose from the first film) to take out an enemy nation's uranium enrichment facility.
tom cruise still remains as charismatic as ever as maverick, but he's more thoughtful and wise this time.
the new recruits are all very strong in their performances, especially miles teller; the emotional and dramatic tensions between him and maverick over goose's death feel realistic and believably raw.
jennifer connelly is also great as penny, a bar owner and maverick's love interest.

unlike many other blockbusters that feel they could have been trimmed by 30 minutes or so, the film is practically immaculately paced--with no scenes that feel too long or too short to keep the audience thoroughly interested and entertained through its entire runtime of a little over 2 hours.

"top gun: maverick" proves that you can have a summer blockbuster that manages to excel in the highest levels of technical and aesthetic prowess and never lose sight of a genuinely powerful, relevant, and thoughtful story--all while simultaneously keeping the audience entertained and thrilled from beginning to end.

cruise was in his early 20s when he first played pete "maverick" mitchell, the cocky young navy pilot with the aviator sunglasses, the kawasaki motorcycle and the need for speed.

in the sequel, he's as arrogant and insubordinate as ever: now a navy test pilot in his late 50s, maverick still knows how to tick off his superiors, as we see in an exciting opening sequence where he pushes a new plane beyond its limits.

and so the three screenwriters of top gun: maverick - including cruise's regular mission: impossible writer-director, christopher mcquarrie - have taken the threads of the original and spun them into an intergenerational male weepie, a dad movie of truly epic proportions.
in that respect, top gun: maverick feels like a throwback to a lost era of practical moviemaking, before computer-generated visual effects took over hollywood.

you start to understand why cruise, the creative force behind the movie, was so driven to make it: in telling a story where older and younger pilots butt heads, and state-of-the-art f-18s duke it out with rusty old f-14s, he's trying to show us that there's room for the old and the new to coexist.

top gun: maverick is a long-awaited sequel to the 1986 classic top gun, which left a lasting impact on pop culture with its iconic soundtrack, memorable characters, and thrilling aerial combat scenes.

as a fan of the original film, i was excited to see how top gun: maverick would live up to its predecessor.

the movie follows the story of pete "maverick" mitchell, now a veteran pilot who is tasked with training a new group of top gun graduates.

as he navigates his new role as a mentor, maverick must also confront his past and overcome personal challenges.

the film does a great job of capturing the nostalgia of the original while also introducing new and exciting elements.

the addition of new aircraft and technology also adds to the excitement.

tom cruise delivers a strong performance as maverick, showing both his confident and vulnerable sides.

the story explores themes of loss, redemption, and loyalty, making the characters more relatable and giving the film more depth than just a simple action flick.

overall, top gun: maverick is a worthy successor to the original film, delivering on the nostalgia and excitement that fans have been waiting for while also introducing new elements to keep things fresh.

top gun: maverick (also called top gun 2: maverick) is a 2022 american action drama film directed by joseph kosinski, a sequel to the 1986 film top gun.

it premiered on may 27, 2022 in the united states.

it grossed $1.493 billion worldwide, becoming the second highest-grossing film of 2022, the second film released since the covid-19 pandemic to gross $1 billion, and the highest-grossing film of tom cruise's career.

the best thing about the movie was knowing that maverick (tom cruise), although more than 30 years have passed, still does not forget the death of goose (anthony edwards) since every time he looks at rooster (miles teller) it always comes to him.

now, in 2022, with my family tow, we sat in the lido again, seeing these these iconic words flash across the screen, that unstoppable rush of nostalgia gushes out with palpable force from the very first frame of top gun maverick, and what a fantastic movie it has been!
the people behind the movie, jerry bruckheimer, joseph kosinski, tom cruise et al have made this a labour of their love.

with the passing of time comes emotional maturity, and dear me, the emotional segments, especially that brief reunion scene between maverick and ice man reaches deep into your memory and pulls out those bygone feelings which has been buried deep in your heart for so many years.

36 years is a long time wait but top gun: maverick delivers for both new and returning audiences in a sequel that is superior to the original 1986 box office hit.
as executive producer for the film, cruise's insistence on authenticity and excellence are on display throughout the film.

audience response has been nothing short of phenomenal, earning over $1.4 billion at the box office to date.

as the film opens, viewers discover that pete mitchell (aka maverick) has aged but he's still the maverick.

ignoring orders from his ceo, maverick skips an intermediate stealth fighter test and switches directly to the project final objective target (mach 10) to save the project and succeeds but at the cost of the aircraft which explodes.

fully expecting dismissal by commanding radm in charge of the project, maverick is informed he has been reassigned to fightertown usa (top gun training school) instead.

a secret mission is necessary to eliminate a uranium refining complex being developed against international sanctions in an underground location within a mountain that's due to start receiving nuclear materials within 3 weeks by a rogue nation.
sounds like a job for ethan hunt but maverick will have to do.
to succeed maverick will have to resort to unorthodox training techniques to develop personnel who function as a team and think outside the book.

his role is complicated by the inclusion of the son (rooster) of his deceased best friend (goose) on the training roster.

top gun: maverick succeeds in every level possible.
cruise has committed every resource to this personal project.
guess who really owns that wwii vintage mustang in maverick's hangar?
did the cruise missiles come from that same source?

and the movie also injects humor into the film regularly to offset the more serious themes.

cruise fully committed himself to his signature role as maverick eliminating the cockiness of the youthful character for a more measured performance but retaining his rep as a 'maverick'' at critical moments within the structure of the story.

not only does maverick have to contend with his own morality, obstinate superiors, and the eventual end of his flight career but he also wrestles with his guilt over goose's death, along with potential casualties among his trainees if he fails as an instructor (especially rooster, because it involves a promise).

will maverick ever be able to form long-term relationships with the opposite sex or just die alone?

cruise's performance is backed by the entire cast including ed harris (cain to maverick's able), jon hamm (cyclone), charles parnell (warlock) and bashir salahuddin (hondo) with newcomers monica barbaro (phoenix), glen powell (hangman) and miles teller (rooster) shining among the mission's top gun candidates.
jennifer connelly as maverick's old flame, penny, is believable in a romance targeted for mature audiences which rates almost a pg rating.

as the only returning member from the 1986 hit, val kilmer's gives a touching performance (to anyone who's aware of kilmer's real-life medical plight) as maverick's confident and 'guardian angel' iceman (adm.
doesn't penny's porsche bear a striking resemblance to the same vehicle from cruise's 1st hit in 1983?
was that obi wan imploring rooster to trust his instincts or maybe jedi master maverick on the headphones?

the film exceeded all expectations, so i give top gun: maverick 11 stars out of 10 stars.

the danger zone for sequels is merely rehashing what worked before and hoping the audience didn't notice the lack of quality or care in the midst of six-packs, beach games, and high-flying jets--something "top gun: maverick" wisely avoids.

when you're in the company of hollywood's tireless maverick in tom cruise, premium entertainment is promised.
it's been over 30 years since cruise's pete mitchell aggressively took to the skies to steal the hearts of 80s romantics and beat the bad guys in the end, but little rust can be seen on the new film.

the wait was well worth it, because these scenes push the envelope for what hollywood can do in the sky.

think of cruise's pilot as that incendiary (for a good reason) element that won't accept less than top-tier entertainment.

when maverick finishes the flight by going so fast over a closed down gas station that the roof lifts temporarily into the air, you'll feel the good vibrations too just like ed harris' old curmudgeon rear admiral does, even if his "hammer" doesn't approve of the younger captain's methods.

every character has unique call names, like glen powell's hangman (a combo of young maverick and iceman) and miles teller's rooster.
it's teller's affecting portrayal of the son of goose, anthony edwards' best friend to cruise's pilot in the first film, that acts as the launch pad of the plot.
when maverick is called back in to train young top guns, the tempestuous relationship with teller's ben bradshaw burns at the core of the mission.
the arrival of jennifer connelly as the flame that got away from maverick is a classy, old-school cinema romance, and jon hamm makes for a steely admiral.

it all just works well together.

little works better or will become more emotional than val kilmer's return scene as maverick's former rival and current friend, tom "iceman" kazansky.

soulful is the word, and it's a scene you won't soon forget.

"top gun: maverick" is a movie i won't soon forget.
with all the tragedy happening throughout the world, a little cruise goes a long way.
he's the real-life maverick, pushing the envelope until it sticks together, forming a cohesive sequel that makes you feel the rugged yet exhilarating power of scott's original.

as people call into question his ruthlessness on set and his unusual offscreen persona, the legendary actor proves he's still got the need for speed--as do we.

cruise and company were all set to get this film going ten years ago before the director's untimely death, and i think this is something ridley's brother would absolutely adore.

from the lady gaga theme song-she's easier on the eyes and ears than kenny loggins-to the piano sing-along scene to the thrilling finale that will keep you guessing, "top gun: maverick" checks all the boxes of a worthy sequel.

cruise was in his early 20s when he first played pete "maverick" mitchell, the cocky young navy pilot with the aviator sunglasses, the kawasaki motorcycle and the need for speed.

in the sequel, he's as arrogant and insubordinate as ever: now a navy test pilot in his late 50s, maverick still knows how to tick off his superiors, as we see in an exciting opening sequence where he pushes a new plane beyond its limits.

and so the three screenwriters of top gun: maverick - including cruise's regular mission: impossible writer-director, christopher mcquarrie - have taken the threads of the original and spun them into an intergenerational male weepie, a dad movie of truly epic proportions.
in that respect, top gun: maverick feels like a throwback to a lost era of practical moviemaking, before computer-generated visual effects took over hollywood.

you start to understand why cruise, the creative force behind the movie, was so driven to make it: in telling a story where older and younger pilots butt heads, and state-of-the-art f-18s duke it out with rusty old f-14s, he's trying to show us that there's room for the old and the new to coexist.

top gun: maverick (2022), directed by joseph kosinski, is a triumphant return to the high-flying action and emotional depth that made its predecessor iconic.
tom cruise reprises his role as pete "maverick" mitchell, now a seasoned navy aviator who remains a test pilot, dodging promotions that would ground him.

the film explores maverick's struggle with his past, his fears, and his connection to the next generation of pilots, all while delivering heart-pounding aerial combat sequences.

the story, while familiar in its themes of redemption and confronting past demons, is brought to life by the powerful performances of the cast.
tom cruise, as always, exudes charisma and emotional depth as maverick, portraying a man caught between the thrill of flying and the weight of his past.
bradley "rooster" bradshaw, brings a compelling mix of defiance and vulnerability to his role, effectively capturing the tension and unresolved grief between maverick and rooster.

jennifer connelly also shines as penny, maverick's love interest, providing both warmth and complexity to her character.

the film's pacing is deliberate, allowing time for character development before launching into its exhilarating flight sequences.

the sound design and music, including the iconic "danger zone," heighten the adrenaline of the action and the emotional stakes of the story.

top gun: maverick is not just a nostalgic ride for fans of the original film; it is a testament to the power of personal growth, legacy, and sacrifice.

top gun maverick is like the original movie, only bigger in every department (well, except for cruise, who is still short): the action scenes are jaw-dropping, adrenaline-fuelled cinema guaranteed to get the scalp tingling in excitement, while the macho posturing and romantic drama is cheeze, smothered with cheeze, with an extra layer of cheeze, topped with a sprinkling of '80s clichés.
likewise, this sequel's dramatic moments - the bar scene, the love interest, the rivalry, maverick's soul-searching - make much of the film feel like a very silly parody.

fortunately, when the film leaves the ground, things improve considerably: maverick's opening mach 10 flight is edge-of-the-seat stuff, the training scenes are thrilling, and the final mission is some of the best action that i have seen in a long time, ending the movie on a high, viewers leaving the theatre with a grin almost as wide as tom's.

if you are looking for a fun summer movie, anticipating the nostalgia for the top gun 1986 hit, want a theatre movie that the whole family can enjoy, or you simply like a well-made mixture of drama, action, and romance, you really can't go wrong by giving top gun:maverick a watch on the big screen.

bringing back the main character from the first top gun film, tom cruise as captain pete "maverick" mitchell, top gun: maverick shows maverick 30 years (or so) after the events of the first film with "just one more" mission to go.

maverick is brought back to train a dozen hot-shot pilots, including one that is the son of his best friend - a friend who's death maverick has been traumatized by during the past 30 years.

cruise, of course, is perfect in this role.

jennifer connelly is on board as the requisite love interest and she more than holds her own with cruise in what is an underwritten role as are all of the roles in this film by writer peter craig (bad boys for life) with direction by joseph kosinski (oblivion).

miles teller (the son of the man who maverick is mourning, who blames maverick for his dad's death), john hamm (the a-hole boss that thinks that maverick is "writing checks his body can't cash"), glen powell (the arrogant young hot shot) and the rest are all one-note caricatures that leaves the audience not really caring about their fate.

only val kilmer (reprising his role as "iceman" from the first movie) comes out of this unscathed for his character is suffering from throat cancer and cannot speak above a whisper (much like kilmer in real life).

it is the type of flick that one doesn't have to pay to close attention to, but when it does grab your attention, it does it well...enough.

if you have the need...the need for speed...you can do much worse than top gun: maverick.

36 years later, tom cruise returns as maverick in the sequel to tony scott's top gun.

after more than 30 years of service as one of the navy's top aviators, pete "maverick" mitchell is where he belongs, pushing the envelope as a courageous test pilot and dodging the advancement in rank that would ground him.

training a detachment of graduates for a special assignment, maverick must confront the ghosts of his past and his deepest fears, culminating in a mission that demands the ultimate sacrifice from those who choose to fly it.

through a cleaner lens, kosinski captures a slick tom cruise suiting up with his iconic shades and leather jacket before speeding through los angeles open space as the sun sets in the background.
a fitting scene to translate: maverick is back.
cruise and teller master their art in difficult roles.

allusions to the past help facilitate the forward direction of the plot, though, they also offer scenes of nostalgia, particularly in an exchange between kilmer and cruise, the former, whom suffers from throat cancer, ensured he encapsulated the respect and integrity of his famous name 'iceman'.

the action in this film swirls inexorably around captain pete 'maverick' mitchell.
an admiral arrives played by ed harris to shut the project down, but instead of being forced out of the navy maverick is ordered back to top gun school in miramar, ca to be a special instructor.

the navy has assembled a best of the best of recent top gun classes for a specialized combat mission, and thanks to the events of the first film, maverick is one of the only pilots to engage the enemy and therefore is deemed an appropriate person to train the mission.

while most of the navy seems to hate maverick iceman maintains an affinity for him and has been able to ensure he stays gainfully employed by the navy all these years as he has attained the rank of admiral and serves as commander of the us pacific fleet thereby in a perfect position to be a guardian angel for maverick.
he bears a grudge against maverick not only for the death of his father, but maverick blocked bradshaw's ability to enter the naval academy delaying his career.
the mission they are set to fly seems impossible until in a last ditch brash move maverick flies the course and in the process becomes the team leader of the mission as if no one saw that coming.

maverick and rooster make amends and bond, while mav also has a love interest that solidifies over the course of the story.

this film essentially begins with navy aviator "pete 'maverick' mitchell" (tom cruise) now working as a test pilot on a project designed to evaluate the capability of a protype jet designed to travel at mach 9.

to that effect, rather than allowing the project to be terminated, maverick makes boards the protype with the stated intention of flying it at mach 10-regardless of whether the airplane can handle the stress or not.

infuriated by all of this, rear admiral cain considers ending captain mitchell's career but is prevented from doing so when orders come through transferring maverick to the top gun school for a special assignment.

not only that, but one of the pilots by the name of "lieutenant bradley 'rooster' bradshaw" (miles teller) has been nursing a personal grudge against maverick for some time and, in the course of the training, it spills over for all to see.
