basically, over thirty years since the previous events, captain pete "maverick" mitchell (tom cruise) has avoided promotion and continues serving and flying as a u.
maverick decides to take the darkstar prototype and reach its mach 10 speed objective before cain shows up.
cain arrives just as maverick takes off, and he watches as he does the objective.
but maverick cannot help himself and decides to push further into high-hypersonic speed, resulting in the destruction of the prototype.
maverick survives the crash and is threatened to be grounded by cain for his recklessness.

but instead, he is sent to nas (naval air station) north island, back to naval fighter weapons school, better known as topgun, to be an instructor, under the orders of maverick's friend and former rival, admiral tom "iceman" kazansky (val kilmer), the commander of the u.
maverick is ordered to train a group of elite pilots assembled by vice admiral beau "cyclone" simpson (jon hamm) and rear admiral solomon "warlock" bates (charles parnell).
maverick plans an attack with two pairs of super hornets, which will fly through a canyon and destroy the plant, while also exceeding the hornet's limits.

maverick is initially rebuffed by the pilots, particularly by the self-confident lieutenant jake "hangman" seresin (glen powell) and by lieutenant bradley "rooster" bradshaw (whiplash's miles teller), the son of maverick's late best friend of co-pilot nick "goose" bradshaw.
as the pilots observe maverick's skill, they reassess and begin to respect him.
meanwhile, maverick reunites with former love interest penny benjamin (jennifer connelly), who reveals that rooster's now-dead mother carole made him promise to keep her son from flying.
it turns out that maverick blocked rooster's application to the naval academy, setting back his career for a few years, hence why he had a disdain for him.
maverick later meets with iceman, who has throat cancer and communicates by typing on his computer.
he reassures maverick about teaching the pilots and says he needs to let go of any guilt he has for goose's death.
iceman loses his battle with cancer and passes away days later, with maverick and the pilots attend his funeral.
with iceman gone, cyclone removes maverick as mission trainer.
however, maverick makes an unauthorised flight of the simulated course with the original parameters he planned, with a demonstration of the targeted bombing, and proves that it can be done.
cyclone is convinced, and reluctantly appoints maverick as strike leader.

maverick chooses the mission pilots and is paired with lieutenant natasha "phoenix" trace (monica barbaro) and her wso (weapon systems officer) lieutenant robert "bob" floyd (lewis pullman, bill's son), while rooster is paired with lieutenant reuben "payback" fitch (jay ellis) and his wso lieutenant mickey "fanboy" garcia (danny ramirez).
the team launches from the aircraft carrier uss theodore roosevelt while the cruiser uss leyte gulf fires tomahawk cruise missiles to destroy the air base near the plant.
when rooster runs into trouble, maverick sacrifices his jet to protect him and ejects.
maverick is believed to be killed in action, so the remaining aircraft return to the carrier.
against orders, rooster turns back to rescue maverick from an mi-24 helicopter gunship.
maverick and rooster shoot down two intercepting su-57s, but a third arrives as they run out of weapons and countermeasures.
the third su-57 is shot down by hangman arrives from standby, and the planes return to the carrier, with everyone praising them, and maverick and rooster reconcile.
sometime after the mission, maverick and rooster work together on a p-51 mustang at a hangar near the test facility where maverick was previously stationed.
penny arrives with her teenage daughter amelia (lyliana wray), and maverick takes her for a ride in the aircraft.
rooster walks to a photo board and acknowledges a photo of their mission's success, alongside a photo of his late father and a younger maverick.

the student becoming the teacher is pretty much the only intelligent inversion in this film.

imagine the final act of star wars a new hope, from the briefing to the trench run.

now stretch that bad boy out to two hours.

that's top gun: maverick.

to be fair, it's also two hours of smirky macho one-upmanship.

great flying sequences, but maybe the combat training would go smoother if everyone stopped comparing their johnsons every two minutes.

two hours of women used only as wise-woman emotional-support cheerleaders.

two hours of maverick impulsively saving people from impulsive decisions by teaching them to act more impulsively.

this recklessness - dare i say 'maverick nature' - seemingly permeates the environment.

the premise itself of using cadets to conduct a half-baked pre-emptive strike on a sovereign nation is impulsiveness on a strategic and political scale (wmds, anyone?).

please stop thwacking us over the head with it.

the sad thing is not that so much was unthought-through.

the sad thing is that impulsiveness led to so much waste.

jennifer connelly is wasted as the torch-carrying single-mum.

glen powell and monica barbaro are wasted as supposedly pivotal squadron members who are sidelined as soon as they spur the protagonists' character development.

ed harris is wasted as the hard-ass admiral, whose ominous drone program i swore would feature later on.

eight of the twelve pilots - including my fave manny jacinto - are wasted, as nothing they do matters, and the story only focuses on a few, especially maverick's son-figure.

the biggest waste was the potential for maverick to pass the torch graciously to the next generation.

the original film's director, tony scott, passed away in 2012 at age 68, and joseph kosinski (oblivion, 2013, also starring tom cruise) takes the helm.

callbacks to the original are plentiful, and we get our first in the opening title card - the same one used in 1986 to explain the "top gun" training center.
of course, there is one reason we are here, and that's tom cruise.
he was only 24 years old in the original, and now lives and exudes the swagger of pete "maverick" mitchell.

when the film opens, maverick is an extreme test pilot pushing himself and an experimental aircraft to mach 10, and yes, this goes against the wishes and order of the program's rear admiral in charge played by a curmudgeonly ed harris.
it's a shame that harris only has a couple of brief scenes, but he is the one that informs maverick of his new orders to return to top gun immediately.
his new commanding officer is beau "cyclone" simpson (jon hamm), who is none too happy about maverick being back.

however, the order came directly from maverick's old nemesis/friend, tom "iceman" kazansky (val kilmer), now a highly decorated admiral in failing health.

maverick is disappointed to learn that he has been brought in, not to fly, but to teach a group of top gun graduates how to execute an extraordinarily dangerous mission involving extended high speeds at a low altitude, dropping bombs on the uranium enhancement plant protected by a mountain range, and then immediately elevating to a nearly impossible level to avoid a crash - all while being targeted by the enemies radar and defense system.

plus, this film is about thrills and action, not a political statement.

being back means maverick crosses paths with penny benjamin (jennifer connelly), who was mentioned briefly in the first film as an admiral's daughter.
she now owns the local bar, has a daughter, races sailboats, and still carries a bit of a torch for maverick, although she's quick to bust his chops whenever possible.
however, it's the pilots he's charged with training that cause the biggest issue for maverick.
rooster is the son of "goose" (played in the original by anthony edwards), who flew with maverick as his radio intercept officer (rio) and died in an ejection mishap.
rooster holds maverick responsible and maverick is still haunted by his friend's death.

the conflict between rooster and maverick adds complications to the mission - and a bit of melodrama to the entire film.

the newbies (and the navy) consider maverick a relic of a bygone era, so of course, 'instructor' maverick takes to the sky to strut his pilot stuff.

in addition to rooster, the standouts in the new group include phoenix (monica barbaro), bob (lewis pullman), and hangman (glen powell), the latter of whom, along with rooster, tries to recreate that symbiotic relationship we originally saw with iceman vs maverick.

teller and powell are both solid, but this aspect never really clicks like the rooster vs maverick piece.

we can't help but notice that the dramatic elements seem to be more of a focus this time around.
the situation is handled with grace, and we are appreciative of cruise standing firm in his demand for kilmer to appear in the film.
as for the love story between penny and maverick, it had to be a bit frustrating for ms.

connelly to work so hard on an underwritten role, while jon hamm's constant furrowed brow and barking leaves him coming across as little more than jealous of maverick.

obviously it's the fighter jets and aerial sequences that folks will come for, and spectacular and exhilarating are the best words i can find to describe what we see.

sand volleyball has been replaced by some semblance of shirtless and sweaty beach football as a team-builder, and yes, we get the patented tom cruise sprints - three times: on a treadmill, during beach football, and in a forest.
those from the original who are absent this time are the great tom skerritt, james tolkan, kelly mcgillis, and meg ryan (whose character is mentioned as having passed away).

taking place 36 years after the first top gun film, this sequel follows captain steve "maverick" mitchell as he confronts his past and returns to top gun as a trainer.
one of the pilots he must train is bradley "rooster" bradshaw, the son of maverick's deceased best friend goose.

maverick faces the grievance of losing goose again as he tries to find a way to make sure that rooster and the other new pilots do not die in the new mission.

what i like the most about top gun: maverick is that above all else, it is a movie about dealing with a loss and letting go of guilt.
maverick is still racked with guilt over goose's death 36 years ago and with goose's son about to enter a life-threatening mission, maverick hates the idea of even allowing rooster to go the mission.
all it is doing is making the son of maverick's best friend resent him even more.

it is a good way of showing how pushing others back is not the answer.

maverick's guilt also bleeds into the training of the young pilots.
in some of the training sessions, maverick will emphasize the loss of a pilot's life by asking his trainees what they would tell the victim's family and friends.
this is a powerful moment to not only show the dangers of aerial combat, but to also emphasize maverick's motivation: to complete the mission with zero deaths.
the training sessions show that in spite of his rather insane methods, maverick cares about all of the pilots and he does not want any of them to die or to feel the weight of losing each other.

the theme of guilt and letting go of it is tackled professionally and it gives a humane layer to the story of the film.

performance-wise, tom cruise is at his best here.
he is a much more mature maverick here while still carrying the risky and fun personality from over three decades ago.

the chemistry between these two is better here than in the chemistry between cruise and kelly mcginnis in the first film, but even with that, i feel this was a missed opportunity to bring mcginnis back and develop the relationship between maverick and charlie.

i think the romance could have replaced with more scenes of maverick and rooster's interactions.

and now, for the dogfights...
i felt the rush of flight sequences from the moment maverick flies a jet to a speed objective.

the soundtrack is awesome too with the return of some classic songs such as danger zone and a great musical score by harold faltermeyer and hans zimmer.

it certainly helps that top gun: maverick actually has a plot with a beginning, middle, and ending that we can follow, unlike its meandering predecessor.

the story sets up a mission with clear-cut stakes and impossible odds very early on, and the threat and pressure felt by these pilots was felt by me for almost the entirety of the film.

after a clunky first act with very cheesy, expository dialogue, the story really gets going with interesting characters, extremely well shot and edited action sequences that put you in the center of the action, well-intentioned humor, and a romantic subplot that is a lot more believable and relevant than the one in the first movie.

plot-wise, there are certainly several elements that don't make sense and can't stand up to logical scrutiny.
the hero in question was maverick, played by tom cruise, and the original top gun was very much his film.
top gun maverick provides us with a lot more flying and a lot more maverick.

36 years later, one can see how updated technology, of both the plane and camera variety, would make fresh flying scenes appealing, but surely, three-and-a-half decades later, tom cruise as maverick can not be the same heroic figure that he once was.
well, no-one told tom cruise that and nor should they have.
in fact, tom cruise has defied the aging process much more successfully than the original top gun film.
technologically, top gun maverick soars miles above its predecessor.
rooster (played by miles teller) is the son of maverick's late best friend, goose, and his character provides this redemptive arc.
rooster is both a surrogate son and a potential best-friend-in-the-making to maverick.
maverick is much older in years and he has become wistful and reflective over time.
the best scenes in the film, for my money, are at the beginning, when maverick is surveying the generation of fighter pilots who have ostensibly replaced him.
maverick is a man who has seen all of his former colleagues either pass away or age out.
but, of course, this is the world of top gun, and in this world maverick is always the hero.
the higher the stakes, the more heroic maverick will become.

it doesn't matter that maverick is now twice the age of all the other hotshot top gun pilots, he'll outpace and outperform them because that is what top gun requires, the hero must prevail at all costs.

there are many flights of fancy and there is a general sense of unbelievability regarding significant portions of the plot but there is always just enough risk so that the film never quite lets go of its emotional pull.

it taps into a pureness and simplicity that audiences still clearly yearn for but which is now extremely difficult to deliver in a manner that is convincing and satisfying.

more generally, both tom cruise and top gun maverick represent a generation of hollywood which is out-of-step with current trends.

undeniably top gun is one of the biggest cultural benchmarks of the 80s as the film was not only the highest grossing film of 1986, but it's also responsible for launching the careers of tom cruise as an a-list leading man and director tony scott as a uniquely identifiable hand behind blockbuster filmmaking with his high-speed editing and magic hour photography influencing an entire generation of filmmakers.
despite being tom cruise's first major blockbuster, cruise had initially expressed no interest in doing a follow-up as he said as much during a press tour for born on the fourth of july in 1990.

during 2010 however negotiations began with producer jerry bruckheimer, director tony scott, tom cruise and paramount about a follow-up to top gun addressing the end of the dogfighting era and rise in drone warfare, but the development was curtailed with the unfortunate suicide of tony scott in 2012 leaving the projects fate in doubt.

eventually the project regained traction in 2017 with oblivion director joseph kosinski reteaming with cruise as director and the film began production in 2018 but was delayed from its original 2019 release due to the complexity of the aerial sequences and became the poster child for covid delays as top gun: maverick much like the james bond film no time to die went through a cycle of release dates and reschedules as offers from streaming were rejected by cruise who insisted it be released in theaters.
once released the film became the biggest of cruise's career making nearly $1.5 billion against its $170 million budget and has earned rave reviews from both critics and audiences to boot.

top gun: maverick is not only a worthy sequel to top gun, but in many ways it exceeds its predecessor while also revisiting everything that worked about it the first time.

as with the previous film, top gun: maverick is a showcase for some incredible aerial photography.

what really helps sell the illusion is that the actors actually were in the jets for interior shots during filming giving authentic reactions to traveling at those speeds while for exterior shots actual us navy pilots flew and to see some of the elaborate aerial sequences and know they're done without cgi is truly a sight to behold and really shows the enduring appeal of tom cruise as an action star because he dives (quite literally) into the action.

top gun set the standard for how to approach aerial photography and despite attempts by imitators such as fire birds, iron eagle, or (heaven help you) stealth, no one has surpassed that standard until now as maverick features some of the most intricate and engaging aerial dogfights and sequences ever captured on film with the editing and filming making you feel as though you're in the seat of the action.

of course, if top gun: maverick just delivered on the spectacle it would just be an above average actioner, but the movie does give some solid story and characterization that was lacking from the first film and allows cruise to deliver one of the best performances of his career.

with cruise's approach to maverick, it's very much a reflective piece as like maverick cruise is getting up in years and he's still the best at pulling these dare devil stunts (such as in his mission: impossible series) but eventually he will have to let go despite his best efforts to do otherwise.

with maverick and rooster there's something of an estranged father/son dynamic as maverick still carries the weight of goose's death very close and has tried to respect goose and his dead wife by protecting rooster even if that means rooster hating him, it's emotional scars like this that really held me with the movie, but easily the biggest was with val kilmer reprising his role as iceman who has been dealing with throat cancer (like the real life kilmer) and despite iceman's presence in this film being mostly via text, it's the buildup to the major scene where kilmer and cruise come together one final time in a scene that was heavy with emotional resonance especially if you know the off camera animosity between kilmer and cruise that came during top gun and there's something cathartic and emotionally cleansing about this scene that's already good in its own right but adds even more when taken into context for the real life undertones.

despite the strengths of top gun: maverick i do have some criticisms.

the fact that penny is an "old flame" of maverick's also struck me as a little odd as it seemed like maybe there was an initial draft where this character was kelly mcgillis' character charlie but now it's a wholly original character, but it doesn't feel like we have the attachment to this character that we should.

i will say at least the movie is built up to this climax as opposed to the original where the climax was tacked on, but the lack of a tangible antagonist does seem rather odd but given the importance of the international market i understand why they did this, and there have been instances like this all the way back to the 1950s such as with captain nemo's "hated nation" from the disney adaptation of 20,000 leagues under the sea.

top gun: maverick delivers on the thrills of the original film and exceeds in the story and characters and making for a more enjoyable sit.

while i did have issues with the film such as the lack of an antagonist character and the penny character feeling slightly extraneous, the film works well where you expect it to and delivers the action and entertainment that has become synonymous with cruise.

i don't think i agree with this being cruise's "best" movie as i personally think live die repeat and mission: impossible 1,4,5 & 6 are more entertaining on the whole, but this is still really solid blockbuster filmmaking.

what makes tom cruise the biggest name in action movies worldwide is the daredevil persona he has carefully maintained over the years, combined with his almost vampiric ability to delay the ageing process.

when "maverick" takes to the control of that fighter jet, you are sucked in again to the mesmeric, fast-paced world of "top gun", with the adrenaline-pumping and goosebumps-inducing narratives only strengthening in this brilliant sequel.

we rejoin captain pete "maverick" mitchell (cruise), a daredevil fighter pilot who still refuses to play by the rules and keeps turning down promotions that would see him grounded instead of being in the air where he belongs.

director joseph krasinski stays true to the vision and world building so painstakingly done by the original film's director, the legendary tony scott, by paying rich tribute to some of the most memorable motifs and elements used by his accomplished predecessor.

miles teller is expectedly terrific as the troublemaker from the class of students, while glen powell and monica barbaro ably play the other cadets that "maverick" has to beat into shape for a crucial real-world mission.

the fighter plane dogfights are painstakingly filmed, with the perfectionist in cruise insisting that each member of the cast portraying a pilot in the film mandatorily fly in one of the fighter jets built by boeing co.

so they could fully comprehend the physical and emotional duress undergone by a pilot operating under the strain of immense gravitational forces.

despite losing his voice to throat cancer, i loved the way the makers still managed to include val kilmer back in his iconic role of "iceman", maverick's bête noire.

jennifer connelly is enthralling and captivating in equal measure as maverick's love interest and i'm glad the director went an age-appropriate way in the romance than pairing up the 59-year-old cruise with a young actress.

the iconic bgm and the music of the original, composed by the legendary harold faltermeyer can never be matched and the makers smartly recreate the same with minimal changes, to doubly recapture the blend of soul-stirring music, bone-crushing action and exhilarating aerial combat sequences that made "top gun" such a cult classic action blockbuster.

the cinematography from claudio miranda captures every dip, swerve, dive and turn with panache and realism, so much so that you feel all the tension and anxiety of the protagonists on screen.
catch it on the biggest screen possible because maverick, he is back baby, in all his legendary glory!

thirty-six years after the original top gun took the world by storm, tom cruise is back as pete "maverick" mitchell in this high-octane sequel that delivers on all fronts.

with its stunning cinematography, exhilarating action sequences, and compelling character development, top gun: maverick is a must-see for fans of the original and newcomers alike.

the film picks up decades after maverick's heroic exploits in top gun, where he is now a seasoned test pilot, pushing the limits of what is possible.

when he is tasked with training a new generation of top gun graduates for a dangerous mission, maverick finds himself facing his own mortality and confronting the ghosts of his past.

tom cruise delivers a career-best performance as maverick, once again demonstrating his undeniable charisma and screen presence.

he captures the character's unwavering confidence, his underlying vulnerability, and his unwavering dedication to his craft.

the supporting cast is equally impressive, with miles teller as rooster, the son of maverick's former rio goose, glen powell as hangman, the cocky rival trainee, jennifer connelly as penny benjamin, maverick's former love interest, and jon hamm as cyclone, the tough-as-nails mission commander.

joseph kosinski, who also directed the 2013 film oblivion, delivers a visually stunning film with breathtaking aerial sequences that will leave you breathless.

the film's use of imax technology is particularly impressive, immersing the viewer in the action and making you feel like you're right there in the cockpit with maverick and his team.

top gun: maverick is a thrilling, action-packed sequel that honors the legacy of the original while also forging its own path.
however, maverick is clearly more conservative except for when he flies; ignoring orders, pushing known limits, and of course pushing back against authority.

we don't get much of the back story to their previous relationship, but it appears by the end that maverick may begin to no longer fly solo and may settle down after the events of this movie.

top gun: maverick (2022) directed by joseph kosinsky is a surpringly original sequel and takes a highly successful retro step to hollywood film making.

the story is set 30 years after its predecessor, and follows maverick's return to the united states navy strike fighter tactics instructor program (also known as "topgun").

the plot is very simple; here, he must confront his past as he trains a group of younger pilots, among them the son of maverick's deceased best friend lieutenant nick "goose" bradshaw, to eliminate a uranium target.

but the sheer finesse and bravour with which cruise, connelly, teller and kosinsky pull this off is impressive.

spectacular action, stunning cinematography, a great score paying homage to it's original predecessor topgun (1986), is all perfectly executed, and that justifies its cheesy style and simple plot.
as usual tom cruise is always at his best in what he is supposed to deliver as a lead actor in any movie offered to him.
val kilmer's short yet impactful role of admiral iceman, now a sufferer of throat cancer, shares emotional bonding with pete in a part.

role of young pilot trainees and graduates played by miles teller, glenn powell and monica barbaro are outstanding and performed exceptionally brilliant.

last but not the least, jennifer connelly deserves a strong applaud for her performance as pete's new love interest penelope and a single mother.

her presence alongside tom adds a slight comfort and helps in moving the story forward.

overall, this one is a highly recommendable sequel and more powerful than the original.

overall, this paid homage to the first film and expanded on its themes in a more mature manner.

pete mitchell aka maverick goes from an ambitious, self-absorbed, flirtatious (well, he's still all of that)...
he wants to make peace with goose's son rooster (who acts towards maverick with hostility) and he needs to forgive himself and move on.
it's an adequate arc for both characters (but mainly maverick) to ground the aerial sequences.
the bar scene, the iceman reunion, and pete's visit with penny all added emotional weight compared to the lackluster story of the original.

from a plot perspective, the story and pacing maverick isn't dramatically different from the original: starting with a semi-perilous aerial scene, transitioning into numerous training scenes with a romantic side plot, and concluding with a combat scene.
it's just the filmmaking for maverick was more successful in just about every way.
the ending was certainly feel-good (if not a bit cheesy) with maverick and goose coming home alive, reconciling with one another, and maverick going off with penny.
the message of letting go of the past is nothing new in cinema; but, it was the center of a strong story aimed at completing pete mitchell's character arc from the first film in a satisfying manner.
complex characters, a cohesive story, and some of the most immersive and suspenseful action scenes in recent times prove that maverick soars above the original.

top gun: maverick (2022) -

they might have been able to sell this as a separate film, but i think that the existence of its predecessor'top gun' (1986) was probably necessary to make this one truly work and to give it some awesome marketing power.

with that said, this was certainly the better of the two films in the franchise.

yes, it was more of the same and pretty darn predictable, but i enjoyed it a lot more.

i really hadn't expected to like it, because having rewatched the first film recently i found that i couldn't understand why i had ever liked that one at all.

what i could appreciate about this film was the maturity of the story in comparison and tom cruise's improved performance as the titular character.

it really helped that maverick was more grown up too.

i always seem to point it out in my reviews of his films, but the new calmer, 21st century version of tom has far more going for him than any of his younger 1980's castings.

in this film he returned to one of those previous shouty man roles, but with a more easy disposition and he had definitely improved with age, especially physically in my opinion, woof-woof, hubba-hubba.

the charm of maverick was easier to see and so it made sense that jennifer connelly, who was just enough in the part of penny would realise that he wasn't the same as he had been before.

i liked the fact that they didn't fixate on this romance, but instead used it as a way for him to have at least someone on his side, as no one was particularly keen to learn flying and tactics from such a "maverick".

the admiral beau "cyclone" simpson, played by jon hamm, definitely needed persuading of the benefits of tom's rogue pilot ways, but he wasn't such an over the top hard ass that he was unbelievable or stereotypical and he was a very sexy beast too.

playing the part of mav's old wingman goose's (anthony edwards) son "rooster" was miles teller.

i certainly felt the tension of what they were going through, possibly because i was more interested in the characters this time, due to better acting performances, or because the directors and writers had done their job well in the first place, probably both.

i was genuinely emotional by the end of the film, but i was having withdrawals from years of taking anti-depressants at the time, which could have been a factor of that too.

i had expected more of the same and that was essentially what i got, but this one certainly had more polish to it, mostly because of tom's more mature performance and i would imagine that he had a lot more say in how things were done this time around too.

it was actually a very appropriate sequel and one that worked better for the distance inbetween, a more grown up storyline, structure and better acting.

maverick still carried guilt from so far in the past, and had to get past that, because goose's son is now at top gun for the "very special mission"

then something even stranger happened...top gun maverick got real exciting for the remaining 3 hours (yes it feels that long)...

yes the movie is total fantasy from start to finish, but the damn thing is totally entertaining, which is my number one rule for reviews...stick it out folks...it may be fantasy on steroids, but by the end of the movie you just don't care...

well done...very well done...and don't forget to notice those flying sequences, they are outstanding...aaand i just love the tribute to the first movie by having them find an old f14 tomcat in flyable condition, sorta...
it is easy to be enthusiastic, nay, rapturous about top gun: maverick.
the celebratory energy of top gun: maverick will enrapture plenty.

but even accounting for tom cruise, jerry bruckheimer, and director joseph kosinski's shrewd spell-the influx of timing and properly placed ambition, giving a starved audience the kind of entertainment they needed-top gun: maverick is still a super-charged rush of fresh air; a summer blockbuster both jaw-droppingly thrilling and emotionally fulfilling.

maverick doesn't rewrite the "legacy sequel" rules.
36 years after top gun, tom cruise's pete "maverick" mitchell has graduated from hotshot young stud to seasoned legend.
in fact, maverick is very much the same story as top gun.

at the end of the day, "top gun maverick" succeeds and soars as a nostalgic, deeply emotional surprise triumphant action flick, with flight battle scenes so intense it'll make you sweat in your seat, while it also crashes into some of the mountainous cliches that have been built and established by hollywood throughout the years.
even the instructor's arrival is the same: maverick stands before the students exactly as charlie (kelly mcgillis) did almost four decades earlier.

if before the rivalry was between maverick and iceman (val kilmer, responsible for one of the most exciting passages in the new film), those who now take on these positions are rooster (miles teller, revealing an interesting dramatic potential) and hangman (glen powell, showing with charisma goes beyond an attractive print).

and this is where "maverick" begins to differentiate itself from the original.

instead of subverting what was already known from "top gun" or revisiting this universe with a critical eye, the sequel is more interested in reliving a moment that was so significant for action cinema.

more than 30 years later, maverick continues to have problems with authority in both his professional and personal life, a theme marked by constant reminders that he remains stuck in the rank of captain, even though he has every opportunity to evolve and reach the highest positions in the northern navy.

of course, pete could have evolved and grown - professionally and mentally - like everyone in his class did, but then who would be left to roll up their sleeves and teach the new generation the ropes?

however, the production does not try to justify this tackiness, which is also part of the identity carved out in the 1986 film.

this conversation between the script and the context in which "top gun: maverick" is set is the film's greatest asset.

in a time of soulless reboots and modern re-interpretations of beloved ips, top gun maverick appears to be the usual suspect and prime offender: an 80s cult movie, filled with antiquated ideas of masculinity and absurdly fetishized militarism worthy of james cameron's wet dream.

what a temptation it must have been for the studio and the creatives to board the en-vogue subversion-train and give top gun a 'modern' makeover that online trolls could go to metaphorical war over.

yet, top gun maverick withstands those temptations and instead chooses to honor and respect its cinematic predecessor and give us a true to formula action film, with a refined structure, believable character development and state of the art flight sequences.

all while remaining free of excessive misfires of comedy or the urge to make us feel ashamed about liking 'that sort of entertainment'.

tom cruise fully embraces his aged hero figure while gracefully passing the baton to the younger generation, replacing the unintentional-seeming homo-eroticism of the original film with genuine themes of brotherhood, friendship and forgiveness.

with top gun maverick and following the reinvention of tron in 2010, director joseph kosinski certainly has established himself as the man to honor and preserve an ip while giving it a fresh new layer of paint.
all these things combined make top gun maverick is a standout in 2022's action film offering.

tom cruise's 46th film is an action packed, promising delivered hollywood blockbuster awaiting to be seen from an audience on the big silver screen.

achieving what top gun: maverick finalized is an extraordinary feeling.
the story carries itself with a calm opening staring tom cruise, and a trip down memory lane through portraits on a wall of goose and his family from the first "top gun" film.
we are immediately introduced to the score as well as the personality of maverick himself.

after many years, maverick still seems to be dedicated to flying, and going against commands just like his younger confident/reckless self.

a new series of younger cast members is sweet, and faultlessly introduced.

we meet a good chunk of prior top gun academy graduates at penny's bar, exploring only a few piolets that have the chance to fly in a mission more complicated than any other mission maverick has flown.

monica barbaro playing lt.

the films story is noticeably dull after act i, and easily identifiable during act ii.

director joseph kosinski does a decent job trying to keep the audience hooked, as well as claudio miranda with the shots, but the top gun franchise already having a specific theme and mood set, its harder to identify specific director elements since its a franchise film.

the shots in top gun: maverick are beautifully crafted.

the lighting and jet shots are equally as interesting to watch.

for a film in 2022, top gun: maverick is easily one of the better pieces of film shot using a digital camera (sony venice) still delivering a natural movie look.

although the film started out interesting, and became dull, but later retained the audience based on the more interesting side of the plot, and the exciting score, top gun: maverick was not entirely a bad film, but extremally pleasing for a sequel that has nearly took 4 decades to produce.

however, the sequel, in my opinion, "top gun: maverick" is better than the original film.

the writing: it's very well written.

tom cruise is at his best, but all the actors are great.

the direction: really really amazing.

every scene is filmed as well as possible, especially the flight sequences.

in conclusion, "top gun: maverick" is a very good sequel to "top gun".

and by being true to its identity, top gun maverick is a exciting and very entertaining movie while bringing up heavy nostalgia for the older crowd.

instead of the "big picture" conflict between the us and an interesting adversary, the conflicts were focused on the military men themselves.

cruise as pete "maverick" mitchell reprises his role as a us navy captain test pilot from the original 1986 top gun film.

pete's flaw is that he always has trouble with authority and likes to do things his own way.

this is why he's remained at the rank of captain throughout his long career.

pete invariably butts head with two of his commanders at the beginning and midpoint of the story.

pete keeps the program going by flying the program's supersonic jet at the high speed of "mach 10" but crashes after pushing over the craft's speed limit.

pete's career is saved by his mentor, the commander of the pacific fleet, admiral tom "iceman" kazansky who suffers from throat cancer (played by real-life cancer victim val kilmer).

iceman transfers pete to the top gun school at nas north island in san diego where he's tasked with selecting the best pilots for the mission to take out the uranium enrichment plant.

it's déjà vu all over again when another by-the-book commander, vice admiral beau "cyclone" simpson (joe hamm) --echoing "hammer"-relieves pete of his duties after another one of the planes goes down during training exercises.

and like before, pete demonstrates that the mission can be accomplished by proving he has the skills to get the job done.

cyclone reluctantly agrees to let pete pilot one of the jets during the mission which was not the original plan to keep him as an instructor.

in addition to these cliched conflicts, pete also is paired off against lieutenant bradley "rooster" bradshaw (miles teller).
rooster hates pete as he holds him responsible for his father's death, pete's former supervisor and good friend goose.

it doesn't matter to rooster that pete was exonerated for the death of his father as it was deemed a combat death.

what's more pete, at the behest of rooster's mom, turned down his naval academy application, delaying his career for four years.

pete also believed rooster wasn't ready for training.

you can predict what happens between pete and rooster-during the mission taking out the uranium enrichment plant, rooster saves pete after he's forced to eject from his plane.

no matter what one thinks of his politics, social life, or general tom cruiseacity, the man's career is undeniably one of the most successful in the history of hollywood.

cruise has helmed some of the profitable films in existence, starting his career with top gun and journeying through the mission: impossible franchise.

his career comes full circle with top gun: maverick, a follow up to the original film which provides exactly what one would expect from a sequel to top gun: some fairly mundane melodrama, a new cast of useful idiots, and a stellar gallery aerial combat, sans cgi or digital wizardry.

cruise and director joseph kosinski set out to make a blockbuster reminiscent of yesteryear, and their passion is evident with every flight.

the film follows maverick as he's called back into top gun to train a new class of recruits for a top-secret and extremely dangerous mission.
cruise performed his own stunts, and the realism is left on the screen, as is the budget.

top gun: maverick stands out as a sequel that skillfully blends nostalgia with a modern cinematic touch.
it's a celebration of the past, aimed at fans who have aged alongside the movie's hero, portrayed once again by tom cruise.

however, for those who didn't experience the first film, "maverick" might feel like a relic of a bygone era, echoing a time when such stories were in their prime.

the charm of "top gun: maverick" lies in its ability to transport viewers back to the days of the original film, yet it also struggles to fully engage those seeking a contemporary action experience.

the movie walks a fine line between honoring its roots and adapting to modern filmmaking standards.

in essence, "top gun: maverick" is a journey through time, revisiting iconic characters in a world that has evolved yet remains anchored in its origins.

i think very few people - if any - would remember tg: maverick in years to come.

usually, dogfights make the movie stay in audiences' memory long after it disappears from the box office (e.g blue thunder); unfortunately, maverick doesn't give us classic battle scenes.

the 80s top gun made an impact because it was a cultural statement, especially during the cold war / east vs west thing.

it was the era of rocky vs drago, rambo vs the commies.

tg also announced the arrival of the cocky screen persona of a young tom cruise as a global hollywood brand, who went on to solidify that persona and his box office cred in subsequent movies.
then, there was also the evolution of cruise as an actor who sought to move away from a teeny-bop poster boy, with movies like born on the fourth of july, few good men.

with the mission impossible franchise, he went on to achieve the near impossible - intelligent action movies that consistently satisfy both critics & audiences.

maverick doesn't belong in that league.

throw in the 80s soundtrack - and i'm guessing this was to attract nostalgic audiences who grew alongside cruise's movies.

as its predecessor, maverick doesn't try to punch above its weight as pop corn fare.
the only exciting scene was the opener, where maverick pilots a b-2 bomber-like experimental plane to exceed mach 10.

but the f-18s didn't have that same punch in your gut sensation, so the finale turns out to be a lame bomb-the-enemy exercise.

couple that with cliched plot material & movie dialogue, or characters that occupy space to fill up time in between action scenes, and maverick missed an opportunity to reinvent the dogfight movie.
guess the production team wanted big names to give credence to maverick.

most of the actors' emotional projection - including cruise's - seem laboured and unconvincing.

only miles teller manages to inject some emotional depth into his rooster; the loss of his father and the tension it creates with maverick, is well projected by teller, despite the fact that this too, belongs to the cliched school of movie plots.
leave maverick for rainy days streaming.

pete "maverick" mitchell is a hot shot super jet pilot in waiting.

selected for training at the top gun school in san diego, mitchell must harness his ability and realise his dreams, or else face the consequence.

top gun is a golden film, why you ask?

yes the film has no substance, but director tony scott and scallywag producers don simpson and jerry bruckheimer merged a number of crowd pleasing elements to create a box office smash, and in the process launch one time poster boy tom cruise into the stratosphere of super stardom.

we have a military setting, daring do training programme, buff bodies for those of any sexual persuasion, competitive edginess, and of course the obligatory love interest romance that here is as unlikely as it is actually forced.
tho to be fair to both cruise {great and cocky} and kelly mcgillis {miscast and poor}, their love scenes are tender and comfortably raising the pulse beat in 80s cinema sensuality.
much macho posturing drips from every other frame, be it cruise tearing around on his motorcycle or val kilmer {iceman} pumping out his bare chest and smirking away.

the jet maneuvers shown are both impressive & exciting and might tend to increase the viewer's respect (as it certainly did mine) for the amazing skill and incredible nerve of real life fighter pilots.

the story revolves around a bold, daring, and overconfident navy fighter pilot, lieutenant pete mitchell (call name 'maverick'), who is sent to the top gun naval flying school along with his close pal, goose.

maverick strives to prove himself the best pilot in this demanding course, but faces both stiff competition from a fellow pilot named iceman as well as personal conflict dealing with his own haunting demons following the mysterious death of his father, also an air ace pilot.

meanwhile, he falls for a lovely civilian astrophysics instructor, charlotte (charlie) blackwood.

tom cruise is well cast in the role of the hotshot pilot...the cocky, audacious, fearless, but ultimately conflicted and anguished maverick.
other stars include tom skerrit as a real top gun flight instructor, commander metcalf (viper), who proves to be both a skilled and professional pilot but also a compassionate individual.
maverick's personal story, his inner strife, and his romance with charlie prove less riveting than the incredible airborne stunts with these jets.

the film also does a great job at depicting all the male bonding between these pilots...the camaraderie, rivalry, banter, inter dependency, and genuine close friendship.

tom cruise stars as a united states naval aviator lieutenant by the name of pete "maverick" mitchell, a young, hot-shot aviator who loves flying and goofing off when he really should be working.

his partner-and-crime and longtime friend, whom he considers family, is nick "goose" bradshaw (anthony edwards), who has a wife and kid back home, but accepts maverick mainly because of the fact that he doesn't have much else besides him.

maverick's father was killed in vietnam, which only leaves maverick in denial that his dad's death was because of circumstance, rather than the actuality of the situation being a personal mistake.

after one goof-off session too many, maverick and goose are sent to fighter weapons school (nicknamed "top gun") by their superior officer, who admires their talents but simply can't control them and recognizes they deserve to be placed in the elite squad of pilots.
upon arriving to top gun, maverick meets a wonderful woman by the name of charlotte blackwood (kelly mcgillis), who he learns is his instructor during his time at the school.

he also clashes with rival student lieutenant tom "iceman" kazanski (val kilmer), whom, while he detests on his competitive level, thoroughly admires him for his skill and devotion to flying.

one of top gun's underlying strengths is how it doesn't settle for being another indistinguishable piece of action filmmaking nor a fluffy romantic piece with some disjointed shots of aerial combat thrown in as an excuse for screen writing diversity.

the film's story often feels too cluttered, as i said, struggling to fit so much into its one-hundred and nine minute runtime, and then on top of that, you have average acting by cruise and mcgillis, some strong work by edwards, and some seriously mediocre and over-the-top acting by kilmer, who throws scenes off instantly when he walks on screen.

as difficult as it is to define and place, top gun can't be written off with a few words, and instead, must be given some solid care and attention as if it were an award-worthy movie rather than just a piece of summer fluff.

while cruise is flamboyant and unpredictable, his partner goose is down-to-earth and pragmatic, which makes for a good team.

when they come to the flight school, they meet their competition, lt tom "iceman" kazanski (val kilmer), who is just as haughty and cocky as maverick.
the only difference: iceman plays it safe while maverick takes risks, which makes him the more dangerous of the two.

the casting is excellent.
cruise makes the perfect rock star pilot, unfazed by the criticism of his commanding officers.
kilmer is memorable as the unlikable rival, probably the only actor of the time who could keep up with cruise's perceived cockiness and haughtiness.
tom skerrit has a supporting role as cdr mike "viper" metcalf, the former polite-turned-educator in charge of the school.
the contrived love story between mcgillis and cruise involves a lot of scenes with the two of them either on his motorcycle or in her bed with the song "take my breath away" in the background.

in "an officer and a gentleman", we learn about what the tough sergeant is up to, and why he feels compelled to use unfair methods to get the best out of the trainees, but the leadership is much more in the background for much of "top gun".

not until tragedy strikes does the film become slightly deeper, and the mystery of maverick's father comes to light.

tony scott's "top gun" was obviously built on the template of 1982's "an officer and a gentleman" and was a mega-hit in may/june of 1986.

the plot: two hotshot navy pilots, maverick (tom cruise) and goose (anthony edwards), are sent to a prestigious flight school in san diego where they must endure the rivalry of other pilots, like iceman (val kilmer).

maverick seeks a relationship with one of the school's civilian instructors (kelly mcgillis) and also faces a crisis when his cocky confidence is shaken.

"top gun" is basically a modern "the blue max" in that it mixes the drama on the ground with the excitement in the air.
for example, the rivalry of the pilots, the mystery of maverick's father, the grievous death of one of the main characters, and maverick's crisis of confidence.
a good example of the film's depth can be seen in the scene where iceman confronts maverick in the locker room after a tragedy.
iceman is sincere but walks on eggshells because he respects maverick's unpredictable and dangerous nature.

the scene rings true-to-life.

tom skerritt is notable as one of the older instructors of the school, viper.

there's a good scene in the 2nd half where maverick visits viper's house on a sunday, which features a great (funny) line from skerritt ("i'm not going to blow sunshine").

unfortunately, the film has been accused of being somehow "homo-erotic." nonsense.
in case these clueless critics didn't notice, maverick is chasing mcgillis' character throughout the film and even "breaks into" a ladies room to see her.
besides, notice that maverick leaves the game prematurely to go see his babe.

the film runs 110 minutes, by the way.

united states naval aviator lt pete "maverick" mitchell (tom cruise) and his radar intercept officer (rio) ltjg nick "goose" bradshaw (anthony edwards) stationed aboard the uss enterprise are sent to attend topgun, the naval fighter weapons school at naval air station miramar.

once there maverick strikes up a romance with civilian contractor and topgun flight instructor charlotte "charlie" blackwood (kelly mcgillis) and a rivalry with lt tom "iceman" kazansky (val kilmer).

top gun was inspired by the article "top guns" by ehud yonay, from the may 1983 issue of california magazine which detailed the lives of fighter pilots at naval air station miramar in san diego, self-nicknamed as "fightertown usa".
tony scott had directed the commercial for saab wherein a saab car races a saab jet leading the producers to hire him, with tom cruise eventually cast for the lead of pete "maverick" mitchell.

when top gun was released, it became a breakout success staying in theaters for six months and going on to become the highest grossing film of 1986 and spring boarding the careers of tom cruise, director tony scott, and even meg ryan in a smaller supporting performance.

while risky business was tom cruise's first time headlining a leading role, it's here in top gun where he cultivates the daredevil rogue persona that would define many of his future acting roles.

maverick is brash, abrasive, and arrogant, but unlike many imitators that tried and failed to do this character type (such as charlie sheen's hawkins in navy seals) the movie builds a character and story around it rather than just plopping it in front of us.

with top gun it is a showcase for impressive aerial stunts and photography, but we also learn what drives maverick as a character and build his relationships with other people such as anthony edwards' goose, kelly mcgillis' charlie, or rivalries with others such as val kilmer's iceman.

many movies that tried to ape this character archetype only took the surface level of maverick (with the brash arrogance) and didn't add any substance to it which left many of the imitators insufferable at best.

here cruise is not only a solid actor, but he's given some good meat to chew on character wise.

top gun was the "king of cool" in the 1980s thanks to the self-satisfied performance of tom cruise as hotshot "jock" pilot peter "maverick" mitchell.

the film revels in mitchell's arrogant disregard for rules (he is a walking section eight), from his absurd guidance of a terrified comrade onto the deck of the uss enterprise (this despite the fact maverick's f-14 lacks the fuel to land itself) through the remarkably weak punishments he gets for breaking such rules as hitting on his dod instructor (kelly mcguiness) to getting his radar intercept officer "goose" bradshaw (er's anthony edwards) killed in a thoroughly stupid contest with tim "iceman" kazansky (val kilmer) over who will be first to "kill" the enemy plane late in the navy's top gun dogfighting exercises; the film wimps out badly when, in this incident, maverick's flying through iceman's jetwash (thus killing his own engines and leading to the ejection punch-out where goose slams into the cockpit canopy and severs his windpipe) is more accidental than anything; the scene should have been clearly 100% the fault of maverick, since he practically sticks his f-14's nose into iceman's thrusters.

but if it were thus portrayed accurately, then the film comes to an end, with maverick grounded or even dishonorably discharged, thus underlining the weakness of playing up maverick as incapable of discipline.

throughout the film maverick acts in thoroughly unprofessional manner (any pilot who performed a close-in flyby on a tower would be court-martialed) and never is called on it except in the most perfunctory and insincere fashion, not even when goose bradshaw pleads with him early on that he, goose, can't afford to blow the opportunity presented to him.

cruise and mcguiness are not worth investing the time needed to watch the film; the real stars are the supporting cast - tom skerritt, michael ironside, anthony edwards, val kilmer, and rick rossovich - and the superb aerial dogfight footage; the use of f-5s as soviet migs is a bit distracting, since the f-5s don't look at all like soviet warplanes.
after all, the film launched tom cruise's hollywood career.

in terms of action, scott definitely delivered.

"top gun" is a 1986 action drama directed by tony scott starring tom cruise and kelly macgillis.
over the years and against my own expectations, tom cruise has by now become one of my favourite actors of all time.
while jake gyllenhaal still wears the crown and will forever defend the top spot, cruise is very close behind him and comes second place.

the focus of course lies on the glamour boy peter "maverick" mitchell, charmingly portrayed by the twenty-four-year-old cruise, and how he wants to be the very best (like no one ever was) in the naval aviator business.

as the son of the myth-enshrouded pilot duke mitchell who mysteriously vanished on his last mission, he tries to follow in his own father's footsteps and always wants to be the best to both make his father proud and make up for the lack of acknowledgement of a father figure that has never been there for him.

this tragic effect increases even more after the devastating death of his co-pilot and best friend goose, the man he claims to be his own family he has left, and even though his passing seems to not bother him that much on the outside, you can see it in mav's eyes and by cruise's acting that he is extremely tortured by the fact that he has no one left in his life, except for maybe one.

as if the dogfights in the beginning that are part of the training are not already utterly exciting enough, the film steps up its game in the final act when the newly graduated students have to go into their first serious combat, and this is also the moment when the inner conflict of maverick concludes.

still reminded of his own mortality and vulnerability after the tragic incident, he is still traumatized and not confident enough, but as soon as his mates need him he brings himself to overcome what haunts him the most and do what is necessary: fly like a maverick.

it works as both, a pop corn flick to shut your brains off to and a subliminal character drama, and thanks to likeable characters, a talented cast and a decent leading performance by cruise, it becomes something that conjures a smile on my face.
even if i am a professed admirer of tom cruise and it might appear a little overrated to some, this film is without a doubt one you must have seen at least once in your lifetime.

well known as the picture that turned tom cruise into an international icon and coming with one of the great memorable soundtracks, "top gun" is an enjoyable first-rate eighties movie.

maverick (cruise) and his best friend goose (anthony edwards) are two cocky, talented pilots working in the us navy.

both movies are set inside a flight school, both have a troubled central character (in that movie it was richard gere, here it's tom cruise) who must confront their past and negotiate a romance in the course of the movie.
the main strength in the cast is cruise, who holds the movie up with likable charm and strong inner intensity.
she performs the role well, but she cannot really compete with cruise.

tom skerrit, micheal ironside and james tolkan are fine as the flight school commanders and val kilmer is enjoyable arrogant as maverick's rival iceman.

the brilliantly shot dogfight sequences give a stirring and disorienting realistic feel of real-life airborne combat, and these combined with the searingly memorable title track "take my breath away" are the picture's technical highlights.

think about it: "iceman", "maverick", "take my breath away" or just the first synthetic notes, there's also that death i won't spoil but that still upsets many fans because the character was so damn likable...
the uniforms, the special effect, the motorcycle rides, hell, the face of a young baby-faced cruise...

and yes it was commercial but who cares when the story is the placed product (except maybe for "the emoji movie").

indeed, it's not about tom cruise alone, not about the cool-sounding call-names not even about the aerial effects which are impressive (and still hold up today) but it's the combination of these factors, the story it tells, the way for one hundred minutes, the film makes you want to be part of a team, where everyone's young, competent and take the job seriously.

now i must say i saw "top gun" once when i was 10 but i had "hot shots" recorded, so rediscovering it was like finally getting ahold on the source and yes everything in this film is begging for being replicated: the rivalry between cruise and val kilmer, the tension that is certainly more palpable than the chemistry with kelly mcgillis, the past secret, the nervous sweating and cigar-chumping commander played by james tokian who was born to play angry authority figures and maybe the homoerotic subtext of the volley ball that has been quite exaggerated to tell the truth.

but what the film gets right is the spectacular action sequences, i just watched 1949 "twelve o'clock high" and i was frustrated by how desperately lacking in battles it was, that's not to say that the fight are always easy to follow but we know what is a radar interceptor, a wingman and we know way too well what the troubles caused from an canopy malfunction...

maverick is the cocky rebel who's got something to prove, iceman the rival who never loses his cool and hides behind an enigmatic smile the fear that this wise-guy might steal his thunder, he's not actually an antagonist but perhaps the competitive guy who acknowledges his worth, in others situations, they would be best friends but that spot is occupied by anthony edwards ,with more facial hair (and less hair period) than in "e.

r.", steals the show as goose, tom skerrit is the respected and caring superior and meg ryan was a brief little sunshine.

i agree that the romance isn't exactly the film's strongest suit and seems like designed as an afterthought in order to plug the "take my breath away" song, (good call, it won the oscar) as it's true that if she was just a friend and a coach it wouldn't have made the film any less good and wouldn't have provided arguments for dismissing it.

the action is great, as is the pacing and music; even with "take my breath away" being slightly overused at one point.

tom cruise is excellent in the lead role, no doubt the perfect choice to play maverick.
kelly mcgillis, val kilmer, anthony edwards, tom skerritt, michael ironside...

they all commit to their roles and give noteworthy performances.

'top gun: maverick' is literally right around the corner.

tom cruise has never bettered this performance in my eyes, val kilmer has never achieved quite this level of cool and kelly mcgillis is as fantastic as always.

top gun stars tom cruise (jerry maguire) who plays pete mitchell, a young naval aviator who with his reel goose, played with great humor by anthony edwards (er) are selected by their higher up at the beginning of the movie to attend the prestigious top gun fighter school in southern california to become even better fighter pilots.

it is at top gun where maverick and goose, cruise and edward's call signs respectively, go up against outstanding fliers ice, played by val kilmer (batman forever), cougar, performed by john stockwall, and ice's reel slider played by rick rossovich (navy seals).

besides going out for daily ops against each other and training in f-16 fighter jets maverick - by pure luck - hits on & falls in love with one of his instructors played wonderfully by kelly mcgillis (witness).
maverick is also supported by two of his superiors at top gun who have seen live action themselves in viper and jester played by tom skerritt and michael ironside respectively.
along with the conflict between maverick and iceman and how in the end they made up.
then in the other movies iceman helps out maverick a lot during his time as an admiral .
although it was sad when goose died since he was such a good best friend to maverick and just such a good character over all.

(though i would admit the dialogues are slightly over the top in some places, but then again, you don't have those memorable quotes for nothing.)

pete "maverick" mitchell(tom cruise) is one of the best fighter pilots in the navy, and aspires to be the top gun.
what i absolutely loved about maverick is his attitude.

and nonetheless, the unforgettable chemistry between charlie(kelly mcgilles) and maverick.

it has some astounding fighter pilot combat stunts with some stunning visuals.
maverick is such a likable protagonist and a perfect mix of cocky and charming.

the audience and the flight instructors in charge of the top gun program are on the same journey- evaluating whether he's willing to attempt skills outside of the rules because he's brave and cunning or because he's overeager and reckless.

side plots surrounding maverick's fight to be the top of the class further ground him as more than just an ambitious pilot and fit into the film quite seamlessly without coming off as just down-time in between flying sequences.

being made in 1986, there's a specific look to the camera quality and elements of the audio quality that just have a nostalgic feeling and the classic 80's songs in the soundtrack are instantly recognizable- both as tied to the movie and tied to the time period which i love.

without the subtle color contrast and purposeful light design, it would be hard to see the character tension behind all of the action scenes and top gun goes about the even saturation very well.

more than anyone else in the cast, i would say tom cruise was absolutely the perfect choice for the film; of course, i recognize it's very easy to say that now because it has had such a long lasting impact on pop culture almost forty years later and he returned for a second installment.

the movie follows the story of pete "maverick" mitchell, a hotshot fighter pilot who is sent to the elite top gun naval flying school.

along with his wingman, nick "goose" bradshaw, maverick goes head-to-head with other pilots in intense dogfights, all while trying to prove himself as the best of the best.

the film boasts incredible aerial sequences, showcasing the power and speed of fighter jets.
the chemistry between tom cruise as maverick and anthony edwards as goose is palpable, and their friendship adds a layer of heart to the film.

kelly mcgillis also delivers a strong performance as maverick's love interest, charlie.

top gun is not only a thrilling action movie, but it also captures the camaraderie and competition that comes with being part of an elite team.

radical air pilot maverick (cruise) and his friend goose (edwards) are sent to top gun, the toughest challenge for the pair who compete to be the best.

tony scott's pulsating actioner is remembered today for those terrific jet sequences, the swift introduction of the then fastest motorbike in the world, and perhaps significant in today's modern culture, tom cruise's macho bravado smile.

over 20 years have passed and the lead star and director have certainly moved up in the world.
cruise receiving three oscar nominations and scott winning a primetime emmy.

top gun opens with cruise's maverick disregarding a direct order to help out a fellow pilot, getting told off before getting his just desserts, a reward to go to the most famous academy, top gun, and herein lies the action, the drama and even some exquisitely handled comedy.

above all, this scott picture is an out and out action drama that spices up the situations with that cheeky comedy only somebody called tom cruise can bring.
maverick is the catalyst of sharp intake and a bravado icon that would make any guy instantly jealous of his quick thinking and constant confidence.
yes, it is targeted towards the type of guy who enjoys a tom clancy novel.

the training and pushing to be the best inevitably lands goose and maverick in trouble and some friction generates from the ice man, giving the film a spicy drama, along with one of the most sad twists for friendship to ever hit our screens.

"top gun" is just one of those must-see 1980s films, very quotable, with a classic cast of tom cruise, anthony edwards, meg ryan and val kilmer, among others.
it ranks, at least for me, as one of tom cruise's top three most enjoyable films and is definitely at the peak of his career.

the story of the movie revolves around a pilot in the us navy, lieutenant "maverick" mitchell (tom cruise) and the challenges that come with being a part of the world's most powerful military.
enemy mig 28 jets (not a real aircraft) have been spotted close to the carrier, and maverick is sent to stop them.
one of his wingmen, cougar, is too stricken with ptsd to land his plane, causing maverick to disobey orders and fly after him.
maverick's superior officer then sends him to the navy weapons school in california, named top gun.
once the class begins, maverick manages to beat one of his instructors in a mock dogfight, but uses dishonest tactics to do so.
meanwhile, another pilot called iceman does not view maverick in a positive light, and considers him foolish and reckless due to his tendency to ignore orders and fight aggressively.
later on, maverick is shown not to be as tough as he appears to be, since viper manages to bait him into a move that puts an enemy pilot on his tail.
during a similar mission that pits maverick against iceman, maverick's f-14 flies through the jet wash of iceman's plane, causing both his engines to stall.
maverick's plane goes into an unrecoverable spin, and his radar intercept officer goose is killed after the ejection seat smashes his head against the plane's windscreen.
maverick initially has the death of his friend pinned on him, but is later said to be not guilty.
at the end of the film, maverick and his fellow pilots are called upon once again to shoot down more migs that are threatening a ship.
after being in the heat of battle with both their lives at stake, maverick and iceman gain respect for each other, and maverick returns to top gun to teach new pilots.
maverick does get a love interest later in the movie, but there really isn't any point.

there's also the scene that involves maverick's plane having its engines die because of a disruption in airflow, when this was remedied by grumman in the new f-14 models by replacing the pratt and whitney turbofans with ones made by general electric.

if you haven't already seen "top gun" then you are missing out on one of the most memorable movies from the mid-eighties.

basically, in the indian ocean aboard the uss enterprise, us naval aviator lieutenant pete "maverick" mitchell (tom cruise) and his rio (radar intercept officer) ltjg (lieutenant junior grade) nick "goose" bradshaw (anthony edwards) are stationed and fly the f-14a tomcat.

during an interception with two hostile mig-28s (portrayed by usn f-5s), maverick goes against orders to rescue his former wingman lieutenant bill "cougar" cortell (john stockwell) from a missile-lock from a hostile and to help him back to the carrier.
maverick and goose are sent in cougar's place by commander tom "stinger" jardian (james tolkan) to attend naval fighter weapons school, better known as topgun, at naval air station miramar.

the day before topgun starts, maverick and goose go to a bar and meets with other naval officers, including lieutenant tom "iceman" kazansky (val kilmer) and his rio ltjg ron "slider" kerner (rick rossovich).
the following day, maverick is surprised to see the woman, charlotte "charlie" blackwood (kelly mcgillis), who is an astrophysicist and civilian instructor at topgun.
she later becomes interested in maverick learning about his skills in the air.
at the first training hop, breaking a major rule and through reckless flying, maverick defeats instructor lcdr rick "jester" heatherly (michael ironside).
maverick and goose are reprimanded by chief instructor cdr mike "viper" metcalf (tom skerritt).
privately, jester tells viper he admires maverick's skill but is unsure if he could trust him as a teammate in combat.

iceman is a top student and becomes maverick's rival, he believes maverick's attitude "foolish" and his flying "dangerous" since he often abandons his team to pursue reckless objectives, making him "unsafe" to fly with.
on training hop 19, maverick abandons his wingman lieutenant rick "hollywood" neven (whip hubley) to chase viper.
maverick's flying abilities impress viper, but he still defeated when manoeuvred by him.
viper's wingman jester shoots maverick from behind, and the value of teamwork over an individual is confirmed.

jester publicly tells maverick his flying is excellent, but he should "never leave his wingman." maverick and iceman are competing for the topgun trophy, with the scoring based on the time taken for every dogfight to conclude.
in hop 31, the task is to chase an a-4, during which iceman score higher than maverick, but he pressures ice to break off his engagement to shoot the a-4 down himself.
maverick and goose are forced to eject, but goose's aircraft canopy malfunctions, his ejector seat jettisons, and goose goes head-first into the roof and is killed.
maverick is cleared of the responsibility for goose's death by the board of inquiry, but he is shaken and overcome by guilt.
charlie and others try to console maverick, but he considers quitting.
he seeks advice from viper, who served with maverick's father, duke mitchell, on the uss oriskany where he was killed in battle during the vietnam war.
official reports faulted mitchell, but contrary to this, viper says his father died heroically.
viper assures maverick he can succeed if he regains his self-confidence.
maverick chooses to graduate, and iceman wins the topgun trophy.

then a "crisis situation" comes up, and iceman, hollywood, and maverick are sent to the enterprise to provide air support to rescue the disabled communication ship ss layton which has drifted into hostile waters.
maverick and cougar's former rio ltjg sam "merlin" wells (tim robbins) are backup for f-14s flown by iceman and hollywood, with iceman concerned about maverick's mental state.
maverick is nearly forced to retreat after a catapult failure, encountering similar circumstances to those that caused goose's death.
maverick manages to rejoin iceman, but refuses to leave him without a wingman, shooting down three migs.
maverick and iceman triumphantly return to enterprise, and they share a newfound respect for each other.
maverick throws goose's dog tags overboard, having come to terms with himself and his friend's death.
maverick is offered assignments, but chooses to return to topgun as an instructor, and later reunites with charlie at a bar in miramar.

it centres around maverick (played by tom cruise), a bravura naval aviator who plays by his own rules and almost always finds a way to win.
maverick's unique skill-set sees him enter top gun, a training programme for elite naval pilots.

alongside telling the story of maverick's constant ability to overcome the odds, top gun is notable for its copious, often groundbreaking, flying scenes and its provision of a plethora of semi-naked, glistening male bodies.
there is also a slight element of depth to the film when an event of genuine tragedy occurs which finally makes maverick doubt his preternatural abilities.

on that note, it's worth looking at the background to this triumph in a little more detail.

maverick's major obstacles in this film are, firstly, the top gun top-brass; he needs to prove not only that he is the best pilot, but he needs to prove to them that he can only be the best by doing things his way.
we also have unresolved father issues stemming from a murky death during aerial combat: maverick must solve the mystery of his father's final acts to conquer the past as well as the present.
but maverick's greatest obstacle comes from the man who is both his most prominent rival and critic: ice (played by val kilmer).
gaining his approval is what will truly cement maverick as a leader among men.

i will not reveal the resolutions of these plot strands just in case there are some who have not yet got around to seeing this film, but suffice it to say that maverick's arc very much plays out as a hero's journey.

the greatest objection i have to this film, besides the incessant flying scenes, is the solipsistically obsessive attention it pays to its main character and the toxic message this plays into when it comes to defining and understanding masculinity.
when watching this film, i challenge you to find a single piece of dialogue which takes place outside of the flying or teaching scenes which does not reference maverick directly.
every utterance, every snipe, every chance interaction is based around establishing the fact that maverick is firmly at the centre of this narrative.
i understand that maverick is the hero of this journey but to force this concept so incessantly risks moving the film from being mere fantasy into the category of wildly-unrealistic aspiration.
insecure, directionless men may look to maverick as a pin-up for their own arrested psyches.

they can perhaps imagine that one day they could be a fraction as important as maverick clearly is in this make-believe world.

a particularly egregious consequence of the maverick obsession is that we are fed diabolically underdeveloped and underwritten supporting characters, the worst example of which is charlie.
she starts out well enough as a young, driven woman who refuses to be impressed by maverick's irrepressible cockiness and insufferable self-assurance.
the problem is that she very quickly becomes an appendage to maverick.
he can not resist any opportunity to criticise and undermine the noble, brilliant maverick, until, of course, he too is won over.

when it comes to maverick, even the haters can't keep up their hate.

the seemingly overt homo-eroticism of the film is worth remarking upon due to its notoriety and quirkiness but it is, in my view, often misunderstood.

the movie stars tom cruise as maverick, a hotshot us navy fighter jet pilot who is equal parts skill and attitude.
